<a id="p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented` — Almost finitely generated, uniformly almost finitely generated and almost finitely presented modules

*Definition.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module, M = N^a over A = R^a. N^a is almost finitely generated if for every finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m there are n and an R-linear φ : Rⁿ → N with m₀·coker φ = 0; uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n if one n works for all m₀; almost finitely presented if for every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m there is a complex R^k →ψ Rⁿ →φ N with m₀·coker φ = 0 and m₀·ker φ ⊆ im ψ. These conditions depend only on N^a (not on the representative N), and agree with GR's definitions through the uniform structure on isomorphism classes (GR Definition 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.10); under condition (A) (e.g. root and valuation setups) they are equivalent to Sch12's ε-formulation: for every ε ∈ m there is a finitely generated (presented) R-module N_ε and N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion). For an arbitrary almost algebra A they are applied to M_* over A_* (P0/almost-algebras). Pinned: our uniform notion (maps from Rⁿ with small cokernel) implies GR's U_n(A) in general and is equivalent to it under (A) (GR Remark 2.3.9).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; R a V-algebra; N an R-module.

**Proof outline.**

1. Definitions as stated, with finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m (Mathlib `Submodule.FG`).
2. Independence of the representative: if N → N' is an almost isomorphism, replace m₀ by m₁ with m₀ ⊆ m₁² ... using m = m²: generators of N' multiplied by elements of m lift to N (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); the kernel condition for presentations is handled as in GR Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12.
3. Comparison with GR 2.3.8: GR Proposition 2.3.10(i) and (ii)(c) are exactly our conditions for almost finitely generated and presented modules.

**API.**

- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG` (data): ∀ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG → ∃ n (φ : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] N), m₀ • ⊤ ≤ LinearMap.range φ (read in the quotient N ⧸ range φ).
- `Almost.Module.UniformlyAlmostFG` (data): ∃ n, the same with n independent of m₀.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFP` (data): ∀ m₀ f.g., ∃ complex R^k → Rⁿ → N with m₀ • coker = 0 and m₀ • ker ≤ range.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG.of_almostIso` (extensionality): The predicates depend only on N^a: they are invariant under almost isomorphisms.
- `Almost.Module.almostFG_of_finite` (compatibility): Module.Finite R N → AlmostFG; Module.FinitePresentation R N → AlmostFP.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG.extension` (relation): Extensions of almost f.g. (f.p.) modules are almost f.g. (f.p.); for M almost f.p., a quotient is almost f.p. iff the kernel is almost f.g. (GR Lemma 2.3.17).
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along A → B preserves AlmostFG, AlmostFP and uniform bounds.
- `Almost.Module.almostFP_iff_alHom_colim` (characterisation): AlmostFP M ↔ alHom_A(M, −) commutes with filtered colimits (GR Proposition 2.3.15).
- `Almost.Module.almostFG_iff_epsilon` (characterisation): Under condition (A): AlmostFG ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃ f.g. N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG_test_quadratic` (computation): For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, and L = K(√p): with R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K° ⊆ L°, the cokernel of R_n → L° is killed by p^{1/p^{n−1}}, so L°a is UniformlyAlmostFG with bound 2 and AlmostFP (Bhatt Example 4.2.7).
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG_test_zero` (degenerate): Every almost zero R-module N gives N^a ≅ 0, which is UniformlyAlmostFG with bound 0 and AlmostFP.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V: AlmostFG (N^a) ↔ Module.Finite R N and AlmostFP (N^a) ↔ Module.FinitePresentation R N.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG_test_infinite_sum` (non-example): For S = ofValuationRing K°: N = ⊕_{n∈ℕ} K° is not almost finitely generated: for m₀ = (ϖ), no map (K°)^n → N has cokernel killed by ϖ (the image misses all but finitely many summands).

**Uses.**

- Sch12 Definition 4.13: finite étale = étale + almost finitely presented
- Sch12 Theorem 4.11 (P0/rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective): uniformly finite projective modules have a rank decomposition
- GR 5.1.6 (P0/almost-nakayama), 5.3.18, 5.3.24: Nakayama and adic lifting need almost finite generation
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p: S°a uniformly finite projective over R°a
- KL Definition 5.5.8: (uniformly) almost finite projective via finite free modules of bounded rank

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Example 4.9 / Bhatt Example 4.2.7: for K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): L°a is almost finitely presented and uniformly almost finitely generated with bound 2 over K°a.
- In the classical setup the notions are finite generation and finite presentation.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), `mathlib:Submodule.FG`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`, `mathlib:Module.FinitePresentation`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Finiteness

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.3, Proposition 2.3.10(i), p. 18. The characterisation used as definition.
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.3, Proposition 2.3.10(ii)(c), p. 18. Almost finite presentation.
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.3, Definition 2.3.8(iii), p. 17. Uniform bound.

<a id="p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness` — Flat, faithfully flat, almost projective and almost finite projective almost modules

*Definition.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. M is flat if M ⊗_A − : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact, faithfully flat if moreover M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 implies N ≅ 0, almost projective if alHom_A(M, −) : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact (GR Definition 2.4.4), and almost finite projective if it is almost projective and almost finitely generated (P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented); 'uniformly almost finite projective' adds a uniform bound. Pinned convention: categorical projectivity (Hom(M, −) exact) is never used — Almost.Module S has no nonzero projective objects when V is local and m ≠ V (GR Example 2.4.5). For a V-algebra R and an R-module N: N flat (faithfully flat, projective) implies N^a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) over R^a (GR 2.4.8). Characterisations: Tor and Ext criteria (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion), ε-factorisation (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), finite projective = flat + almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost V-algebra; A-Mod as in P0/almost-algebras.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define the three predicates on objects of A-Mod through the functors M ⊗_A − and alHom_A(M, −) (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom for A-Mod).
2. Compatibility with honest modules: if N is R-flat then N ⊗_R − preserves almost zero modules and exact sequences, so it induces an exact functor on the Serre quotient (GR 2.4.8); faithfulness from m ⊗ (N ⊗ X) = 0 ⇔ m ⊗ X = 0 for N faithfully flat; projective N is a summand of a free module and alHom(R^{(I)}, −) = ∏ is exact.
3. Almost projective ⇒ flat: multiplication by ε factors through a free module (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)).
4. Stability: tensor products and base change preserve flatness and almost projectivity (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii)); transitivity along almost algebra maps (GR Lemma 2.4.7).

**API.**

- `Almost.Module.Flat` (data): M ⊗_A − preserves finite limits (it is exact).
- `Almost.Module.FaithfullyFlat` (data): Flat and M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 → N ≅ 0.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective` (data): alHom_A(M, −) preserves epimorphisms.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostFiniteProjective` (data): AlmostProjective ∧ AlmostFG; uniformly with bound n.
- `Almost.Module.flat_toAlmost` (compatibility): Module.Flat R N → Flat ((toAlmost _).obj N); likewise FaithfullyFlat and Projective → AlmostProjective.
- `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective.flat` (relation): AlmostProjective M → Flat M.
- `Almost.Module.Flat.tensor` (structure): Flat and AlmostProjective are stable under ⊗_A and under base change B ⊗_A −.
- `Almost.Module.Flat.trans` (functoriality): If B is a flat (almost projective, almost f.g., almost f.p.) A-algebra and M such a B-module, M is such an A-module (GR Lemma 2.4.7).
- `Almost.Module.flat_iff_tor` (characterisation): Flat (N^a) ↔ ∀ X i, 0 < i → IsAlmostZero (Tor_i^R(N, X)) (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion).
- `Almost.Module.almostProjective_iff_factor` (characterisation): For M almost f.g.: AlmostProjective M ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃ n u v, v ∘ u = ε • 𝟙 through A^n (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).
- `Almost.Module.almostFiniteProjective_iff` (characterisation): AlmostFiniteProjective M ↔ Flat M ∧ AlmostFP M (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Module.Flat_test_valuation` (computation): For S = ofValuationRing K°: (toAlmost S).obj K° is Flat and (toAlmost S).obj (K° ⧸ ϖ) is not Flat (its almost elements have ϖ-torsion).
- `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective_test_not_projective` (non-example): For V local with S.ideal ≠ ⊤: (toAlmost S).obj V is AlmostProjective but not Projective in Almost.Module S; a definition using categorical projectivity would exclude the unit object.
- `Almost.Module.Flat_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V and a V-module N: Flat (N^a) ↔ Module.Flat V N, FaithfullyFlat (N^a) ↔ Module.FaithfullyFlat V N, and AlmostProjective (N^a) ↔ Module.Projective V N.
- `Almost.Module.FaithfullyFlat_test_zero` (degenerate): The zero module is Flat and AlmostProjective but not FaithfullyFlat (unless A ≅ 0).

**Uses.**

- Sch12 Definition 5.1(ii) and Lemma 5.3: perfectoid K°a-algebras are flat; flatness over K°a is ϖ-torsion-freeness of M_*
- Sch12 Proposition 4.10, Definition 4.13; GR 3.1.1: finite projective modules and flat/étale morphisms of almost algebras
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected, D2/v-descent-of-functions: (S⁺/ϖ)^a is faithfully flat over (R⁺/ϖ)^a (automatic flatness)
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.9.11 (André), PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/Q4: almost faithful flatness of A°/ϖ → B°/ϖ in the Tor formulation
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p: S°a is (uniformly) almost finite projective over R°a
- KL Definition 5.5.8; Bhatt Definition 4.2.4: almost finite projective via ε-factorisations and via Ext vanishing

**Acceptance.**

<a id="p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion` — Tor and Ext criteria for almost flatness and almost projectivity

*Lemma.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module. (i) For R-modules M, N and i ≥ 0 there are natural isomorphisms Tor_i^{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Tor_i^R(M, N)^a and alExt^i_{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Ext^i_R(M, N)^a, where Tor^{R^a} and alExt are the derived functors of ⊗ and alHom on R^a-Mod (computed by flat resp. injective resolutions). (ii) N^a is flat over R^a iff Tor_i^R(N, X) is almost zero for all R-modules X and all i > 0; (iii) N^a is almost projective iff Ext^i_R(N, X) is almost zero for all X and i > 0; (iv) N^a is faithfully flat iff it is flat and, for every R-module X, N ⊗_R X almost zero implies X almost zero. (v) An almost projective module is flat.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; R a V-algebra.

**Proof outline.**

1. Derived functors on R^a-Mod exist: enough injectives and enough flat and almost projective objects (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints; GR 2.4.8, 2.4.10); bounded above exact complexes of flat (almost projective) objects are acyclic for ⊗ (alHom(−, M)).
2. (i): the exact functor (−)^a takes a flat resolution of M to a flat resolution of M^a (GR 2.4.8), whence (2.4.11); for Ext use the adjunction between (−)_! and (−)^a on derived categories (GR 2.4.9, Lemma 2.4.14(i)).
3. (ii)-(iii): M is flat (almost projective) iff all higher Tor (alExt) vanish (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)); combine with (i) and P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (vanishing of M^a iff M almost zero).
4. (iv): faithfulness of N^a ⊗ − means N^a ⊗ X^a ≅ 0 ⇒ X^a ≅ 0.
5. (v): multiplication by ε ∈ m on an almost projective M factors through a free module (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).

**Acceptance.**

- Over S = (K°, K°°): M^a flat iff Tor_1(M, K°/ϖ) = M[ϖ] is almost zero, iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.9.11: A°/ϖ → B°/ϖ almost faithfully flat means Tor_i^{A°/ϖ}(M, B°/ϖ) almost zero for i > 0; by (ii) this is flatness of (B°/ϖ)^a over (A°/ϖ)^a.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`](#p0-almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`](#p0-almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.4, Remark 2.4.12(i), p. 24. Tor/Ext vanishing criterion.

<a id="p0-almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation` — Almost projectivity via ε-factorisations through free modules

*Lemma.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and M an A-module. (i) M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there is a set I and A-linear maps M →u A^{(I)} →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M. (ii) If M is almost finitely generated, M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there are n(ε) ∈ ℕ and M →u Aⁿ →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M; M is uniformly almost finite projective with bound n iff n can be taken independent of ε (Kedlaya–Liu's definition of (uniformly) almost finite projective).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; M an A-module.

**Proof outline.**

1. ⇐: applying alExt^i(−, N) to M → A^{(I)} → M shows that ε kills alExt^i(M, N) for i > 0; as ε ∈ m is arbitrary these are almost zero, hence zero in A-Mod (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion).
2. ⇒ (finitely generated case, GR proof of Lemma 2.4.15): choose φ_ε : Aⁿ → M with ε·coker φ_ε = 0, factor through its image M_ε; almost projectivity makes alHom(M, Aⁿ) → alHom(M, M_ε) an epimorphism, so for δ ∈ m the map δ·γ_ε (with ε·1_M = j_ε ∘ γ_ε) lifts to u_{εδ} : M → Aⁿ; then φ_ε ∘ u_{εδ} = εδ·1_M; products εδ span m.
3. ⇒ (general case): the same argument with a free module A^{(I)} surjecting onto M.

**Acceptance.**

- For P = L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): the maps L° → (K°)² → L° with composite p^{1/p^{n−1}} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7) exhibit P as uniformly almost finite projective with bound 2.
- KL Definition 5.5.8 takes (ii) as the definition of almost finite projective.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.15, p. 25. Statement (ii).
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.15, p. 25. The factorisation condition.

<a id="p0-almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion` — The ε-criterion for almost finite generation and presentation under condition (A)

*Lemma.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup satisfying condition (A) (m is a filtered union of principal ideals; e.g. root setups and valuation setups), R a V-algebra and N an R-module. Then N^a is almost finitely generated (resp. almost finitely presented) iff for every ε ∈ m there are a finitely generated (resp. finitely presented) R-module N_ε and an R-linear map N_ε → N whose kernel and cokernel are killed by ε; and N^a is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n iff for every ε ∈ m there is Rⁿ → N with cokernel killed by ε. In a general basic setup the same equivalences hold with ε replaced by finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m, which is the definition of P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup with condition (A).

**Proof outline.**

1. Under (A) every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m lies in a principal ideal εV ⊆ m, and every ε ∈ m generates a finitely generated subideal; so the m₀-conditions and the ε-conditions are equivalent for generation (take N_ε := image, kernel 0).
2. Presentation: GR Proposition 2.3.10(ii), equivalence of (a), (b), (c), with (b) the ε, δ-formulation; from a complex R^k → Rⁿ → N with ε-small cokernel and δ-small homology one builds N_ε := Rⁿ/im ψ and conversely (Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12).
3. Uniform bound: GR Remark 2.3.9.

**Acceptance.**

- For S = ofValuationRing K°, Sch12 Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii) is this ε-formulation.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup`](#p0-almost-basic-setup).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), arXiv v1, §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii), p. 19. Sch12's ε-formulation (citing GR book Definition 2.3.8, Remark 2.3.9(i), Corollary 2.3.13).

<a id="p0-almost-finite-projective-iff"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff` — Flat + almost finitely presented ⟺ almost projective + almost finitely generated

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. (i) If M is almost projective and almost finitely generated, M is almost finitely presented (and flat). (ii) If M is flat and almost finitely presented, M is almost projective. Hence 'finite projective' in Sch12's sense (flat and almost finitely presented) coincides with almost finite projective (almost projective and almost finitely generated). (iii) If A → B is a monomorphism of almost algebras and M is an almost finitely generated flat A-module with B ⊗_A M almost finitely presented over B, then M is almost finitely presented.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. (ii) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(ii): for ε, δ ∈ m pick A^m →ψ Aⁿ →φ M with ε·coker φ = 0 = δ·(ker φ/im ψ); P := coker ψ_* is a finitely presented A_*-module; flatness and Lemma 2.4.17 (Tor_1 of the transposed presentation) give γ·φ = w ∘ v through a free module for every γ ∈ m; assemble α, β with β ∘ α = εδγ·1_M and conclude by P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation.
2. (i) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(i): for a finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m pick φ : A^r → P with m₀·coker φ = 0; ε_i·1_P lifts to P → A^r/ker φ and, P being almost projective, ε_jψ_i lifts to A^r; Claim 2.3.11 gives finitely generated submodules of ker φ containing ε_iε_j ker φ, so m₀²·ker φ lies in a finitely generated submodule.
3. (iii) GR Proposition 2.4.19.

**Acceptance.**

- For the classical setup this is the statement that finitely presented flat modules are projective and finitely generated projective modules are finitely presented.
- Sch12 Proposition 4.10 is the case S = (K°, K°°).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`](#p0-almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion).

<a id="p0-tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective` — E ⊗ alHom(F, N) → alHom(F, E ⊗ N) is an isomorphism for almost finite projective E or F

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and E, F, N A-modules. The natural map E ⊗_A alHom_A(F, N) → alHom_A(F, E ⊗_A N) is (i) an isomorphism if E or F is almost finite projective, if E is flat and F almost finitely presented, if F is almost projective and E almost finitely presented, or if E is almost projective and F almost finitely generated; (ii) a monomorphism if E is flat and F almost finitely generated, or if E is almost projective; (iii) an epimorphism if F is almost projective and E almost finitely generated. Consequences: for P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism, P is reflexive (P ≅ P**), and B ⊗_A alHom_A(P, N) ≅ alHom_B(B ⊗_A P, B ⊗_A N) for every A-algebra B.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. Free finite case: alHom(Aⁿ, N) ≅ Nⁿ and the map is an isomorphism.
2. Almost finite projective F: for ε ∈ m apply the natural transformation to F →u_ε A^{I(ε)} →v_ε F (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation) with I(ε) finite; a diagram chase shows that kernel and cokernel are killed by ε, hence almost zero, hence zero (GR proof of Lemma 2.4.29).
3. The remaining cases reduce, via almost elements and ε-approximations, to classical statements for finitely generated (presented) modules and free modules (Bourbaki Algèbre commutative I §2 Prop. 10), as in GR.
4. ω_{P/A} is the case E = P, N = A; reflexivity and base change: GR Lemma 2.4.31.

**Acceptance.**

- For P = (Rⁿ)^a free: ω_{P/A} is the usual identification Rⁿ ⊗ (Rⁿ)^∨ ≅ End(Rⁿ) after almostification.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`](#p0-almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`](#p0-almost-tensor-and-internal-hom), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

<a id="p0-almost-dual-and-trace"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace` — Duals, traces of endomorphisms and the trace form of an almost finite projective algebra

*Construction.* Let S be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. For an A-module M, the dual is M* := alHom_A(M, A) with evaluation ev_{M/A} : M ⊗_A M* → A. For P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism (P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective) and the trace is tr_{P/A} := ev_{P/A} ∘ ω_{P/A}⁻¹ : End_A(P)^a → A. For an A-algebra B which is almost finite projective as an A-module, μ : B → End_A(B)^a (b ↦ multiplication by b, defined on almost elements) gives the almost trace Tr_{B/A} := tr_{B/A} ∘ μ : B → A, the trace form t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A, and τ_{B/A} : B → B*; t_{B/A} is a perfect pairing if τ_{B/A} is an isomorphism. Properties: tr(ψ∘φ) = tr(φ∘ψ); tr(φ ⊗ ψ) = tr(φ)·tr(ψ); additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules; Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}; Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}; τ is B-linear and compatible with base change. Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` (zero on non-free modules) is not used for almost finite projective modules; it agrees with tr on free modules.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; P almost finite projective; B an A-algebra, almost finite projective as A-module.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define P*, ev and ω on almost elements (GR Definition 2.4.23, 2.4.26); ω iso by P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective; tr := ev ∘ ω⁻¹ and ζ_P := ω⁻¹(1_P) (GR Definition 4.1.1).
2. Cyclicity: reduce by A-linearity to rank-one maps x ↦ n·α(x), then compute (GR Lemma 4.1.2); multiplicativity (Lemma 4.1.3); additivity via the ε-split pullback trick (Proposition 4.1.4).
3. Algebra traces: μ is a B-linear monomorphism (GR 4.1.7); base change and transitivity (Proposition 4.1.8); τ_{B/A} and base change (Lemma 4.1.13).
4. Compatibility with free modules: for P = (Rⁿ)^a, ω and ev are almostifications of Mathlib's `dualTensorHom` and evaluation, so tr = (LinearMap.trace)^a.

**API.**

- `Almost.Module.dual` (constructor): M* := alHom_A(M, A), with evaluation M ⊗_A M* ⟶ A.
- `Almost.Module.dualTensorHomIso` (equivalence): For P almost finite projective: ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* ≅ End_A(P)^a.
- `Almost.Module.trace` (constructor): tr_{P/A} : End_A(P)^a ⟶ A := ev ∘ ω⁻¹.
- `Almost.Module.trace_comp_comm` (relation): tr_{M/A}(ψ ∘ φ) = tr_{N/A}(φ ∘ ψ).
- `Almost.Module.trace_tensor` (relation): tr_{M⊗N/A}(φ ⊗ ψ) = tr_{M/A}(φ) · tr_{N/A}(ψ).
- `Almost.Module.trace_additive` (relation): Additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules with compatible endomorphisms.
- `Almost.Module.isReflexive` (characterisation): P ≅ P** for P almost finite projective.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace` (constructor): Tr_{B/A} : B ⟶ A for B almost finite projective over A.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_baseChange` (compatibility): Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_trans` (functoriality): Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_of_iso` (simp): If A → B is an isomorphism, Tr_{B/A} is its inverse.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm` (constructor): t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B ⟶ A and τ_{B/A} : B ⟶ B*.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsPerfectTraceForm` (data): τ_{B/A} is an isomorphism.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceFormDual_baseChange` (compatibility): η ∘ (1_C ⊗ τ_{B/A}) = τ_{C⊗B/C} (GR Lemma 4.1.13).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Module.trace_test_free` (compatibility): For P = (toAlmost _).obj (Fin n → R): Almost.Module.trace P ((toAlmost _).map f) = (toAlmost _).map (LinearMap.trace R _ f) (Mathlib's trace), and for a free finite R-algebra R', Almost.Algebra.trace = (Algebra.trace R R')^a.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_test_quadratic` (computation): For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2 and IsPerfectTraceForm (L°a/K°a).
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_zero` (degenerate): For P = 0, tr_{P/A} = 0; for B = 0, Tr_{B/A} = 0 and t_{B/A} is perfect.
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_not_linearMap_trace` (non-example): For P = L°a over K°a (L° is not a free K°-module), (LinearMap.trace K° L°)^a = 0 ≠ tr_{P/A}(1) = 2: the almost trace cannot be defined through Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` of a representative.

**Uses.**

- Sch12 Definition 4.14 and Theorem 4.16 (P0/trace-form-criterion): finite étale iff the trace form is perfect
- KL Definition 5.5.8 and Theorem 5.5.9: almost finite étale defined by an almost perfect trace pairing
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p: S₀^⊥ via the perfect trace pairing, and the ε-splittings built from the diagonal idempotent and the trace
- GR 4.3 (P0/rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective): χ_P(X) = Σ tr(Λ^i 1_P) X^i determines the rank
- GR Corollary 4.1.11: the trace of a faithfully flat finite étale map is an epimorphism

**Acceptance.**

- For B = (Rⁿ)^a with R-algebra structure free of rank n: Tr_{B/A} = (Algebra.trace R Rⁿ)^a.
- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)): Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2 and t_{L°a/K°a} is perfect, while the honest trace form on R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K° has discriminant 4p^{1/p^n} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective`](#p0-tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`](#p0-almost-tensor-and-internal-hom), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), `mathlib:LinearMap.trace`, `mathlib:Algebra.trace`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §4.1, Definition 4.1.1, p. 72. tr_{P/A} := ev ∘ ω⁻¹.

<a id="p0-rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective` — Rank decomposition of uniformly almost finite projective modules

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup satisfying condition (B) (k-th powers generate m; implied by (A)), A an almost V-algebra and P a uniformly almost finite projective A-module. Then P has finite rank: Λ^r_A P = 0 for some r. For P almost projective with Λ^r_A P = 0 there is a unique decomposition A ≅ A_0 × A_1 × ⋯ × A_{r−1} such that P_i := P ⊗_A A_i has constant rank i over A_i: Λ^{i+1}_{A_i} P_i = 0 and Λ^i_{A_i} P_i is an invertible A_i-module (P_i ⊗ P_i* ≅ A_i). The decomposition is compatible with base change A → A'.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup with condition (B) (used for uniform continuity of Λ^r, GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi), and for Proposition 4.3.4); root and valuation setups satisfy (A) hence (B).
- Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 4.11 cites GR Proposition 4.3.27 and Remark 4.3.10(i) in book numbering; the arXiv v3 statements with these numbers are the ones quoted here.

**Proof outline.**

1. Finite rank: a uniformly almost finitely generated module with bound n lies in the closure U_n(A) of the modules generated by n almost elements; under (B) the operation Λ^{n+1} is uniformly continuous (GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi)) and vanishes on modules generated by n elements, so Λ^{n+1}P = 0 (GR Remark 4.3.10(i)).
2. Formal rank: χ_P(X) = Σ_i tr(Λ^i 1_P) X^i defines an endomorphism of Ĝ_m (GR Corollary 4.3.8, from Proposition 4.3.4 whose proof uses (B)); for finite rank it is (1 + X)^α for a locally constant α (Remark 4.3.10(ii)).
3. Decomposition: induction on r, the case r = 2 being GR Lemma 4.3.12, the inductive step using Lemma 4.3.26 (Λ²(Λ^{r−1} P) = 0) (GR Proposition 4.3.27).
4. Uniqueness and base change: the idempotents are determined by χ_P, which is compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.3.2(i)).

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): r = 3, A = A_2 (constant rank 2).
- For A = K°a × K°a and P = K°a × 0: A_1 = first factor, A_0 = second factor.

<a id="p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras` — Flat, unramified, étale and finite étale morphisms of almost algebras

*Definition.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost V-algebras; view B as a B ⊗_A B-algebra through the multiplication μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B, with kernel I_{B/A}. Following GR Definition 3.1.1: φ is flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) if B is a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) A-module; (uniformly) almost finite if B is a (uniformly) almost finitely generated A-module; weakly unramified (unramified) if B is a flat (almost projective) B ⊗_A B-module; weakly étale (étale) if flat and weakly unramified (unramified). φ is finite étale if it is étale and B is an almost finitely presented A-module (Sch12 Definition 4.13; GR's A-Ét_afp; Kedlaya–Liu's and Bhatt's 'almost finite étale'); then B is almost finite projective over A (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff). A_fet denotes the full subcategory of A-algebras that are finite étale over A. Equivalent descriptions: unramified iff there is a diagonal idempotent e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with μ(e) = 1 and I_{B/A,*}·e = 0 (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation, Sch12's definition); for B almost finite projective over A, étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} is perfect (P0/trace-form-criterion). Pinned: 'finite étale' always means étale and almost finitely presented; in the classical setup it is Mathlib's finite étale (P0/finite-etale-localizes), while GR's 'étale' without finiteness is more general than EGA étale (GR Remark 3.1.3(i)).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras; module notions as in P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness and P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented, applied to B as an A-module and as a B ⊗_A B-module.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define the predicates on morphisms of Almost.Algebra S through the module structures of B over A and over B ⊗_A B (μ_{B/A} a morphism of almost algebras).
2. A_fet := full subcategory of Under A on the finite étale morphisms.
3. The characterisations are P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation (GR Proposition 3.1.4), P0/trace-form-criterion (GR Theorem 4.1.14) and P0/etale-morphisms-stability (GR Lemma 3.1.2).

**API.**

- `Almost.Algebra.IsFlat` (data): φ : A ⟶ B is flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) if B is so as an A-module.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsUnramified` (data): B is almost projective over B ⊗_A B via μ_{B/A}; IsWeaklyUnramified: flat instead of almost projective.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale` (data): IsFlat ∧ IsUnramified; IsWeaklyEtale: IsFlat ∧ IsWeaklyUnramified.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale` (data): IsEtale ∧ AlmostFP B over A.
- `Almost.Algebra.FiniteEtale` (data): A_fet: the full subcategory of Under A on finite étale morphisms.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.baseChange` (compatibility): Flat, unramified, étale, weakly étale and finite étale morphisms are stable under base change A → A'.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.comp` (functoriality): and under composition (P0/etale-morphisms-stability).
- `Almost.Algebra.isUnramified_iff_exists_idempotent` (characterisation): IsUnramified φ ↔ ∃ e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* idempotent, μ(e) = 1, I_{B/A,*} e = 0 (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation).
- `Almost.Algebra.isEtale_iff_isPerfectTraceForm` (characterisation): For B almost finite projective over A: IsEtale φ ↔ IsPerfectTraceForm φ (P0/trace-form-criterion).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale.almostFiniteProjective` (relation): B is almost finite projective over A.
- `Almost.Algebra.isFiniteEtale_toAlmost` (compatibility): Mathlib finite étale R → R' gives a finite étale R^a → R'^a (P0/finite-etale-localizes).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_quadratic` (computation): For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost _).map (algebraMap K° L°)) over S = ofValuationRing K°.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_idempotent_not_honest` (non-example): In the same example the diagonal idempotent is an almost element of L°a ⊗ L°a but does not lie in L° ⊗_{K°} L° (only p^{1/p^n}e does, for every n): a definition requiring an honest idempotent of B_* ⊗_{A_*} B_* would reject L°a/K°a.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V and a V-algebra map R → R': IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost S).map f) ↔ Algebra.Etale R R' ∧ Module.Finite R R' (Mathlib).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_trivial` (degenerate): 𝟙 A, A → 0 and the diagonal A → A × A are finite étale.

**Uses.**

- P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras (Sch12 Theorem 4.17, GR Theorem 5.3.27): the lifting equivalence A_fet ≅ (A/ϖ)_fet
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem (ECD Theorem 6.1(iii), KL Theorem 5.5.9): S° is almost finite étale over R°
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (Sch12 Propositions 5.22-5.23): finite étale algebras over perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras and S°a/R°a in characteristic p
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the chain R_fet ← A_fet ≅ Ā_fet ≅ A♭_fet → R♭_fet
- P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (GR Theorem 3.2.18): weakly étale and étale algebras lift along nilpotent ideals
- P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent: étale and weakly étale algebras descend along faithfully flat maps

**Acceptance.**

- Bhatt Example 4.3.2: for K = completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), L = K(√p), p ≠ 2: L°a is finite étale over K°a; the diagonal idempotent e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1) satisfies p^{1/p^n} e ∈ L° ⊗ L° for all n, so e ∈ (L°a ⊗ L°a)_*, although e ∉ L° ⊗_{K°} L°.
- Sch12 Theorem 4.17 and GR Theorem 5.3.27 are statements about A_fet (P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`](#p0-almost-tensor-and-internal-hom), `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Algebra.FormallyUnramified`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.1, Definition 3.1.1(iv), p. 39. Weakly étale and étale.

<a id="p0-unramified-idempotent-characterisation"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation` — Unramified ⟺ existence of the diagonal idempotent

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. φ is unramified (B almost projective over B ⊗_A B) iff there is an almost element e_{B/A} ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with e² = e, μ_{B/A}(e) = 1 and x·e = 0 for every x ∈ (I_{B/A})_*. The element e is unique, and B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B as B ⊗_A B-algebras (I_{B/A} with unit 1 − e). More generally, for an ideal I of an almost algebra A, A/I is almost projective over A iff I is generated by an idempotent of A_*, which is then unique.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. ⇒: for ε ∈ m almost projectivity gives an ε-splitting u_ε : B → B ⊗_A B of μ with μ ∘ u_ε = ε·1_B (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation); e_ε := u_ε(1) satisfies e_ε² = ε e_ε, μ(e_ε) = ε and I_*·e_ε = 0 by B ⊗_A B-linearity.
2. δ e_ε = ε e_δ for ε, δ ∈ m, so ε ⊗ δ ↦ δ·e_ε is a well defined map m ⊗_V m → (B ⊗_A B)_*, i.e. an almost element e (GR (3.1.7)), with the required properties.
3. ⇐: u(b) := e·(1 ⊗ b) is B ⊗_A B-linear by the annihilation property and splits μ, so B is a direct summand, hence almost projective (GR Lemma 2.4.15).
4. Uniqueness and the product decomposition: GR Corollary 3.1.9 and Remark 3.1.8.

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the idempotent is Bhatt's e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1).
- In the classical setup with B finite étale over A, ker μ is a finitely generated idempotent ideal, generated by the idempotent 1 − e (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`](#p0-almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), `mathlib:IsIdempotentElem`, `mathlib:Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.8, p. 40. Idempotent ideals.

<a id="p0-etale-morphisms-stability"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/etale-morphisms-stability` — Stability of flat, unramified and étale morphisms of almost algebras

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B, ψ : B → C morphisms of almost algebras. (i) Flatness, almost projectivity, faithful flatness, almost finiteness, weak unramifiedness, unramifiedness, weak étaleness and étaleness are stable under base change A → A' and (ii) under composition. (iii) If φ is flat and ψ ∘ φ faithfully flat then φ is faithfully flat. (iv) If φ is weakly unramified and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly étale) then ψ is flat (weakly étale). (v) If φ is unramified and ψ ∘ φ étale then ψ is étale. (vi) φ is faithfully flat iff it is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (vii) If φ is almost finite and weakly unramified then φ is unramified. (viii) If ψ is faithfully flat and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly unramified) then φ is flat (weakly unramified). Finite étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i), (ii), (iii), (viii): the module-theoretic stability of P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii), Lemma 2.4.7) applied to B over A and over B ⊗_A B.
2. (vi): Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0.
3. (vii): B is an almost finitely presented B ⊗_A B-module (I_{B/A} is a quotient of (B ⊗_A B) ⊗_A B), so flat implies almost projective (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).
4. (iv), (v): μ_{B/A} is étale when φ is unramified; Γ_ψ := 1_C ⊗_B μ_{B/A} is étale by (i), p := (ψ∘φ) ⊗_A 1_B is flat (étale), and ψ = Γ_ψ ∘ p; apply (ii).
5. Finite étale: base change and transitivity of almost finite presentation (GR Lemma 2.4.7, 2.3.7(v)).

**Acceptance.**

- In the classical setup (vi) is the usual criterion 'faithfully flat iff injective with flat cokernel'.
- Base change of L°a/K°a along K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a gives a finite étale (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-iff), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`](#p0-unramified-idempotent-characterisation).

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(v)-(vii), p. 39. Faithful flatness criterion.

<a id="p0-trace-form-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion` — Almost finite projective algebras are étale iff the trace form is perfect

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras with B almost finite projective as an A-module. Then φ is étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A is a perfect pairing, i.e. τ_{B/A} : B → B* = alHom_A(B, A) is an isomorphism. In that case (1_B ⊗ τ_{B/A})(e_{B/A}) = ζ_B, where e_{B/A} is the diagonal idempotent and ζ_B = ω_{B/A}⁻¹(1_B). In particular, for B almost finitely presented, φ is finite étale iff B is flat over A and t_{B/A} is perfect.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; B almost finite projective over A.

**Proof outline.**

1. τ_{B/A} is B-linear and compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.1.13), giving the B ⊗_A B-linear diagram (4.1.15).
2. ⇒: for φ étale, B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation), so τ_{B⊗B/B} = τ_{B/B} ⊕ τ_{I/B} and after B ⊗_{B⊗_A B} − all arrows of (4.1.15) are isomorphisms, in particular τ_{B/A}.
3. ⇐: put e := (1_B ⊗ τ⁻¹)(ζ_B); Claim 4.1.16 (I_{B/A}·ζ_B = 0 and σ(ζ_B) = Tr_{B/A}) gives I_{B/A}·e = 0 and μ(e) = 1, hence e is the diagonal idempotent (GR Proposition 3.1.4).

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the trace form is perfect on the almost level (the discriminants 4p^{1/p^n} of the approximations R_n tend to a unit up to m).
- In the classical setup with B finite free: the classical criterion 'finite free étale iff discriminant is a unit'.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace`](#p0-almost-dual-and-trace), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`](#p0-unramified-idempotent-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Trace

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §4.1, Remark 4.1.17, p. 76. The formula (1 ⊗ τ)(e) = ζ_B.

<a id="p0-almost-inversion-and-completion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion` — Inverting an element of m: almost modules become honest modules over V[1/ϖ]

*Construction.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and ϖ ∈ m. The localisation M ↦ M[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] ⊗_V M is exact and kills almost zero modules (ϖM = 0), so it factors, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, through an exact functor Almost.invert ϖ : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V[1/ϖ] with invert(M^a) ≅ M[1/ϖ] and invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ] ≅ M_![1/ϖ]. Consequences: almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms and almost exact complexes become exact after inverting ϖ; the setup S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical (m·V[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ]), so Almost.Module over it is ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]; invert is symmetric monoidal and sends almost algebras to V[1/ϖ]-algebras. The ϖ-adic completion side of this passage — completeness of M versus M_*, and exactness of complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ, with the lim¹ term kept — is P0/almost-completeness-via-almost-elements and P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m (so ϖ kills almost zero modules; ϖ need not be a nonzerodivisor).

**Proof outline.**

1. M ↦ M[1/ϖ] is exact (Mathlib localisation is exact) and kills almost zero modules; by Mathlib `SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft` it factors through toAlmost as an exact functor.
2. invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ]: apply the factorisation to M ≅ (M_*)^a (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).
3. S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical because ϖ ∈ m becomes a unit (P0/basic-setup-base-change); invert is then the composite of change of setup (P0/change-of-basic-setup) and Almost.Module.classicalEquiv (GR 5.2.17: 'A[ε^{-1}] is a usual V-algebra').
4. Monoidality: localisation commutes with tensor products, so invert is symmetric monoidal and carries commutative monoids to commutative V[1/ϖ]-algebras.

**API.**

- `Almost.invert` (constructor): The exact functor Almost.Module S ⥤ ModuleCat (Localization.Away ϖ) for ϖ ∈ S.ideal.
- `Almost.toAlmostCompInvertIso` (compatibility): toAlmost S ⋙ invert ϖ ≅ localisation at the powers of ϖ.
- `Almost.invert_preservesFiniteLimits` (instance): invert ϖ is exact.
- `Almost.invertElementsIso` (characterisation): (invert ϖ).obj M ≅ LocalizedModule (powers ϖ) M.elements.
- `Almost.isIso_localization_of_isAlmostIso` (relation): An almost isomorphism f becomes an isomorphism after inverting ϖ.
- `Almost.localization_subsingleton_of_isAlmostZero` (relation): IsAlmostZero M → Subsingleton (LocalizedModule (powers ϖ) M).
- `Almost.BasicSetup.baseChange_away_eq_classical` (example): S.baseChange (Localization.Away ϖ) = classical (Localization.Away ϖ).
- `Almost.invertMonoidal` (instance): (invert ϖ).Monoidal; Almost.Algebra.invert sends almost algebras to Localization.Away ϖ-algebras.
- `Almost.exact_invert_of_almostExact` (relation): A complex of V-modules with almost zero cohomology becomes exact after inverting ϖ.

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.invert_test_residue` (computation): For S = ofValuationRing K° and ϖ ∈ K°°: (invert ϖ).obj ((toAlmost S).obj (K° ⧸ ϖ)) ≅ 0 and (invert ϖ).obj ((toAlmost S).obj K°) ≅ K.
- `Almost.invert_test_unit` (degenerate): If ϖ is a unit of V (then S.ideal = ⊤ as ϖ ∈ S.ideal), invert ϖ ≅ Almost.Module.elements composed with the identification V[1/ϖ] = V.
- `Almost.invert_test_not_equivalence` (non-example): invert ϖ is not faithful: for S = ofValuationRing K°, the nonzero almost module (K°/ϖ)^a is sent to 0 (Bhatt Exercise 4.1.9); almost statements are strictly finer than statements after inverting ϖ.
- `Almost.invert_test_mathlib` (compatibility): toAlmost S ⋙ invert ϖ ≅ the Mathlib localisation functor M ↦ LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers ϖ) M, as functors ModuleCat V ⥤ ModuleCat (Localization.Away ϖ).

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/higher-v-acyclicity, D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: 'invert ϖ to obtain the statement for O' from almost vanishing for O⁺
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: 'inverting ϖ♯ gives R♯ as the equalizer of S♯ and T♯'
- PerfectoidSpaces:P9/higher-inverse-limits-vanish-on-towers: almost statements become exact statements after inverting p
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary: A ↦ A_*[1/ϖ] from perfectoid K°a-algebras to perfectoid K-algebras

<a id="p0-finite-etale-localizes"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-localizes` — Comparison of finite étale almost algebras with Mathlib's finite étale algebras

*Comparison.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and R → R' a map of commutative V-algebras. (i) If R' is finite étale over R in Mathlib's sense (`Algebra.Etale R R'` and `Module.Finite R R'`), then R^a → R'^a is finite étale in the almost sense. (ii) In the classical setup (m = V) the converse holds, so A_fet for A = R^a is equivalent to Mathlib's category of finite étale R-algebras. (iii) For ϖ ∈ m, if R'^a is finite étale over R^a then R'[1/ϖ] is finite étale over R[1/ϖ] in Mathlib's sense (inverting ϖ turns almost statements into honest ones, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion). (iv) GR-étale morphisms in the classical setup are exactly the absolutely flat (weakly étale) maps whose diagonal is almost projective; they need not be of finite presentation, and a classical étale map in EGA's sense is étale in GR's sense.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; R → R' a map of V-algebras.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) R' is a finitely presented projective R-module (finite étale ⇒ finite, flat, finitely presented), so R'^a is almost finite projective (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness); the kernel J of R' ⊗_R R' → R' is finitely generated with J = J² (Ω_{R'/R} = 0), hence generated by an idempotent (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`), whose image is the diagonal idempotent (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation).
2. (ii) In the classical setup almost notions are honest: almost finitely presented = finitely presented, the diagonal idempotent gives Ω_{R'/R} = 0 (formally unramified), and a flat, finitely presented, formally unramified algebra is étale (GR 3.4.44: étale = absolutely flat and finitely presented).
3. (iii) Apply the exact monoidal inversion functor (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and (ii) for the classical setup (V[1/ϖ], V[1/ϖ]).
4. (iv) GR Remark 3.1.3(i) and digression 3.4.44.

**Acceptance.**

- For K a perfectoid field and L/K finite separable: L°a is finite étale over K°a (ECD/Sch12), while L° need not be finite étale over K° in Mathlib's sense (it is not finitely presented in general); (i) is strictly weaker than the almost statement.
- For R → R' = R × R the diagonal idempotent is (1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`](#p0-unramified-idempotent-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`, `mathlib:Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`, `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Etale

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.44), p. 64. The classical-limit comparison.
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39. GR-étale versus EGA-étale.
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.3, Construction 4.3.3, p. 26. A finite étale algebra is a direct summand of a free module via the diagonal idempotent and the trace.

<a id="p0-almost-differentials"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials` — Almost Kähler differentials Ω_{B/A} and almost derivations

*Construction.* Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras, I_{B/A} = ker(μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B). The module of almost differentials is the B-module Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}², with the A-derivation δ : B → Ω_{B/A}, b ↦ 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 on almost elements. For a B-module M, an A-derivation B → M is an A-linear ∂ with ∂(b₁b₂) = b₁∂(b₂) + b₂∂(b₁) on almost elements; they form a V-module Der_A(B, M), and f ↦ f ∘ δ is an isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M). Properties: Ω_{C⊗_A B/C} ≅ C ⊗_A Ω_{B/A}; for A → B → C an exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0; for C = B/I an exact sequence I/I² → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → 0; Ω commutes with colimits; (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}; for V-algebras R → R', Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (Ω_{R'/R})^a (Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define I_{B/A}, Ω_{B/A} and δ in B ⊗_A B-Mod (P0/almost-algebras).
2. Universal property (2.5.24) and Proposition 2.5.25 as for rings, working on almost elements (GR 2.5.23 leaves them as exercises).
3. (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}: compare derivations B_!! → M with almost derivations B → M^a (GR Lemma 2.5.28).
4. Comparison with Mathlib: (−)^a is exact and monoidal, so it carries the kernel of R' ⊗_R R' → R' and its square to I_{B/A} and I_{B/A}².

**API.**

- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential` (constructor): Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}² as a B-module.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.d` (data): The universal A-derivation δ : B ⟶ Ω_{B/A}.
- `Almost.Algebra.Derivation` (data): A-derivations B ⟶ M, a V-module.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.liftEquiv` (universal-property): (Ω_{B/A} ⟶ M) ≃ₗ[V] Derivation A B M, f ↦ f ∘ δ.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.baseChangeIso` (compatibility): Ω_{C⊗_A B/C} ≅ C ⊗_A Ω_{B/A}.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.exact_seq` (relation): C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0 exact; conormal sequence for C = B/I.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.shriekIso` (compatibility): (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!} (Mathlib KaehlerDifferential of A_!! → B_!!).
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential_toAlmost` (compatibility): Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (KaehlerDifferential R R')^a.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential_eq_zero_of_isUnramified` (relation): φ unramified ⇒ Ω_{B/A} = 0.

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_polynomial` (computation): For A an almost algebra and B = (A_*[X])^a: Ω_{B/A} ≅ B, generated by δX.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_self` (degenerate): Ω_{A/A} = 0 and, for an ideal I, Ω_{(A/I)/A} = 0.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_mathlib` (compatibility): For V-algebras R → R': Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (toAlmost _).obj (KaehlerDifferential R R') as R'^a-modules, compatible with the derivations.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_not_elements` (non-example): The derivation δ is not defined on the honest ring B_! (a non-unital algebra); one must use B_* or B_!!: Ω_{B!!/A!!} ≅ (Ω_{B/A})_! (GR 2.5.28), whereas Ω of the non-unital B_! is not defined by Mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential`.

**Uses.**

- GR Proposition 2.5.29 (P0/almost-cotangent-complex): Ext⁰(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M)
- GR Corollary 5.2.15 and Theorem 5.2.12(iv) (P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction): an almost finite algebra is unramified iff Ω_{B/A} = 0 after reduction
- GR Proposition 3.2.9(iii), Proposition 3.2.16 (P0/almost-deformation-theory, P0/almost-morphism-lifting): automorphisms of deformations and torsors of lifts are Der_{B₀}(C₀, J)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi: H_0 of the almost cotangent complex is Ω, which vanishes for perfect algebras

**Acceptance.**

- Ω_{A[X]/A} ≅ A[X] (free on δX) for the polynomial almost algebra A[X] := (A_*[X])^a.
- Ω_{B/A} = 0 for φ unramified (the idempotent kills I_{B/A}, so I = I²).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`](#p0-almost-tensor-and-internal-hom), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`](#p0-almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek), `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`, `mathlib:Derivation`.

<a id="p0-almost-cotangent-complex"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex` — The almost cotangent complex L_{B/A}

*Construction.* Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras. Put Ã := V^a × A and B̃ := V^a × B (exact almost algebras). The almost cotangent complex is L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗_{B̃_!!} L_{B̃_!!/Ã_!!}, an object of the derived category of B_!!-modules, where L_{−/−} is the classical cotangent complex of the ring map Ã_!! → B̃_!! (simplicial polynomial resolution; supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0); its almostification L^a_{B/A} ∈ D(B-Mod) is the object used in deformation theory. Properties: H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}; Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M) (GR (3.2.8)), Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M) (P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison); transitivity triangle (P0/cotangent-transitivity); Tor-independent base change (P0/cotangent-flat-base-change); L_{colim B_λ/colim A_λ} ≅ colim L_{B_λ/A_λ} for filtered systems; vanishing for weakly étale maps (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale); for V-algebras R → S, L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a (P0/almost-cotangent-comparison-classical), so 'the almost cotangent complex depends only on R^a → S^a' (Sch12 §5).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, used in Proposition 2.5.34 and Theorem 2.5.35).
- The classical cotangent complex of a ring map, with transitivity, base change for Tor-independent squares, filtered colimits, H_0 = Ω and Ext¹ = Exal, is imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 (request); the pinned Mathlib has only the naive cotangent complex (`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`).

**Proof outline.**

1. Replace A → B by Ã → B̃: these are exact almost algebras, and (−)_!! commutes with finite products and tensor products (P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek).
2. Define L_{B/A} by the base change formula of GR Definition 2.5.20 from DD.0's L_{B̃!!/Ã!!}.
3. Derived category: B_!!-modules form an abelian category with enough injectives; the almostification functor to B-Mod is exact and induces D(B_!!-Mod) → D(B-Mod) (GR 2.4.9).
4. The listed properties are the lemmas cited with them; H_0 ≅ Ω is P0/almost-differentials and filtered colimits commute with the construction because (−)_!!, B_!! ⊗ − and DD.0's complex do.

**API.**

- `Almost.cotangentComplex` (constructor): L_{B/A} ∈ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat B_!!), defined by GR's formula from DD.0's cotangent complex.
- `Almost.almostCotangentComplex` (constructor): L^a_{B/A} ∈ DerivedCategory (B-Mod), the almostification.
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_H0` (characterisation): H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}.
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_ext_iso` (compatibility): Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M) (GR (3.2.8)).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_ext_zero` (characterisation): Ext⁰(L^a_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M) (GR 2.5.29).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_ext_one` (characterisation): Ext¹(L^a_{B/A}, M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M) (P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_transitivity` (relation): Distinguished triangle C ⊗ L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → (P0/cotangent-transitivity).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_baseChange` (compatibility): Tor-independent base change (P0/cotangent-flat-base-change).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_colim` (compatibility): L of a filtered colimit is the colimit (GR 2.5.33).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_toAlmost` (compatibility): L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a for V-algebras R → S (P0/almost-cotangent-comparison-classical).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_eq_zero_of_isWeaklyEtale` (relation): Weakly étale (more generally Tor-trivial diagonal) ⇒ L_{B/A} ≃ 0 (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.cotangentComplex_test_polynomial` (computation): For B = (A_*[X])^a: H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ B·δX and H_i(L^a_{B/A}) = 0 for i > 0.
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_test_identity` (degenerate): L_{A/A} ≃ 0 for every almost algebra A (the identity of Ã_!!).
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V and V-algebras R → R': L^a_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ L_{R'/R} (DD.0's cotangent complex), and H_1 agrees with Mathlib's `Algebra.H1Cotangent R R'`.
- `Almost.cotangentComplex_test_not_naive` (non-example): Defining L_{B/A} as the classical cotangent complex of A_* → B_* would be wrong: for A_* → B_* not of the form Ã_!! → B̃_!! the result is only almost quasi-isomorphic after almostification (GR Proposition 8.1.7), and for B_* the unit and the non-exactness of B_! intervene; the definition must pass through the exact algebras V^a × A, V^a × B.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi (Sch12 Corollary 5.16): L^a_{A/(K°a/ϖ)} vanishes for perfectoid A, via B = (A × K°a/ϖ)_!!
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras (Sch12 Theorem 5.10): obstruction and deformation groups Ext^{2,1,0}(L^a, −) vanish; triangle L_{A/(K°/ϖ)^a} → L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a} → L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a}
- GR Theorem 3.2.18 (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras): weakly étale maps have vanishing cotangent complex, hence unique liftings
- DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 (supplier of the classical cotangent complex): the almost-context extension of DD.0's classical cotangent complex, compared with the ordinary one, is owned here
- GR Theorem 2.5.43: the spectral sequence H_{p+q}(Sym^q L^a) ⇒ Tor^A_{p+q}(B, B) for quotients

**Acceptance.**

- For A → A (identity) L_{A/A} ≃ 0; for A → A[X] := (A_*[X])^a, L^a ≃ Ω_{A[X]/A}[0], free of rank one.
- For K perfectoid and A a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra, L^a_{A/(K°a/ϖ)} ≃ 0 (Sch12 Corollary 5.16; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`](#p0-almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`](#p0-almost-differentials), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `mathlib:Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `mathlib:Algebra.H1Cotangent`, `mathlib:DerivedCategory`.

<a id="p0-cotangent-transitivity"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity` — Transitivity triangle for almost cotangent complexes

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and A → B → C morphisms of almost algebras. There is a natural distinguished triangle C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A}[1] in D(C_!!-Mod), and hence C ⊗_B L^a_{B/A} → L^a_{C/A} → L^a_{C/B} → in D(C-Mod); on H_0 it extends the exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply the classical transitivity triangle (Illusie II.2.1.2, from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) to Ã_!! → B̃_!! → C̃_!! and base change to C_!! (GR Theorem 2.5.32).
2. Almostify (exact functor) for the L^a version; H_0 by P0/almost-differentials.

**Acceptance.**

- For A → A[X] → A (X ↦ 0): the triangle A ⊗ L_{A[X]/A} → L_{A/A} ≃ 0 → L_{A/A[X]} → gives L^a_{A/A[X]} ≃ (X)/(X²)[1] ≅ A[1], the conormal module in homological degree 1.
- Used in Sch12's proof of Theorem 5.10 for A → A_n → A_{n−1} (with base change).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`.

<a id="p0-almost-cotangent-comparison-classical"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-comparison-classical` — The almost cotangent complex of R^a → S^a is the almostified classical one

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and f : R → S a map of V-algebras. (i) If f^a : R^a → S^a is an isomorphism, then (L_{S/R})^a ≃ 0 in D(S^a-Mod). (ii) The natural map L^a_{S^a/R^a} → (L_{S/R})^a is an isomorphism in D(S^a-Mod). Hence the almost cotangent complex of a morphism of almost algebras coming from V-algebras is computed by the classical cotangent complex, and it depends only on R^a → S^a.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; L_{S/R} the classical cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).

**Proof outline.**

1. (ii) from (i) by transitivity applied to (R^a)_!! → R and (S^a)_!! → S, whose almostifications are isomorphisms.
2. (i) by induction on q of H_q(L^a_{S/R}) = 0: transitivity for R → f(R) → S reduces to f injective or surjective; replace S by its standard free simplicial resolution S_• and R by R_• := S_• ×_S R (levelwise almost isomorphisms) and use the spectral sequence H_j(L_{S[i]/R[i]}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ_{S_•/R_•}); for S = V[T] free: if f surjective use a section; if f injective, compare with Sym(m̃ ⊗ F) ⊆ R ⊆ Sym(F) using flatness of m̃ and F (GR proof of Proposition 8.1.7).

**Acceptance.**

- For R = V and S = V × k (k = V/m): f^a is an isomorphism (cokernel k almost zero), and L_{S/V} ≅ 0 × L_{k/V} has homology consisting of k-modules, hence almost zero, as (i) predicts.
- Sch12 §5 uses (ii) implicitly when stating that L^a_{S/R} depends only on R^a → S^a.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`](#p0-cotangent-transitivity), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7, p. 219. The comparison, located in GR §8.1 (simplicial almost algebras).
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7(i)-(ii), p. 220. Part (ii).
- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), arXiv v1, §5, before Remark 5.15, p. 25. Sch12's statement that L^a depends only on the almost morphism.

<a id="p0-cotangent-flat-base-change"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-flat-base-change` — Tor-independent base change for almost cotangent complexes

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, A → B and A → A' morphisms of almost algebras, B' := B ⊗_A A', and suppose the natural map B ⊗^L_A A' → B' is an isomorphism (Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0 for i > 0; e.g. B or A' flat over A). Then B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'} and (B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A}) ⊕ (B'_!! ⊗_{A'!!} L_{A'/A}) → L_{B'/A} are quasi-isomorphisms. This is the result Sch12 cites as 'Theorem 2.5.36 of [14]' (LNM 1800 book numbering) in the proof of Theorem 5.10; in arXiv v3 it is Theorem 2.5.35 (arXiv Theorem 2.5.36 is the vanishing statement of P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, used in Proposition 2.5.34).

**Proof outline.**

1. Proposition 2.5.34: if A, B, C, B ⊗_A C are exact, m̃ ⊗ Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) → Tor_i is an isomorphism for i > 0, and Tor^A_i(B, C) = 0 implies Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) = 0 (uses m̃ flat).
2. Replace algebras by V^a × (−) (commutes with tensor products) so that everything is exact, then apply the classical Tor-independent base change (Illusie II.2.2.1, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) (GR proof of Theorem 2.5.35).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 proof of Theorem 5.10: for A_n flat over (K°/ϖ^n)^a the square (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, A_n → A_{n−1} is Tor-independent, so L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ≅ A_{n−1} ⊗ L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}; with transitivity this gives the triangle used there.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`](#p0-almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`.

<a id="p0-cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale` — Vanishing of the almost cotangent complex when the diagonal is Tor-trivial

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and R → S' a morphism of almost algebras with Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 and Tor^{S'⊗_R S'}_i(S', S') = 0 for all i > 0 (S' ⊗_R S'-module structure via μ). Then L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 in D(S'_!!-Mod). In particular L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 for every weakly étale (hence every étale, every finite étale) morphism R → S'.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 gives, by P0/cotangent-flat-base-change, (S'⊗S')_!! ⊗ L_{S'/R} ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/S'} and (…⊗L) ⊕ (…⊗L) ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/R}.
2. Tor^{S'⊗S'}_i(S', S') = 0 gives L_{S'/S'⊗_R S'} ≅ L_{S'/S'} ≃ 0.
3. Transitivity for R → S' ⊗_R S' → S' (P0/cotangent-transitivity): S'_!! ⊗ L_{S'⊗S'/R} ≅ L_{S'/R}; combined, L ⊕ L → L is an isomorphism that is the sum map, so L ≃ 0 (GR Theorem 2.5.36).
4. Weakly étale: S' is flat over R and over S' ⊗_R S', so both Tor conditions hold.

**Acceptance.**

- Every idempotent quotient A → A/eA is weakly étale, so L_{(A/eA)/A} ≃ 0.
- For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra the vanishing L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0 is of a different nature (Frobenius; Sch12 Proposition 5.13, PerfectoidSpaces:P1).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-flat-base-change`](#p0-cotangent-flat-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`](#p0-cotangent-transitivity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36. The vanishing theorem (arXiv numbering).
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36. Conclusion.
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.18, p. 43. Use for weakly étale lifting.

<a id="p0-almost-exal-ext-comparison"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison` — Square-zero extensions of almost algebras are classified by Ext¹ of the almost cotangent complex

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup, A → B a morphism of almost algebras and M a B-module. (i) Almostification Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) → Exal_A(B, M) is an equivalence of categories of square-zero extensions, inducing a group isomorphism on isomorphism classes, functorial in all arguments. (ii) There are natural isomorphisms Ext⁰_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Exal_A(B, M) ≅ Ext¹_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext¹_B(L^a_{B/A}, M). (iii) For an epimorphism A → B with kernel I, Hom_B(I/I², M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M) via pullback of 0 → I/I² → A/I² → B → 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A-extensions of B by M are short exact sequences 0 → M → E → B → 0 in A-Mod with E an A-algebra, M a square-zero ideal with its given B-module structure (GR 2.5.2–2.5.7).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): send X = (0 → I → E → B → 0) to X_! = (0 → I_! → E_!! → B_!! → 0), right exact, and push out along I_! → I_* (GR Lemma 2.5.17, Remark 2.5.19); the category is additive by the Baer-sum construction on ExalC (GR 2.5.5–2.5.6) and (2.5.15).
2. (ii): Ext⁰ via Illusie II.1.2.4.2 and Lemma 2.5.28 (GR Proposition 2.5.29); Ext¹ via Illusie III.1.2.3 applied to Ã_!! → B̃_!! and (i) (GR Theorem 2.5.30); the almost form via (3.2.8), which uses GR Proposition 2.5.42 and Lemma 2.4.14(i).
3. (iii): GR Lemma 3.2.1 (factor the structure map through A/I²).

**Acceptance.**

- For the trivial extension B ⊕ M, the class is 0; for A → B = A/I with I² = 0 the extension A itself corresponds to 1_{I}.
- In Sch12 Theorem 5.11 these groups classify deformations of perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`](#p0-almost-differentials), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`](#p0-almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`.

<a id="p0-almost-local-flatness-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion` — Local flatness criterion for square-zero thickenings, honest and almost

*Lemma.* (i) (classical) Let R be a ring, J ⊆ R an ideal with J² = 0, R' = R/J, and M an R-module; put M' = M/JM. Then M is R-flat iff M' is R'-flat and the natural map u(M) : J ⊗_{R'} M' → JM (x ⊗ m' ↦ xm) is an isomorphism. (ii) (almost) Let S be a basic setup and f̃ : B̃ → C̃ a morphism of A-extensions 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0 and 0 → J → C → C₀ → 0 (I² = J² = 0) whose square is cofibred (C₀ ≅ C ⊗_B B₀). Then B → C is flat iff B₀ → C₀ is flat and C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- J² = 0 (nilpotent of order two; the general nilpotent case follows by induction).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 22.3 ((1)⇔(3) for a nilpotent ideal), as recalled by GR (3.2.19): ⇒ tensor 0 → J → R → R' → 0 with M; ⇐ show Tor_1^R(N, M) = 0 for all N by dévissage 0 → JN → N → N/JN → 0 to R'-modules N', where Tor_1^R(N', M) is controlled by u(M) and flatness of M'.
2. (ii) Apply (i) to the ring map B_!! → C_!! and almost elements, using exactness of (−)^a, (−)_! and the Tor comparison of P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion (GR Lemma 3.2.6: 'the almost version of the local flatness criterion').

**Acceptance.**

- For R = k[ε]/(ε²), M = R: M' = k flat and u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → εR bijective; for M = k: u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → 0 not injective, and k is not flat over R.
- Used in P0/almost-deformation-theory to identify flat deformations with extensions by C₀ ⊗ I.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`](#p0-almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek), `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `mathlib:TensorProduct`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §3.2, Lemma 3.2.6, p. 41. Part (ii).

<a id="p0-almost-deformation-theory"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-deformation-theory` — Flat square-zero deformations of almost algebras: obstruction, torsor, automorphisms

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ = (0 → I → B → B₀ → 0) an A-extension (I² = 0) and f₀ : B₀ → C₀ a flat morphism of almost algebras. Let ω(B̃, f₀) := ∂(I → C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ∈ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I), ∂ the boundary of the transitivity sequence for B → B₀ → C₀. Then (i) ω(B̃, f₀) = 0 iff there is a flat deformation of C₀ over B, i.e. a B-extension C̃ = (0 → C₀ ⊗ I → C → C₀ → 0) with C flat over B and C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀; (ii) if ω = 0, the isomorphism classes of flat deformations form a torsor under Exal_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext¹_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I); (iii) the automorphism group of a flat deformation (acting trivially on C₀ and on C₀ ⊗ I) is Der_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I). More generally (GR Proposition 3.2.9) for any B₀-linear u : I → J the obstruction ω(B̃, f₀, u) = v_! ∘ ω(B̃, f₀) governs extensions C̃ with kernel J.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat); I² = 0; f₀ flat.
- Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 5.11 cites GR Proposition 3.2.9 (same number in arXiv v3).

**Proof outline.**

1. Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀ gives Exal_{B₀}(C₀, J) → Exal_B(C₀, J) → Hom_{B₀}(I, J) →∂ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, J) (P0/cotangent-transitivity, P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison, GR Lemma 3.2.1).
2. Obstruction, torsor and automorphisms as in Illusie III.2.1.2.3, applied through the almost Exal/Ext dictionary (GR Proposition 3.2.9).
3. Flatness of the deformation: by P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion, C is flat over B with C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀ iff its kernel is C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I via (3.2.5), which is the choice u = (I → C₀ ⊗ I) (GR 3.2.10, Corollary 3.2.11).

**Acceptance.**

- If L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ 0 (e.g. C₀ étale over B₀, or a perfectoid (K°/ϖ)^a-algebra over (K°/ϖ)^a) then a flat deformation exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; Sch12 Theorem 5.10 applies this over (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a.
- For A = B = B₀ ⊕ I trivial and C₀ = B₀[X] (almost polynomial), the trivial deformation C₀ ⊕ C₀ ⊗ I exists and deformations form a torsor under Ext¹(L^a, −) = 0.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison`](#p0-almost-exal-ext-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`](#p0-cotangent-transitivity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion`](#p0-almost-local-flatness-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`](#p0-almost-differentials).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

<a id="p0-almost-morphism-lifting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-morphism-lifting` — Lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions of almost algebras

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ an A-extension 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0, and C̃ⁱ = (0 → Jⁱ → Cⁱ → C₀ⁱ → 0), i = 1, 2, A-extensions with morphisms f̃ⁱ : B̃ → C̃ⁱ, together with v : J¹ → J² and g₀ : C₀¹ → C₀² such that u² = v ∘ u¹ and f₀² = g₀ ∘ f₀¹. The class v_* e(C̃¹) − e(C̃²) ∗ g₀ ∈ Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) is the obstruction to a morphism of A-extensions g̃ : C̃¹ → C̃² over v and g₀ with f̃² = g̃ ∘ f̃¹; when it vanishes, such g̃ form a torsor under Der_{B₀}(C₀¹, J²) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀²}(C₀² ⊗ L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²). In particular, if C and C' are flat over B with reductions C₀, C₀' and f₀ : C₀ → C₀', the obstruction to lifting f₀ lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I) and lifts form a torsor under Hom(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; I² = 0.

**Proof outline.**

1. The classes e(C̃ⁱ) ∈ Ext¹(L^a_{C₀ⁱ/B}, Jⁱ) come from P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison; the problem is solvable iff v_*C̃¹ and C̃² ∗ g₀ coincide.
2. Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀¹ shows the difference lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) (GR (3.2.15)); conclude as in Illusie III.2.2.2 (GR Proposition 3.2.16).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Theorem 5.12 (almost version) is the flat case; with L^a ≃ 0 it gives unique lifting of morphisms, the full faithfulness in Sch12 Theorem 5.10.
- For C₀ étale over B₀: morphisms lift uniquely (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (i)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison`](#p0-almost-exal-ext-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`](#p0-cotangent-transitivity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`](#p0-almost-cotangent-complex).

<a id="p0-nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras` — Étale almost algebras lift uniquely along nilpotent ideals

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a nilpotent ideal, A' := A/I. (i) For B weakly étale over A, C any A-algebra and J ⊆ C nilpotent, Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C) → Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C/J) is bijective. (ii) B ↦ A' ⊗_A B is an equivalence from weakly étale A-algebras to weakly étale A'-algebras; (iii) it restricts to an equivalence of étale algebras A-Ét ≃ A'-Ét and (iv) to an equivalence of finite étale algebras A_fet ≃ A'_fet (étale and almost finitely presented).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; I nilpotent (induction reduces to I² = 0).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): I² = 0 by induction; lifts of morphisms are governed by Ext^{1,0}(L^a_{B/A}, −) (P0/almost-morphism-lifting), and L_{B/A} ≃ 0 for B weakly étale (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).
2. (ii): a weakly étale B' over A' has a unique flat lift B (P0/almost-deformation-theory with L ≃ 0); B is weakly étale: μ_{B'/A'} is weakly étale, lifts to a flat μ̃ : B ⊗_A B → C, and by (i) C ≅ B compatibly, so B is B ⊗_A B-flat (GR proof of Theorem 3.2.18(ii)).
3. (iii): if B' is étale, I_{B'/A'} is an étale B' ⊗ B'-algebra (Corollary 3.1.9), lifts, and B ⊗_A B ≅ C ⊕ B, so B is almost projective over B ⊗_A B.
4. (iv): an étale B with A' ⊗_A B almost finitely presented is almost finitely presented (GR Lemma 3.2.25(iii), Tor^A_1(A', B) = 0 by flatness) (GR Theorem 3.2.28(ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- A = (K°/ϖ^n)^a, I = ϖ^{n−1}A: finite étale (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a-algebras lift uniquely to (K°/ϖ^n)^a; this is the finite-level step of GR Theorem 5.3.27.
- In the classical setup (iii) is SGA 1 I.8.3 in GR's generality of étale (not necessarily finitely presented) algebras.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-deformation-theory`](#p0-almost-deformation-theory), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-morphism-lifting`](#p0-almost-morphism-lifting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale`](#p0-cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`](#p0-unramified-idempotent-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented).
