<a id="p0-lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness` — B ↦ B_!! preserves and reflects faithful flatness, but not flatness

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is faithfully flat iff φ is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (ii) φ is a monomorphism iff φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is injective, and B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! is flat over A_!! iff B/A is flat over A. (iii) Hence φ is faithfully flat iff φ_!! is a faithfully flat ring map. (iv) Flatness is not preserved: for S = ofValuationRing V with residue field k, the flat projection V^a × V^a → V^a becomes V ×_k V → V under (−)_!!, which is not flat.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; m̃ flat is used in (ii) through GR Proposition 2.4.35.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): GR Lemma 3.1.2(vi), Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0 in A-Mod.
2. (ii): the kernel of φ_!! is (ker φ)_! and (−)_! reflects zero; B_!!/Im A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! (both are cokernels of V ⊕ (−)_! modulo the same ideal); (−)_! takes flat modules to flat modules and back (GR Proposition 2.4.35, Remark 3.1.3(ii)).
3. (iii): apply (i) to φ and the classical criterion to φ_!!.
4. (iv): (V^a × V^a)_!! = V ×_k V (fibre product of rings over the residue field) and V ×_k V → V is not flat (GR Remark 3.1.3(ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- For φ = identity, φ_!! is the identity.
- Bhatt Remark 4.2.8(2): (−)_!! preserves faithful flatness but may not preserve flatness.

<a id="p0-almost-faithfully-flat-descent"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent` — Faithfully flat descent for almost modules and almost algebras

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is of effective descent for modules: M ↦ (B ⊗_A M, can) is an equivalence from A-Mod to the category Desc(B/A) of B-modules N with a B ⊗_A B-linear isomorphism β : p₂*N ≅ p₁*N satisfying the cocycle condition p₁₂*(β) ∘ p₂₃*(β) = p₁₃*(β); (ii) the same holds for A-algebras; (iii) both statements are stable under base change A → A' (universal effective descent); (iv) under (i) the full subcategories of flat, almost finitely generated, almost finitely presented and almost finite projective modules correspond, and under (ii) those of weakly étale, étale and finite étale algebras correspond; (v) almost projectivity descends when B is almost finitely presented over A (for general faithfully flat φ this is not asserted: GR Remark 3.2.26(iii) leaves it open).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness).

**Proof outline.**

1. φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is a faithfully flat ring map (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness).
2. Classical descent: extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`); the identification of comonad coalgebras with descent data (cocycle and uniqueness), and descent for algebras, is Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 0E (request).
3. Transport: a descent datum (N, β) over B/A gives (N_!, β_!) over B_!!/A_!! because (−)_! commutes with tensor products (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom) and (B ⊗_A B)_!! ≅ B_!! ⊗_{A_!!} B_!!; descend to an A_!!-module and almostify; A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_!!) via A ≅ (A_!!)^a (P0/change-of-basic-setup).
4. (iv): descent of flatness, almost finite generation and presentation (GR Remark 3.2.26(ii)), of almost finite projectivity (Remark 3.2.26(iii) with P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), of (weakly) étale algebras (GR 3.4.1, P0/etale-morphisms-stability (viii)).
5. (v): GR Remark 3.2.26(iv) via Lemma 2.4.31(i) and Proposition 2.4.18(ii).

**Acceptance.**

- For V-algebras R → R' with R' faithfully flat, the almostification of Grothendieck's descent is (i) for R^a → R'^a.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3: with (S⁺/ϖ)^a faithfully flat over (R⁺/ϖ)^a (automatic flatness), the descent datum on (S̃⁺/ϖ)^a descends to an almost (R⁺/ϖ)^a-algebra.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness`](#p0-lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`](#p0-almost-tensor-and-internal-hom), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/change-of-basic-setup`](#p0-change-of-basic-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-iff), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/etale-morphisms-stability`](#p0-etale-morphisms-stability), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), `mathlib:comonadicExtendScalars`, `mathlib:ModuleCat.extendScalars`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`.

<a id="p0-almost-amitsur-complex-exact"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact` — The Amitsur complex of an almost faithfully flat map is exact

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras and M an A-module. The augmented Amitsur complex 0 → M → M ⊗_A B → M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B → ⋯ (differentials the alternating sums of the coface maps) is exact in A-Mod. In honest terms: for V-algebras R → R' such that R'^a is faithfully flat over R^a (e.g. Tor_i^R(X, R') almost zero for i > 0 and X ⊗_R R' almost zero only if X is), and any R-module N, the cohomology of 0 → N → N ⊗_R R' → N ⊗_R R' ⊗_R R' → ⋯ is almost zero; in particular N^a is the equalizer of (N ⊗ R')^a ⇉ (N ⊗ R' ⊗ R')^a.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat.

**Proof outline.**

1. After base change along φ the complex acquires a contracting homotopy (the extra degeneracy from the multiplication B ⊗_A B → B).
2. B ⊗_A − is exact and faithful on A-Mod, hence reflects exactness of complexes.
3. Honest form: (−)^a is exact, so cohomology of the honest complex almostifies to the cohomology of the almost complex; P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion translates the Tor hypotheses into faithful flatness of R'^a.

**Acceptance.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions: R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ ⇉ S⁺/ϖ ⊗ S⁺/ϖ is almost exact (ECD Proposition 8.8 uses the honest faithfully flat version for totally disconnected X).
- For A → A × A (faithfully flat, split) the Amitsur complex is split exact.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`](#p0-almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base), `mathlib:CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`.

<a id="p0-tight-ideal"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal` — Tight ideals, the Jacobson radical and henselian pairs of almost algebras

*Definition.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. An ideal I ⊆ A is tight if there are a finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m and n ∈ ℕ with Iⁿ ⊆ m₀·A (GR Definition 5.1.5); for ϖ ∈ m the ideal ϖA is tight. The Jacobson radical of A is rad(A) := rad(A_*)^a (GR 5.1.1); for a V-algebra R and an ideal J ⊆ R, J^a ⊆ rad(R^a) iff mJ ⊆ rad(R) (GR Lemma 5.1.2). A pair (A, I) with I ⊆ rad(A) is henselian if (A_*, m·I_*) is a henselian pair (Mathlib `HenselianRing A_* (m·I_*)`), and tight henselian if moreover I is tight (GR Definition 5.1.8); (R^a, J^a) is henselian iff (R, mJ) is (GR Lemma 5.1.10). If A is I-adically complete (A → lim A/Iⁿ an isomorphism), (A, I) is henselian (GR Remark 5.3.7).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; ideals of A are subobjects I ↪ A stable under multiplication, with powers Iⁿ the images of I^{⊗n}.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define IsTight via Submodule.FG subideals of m and the ideal m₀·A.
2. Define rad(A) and henselian pairs through almost elements, using Mathlib's `Ideal.jacobson` and `HenselianRing`.
3. Lemma 5.1.2 and Lemma 5.1.10: compare R with (R^a)_* through the map R → (R^a)_*, whose kernel is square-zero (killed by m) and whose image differs from (R^a)_* by an almost zero module; henselianity is insensitive to nilpotent ideals (GR Remark 5.1.9).
4. Complete ⇒ henselian: lift factorisations of monic polynomials through A_*/I_*^{n+1} (GR Remark 5.3.7; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing` for the honest step).

**API.**

- `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight` (data): ∃ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG ∧ ∃ n, Iⁿ ≤ m₀ • A.
- `Almost.Algebra.isTight_span` (example): For ϖ ∈ S.ideal, (ϖ • A) is tight.
- `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.mono` (relation): A subideal of a tight ideal is tight; powers of tight ideals are tight.
- `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.map` (functoriality): Tightness is preserved by base change along A → A'.
- `Almost.Algebra.jacobson` (constructor): rad(A) := (Ideal.jacobson ⊥ of A_*)^a.
- `Almost.Algebra.le_jacobson_toAlmost_iff` (characterisation): J^a ≤ rad(R^a) ↔ S.ideal • J ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥ (GR 5.1.2).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair` (data): I ≤ rad A ∧ HenselianRing A_* (S.ideal • I_*).
- `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_toAlmost_iff` (characterisation): IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R (S.ideal • J) (GR 5.1.10).
- `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_of_isAdicComplete` (compatibility): If A ≅ lim A/Iⁿ then (A, I) is henselian (GR Remark 5.3.7).
- `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.elements_le_jacobson` (relation): For I tight in rad(A): I_* ≤ rad(A_*), and (A_*, I_*) is henselian if (A, I) is (GR Corollary 5.1.16).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_varpi` (computation): For ϖ ∈ S.ideal, the ideal ϖA is tight (m₀ = ϖV, n = 1).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_unit` (non-example): For S = ofValuationRing K° and A = V^a, the unit ideal A is not tight: A ⊆ m₀A would force m ⊆ m₀ for a finitely generated (hence principal) m₀ = εK° ⊊ m.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_zero` (degenerate): The zero ideal of any almost algebra is tight.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V: every ideal is tight and IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R J (Mathlib), since then m·J = J and (R^a)_* = R.

**Uses.**

- GR Theorems 5.3.24 and 5.3.27 (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras): the lifting equivalences hold for tight ideals
- GR Lemma 5.1.6 (P0/almost-nakayama): Nakayama for almost finitely generated modules needs I tight and in rad(A)
- GR Proposition 5.1.17 (P0/tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting): idempotents lift along tight henselian pairs
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (GR 5.4, Sch12 Proposition 7.4): henselian pairs along (ϖ) and their almost versions
- P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi: Nakayama along the tight ideal generated by a root of ϖ

**Acceptance.**

- For ϖ ∈ m and A = R^a with R ϖ-adically complete: (A, ϖA) is tight henselian.
- In the classical setup, every ideal is tight and henselian pairs are Mathlib's henselian pairs.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`](#p0-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Submodule.FG`.

<a id="p0-almost-nakayama"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-nakayama` — Almost Nakayama lemma for tight ideals

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ rad(A) a tight ideal. (i) If M is an almost finitely generated A-module with IM = M, then M = 0. (ii) If φ : N → M is a morphism of almost finite projective A-modules such that φ ⊗_A A/I is an isomorphism, then φ is an isomorphism. (iii) If M is almost finitely generated and M ⊗_A A/I = 0 then M = 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; I tight (Iⁿ ⊆ m₀A) and I ⊆ rad(A).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): pick a finitely generated Q with m₀M ⊆ Q ⊆ M; then M = IⁿM ⊆ m₀M ⊆ Q, so M = Q is finitely generated; for a finitely generated A_*-submodule M₀ with M₀^a = M one gets m₀M₀ ⊆ mI_*·m₀M₀, and mI_* ⊆ rad(A_*) (GR Lemma 5.1.2), so m₀M₀ = 0 by Nakayama, whence mM₀ = 0 and M = 0 (GR proof of Lemma 5.1.6).
2. (ii): Coker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 and Coker φ almost finitely generated (GR Lemma 2.3.17(i)) give Coker φ = 0; then Ker φ is almost finitely generated (Lemma 2.3.17(ii), M almost finitely presented) and Ker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 by flatness of M, so Ker φ = 0 (GR Corollary 5.1.7).
3. (iii) is (i) since M ⊗ A/I = M/IM.

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a (K perfectoid), I = ϖA: an almost finitely generated M with M = ϖM is zero; the hypothesis 'almost finitely generated' is needed, since K = K°[1/ϖ] satisfies K = ϖK.
- Used in P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi with I generated by a root of ϖ.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`](#p0-tight-ideal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-iff), `mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`.

<a id="p0-tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting` — Idempotents lift uniquely along tight henselian pairs

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup and (A, I) a tight henselian pair of almost algebras (e.g. A I-adically complete with I tight). Then A → A/I induces a bijection from the idempotents of A_* to the idempotents of (A/I)_*.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; (A, I) tight henselian.

**Proof outline.**

1. If m̃ has homological dimension ≤ 1: (A_*, I_*) is henselian (GR Corollary 5.1.16), so idempotents of A_* and A_*/I_* correspond; an idempotent almost element of A/I lifts to an almost element of A because the obstruction in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, I) dies in Ext¹(V^a, I) coming from Ext¹(V^a, Iⁿ) for n large (Claim 5.1.19, using Ext²(V^a, −) = 0 from Lemma 2.4.14), and liftings of idempotents along nilpotent thickenings are unique (GR Proposition 2.5.13(i)).
2. General m: write m as a filtered union of subideals m_λ with m_λ² = m_λ and m̃_λ flat of homological dimension ≤ 1 (GR Theorem 2.1.12), apply the first case to each (V, m_λ) and glue the unique lifts (GR proof of Proposition 5.1.17).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = (V⟦X⟧)^a and I = XA: idempotents of A_* and of (A/I)_* = (V^a)_* = V_*-idempotents agree.
- Used with the rank decomposition to lift the decomposition A/ϖ = ∏ Ā_i to A (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`](#p0-tight-ideal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`](#p0-almost-flatness-tor-criterion), `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:IsIdempotentElem`.

<a id="p0-adic-almost-projective-modules"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules` — Almost finite projective modules over I-adically complete almost algebras

*Theorem.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism, A_n := A/I^{n+1}. Then M ↦ (M ⊗_A A_n)_n is an equivalence from almost finite projective A-modules to compatible systems (M_n) of almost finite projective A_n-modules (M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n), with quasi-inverse (M_n) ↦ lim_n M_n; in particular P ≅ lim_n P ⊗_A A_n for every almost finite projective P. Moreover an I-c-adic A-module whose reduction M_0 is almost finitely generated is almost finitely generated with M ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete (GR's conditions (a), (b) of Lemma 5.3.5 for A_n = A/I^{n+1}).

**Proof outline.**

1. Topological modules over A∞ with I-c-adic topology correspond to compatible systems (GR Lemma 5.3.16).
2. Almost finite generation of lim M_n from M_0 almost finitely generated and I tight: find almost elements whose images generate modulo m₀ at level n+1, then I^{n+1}M ⊆ N and N is closed (GR Lemmas 5.3.17, 5.3.18).
3. Almost projectivity of lim M_n: a topologically almost split surjection from the completed free module and ε-factorisations (GR Lemma 5.3.20).
4. Full faithfulness: P → lim P ⊗ A_n is an isomorphism, first for P = A^r, then for P almost finite projective via ε-factorisations P → Aⁿ → P (GR Claim 5.3.25, P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a, I = ϖA: almost finite projective K°a-modules are the limits of compatible almost finite projective (K°/ϖ^n)^a-modules.
- P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras uses this for the underlying modules of finite étale algebras.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`](#p0-tight-ideal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`](#p0-almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`](#p0-almost-finitely-generated-and-presented), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`](#p0-almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).

<a id="p0-unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction` — Unramifiedness lifts from the reduction modulo a tight ideal

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A I-adically complete (A ≅ lim_n A/I^{n+1}). (i) For ideals I, J and φ : A → B: if φ ⊗ A/I and φ ⊗ A/J are unramified then so is φ ⊗ A/IJ. (ii) If B is an almost finite projective A-algebra such that B/IB is unramified over A/I, then B is unramified over A. (iii) More generally, for I ⊆ rad(A) tight and B almost finite over A with B/IB unramified over A/I, B is unramified over A.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete for (ii).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): reduce to IJ = 0; B is B ⊗_A B-flat by the Tor base change (Claim 5.2.13), and almost projective by the 2-cartesian square of almost projective modules over B ⊗ B/(I' ∩ J') (GR Proposition 3.4.21) and Lemma 3.2.25(i) (GR proof of Theorem 5.2.12(ii)).
2. (ii): by (i) with J = Iⁿ, each B_n := B/I^{n+1}B is unramified over A_n; the diagonal idempotents e_n (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation) are compatible by uniqueness and define an idempotent of lim (B_n ⊗ B_n)_* = (B ⊗_A B)_* (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, Claim 5.3.25); μ = lim μ_n and I_{B/A} = lim I_{B_n/A_n} give conditions (ii), (iii) of the characterisation (GR Claim 5.3.29).
3. (iii): Ω_{B/A} is almost finitely generated with Ω ⊗ A/I = 0, so Ω = 0 (P0/almost-nakayama); then I_{B/A} is idempotent and locally generated by idempotents after inverting generators of m₀ and modulo m₀ (GR Corollary 5.2.15 via Theorem 5.2.12(iv) and Theorem 5.2.4).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a and B = L°a (L/K finite étale), unramifiedness of L°a/K°a follows from that of (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

<a id="p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras` — Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely modulo a tight ideal of a complete almost algebra

*Theorem.* Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal such that A is I-adically complete (A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism). Then B ↦ B ⊗_A A/I is an equivalence of categories A_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet, with quasi-inverse B₀ ↦ lim_n B_n, where B_n is the unique finite étale A/I^{n+1}-algebra lifting B₀. In particular, for ϖ ∈ m and A ϖ-adically complete, A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet; this is Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over an arbitrary basic setup (Sch12 states it for S = (K°, K°°) and A flat over K°a). Complements: if A is flat over V^a then every B ∈ A_fet is flat over V^a and ϖ-adically complete (P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete); for root setups B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B/ϖB is over A/ϖ (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, needed for the cotangent complex behind the nilpotent lifting).
- I tight (e.g. I = ϖA with ϖ ∈ m) and A I-adically complete; flatness of A over V^a is not needed for the equivalence itself.
- Sch12 cites GR Theorem 5.3.27 (same number in the book and in arXiv v3).

**Proof outline.**

1. Finite levels: A_{n+1} → A_n has nilpotent kernel, so A_{n+1,fet} ≃ A_{n,fet} (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (iv)); hence 2-lim_n (A_n)_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet (GR proof of Theorem 5.3.27).
2. Passage to the limit: for a compatible system (B_n), B := lim B_n is almost finite projective over A with B ⊗ A_n ≅ B_n (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules), unramified (P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction (ii)), hence étale (almost projective ⇒ flat) and almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), i.e. B ∈ A_fet.
3. Full faithfulness: Hom_A(B, C) = lim_n Hom_{A_n}(B_n, C_n) because C ≅ lim C_n (Claim 5.3.25) and morphisms of finite étale algebras lift uniquely at each finite level.

**Acceptance.**

- S = (K°, K°°), A = K°a, ϖ ∈ K°°: K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet, the middle link in K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet (Sch12 §4).
- A finite étale (A/ϖ)-algebra has exactly one finite étale lift to A, up to unique isomorphism.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`](#p0-tight-ideal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras`](#p0-nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules`](#p0-adic-almost-projective-modules), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction`](#p0-unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-iff), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

<a id="p0-finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete` — Finite étale algebras over complete flat almost algebras are flat and complete

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is ϖ-adically complete (B ≅ lim_n B/ϖⁿB), and if A is flat over V^a then so is B.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; A ϖ-adically complete; for the flatness clause, A flat over V^a.

**Proof outline.**

1. B is almost finite projective over A (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), so B ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A A/ϖ^n (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, Claim 5.3.25) and B ⊗_A A/ϖⁿ = B/ϖⁿB.
2. B almost projective over A ⇒ flat over A; flatness is transitive along A → B (GR Lemma 2.4.7), so B is flat over V^a.

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a and B = L°a (L/K finite, K perfectoid): L°a is flat and ϖ-adically complete, as L° is.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules`](#p0-adic-almost-projective-modules), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-iff), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness).

<a id="p0-uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi` — Uniform finite projectivity of a finite étale algebra can be checked modulo ϖ (root setups)

*Lemma.* Let S be the root setup of (ϖ_n) (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup), ϖ = ϖ_0, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is uniformly almost finitely generated over A with bound r iff B/ϖB is uniformly almost finitely generated over A/ϖ with bound r; hence B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B ⊗_A A/ϖ is uniformly finite projective over A/ϖ. (Sch12 Theorem 4.17, last sentence, over (K°, K°°); in a general basic setup no source proves the reverse implication.)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a root setup (used to find, for each k, elements ϖ_{k+1} and t = ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} with ϖ = ϖ_{k+1}²·t); A ϖ-adically complete; B finite étale over A.

**Proof outline.**

1. ⇒: base change preserves uniform bounds (GR Lemma 2.3.7(v)).
2. ⇐: fix k ≥ 1 and δ := ϖ_{k+1}. Choose φ̄ : (A/ϖ)^r → B/ϖB with cokernel killed by δ, and lift δ·φ̄ to φ : A^r → B (almost elements lift up to multiplication by δ, P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); then δ²B ⊆ φ(A^r) + ϖB.
3. Let C := coker φ, an almost finitely generated A-module; δ²C ⊆ ϖC = t·δ²C with t := ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} ∈ m (p^{k+1} ≥ 3 for k ≥ 1), so M := δ²C satisfies M = tM.
4. tA is tight (t ∈ m) and contained in rad(A) because t^{p^{k+1}} ∈ ϖA and A is ϖ-adically complete; M is almost finitely generated, so M = 0 by P0/almost-nakayama; hence δ² = ϖ_{k+1}² kills coker φ, and so does ϖ_k (a multiple of ϖ_{k+1}²).
5. Every ε ∈ m is a multiple of some ϖ_k, so for every ε there is A^r → B with cokernel killed by ε: B is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound r (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion, condition (A)).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over (K°, K°°) with ϖ having compatible p-power roots; used by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for 'S°a is uniformly finite projective over R°a'.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`](#p0-root-ideal-basic-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-nakayama`](#p0-almost-nakayama), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`](#p0-tight-ideal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion`](#p0-almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.17, p. 21. The statement, whose proof Sch12 calls easy.
- [`gr-almost`](#source-p0-gr-almost), arXiv v3, §5.1, Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103. The Nakayama step of the proof.

<a id="p0-almost-completeness-via-almost-elements"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-completeness-via-almost-elements` — ϖ-adic completeness of an almost module and of its almost elements

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, and M an almost V-module whose almost elements M_* have no ϖ-torsion. Then: (i) (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿM_* for all n; (ii) M_*/ϖⁿM_* → (M/ϖⁿM)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel; (iii) M is ϖ-adically complete (M → lim_n M/ϖⁿM an isomorphism in Almost.Module S) iff M_* is ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) M_*`); the comparison lim M_*/ϖⁿ → lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* = (lim M/ϖⁿ)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel, the lim¹ of the almost zero cokernels being almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; M_* ϖ-torsion-free (for S = (K°, K°°) this is flatness of M, Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): ϖ is injective on M_* hence a monomorphism on M, so ϖⁿM ≅ M and (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿ M_*.
2. (ii): left exactness of (−)_* gives injectivity; the cokernel embeds in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M)[ϖⁿ], and Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M) is almost zero because V^a is almost projective (Bhatt proof of Lemma 4.4.1(3)).
3. (iii) ⇒: (−)_* commutes with limits, so M_* ≅ lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* ⊇ lim M_*/ϖⁿ with almost zero cokernel Q (lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero), and Q is killed by ϖ ∈ m; since M_* is ϖ-torsion-free, Bhatt Lemma 4.4.2 (for α injective between ϖ-torsion-free modules with ϖ-torsion cokernel, the source is complete iff the target is) shows M_* is complete.
4. (iii) ⇐: (−)^a preserves limits (it has a left adjoint (−)_! and a right adjoint), and M ≅ (M_*)^a.

**Acceptance.**

- For S = (K°, K°°) this is Sch12 Lemma 5.3(iii)-(iv); for Bhatt's setup (R, I) and a finitely generated J, Bhatt Proposition 4.4.3 proves the analogue without torsion-freeness using derived completeness.
- M = (K°/ϖ)^a is ϖ-adically complete but M_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ) has ϖ-torsion: the torsion-freeness hypothesis is not decorative for (i).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`](#p0-almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), arXiv v1, §5, Lemma 5.3(iv), p. 22. Statement (iii) over (K°, K°°).
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.4, Lemma 4.4.1(3), p. 30. Statements (i)-(ii).

<a id="p0-almost-exactness-passes-to-completion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion` — Complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ are almost exact, with the lim¹ term controlled

*Lemma.* Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m and C^• a cochain complex of V-modules (C^i = 0 for i < 0) such that every C^i is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete. If the cohomology of C^•/ϖC^• is almost zero in every degree, then: (i) H^i(C^•/ϖⁿC^•) is almost zero for all n ≥ 1 and all i; (ii) for every i there is an exact sequence 0 → lim¹_n H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) → H^i(C^•) → lim_n H^i(C^•/ϖⁿ) → 0 (Milnor sequence of the tower C^• = lim_n C^•/ϖⁿ, whose transition maps are termwise surjective), and both outer terms are almost zero, so H^i(C^•) is almost zero; (iii) C^•[1/ϖ] is exact. Neither the torsion-freeness nor the completeness can be dropped, and the lim¹ term is not discarded: it is almost zero because every H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) is.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; C^i ϖ-torsion-free (for exactness of 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} → C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0) and ϖ-adically complete (C^i = lim C^i/ϖⁿ).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): torsion-freeness makes 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} →·ϖ C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0 exact; the long exact cohomology sequence (Mathlib `ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`) and closure of almost zero modules under extensions (P0/almost-zero-serre-class) give induction on n.
2. (ii): completeness and surjectivity of transitions give the short exact sequence of complexes 0 → C^• → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → 0 (second map (x_n) ↦ (x_n − x̄_{n+1})); its long exact cohomology sequence, with H^i(∏_n −) = ∏_n H^i(−) for modules, is the Milnor sequence.
3. Products, lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), so H^i(C^•) is an extension of almost zero modules.
4. (iii): localisation at ϖ is exact and kills almost zero modules (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

**Acceptance.**

- Non-example for completeness: C^0 = V[1/ϖ] (torsion-free, not ϖ-adically separated), C^i = 0 otherwise: C/ϖ = 0 is exact, but H^0(C) = V[1/ϖ] is not almost zero.
- ECD Proposition 8.8: the complex 0 → R⁺ → S⁺ → O⁺(Y ×_X Y) → ⋯ for a v-cover of a totally disconnected X is almost exact because it is so modulo ϖ; Berkeley proof of Proposition 8.2.8 for affinoid pro-étale covers.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`](#p0-almost-zero-serre-class), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`](#p0-almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.homology`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Completion

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 8, proof of Proposition 8.2.8, p. 60. The same step in the Berkeley lectures.

<a id="p0-almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology` — Almost sheaves, almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech complexes on a site

*Construction.* Let (C, J) be a site and S = (V, m) a basic setup. For a sheaf F of V-modules on (C, J) (Mathlib `Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)`): F is almost zero if m·F(U) = 0 for all U; almost zero sheaves form a Serre class of the abelian category of sheaves, and the Serre localization Almost.Sheaf J S is the category of sheaves of almost V-modules (GR 3.3.1–3.3.2: a basic setup relative to the topos of (C, J)), with exact localization F ↦ F^a. For X ∈ C and n ≥ 0 the cohomology H^n(X, F) of the underlying abelian sheaf (Mathlib `Sheaf.H'`) is a V-module through the action of V on F, and its almostification H^n(X, F)^a ∈ Almost.Module S depends only on F^a (almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology); F is almost acyclic on X if H^n(X, F)^a = 0 for n > 0. For a family 𝔘 = (U_i → X) the Čech complex Č(𝔘, F) (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` on the underlying presheaf) is a complex of V-modules with almostification Č(𝔘, F)^a, and the augmented complex F(X) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact if its cohomology is almost zero. The Čech-to-derived comparison for almost acyclic bases is P0/almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (C, J) a site whose category of sheaves of V-modules is abelian with enough injectives (Mathlib `sheafIsAbelian`, `HasSheafify`); S a basic setup.

**Proof outline.**

1. Almost zero sheaves: m·F = 0 is closed under subsheaves, quotient sheaves (sheafification preserves m-torsion: m kills the presheaf quotient, hence its sheafification) and extensions (m² = m), so it is a Serre class.
2. V-action on cohomology: each v ∈ V acts on F by an endomorphism of sheaves, hence on H^n(X, F) by functoriality (`Sheaf.H.map`), making H^n(X, F) a V-module; if m·F = 0 then ε acts by zero on H^n.
3. Almost Čech complex: apply cechComplexFunctor to the presheaf of V-modules and then toAlmost S termwise.
4. Relative basic setup: Almost.Sheaf J S is equivalent to sheaves on (C, J) with values in almost modules computed through (−)_* (GR 3.3.2: M_* is a sheaf).

**API.**

- `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostZero` (data): For F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat V): ∀ U, S.IsAlmostZero (F.val.obj U).
- `Almost.Sheaf.almostZero_isSerreClass` (instance): The almost zero sheaves form a Serre class of Sheaf J (ModuleCat V).
- `Almost.Sheaf` (data): Almost.Sheaf J S: the Serre localization of Sheaf J (ModuleCat V) at almost isomorphisms of sheaves.
- `Almost.Sheaf.toAlmost` (constructor): The exact localization functor F ↦ F^a.
- `Almost.Sheaf.cohomologyModule` (structure): The V-module structure on H^n(X, F) (Sheaf.H') from the V-action on F.
- `Almost.Sheaf.almostH` (constructor): H^n(X, F)^a := (toAlmost S).obj (H^n(X, F) as V-module).
- `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostAcyclic` (data): ∀ n > 0, IsZero (almostH F n X).
- `Almost.Sheaf.almostCech` (constructor): The almost Čech complex (toAlmost S).mapHomologicalComplex (cechComplexFunctor 𝔘 applied to F).
- `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_eq_zero_of_isAlmostZero` (relation): Almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology in all degrees; almostH factors through toAlmost.
- `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_localization` (compatibility): For ϖ ∈ S.ideal: almostH F n X ≅ 0 ⇒ H^n(X, F) ⊗ V[1/ϖ] = 0 (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

**Unit tests.**

- `Almost.Sheaf.test_point` (degenerate): For the site with one object and only the trivial covering, Almost.Sheaf J S ≌ Almost.Module S and almostH F n X = 0 for n > 0.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_constant_residue` (computation): For S = ofValuationRing K° and the constant sheaf k = K°/K°° on any site, F is almost zero, so almostH F n X ≅ 0 for all n, even when H^n(X, k) ≠ 0.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_not_acyclic` (non-example): On the site of open subsets of the circle S¹, the constant sheaf k has H¹(S¹, k) = k ≠ 0 but is almost acyclic: IsAlmostAcyclic must not be defined as vanishing of H^n.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V, almostH F n X is Mathlib's Sheaf.H' of the underlying abelian sheaf with its V-module structure, via Almost.Module.classicalEquiv.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity (ECD Theorem 3.24, Sch12 Proposition 6.14, Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4): H^i(X, O⁺_X) almost zero for i > 0 from almost exact Čech complexes of rational covers
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity (ECD Theorem 6.3): H^i(X_ét, O⁺_X) almost zero
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves, D2/higher-v-acyclicity (ECD Propositions 8.5, 8.8): almost vanishing of pro-étale and v-cohomology of O⁺, via Čech complexes of affinoid covers
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison: the ordinary Čech-to-derived spectral sequence and acyclic-basis comparison, applied after almostification
- PerfectoidSpaces:P9/almost-cohomology-of-tower: H^q(U_proet, O⁺/p^m) almost isomorphic to continuous group cohomology

**Acceptance.**

- On the one-point site, Almost.Sheaf J S ≃ Almost.Module S and almost cohomology vanishes in positive degrees.

<a id="p0-almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion` — Almost Čech acyclicity on a basis implies almost acyclicity

*Lemma.* Let (C, J) be a site, S a basic setup, F a sheaf of V-modules, and 𝔅 a full subcategory of C stable under fibre products such that every covering of an object of 𝔅 is refined by a covering by objects of 𝔅 (e.g. rational subsets of an affinoid adic space with finite rational covers, or affinoid perfectoid objects of a pro-étale or v-site). If for every U ∈ 𝔅 and every covering 𝔘 of U by objects of 𝔅 the augmented Čech complex F(U) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact, then H^n(U, F) is almost zero for all U ∈ 𝔅 and n > 0 (and H^0(U, F) = F(U)).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S a basic setup; 𝔅 as stated; F a sheaf of V-modules.

**Proof outline.**

1. Almostify DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison: the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence Ȟ^p(𝔘, H^q(F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, F) is a spectral sequence of V-modules; the exact functor toAlmost S carries it to a spectral sequence in Almost.Module S.
2. Induction on n (Cartan's argument, ECD proof of Proposition 8.8): suppose H^q(V, F)^a = 0 for 0 < q < n and all V ∈ 𝔅; for α ∈ H^n(U, F) and ε ∈ m choose a covering 𝔘 by objects of 𝔅 on which α dies (locality of cohomology); the spectral sequence and the almost exactness of the Čech complexes of 𝔘 and of its fibre products show ε·α = 0.

**Acceptance.**

- Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4 and Sch12 Proposition 6.14: almost exact Čech complexes of O⁺ for finite rational covers of a perfectoid affinoid give H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for i > 0.
- In the classical setup this is Cartan's lemma on acyclic bases (D0).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology`](#p0-almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`](#p0-almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`](#p0-almost-zero-serre-class), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Sheaf

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, proof of Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53. Almost Čech exactness as the route to almost acyclicity.

<a id="p1"></a>

## P1. Perfectoid Tate rings, tilts and marked untilts

Work over arbitrary perfectoid Tate rings, in both characteristics and without a base field. Define the topological tilt and sharp map, identify the primitive kernel of Fontaine’s θ, construct marked untilts and the tilting equivalence, and compare with Mathlib’s algebraic PreTilt and the integral-perfectoid theory. The general-base mod-pseudouniformizer almost-category comparison remains partial; its root-annihilator criterion is not asserted to be equivalent to almost flatness without the recorded gap.

**Coverage (`partial`; packet P0).** All targets of the narrowed stage are realised in the generality of ECD Definition 3.1 (no perfectoid base field, both characteristics): the definition and its Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the ϖ^p | p condition kept; the characteristic-p characterisation; the perfectoid-field characterisation including Kedlaya's answer to ECD Remark 3.7; the topological tilt with limiting addition, sharp map (not additive), functoriality, completeness, uniformity and integral subrings; Fontaine's θ (surjectivity from Mathlib, kernel generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor); the classification of marked untilts by primitive ideals with the converse construction, its topology and plus ring; the general-base tilting equivalence with unit and counit; the instantiated almost setup; comparisons with Mathlib PreTilt, PreTilt.untilt, Tilt, PreTilt.val and fontaineTheta; BMS integral perfectoid comparison; compatibility with anchor Layer 6. The field-to-general-Tate proof gaps are closed through Kedlaya–Liu II §3.3 and Kedlaya AWS §§2.6–2.7. Unread inputs are requests (DD.0 cotangent complex, TB.0 Berkovich spectra) or P0 nodes. Of the consumer requests, perfected Tate algebras over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring (in any number of variables) and ℚ_p^cycl are realised here; the completed cyclotomic extension of a finite K/ℚ_p follows from the finite-extension theorem and is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension. The inputs P2–P4 need from the tilting theory (the tilt of a uniform ring, strict inclusions, the metric criterion, sharp approximation, completed filtered colimits) are nodes of this layer. The inputs that P2–P5 need beyond the tilting theory — the tilt of a complete uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1), the metric perfectoid criterion (Lemma 2.8.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2), Euclidean division and sharp approximation (Lemmas 2.6.7, 2.6.9), strict inclusions under tilting (Theorem 2.4.2), completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings and their tilts (Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2), and perfected Tate algebras in any set of variables (Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12) — are nodes of this stage.

**Remaining coverage obligations.**

- Prove the root-annihilator/almost-flatness and field-base comparison in the general mod-ϖ category (review gap).

**Planets.** Perfectoid Tate ring; Tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring; Perfectoid field; Fontaine's map θ; Untilts and primitive ideals; Tilting equivalence.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras` — Perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1), perfectoid algebras and perfectoid Tate pairs

*Definition.* Fix a prime p. Let R be a commutative topological ring which is a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing), complete and Hausdorff, with power-bounded subring R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring). For a commutative ring A and ideals I, J ⊆ A with p ∈ J and x^p ∈ J for every x ∈ I, write Φ: A/I → A/J for the ring homomorphism x mod I ↦ x^p mod J (ECD §3 notational convention). R is a perfectoid Tate ring if (a) R is uniform, i.e. R° is a bounded subset of R (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded), and (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ of R (a topologically nilpotent unit, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer; necessarily ϖ ∈ R°) such that ϖ^p divides p in R° and Φ: R°/ϖR° → R°/ϖ^pR° is bijective. No perfectoid base field is fixed; characteristic 0 and characteristic p are both allowed (for pR = 0 the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous), and p may be a nonzero nonunit (e.g. in a product K × K♭). A perfectoid R-algebra is a perfectoid Tate ring S with a continuous ring homomorphism R → S; morphisms are continuous R-algebra homomorphisms. A perfectoid Tate pair is a Huber pair (R, R+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair) with R perfectoid; the condition depends only on R (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Completeness includes separatedness (anchor convention): CompleteSpace R and T2Space R, with the uniform structure of the topological additive group.
- Uniformity is boundedness of R° in R (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the uniformity of anchor Layer 4.2); it is not implied by (b) (test IsPerfectoidTateRing.not_of_not_uniform).
- The divisibility ϖ^p | p holds in R°, not merely in R; together with (b) it cannot be replaced by surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p alone (ℚ_p, ECD Remark 3.3).

**Proof outline.**

1. Φ is well defined and additive: for i ∈ I, (x + i)^p − x^p ∈ (p, i^p) ⊆ J, and (x + y)^p − x^p − y^p ∈ pA ⊆ J by divisibility of the binomial coefficients.
2. A pseudo-uniformizer ϖ lies in R°, and in every ring of integral elements R+ (ECD §3 preamble; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).
3. The listed equivalent formulations (Berkeley 6.1.1, Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.1, Kedlaya AWS 2.1.1, BMS1 "Fontaine's sense") agree by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer and P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.frobeniusQuot` (data): For a commutative ring A, ideals I, J with (p : A) ∈ J and ∀ x ∈ I, x^p ∈ J: the ring homomorphism A ⧸ I →+* A ⧸ J, [x] ↦ [x^p].
- `Perfectoid.frobeniusQuot_mk` (simp): frobeniusQuot I J hp hIJ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk J (x ^ p).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing` (structure): Prop-valued class on a commutative topological ring R with [UniformSpace R] [IsUniformAddGroup R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [NonarchimedeanRing R] [IsTateRing R] [CompleteSpace R] [T2Space R], with the two fields below.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` (projection): IsBounded (powerBoundedSubring R : Set R).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.exists_pseudoUniformizer` (projection): ∃ ϖ ∈ R°, IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ ∧ ϖ ^ p ∣ p in R° ∧ Function.Bijective (frobeniusQuot (span {ϖ}) (span {ϖ ^ p}) _ _).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_surjective` (constructor): A complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, ϖ^p | p in R°, for which Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective, is perfectoid (injectivity is automatic, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.frobenius_bijective` (characterisation): If R is perfectoid, Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP` (characterisation): A complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff it has a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isReduced` (other): A perfectoid Tate ring is reduced (P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_perfectRing` (characterisation): If CharP R p: R is perfectoid iff PerfectRing R p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_ringEquiv` (functoriality): The class transports along a ring isomorphism that is a homeomorphism (via tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.map_powerBoundedSubring).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod` (instance): R × S is perfectoid when R and S are: (R × S)° = R° × S° and (ϖ_R, ϖ_S) is a pseudo-uniformizer with the required properties.
- `Perfectoid.map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (other): For a Tate ring A, a uniform Tate ring S and a continuous ring homomorphism f: A → S, f(A°) ⊆ S°: for x ∈ A° and ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of A, f(ϖ)f(x)^N is topologically nilpotent for all N, so {f(x)^N} ⊆ f(ϖ)^{-1}S°, which is bounded.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.frobenius_surjective_plus` (other): For every ring of integral elements R+, Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isUniform` (compatibility): Condition (a) is the uniformity predicate of anchor Layer 4.2 (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3); the two propositions are equal.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidPair` (structure): For a Huber pair P = (R, R+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair), the proposition IsPerfectoidTateRing R; perfectoid pairs with Huber-pair morphisms form the category of the untilt classification.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_padic` (non-example): ¬ IsPerfectoidTateRing ℚ_[p]: a pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p has |ϖ| = p^{-k} with k ≥ 1, so |ϖ^p| < |p| and ϖ^p ∤ p in ℤ_p, although Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.not_of_not_uniform` (non-example): R = ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) (product topology on ℂ_p ⊕ ℂ_pε) is a complete Tate ring with ϖ = p^{1/p}, ϖ^p = p, and Frobenius surjective on R°/p = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}/p (as ℂ_pε ⊆ R° and ℂ_pε = p·ℂ_pε), but R° ⊇ ℂ_pε is unbounded, so R is not perfectoid; a definition omitting uniformity would accept it.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_zero` (degenerate): The zero ring is a perfectoid Tate ring (0 is a topologically nilpotent unit and all quotients vanish).
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_padicComplex` (computation): For ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p) with ϖ = p^{1/p}: ϖ^p = p and Φ: 𝒪/ϖ → 𝒪/p is bijective because every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_iff_perfect_laurent` (characterisation): For the t-adic completion R of the perfection of F_p((t)): IsPerfectoidTateRing R ↔ PerfectRing R p, and both hold; for F_p((t)) itself (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing) both fail.

**Uses.**

- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring: a perfectoid frame (R̃, ι, σ) takes R̃ perfectoid in exactly this sense, with no base field and characteristic p allowed
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-uniform: uses that R̃° is bounded (isBounded_powerBoundedSubring) and that R̃ is reduced
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc: proves S⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid by non-surjectivity of Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/split-tate-ring-is-perfectoid, A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion: build perfectoid rings from ϖ with ϖ^p | p and surjective Φ, injectivity being automatic (of_surjective)
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product: C^0(G^k, Â∞) is perfectoid: products and continuous maps with a common ϖ
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field, A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: in characteristic p a perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid (iff_perfectRing)
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond, D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond: Perf is built on perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p; perfectoidness of a completed tower is checked via ϖ^p | p and surjective Frobenius on the integral quotient

<a id="p1-integral-elements-adically-complete"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete` — Rings of integral elements of a complete uniform Tate ring are ϖ-adically and p-adically complete

*Lemma.* Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements; R+ = R° allowed) and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then (a) the subspace topology of R+ is the ϖ-adic topology and R+ is ϖ-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {ϖ}) R+); (b) ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R+ and R = R+[1/ϖ]; (c) if ϖ divides p in R+, then R+ is p-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+); (d) if R ≠ 0 and p is topologically nilpotent in R, then p is not a unit of R+. In particular, for R ≠ 0 perfectoid, R+ satisfies the hypotheses [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+)] and [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+] of Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R complete and Hausdorff; uniformity is used to know that R+ ⊆ R° is bounded.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) R+ is open, hence closed, hence complete; it is bounded, so by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero (for any pair of definition (A_0, I)) the open sets ϖ^nR+ are cofinal among the neighbourhoods ϖ^nA_0 of 0; completeness plus Hausdorffness give IsAdicComplete.
2. (b) ϖ is a unit of R; for x ∈ R, ϖ^nx → 0, so ϖ^nx ∈ R+ for n large because R+ is open.
3. (c) (p) ⊆ (ϖ) are finitely generated ideals of R+, so ϖ-adic completeness implies p-adic completeness (Stacks Tag 090T; the same step in BMS1 §3.1).
4. (d) If p were a unit of R+, then p^{-n} ∈ R+ (bounded) and p^n → 0 would give 1 = p^{-n}p^n → 0, so 1 lies in the closure of 0 and R = 0.

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K° (or an open valuation subring K+) this is the ϖ-adic and p-adic completeness of K+ used in Sch12 Lemma 3.4.
- For R = ℚ_p and R+ = ℤ_p with ϖ = p: ℤ_p is p-adically complete (the lemma needs no perfectoid hypothesis).

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:IsTopologicallyNilpotent`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

<a id="p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion` — Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the pseudo-uniformizer condition kept

*Lemma.* Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ R° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in R°. The following are equivalent: (i) Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective (every element of R°/ϖ^p is a p-th power); (ii) Frobenius on R°/p is surjective; (iii) every element of R°/ϖpR° is a p-th power. The same equivalences hold for any ring of integral elements R+ in place of R° when ϖ ∈ R+ and ϖ^p | p in R+. The divisibility hypothesis is essential: surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p without any ϖ with ϖ^p | p does not give perfectoidness (ℚ_p), and surjectivity of the Frobenius endomorphism of R°/ϖ is weaker than (i) (ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p}, Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- ϖ^p | p in R° is a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
- R° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).

**Proof outline.**

1. (iii) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (i): ϖpR° ⊆ pR° ⊆ ϖ^pR°, so surjectivity passes to coarser quotients.
2. (i) ⇒ (iii): by successive ϖ^p-adic approximation using (i), every x ∈ R° is a convergent sum x = x_0^p + ϖ^px_1^p + ϖ^{2p}x_2^p + ⋯ with x_i ∈ R° (R° is ϖ-adically complete); then x ≡ (x_0 + ϖx_1 + ϖ²x_2 + ⋯)^p modulo pϖR°, since every mixed term of the p-th power is divisible by p and by ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.9 (iii) ⇒ (i)).
3. For R+ the same argument applies to the ϖ-adically complete ring R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).

**Acceptance.**

- ℚ_p: Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is surjective, but no pseudo-uniformizer ϖ has ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p, so the criterion does not apply and ℚ_p is not perfectoid.
- ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p} (ϖ^p = p): Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/ϖ = F_p is surjective, but Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/p = F_p[ϖ]/(ϖ^p) is not (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer` — Injectivity of Frobenius is automatic and the perfectoid condition is independent of the pseudo-uniformizer

*Lemma.* Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. (a) For every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R°, Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is injective. (b) If R is moreover uniform, then for pseudo-uniformizers ϖ, ϖ' with ϖ^p | p and ϖ'^p | p in R°, Φ is bijective for ϖ iff it is bijective for ϖ'; equivalently R is perfectoid iff there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius on R°/p is surjective, and then Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective for every such ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; Berkeley Remark 6.1.3). (c) The same holds for a ring of integral elements R+ in place of R°: if ϖ ∈ R+, ϖ^p | p in R+ and x ∈ R+ with x^p ∈ ϖ^pR+, then x ∈ ϖR+.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (a) and (c) use only that R° (resp. R+) is integrally closed in R and ϖ is a unit of R; (b) uses uniformity and completeness through P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) If x ∈ R° and x^p = ϖ^py with y ∈ R°, then (x/ϖ)^p = y, so x/ϖ ∈ R is integral over R° and lies in R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral), i.e. x ∈ ϖR° (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof).
2. (c) Same argument with the integrally closed R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
3. (b) By (a), bijectivity of Φ for ϖ is its surjectivity, which by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion is equivalent to surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p, a condition independent of ϖ.

**Acceptance.**

- In ℚ_p^cycl, ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1 and ϖ' = ζ_{p³} − 1 both satisfy ϖ^p | p, and Φ is bijective for both.
- In ℂ_p the conditions for ϖ = p^{1/p} and ϖ' = p^{1/p²} coincide.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced` — Uniform (in particular perfectoid) Tate rings are reduced

*Lemma.* A Hausdorff uniform Tate ring R is reduced; in particular every perfectoid Tate ring is reduced (Sch12 Proposition 5.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6 proof).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Uniformity is essential: ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is a complete Tate ring that is not reduced.

**Proof outline.**

1. If x ∈ R is nilpotent, then λx is nilpotent, hence power-bounded, for every λ ∈ R; for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ this gives ϖ^{-n}x ∈ R° for all n, i.e. x ∈ ⋂_n ϖ^nR°.
2. R° is ϖ-adically separated (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), so x = 0.

**Acceptance.**

- ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is not reduced, hence not uniform, hence not perfectoid, although ϖ = p^{1/p} satisfies ϖ^p | p and Frobenius on its power-bounded subring modulo p is surjective.
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-uniform deduces that sousperfectoid rings are reduced from this lemma applied to a perfectoid frame.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `mathlib:IsReduced`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), Sch12 Proposition 5.8, proof, pp. 23–24. The argument: a nonzero nilpotent x gives Kx ⊆ R°, contradicting boundedness.
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 6.1.6, proof, p. 43. Uniformity implies reducedness.

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P1`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p1-perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform` — A perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p is uniform (open mapping theorem)

*Lemma.* Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pR = 0 which is perfect (PerfectRing R p: Frobenius R → R bijective). Then R° is bounded, i.e. R is uniform.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R complete, Hausdorff and Tate; no uniformity is assumed.

**Proof outline.**

1. Φ: R → R is a continuous bijective ring homomorphism. Make the target an R-module through Φ (a·y := a^py); then Φ is R-linear, surjective and continuous, both sides are complete, first countable (a Huber ring has a countable neighbourhood basis of 0) and nonarchimedean, the target is Hausdorff and scalar multiplication on it is continuous, so Φ is open by the open mapping theorem over a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap; ECD Proposition 3.5 proof; Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.0.3 phrases the same step with two norms).
2. Choose a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R_0 for a ring of definition R_0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero). Openness gives n ≥ 1 with ϖ^nR_0 ⊆ Φ(R_0); since Φ(ϖ^jR_0) = ϖ^{pj}Φ(R_0), this yields Φ^{-1}(ϖ^mR_0) ⊆ ϖ^{⌊(m−n)/p⌋}R_0 for every integer m.
3. If y is topologically nilpotent then y^{p^k} ∈ R_0 for some k; applying Φ^{-1} k times and the previous inclusion gives y ∈ ϖ^{-c}R_0 with c = ⌈(n + p)/(p − 1)⌉, independent of y (if m ≥ −c then ⌊(m − n)/p⌋ ≥ −c). For x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so R° ⊆ ϖ^{-c-1}R_0 is bounded. (This integral-exponent estimate replaces the chain Φ^{-k}(R_0) ⊆ ϖ^{-n/p-⋯-n/p^k}R_0 ⊆ ϖ^{-n}R_0 of ECD and Berkeley, whose last inclusion needs ϖ^{q}R_0 ⊆ R_0 for fractional q; see sourceIssues.)

**Acceptance.**

- The t-adic completion of the perfection of F_p((t)) is uniform with R° the completion of F_p[[t]]^{perf} (ECD Example 3.4(ii)).
- A non-uniform complete Tate ring of characteristic p, such as F_p((t))[ε]/(ε²), is not perfect (ε is nilpotent, and Frobenius is not injective), consistently with the lemma.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CharP

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD Proposition 3.5, proof, p. 15. The open-mapping argument for uniformity.
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 6.1.6, proof, p. 43. The same argument with a ring of definition R_00 on which Φ is an isomorphism.
- [`KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings`](#source-p0-kedlayaliu-relativeii-imperfectperiodrings), Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 3.0.3, p. 54. The open-mapping argument recorded with the precise normed setup.

<a id="p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect` — In characteristic p, perfectoid Tate rings are exactly the perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5)

*Theorem.* Let R be a topological ring with pR = 0. Then R is a perfectoid Tate ring iff R is a perfect complete Hausdorff Tate ring. For such R, R° and every ring of integral elements R+ are perfect, Φ: R° → R° is an automorphism, and every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ satisfies the condition of ECD Definition 3.1 (ϖ^p | p = 0 is vacuous).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- pR = 0; completeness includes Hausdorffness.

**Proof outline.**

1. (⇐) R is uniform (P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform). x is power-bounded iff x^p is, so Φ restricts to an automorphism of R°; hence Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective, and it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a).
2. (⇒) If Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism, so is R°/ϖ^n → R°/ϖ^{np} for all n by induction; passing to the limit with R° ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete) gives Φ: R° ≅ R°, and inverting ϖ shows R is perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5 proof).
3. R+ is perfect: if x^p ∈ R+ then x is integral over R+, so x ∈ R+ (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.2).

**Acceptance.**

- The completed perfection of F_p((t)) is a perfectoid field; F_p((t)) is a complete Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing) that is not perfect, hence not perfectoid.
- A nonarchimedean field of characteristic p is a perfectoid field iff it is perfect (Sch12 §3; Bhatt Example 3.1.2(3)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`](#p1-perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform`](#p1-perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`, `mathlib:CharP`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

<a id="p1-inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius` — lim_{x↦x^p} R+ ≅ lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 ≅ lim_Φ R+/p (ECD Lemma 3.10, first part)

*Lemma.* Let R be a nonzero complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ a ring of integral elements and ϖ_0 ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer dividing p in R+. Then projection (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (x^{(n)} mod ϖ_0)_n is a multiplicative bijection lim_{x↦x^p} R+ → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0R+, and a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (R+ with its topology, R+/ϖ_0 discrete); the inverse sends (x̄_0, x̄_1, …) to (x^{(i)})_i with x^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞} x_{n+i}^{p^n} for arbitrary lifts x_j ∈ R+ of x̄_j. The same holds for p in place of ϖ_0, and the ring homomorphism lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 induced by the quotient map is an isomorphism. In Mathlib terms: Perfection.quotientMulEquiv p (span {ϖ_0}) : Perfection R+ p ≃* Perfection (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p, and Perfection (ModP R+ p) p is PreTilt R+ p.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R ≠ 0, so ϖ_0 and p are not units of R+ and R+/ϖ_0 has characteristic p (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (d)).

**Proof outline.**

1. R+ is ϖ_0-adically and p-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a), (c)), and CharP (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p holds; Mathlib's Perfection.quotientMulEquiv applies to I = ϖ_0R+ and to I = pR+. Its inverse is built from Perfection.teichmuller, i.e. the limit x^{(i)} = lim_n x_{n+i}^{p^n}, which converges because x ≡ y mod ϖ_0^n implies x^p ≡ y^p mod ϖ_0^{n+1} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof; Perfection.teichmuller_spec).
2. Continuity of the inverse: x^{(i)} mod ϖ_0^{n+1} depends only on x̄_{i+n} (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
3. The map lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 is a ring homomorphism compatible with the two multiplicative bijections from lim R+, hence bijective (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i)).

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K°, this is Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i).
- For R of characteristic p (so R+ perfect), projection to the zeroth factor identifies lim_{x↦x^p} R+ with R+.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:Perfection`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:Perfection.teichmuller`, `mathlib:Perfection.teichmuller_spec`, `mathlib:PreTilt`, `mathlib:ModP`, `mathlib:Perfection.map`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018`](#source-p0-bms-integralpadichodge-2018), BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19. The canonical maps lim_{x↦x^p} S → lim_Φ S/pS → lim_Φ S/πS are isomorphisms of monoids/rings.

<a id="p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots` — Pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge

*Definition.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. A pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots is an element ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_{n≥0} of the multiplicative monoid lim_{x↦x^p} R (Mathlib Perfection R p) such that ϖ := ϖ^{1/p^0} is a pseudo-uniformizer of R lying in R° with ϖ^p | p in R°. Then every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer in R°, ϖ^q := (ϖ^{1/p^n})^m is well defined for q = m/p^n ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0} (and for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] as a unit of R), and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of the tilt R♭ with (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Attached to ϖ♭ is the spectral gauge |x|_ϖ := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°}: a power-multiplicative, submultiplicative, ultrametric norm defining the topology of R, with |ϖ^qx|_ϖ = 2^{-q}|x|_ϖ, R° = {x : |x|_ϖ ≤ 1} and R°° = {x : |x|_ϖ < 1}. Existence is P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid; the normalisation |ϖ|_ϖ = 1/2 is a convention, and changing ϖ changes |·|_ϖ by a power.

**Proof outline.**

1. ϖ^{1/p^n} is a unit because its p^n-th power is, topologically nilpotent because its p^n-th power is, and power-bounded because R° is integrally closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).
2. Gauge: |x|_ϖ is finite since R = R°[1/ϖ]; submultiplicative and ultrametric since R° is a ring; power-multiplicativity |x^n|_ϖ = |x|_ϖ^n: if x^n ∈ ϖ^{q'}R° and q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with nq ≤ q' then (x/ϖ^q)^n ∈ R°, so x/ϖ^q ∈ R° by integral closedness, and ℤ[1/p] is dense in ℚ.
3. Topology: the balls {|x|_ϖ ≤ 2^{-q}} = ϖ^qR° form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); R°° = ⋃_q ϖ^qR° is P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots` (structure): Structure on a perfectoid Tate ring R with a field roots : Perfection R p and proofs that coeff 0 roots ∈ R°, IsPseudoUniformizer (coeff 0 roots) and (coeff 0 roots)^p ∣ p in R°.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.root` (data): root n := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n ϖ♭ = ϖ^{1/p^n}.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.root_pow` (simp): (root (n + 1)) ^ p = root n; root 0 = ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.isPseudoUniformizer_root` (characterisation): Each root n is a pseudo-uniformizer lying in R°.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.zpow` (data): ϖ^q for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] as a unit of R, with zpow_add and zpow_natCast; ϖ^q ∈ R° for q ≥ 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.exists` (constructor): Every perfectoid Tate ring admits one, starting from any ϖ_1 with ϖ_1^p | p (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.toTilt` (projection): ϖ♭ regarded as an element of the ring tilt R; a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭ with sharp ϖ♭ = ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge` (data): |x|_ϖ = inf {2^{-q} | q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q} x ∈ R°} ∈ ℝ≥0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_mul_le` (structure): |xy|_ϖ ≤ |x|_ϖ |y|_ϖ and |x + y|_ϖ ≤ max |x|_ϖ |y|_ϖ; |x|_ϖ = 0 iff x = 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_pow` (characterisation): |x^n|_ϖ = |x|_ϖ^n (power-multiplicativity).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_zpow_mul` (simp): |ϖ^q x|_ϖ = 2^{-q} |x|_ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_gauge_le_one` (characterisation): x ∈ R° ↔ |x|_ϖ ≤ 1, and IsTopologicallyNilpotent x ↔ |x|_ϖ < 1.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.hasBasis_nhds_zero` (other): The sets ϖ^q R°, q ∈ ℤ[1/p], form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (the gauge defines the topology).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_padicComplex` (computation): For ℂ_p and ϖ♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n: gauge x = 2^{-v_p(x)} for x ≠ 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.isEmpty_padic` (non-example): IsEmpty (PseudoUniformizerRoots ℚ_[p]): a pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p has valuation k ≥ 1, which is not divisible by every p^n, so it has no compatible system of p-power roots; and none satisfies ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.subsingleton_of_charP` (degenerate): If CharP R p then for a fixed pseudo-uniformizer ϖ the compatible system of roots is unique (R is perfect), so PseudoUniformizerRoots over ϖ is a subsingleton.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.iUnion_zpow_eq` (characterisation): ⋃_{q > 0} ϖ^q R° = R°° (the topologically nilpotent elements), P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal.

**Uses.**

<a id="p1-exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots` — Every perfectoid Tate ring has a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (ECD Lemma 3.10)

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ_1 a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ_1^p | p in R°. There is ϖ♭ ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R° with ϖ := ϖ♭^{(0)} ≡ ϖ_1 mod ϖ_1^pR°; then ϖ = ϖ_1·u with u ∈ (R°)^×, ϖR° = ϖ_1R°, ϖ^p | p in R°, and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). If pR = 0 every pseudo-uniformizer has unique compatible roots.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid; the zero ring is allowed (then everything is 0).

**Proof outline.**

1. Put ϖ_0 := ϖ_1^p, which divides p. Frobenius on R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i)), so the zeroth projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 → R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective); by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius choose ϖ♭ ∈ lim R° whose image in R°/ϖ_0 is ϖ_1 (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof).
2. Then ϖ = ϖ_1 + ϖ_1^py = ϖ_1(1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y) with y ∈ R°, and 1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y is a unit of the ϖ_1-adically complete ring R° (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).
3. All components ϖ^{1/p^n} are units and topologically nilpotent because their p^n-th power ϖ is.

**Acceptance.**

- For R = ℂ_p and ϖ_1 = p^{1/p}, the construction returns a unit multiple of p^{1/p} with compatible roots.
- For R of characteristic p, ϖ = ϖ_1 and ϖ^{1/p^n} = Φ^{-n}(ϖ_1).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`](#p1-inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16. Any preimage of ϖ_1 has the right properties.
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44. The same construction from a preimage of ϖ_0 modulo ϖ_0^p.
- [`BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018`](#source-p0-bms-integralpadichodge-2018), BMS1 Lemma 3.9, p. 22. Integral version: a unit multiple of π admits a system of p-power roots.

<a id="p1-frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring` — Every ring of integral elements of a perfectoid Tate ring satisfies the Frobenius condition

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and R+ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then (a) Frobenius on R+/p is surjective, and every element of R+/ϖpR+ is a p-th power for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+; (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+ and p/ϖ^p ∈ R°° (topologically nilpotent), and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+, Φ: R+/ϖ → R+/ϖ^p is bijective; (c) consequently (R, R+) satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 with R+ in place of R°, which is the formulation of Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.1.1 and Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.3.1, and these definitions agree with ECD's: the perfectoid condition on a Huber pair (R, R+) depends on R alone.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid; R+ open and integrally closed, so R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).

**Proof outline.**

1. (b) existence: take ϖ_0 with compatible p-power roots and ϖ_0^p | p in R° (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), write p = ϖ_0^pu with u ∈ R°, and set ϖ := ϖ_0^{1 − 1/p²}; then p = ϖ^p·ϖ_0^{1/p}u with ϖ_0^{1/p}u ∈ R°° ⊆ R+.
2. (a) (BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof) For x ∈ R+ write x = y^p + pϖz with y, z ∈ R° (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (iii) for R°); ϖz ∈ R°° ⊆ R+, so y^p = x − pϖz ∈ R+ and y ∈ R+ by integral closedness; hence x ≡ y^p mod pR+. Surjectivity modulo ϖpR+ then follows from P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion applied to R+.
3. (b) bijectivity: surjectivity from (a) since pR+ ⊆ ϖ^pR+; injectivity from P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (c).
4. (c) is (b) together with P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion; conversely a Huber pair satisfying the R+-condition has R perfectoid by BMS1 Lemma 3.20 (P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison) or Kedlaya–Liu II Proposition 3.3.3.

**Acceptance.**

- For K a perfectoid field and K+ ⊆ K° an open valuation subring of rank 2, Frobenius on K+/p is surjective.
- Mathlib's surjective_fontaineTheta applies to R+ with hypothesis Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R+ p) p) supplied by (a) (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`](#p1-perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018`](#source-p0-bms-integralpadichodge-2018), BMS1 Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 27. The passage from R° to R+ written out in the proof.
- [`Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017`](#source-p0-kedlaya-awsnotes-2017), Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.12, p. 55. Frobenius on A+/(p) is surjective for every perfectoid pair.
