<a id="p1-metric-perfectoid-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion` — Metric criterion: a uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff every element is a p-th power up to a fixed factor c < 1 (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c))

*Lemma.* Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ B° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in B° admitting a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ B° ((ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}, ϖ^{1/p^0} = ϖ). Let |x| := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B°} be the spectral gauge of ϖ (the formula of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, here on a ring not assumed perfectoid). Then (a) |·| is an ultrametric, submultiplicative, power-multiplicative norm defining the topology of B, with |ϖ^q x| = 2^{-q}|x| and B° = {x : |x| ≤ 1}; (b) B is a perfectoid Tate ring if and only if there is c ∈ (0, 1) such that for every x ∈ B there is y ∈ B with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|; (c) if B is perfectoid, every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) = (|ϖ|^p, 1) has this property, and y can be taken in B° when x ∈ B°. Kedlaya states the criterion for a uniform analytic Huber pair (A, A⁺) with an ideal of definition I, p ∈ I^p, and the norm attached to I; this node is its Tate-ring form with the gauge of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, which every perfectoid Tate ring has (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots) and which every Tate ring receiving a continuous map from a perfectoid Tate ring has (the image of such a ϖ). Power-multiplicativity of the norm is used: the criterion is a statement about the spectral gauge.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- B complete, Hausdorff and uniform (B° bounded); ϖ^p | p in B° and the roots ϖ^{1/p^n} lie in B.
- No perfectoid base field; B may have characteristic 0, p, or neither (then |p| may be 0 on some factors).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Ultrametricity and submultiplicativity are inherited from B° being an additive subgroup and a subring. Power-multiplicativity: if ϖ^{-nq}x^n ∈ B° then (ϖ^{-q}x)^n ∈ B°, so ϖ^{-q}x is integral over B° and lies in B° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral); rounding exponents in ℤ[1/p] gives |x^n| = |x|^n. If |x| ≤ 1 then ϖ^{1/p^k}x ∈ B° for all k, hence x^n ∈ ϖ^{-1}B° for all n, a bounded set by uniformity, so x ∈ B°. |x| = 0 forces x ∈ ⋂_q ϖ^qB° = 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); the sets ϖ^qB° are a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero).
2. (c), hence ⇒ of (b): if B is perfectoid, Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion). Given c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) and x ≠ 0, choose q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with u := ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B° and 2^{-q} ≤ 2^p c|x|, choose w ∈ B° with u − w^p ∈ ϖ^pB° and put y := ϖ^{q/p}w; then |x − y^p| = 2^{-q}|u − w^p| ≤ 2^{-q-p} ≤ c|x| (Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c), second paragraph).
3. ⇐ of (b): given c and u ∈ B°, put u_0 := u and choose inductively y_k with |u_k − y_k^p| ≤ c|u_k|, u_{k+1} := u_k − y_k^p. Then |y_k^p| ≤ |u_k| ≤ c^k, so y_k ∈ B° by (a). For c^k ≤ 2^{-p}, u − (y_0 + ⋯ + y_{k−1})^p = u_k − (mixed binomial terms), and the mixed terms lie in pB° ⊆ ϖ^pB°; as {|x| ≤ 2^{-p}} = ϖ^pB° by (a), u is a p-th power modulo ϖ^pB°. So Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective, it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a), and B is perfectoid by P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras.
4. Kedlaya AWS proves ⇐ through Lemma 2.8.2, whose hypothesis is that the pair is already perfectoid (recorded in sourceIssues); the successive approximation above replaces it.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: perfectoidness of a uniform ring receiving an isometric dense-image map from a perfectoid ring (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4)
- Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.8.3–2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c), Theorem 3.6.17(b): the metric form of the perfectoid condition in the sources

**Acceptance.**

- B = ℂ_p with ϖ = p^{1/p} (so |p| = 2^{-p}): every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) works, matching "any c ∈ (p^{-1}, 1)" of Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c) for the normalisation |p| = p^{-1}.
- Non-example: for a perfectoid field K, B = K⟨T⟩ (Gauss norm, uniform, ϖ ∈ K with roots) fails the criterion at x = T: the reduction of y^p in (K°/K°°)[T] is a p-th power, so |T − y^p| ≥ 1 = |T| for every y; B is not perfectoid.
- P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: the criterion passes along isometric continuous maps with dense image, since |x − x′| < |x| implies |x′| = |x|.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`](#p1-perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/MetricCriterion

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017`](#source-p0-kedlaya-awsnotes-2017), Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.3, p. 70. The setting of the criterion in the source (Huber pairs, norm from I).
- [`Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017`](#source-p0-kedlaya-awsnotes-2017), Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.3, p. 70. The criterion (b).

<a id="p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring` — The tilt R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.9, Lemma 3.10)

*Construction.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Its tilt is R♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} R, the multiplicative monoid Perfection R p of compatible sequences (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} with (x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}, with the inverse-limit topology (induced from ∏_ℕ R), pointwise multiplication and addition (x + y)^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. The limit exists and R♭ is a topological ring of characteristic p which is perfect (ECD Lemma 3.10; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1). Concretely, for ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ_0 | p, the submonoid lim_{x↦x^p} R° is identified with the ring lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭] as monoids, and the ring structure of R♭ is that of this localisation; it is given by the limit formula and does not depend on ϖ_0 or ϖ♭. For a Huber pair (R, R+) with R perfectoid, the tilt pair is (R♭, R♭+) with R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting). If pR = 0 then x ↦ x^{(0)} is an isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid; the construction of the ring structure uses ϖ_0 | p and completeness of R°.
- Additivity of the zeroth projection is not asserted (P1/sharp-map).

**Proof outline.**

1. Ring structure on lim R°: transport along the multiplicative bijection with lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); the resulting sum has i-th component lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} because at level i + n both reduce to x̄_{i+n} + ȳ_{i+n} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec characterises the limit), and this formula shows independence of ϖ_0.
2. R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭]: for x ∈ lim R, ϖ^Nx^{(0)} ∈ R° for some N; then (ϖ^{N/p^n}x^{(n)})^{p^n} ∈ R° and, R° being integrally closed, ϖ♭^N x ∈ lim R° (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof, "R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] as multiplicative monoids, and in fact as rings").
3. Characteristic p and perfectness: p·1 = 0 in lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 since ϖ_0 | p; Frobenius is (x^{(n)}) ↦ ((x^{(n)})^p), with inverse the shift (x^{(n)}) ↦ (x^{(n+1)}).
4. Topology: the inverse-limit topology on lim R° equals that of lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 with discrete factors (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); it is a ring topology (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)).
5. Characteristic p: R is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), so projection to the zeroth factor is bijective, and the limit formula is constant, hence the projection is additive.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt` (data): tilt R := Perfection R p (type synonym) carrying the ring structure above; notation R♭.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.instCommRing` (instance): CommRing (tilt R), with the monoid structure of Perfection R p; together with instTopologicalSpace (induced from ℕ → R) and instIsTopologicalRing.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.charP` (instance): CharP (tilt R) p and PerfectRing (tilt R) p.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff` (projection): coeff n : tilt R →* R, the n-th coordinate (Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n); coeff_pow: coeff (n + 1) x ^ p = coeff n x.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.ext` (extensionality): x = y ↔ ∀ n, coeff n x = coeff n y.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_add` (characterisation): Tendsto (fun m ↦ (coeff (i + m) x + coeff (i + m) y) ^ p ^ m) atTop (𝓝 (coeff i (x + y))).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_mul` (simp): coeff n (x * y) = coeff n x * coeff n y; coeff n 1 = 1; coeff n 0 = 0.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_frobeniusEquiv_symm` (simp): coeff n ((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm x) = coeff (n + 1) x.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): tilt R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (characterisation): x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ ∀ n, coeff n x ∈ R° ↔ coeff 0 x ∈ R° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.equivOfCharP` (equivalence): If CharP R p: tilt R ≃+* R, x ↦ coeff 0 x, a homeomorphism.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp` (data): The sharp map tilt R →* R (P1/sharp-map).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map` (functoriality): Tilt of a continuous ring homomorphism (P1/tilt-functoriality).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.integralEquivPreTilt` (compatibility): (tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt).
- `Perfectoid.Pair.tilt` (constructor): For a Huber pair P = (R, R+) with R perfectoid: the Huber pair (tilt R, lim_{x↦x^p} R+) (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt.equivOfCharP_laurent` (compatibility): For R the t-adic completion of the perfection of F_p((t)), tilt R ≃+* R via coeff 0, a homeomorphism.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_epsilon` (computation): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl, ε := (ζ_{p^n})_n with ζ_{p^{n+1}}^p = ζ_{p^n}, ζ_1 = 1 satisfies coeff n ε = ζ_{p^n} and ε ≠ 1.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_zero_sub_ne` (non-example): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl, coeff 0 (ε − 1) ≠ coeff 0 ε − coeff 0 1 = 0: coordinatewise subtraction is not the ring structure.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.nontrivial_iff` (degenerate): Nontrivial (tilt R) ↔ Nontrivial R; tilt of the zero ring is zero.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_charP` (characterisation): tilt R is a perfectoid Tate ring and CharP (tilt R) p, for every perfectoid R.

**Uses.**

<a id="p1-tilt-integral-subrings"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings` — R♭° = lim R° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ, R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (ECD Lemma 3.10)

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. Then (a) R♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} R° = {x ∈ R♭ : x^{(n)} ∈ R° for all n} = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°}, and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ_0 of R dividing p in R° projection is a topological ring isomorphism R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (discrete factors) ≅ lim_Φ R°/p; (b) ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭, R♭° is an open and bounded subring whose subspace topology is the ϖ♭-adic one, and R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭]; (c) for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with 0 < q ≤ p, x ↦ x^{(0)} mod ϖ^qR° induces a ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭^qR♭° ≅ R°/ϖ^qR°, in particular R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ; (d) the kernel of R♭° → R°/ϖ^q is ϖ♭^qR♭°.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- ϖ^p | p in R°, so ϖ^q | p for q ≤ p.

**Proof outline.**

1. (c),(d) Kernel: if x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^qR°, then (x^{(n)}/ϖ^{q/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° gives x^{(n)} ∈ ϖ^{q/p^n}R° by integral closedness, i.e. x/ϖ♭^q ∈ lim R°. Surjectivity: Frobenius on R°/ϖ^q is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q → R°/ϖ^q is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective). Ring homomorphism: it is the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius).
2. (b) By (d), ker(pr_n: lim_Φ R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ) = ϖ♭^{p^n}R♭°, so the inverse-limit topology on lim R° is ϖ♭-adic; ϖ♭ is a unit (each coordinate is a unit of R) and topologically nilpotent; lim R° = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°} (integral closedness) is the preimage of the open R° under the continuous zeroth projection, hence open; it is bounded because (ϖ♭^My)^{(i)} = ϖ^{M/p^i}y^{(i)}; and x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NR° for i ≤ n iff x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^{Np^n}R°, so the two topologies agree; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring.
3. (a) lim R° is a bounded open subring, so it consists of power-bounded elements; conversely if x ∈ R♭ is power-bounded, {x^m} ⊆ ϖ♭^{-c}lim R°, so {(x^{(0)})^m} ⊆ ϖ^{-c}R° and x^{(0)} ∈ R°, and x^{(n)} ∈ R° since (x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x^{(0)} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof: lim R° "agrees with the powerbounded elements R♭°").

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K: K♭° = lim K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ and K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(iii)).
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: R♭°/ϖ♭ = (K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}] (Sch12 Proposition 5.20 proof).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`](#p1-inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD Lemma 3.10, p. 16. R♭° = lim R° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ is part of Lemma 3.10.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD after Lemma 3.10, p. 16. The projection defines a ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ.

<a id="p1-tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring` — The tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p

*Lemma.* For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the tilt R♭ is a complete Hausdorff uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Lemma 3.10, "a perfectoid F_p-algebra"); ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer, (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition, and R♭ ≠ 0 iff R ≠ 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid.

**Proof outline.**

1. Huber and Tate: (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)), and ϖ♭ is a topologically nilpotent unit.
2. Complete Hausdorff: R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 is an inverse limit of discrete rings; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] with R♭° open.
3. Uniform: R♭° is bounded (it is a ring of definition).
4. Perfect of characteristic p (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect.
5. 1 ≠ 0 in R♭ iff 1 ≠ 0 in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ iff R ≠ 0 (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)).

**Acceptance.**

- (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = ε − 1 (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- The tilt of a perfectoid ring of characteristic p is itself (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, equivOfCharP).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44. R♭ is a perfect complete Tate ring.

<a id="p1-sharp-map"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map` — The sharp map ♯: R♭ → R (continuous, multiplicative, not additive)

*Construction.* For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the sharp map ♯: R♭ → R, x ↦ x♯ := x^{(0)} (Mathlib Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0 on the underlying monoid Perfection R p) is continuous and multiplicative with 0♯ = 0, and is not additive in general. It satisfies (x^{1/p^n})♯ = x^{(n)}; x ∈ R♭° iff x♯ ∈ R°; x♯ = 0 iff x = 0; for x, y ∈ R♭°, (x + y)♯ ≡ x♯ + y♯ mod pR°; every element of R° is congruent modulo pR° to some y♯ with y ∈ R♭°; reduction of ♯ modulo ϖ is the ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ of P1/tilt-integral-subrings; and (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ. If pR = 0, ♯ is the ring isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid.

**Proof outline.**

1. Multiplicativity and continuity: ♯ is a coordinate projection of the inverse limit (ECD after Lemma 3.10; Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
2. Additivity modulo p: the reduction R♭° → R°/p, x ↦ x♯ mod p, is the zeroth projection of the ring lim_Φ R°/p (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius, P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a)).
3. Surjectivity modulo p: Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/p is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective).
4. x♯ = 0 ⇒ x = 0: x^{(n)} is nilpotent ((x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x♯) hence 0 as R is reduced (P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp` (data): sharp : tilt R →* R := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0; notation x♯.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp₀` (data): The same map as a MonoidWithZeroHom (sharp 0 = 0).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.continuous_sharp` (structure): Continuous (sharp : tilt R → R).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow` (simp): sharp (((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm)^[n] x) ^ p ^ n = sharp x (mirrors Mathlib PreTilt.untilt_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_sharp` (characterisation): x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ sharp x ∈ R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_zero_iff` (characterisation): sharp x = 0 ↔ x = 0.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_add_sub_mem` (relation): For x, y ∈ (tilt R)°: sharp (x + y) − sharp x − sharp y ∈ p • R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.exists_sharp_sub_mem` (other): ∀ x ∈ R°, ∃ y ∈ (tilt R)°, x − sharp y ∈ p • R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharpQuotEquiv` (equivalence): The ring isomorphism (tilt R)° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* R° ⧸ (ϖ) induced by sharp (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_toTilt` (simp): sharp ϖ♭.toTilt = ϖ for a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.gauge_sharp` (compatibility): |sharp x|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭} (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_untilt` (compatibility): Under (tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p, sharp corresponds to Mathlib PreTilt.untilt (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_sub_ne` (non-example): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl: sharp (ε − 1) ≠ sharp ε − sharp 1 = 0 (a ring homomorphism sharp would fail this).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_epsilon` (computation): sharp ε = 1 in tilt ℚ_p^cycl, and sharp p♭ = p in tilt ℂ_p for p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_ringEquiv_of_charP` (degenerate): If CharP R p, sharp is additive and is the ring isomorphism tilt.equivOfCharP.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_zero_iff_test` (characterisation): For R = ℂ_p × ℂ_p♭ (a perfectoid Tate ring), sharp x = 0 only for x = 0.

**Uses.**

- ECD after Lemma 3.10: "continuous, multiplicative (but not additive)" map, and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel: θ([x]) = x♯ and θ(Σ[r_n]p^n) = Σ r_n♯p^n
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field: |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: approximation of functions by sharps of tilted functions (Sch12 Lemma 6.5, Corollary 6.7)

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: f(ϖ) is a pseudo-uniformizer after composing with θ

**Acceptance.**

- In (ℚ_p^cycl)♭: ε♯ = 1 while (ε − 1)♯ ≠ 0, so ♯ is not additive.
- In (ℂ_p)♭: p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) has (p♭)♯ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements).

<a id="p1-spectral-norm-under-sharp"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp` — The spectral gauge is preserved by the sharp map: |x♯|_R = |x|_{R♭}

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, and |·|_ϖ, |·|_{ϖ♭} the spectral gauges of R and R♭ (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, the second for R♭ with its pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ and roots ϖ♭^{1/p^n}), both normalised by |ϖ| = |ϖ♭| = 1/2. Then |x♯|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭} for all x ∈ R♭ (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, "easy to check", over a perfectoid field; it is the norm Kedlaya–Liu put on the tilt by pullback along ♯).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- None beyond the setting.

**Proof outline.**

1. For q ∈ ℤ[1/p]: x ∈ ϖ♭^qR♭° iff ϖ♭^{-q}x ∈ R♭° iff (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯ ∈ R° (P1/sharp-map: membership in R♭° is detected by ♯, and ♯ is multiplicative with (ϖ♭^q)♯ = ϖ^q), so the two infima run over the same set of q.

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and ε = (ζ_{p^n})_n: |(ε − 1)♯| = lim |ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)}, which is |ε − 1| in K♭ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings).

- [`KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings`](#source-p0-kedlayaliu-relativeii-imperfectperiodrings), Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 3.3.8, proof, p. 60. The norm on the tilt is the pullback of the spectral norm along the sharp map.

<a id="p1-tilt-functoriality"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality` — Functoriality of tilting: f ↦ f♭

*Construction.* A continuous ring homomorphism f: R → S between perfectoid Tate rings induces f♭: R♭ → S♭, (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (f(x^{(n)}))_n (Mathlib Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f on the underlying monoids), a continuous ring homomorphism with (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), f♭(R♭°) ⊆ S♭°, id♭ = id and (g ∘ f)♭ = g♭ ∘ f♭; on R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ it induces the reduction of f. A morphism of Huber pairs (R, R+) → (S, S+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom) with R, S perfectoid induces a morphism of the tilt pairs. Hence tilting is a functor from perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) to perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) of characteristic p, and a perfectoid R-algebra S gives a perfectoid R♭-algebra S♭.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- f continuous; no condition on plus rings for the ring-level statement.

**Proof outline.**

1. Multiplicativity is clear. Additivity: f is continuous and a ring homomorphism, so it commutes with the limit formula of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring. Continuity: coordinatewise.
2. f(R°) ⊆ S° for any continuous homomorphism from a Tate ring to a uniform Tate ring (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so f♭ maps lim R° into lim S° = S♭° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); similarly lim R+ into lim S+ when f(R+) ⊆ S+.
3. Functor laws hold coordinatewise; compatibility with ♯ is the zeroth coordinate.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt.map` (data): map f : tilt R →+* tilt S for f : R →+* S continuous, with underlying monoid hom Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_map` (simp): coeff n (map f x) = f (coeff n x).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_map` (simp): sharp (map f x) = f (sharp x).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_id` (functoriality): map (RingHom.id R) = RingHom.id (tilt R).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_comp` (functoriality): map (g.comp f) = (map g).comp (map f).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.continuous_map` (structure): Continuous (map f).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (other): x ∈ (tilt R)° → map f x ∈ (tilt S)°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mapQuot_comm` (compatibility): The square (tilt R)°/(ϖ♭) ≅ R°/(ϖ) → S°/(f ϖ) ≅ (tilt S)°/(map f ϖ♭) commutes.
- `Perfectoid.Pair.tiltHom` (functoriality): Pair.Hom P Q ↦ Pair.Hom P.tilt Q.tilt, compatible with id and comp.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mapEquiv` (equivalence): A ring isomorphism R ≃+* S that is a homeomorphism induces tilt R ≃+* tilt S.
- `Perfectoid.tiltFunctor` (functoriality): The functor from the category of perfectoid Tate rings (continuous ring homomorphisms) to perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p, and its slice version from perfectoid R-algebras to perfectoid R♭-algebras.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_id_test` (degenerate): tilt.map (RingHom.id ℂ_p) = RingHom.id.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_inclusion_epsilon` (computation): For the continuous inclusion ι : ℚ_p^cycl → ℂ_p, tilt.map ι ε = ε.

<a id="p1-tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring` — The tilt B♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} B of a complete uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1)

*Construction.* Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (B is not assumed perfectoid) and B⁺ ⊆ B° a ring of integral elements. Its tilt is B♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} B (Mathlib `Perfection B p`) with the inverse-limit topology, pointwise multiplication, x♯ := x^{(0)}, and addition (x + y)^{(i)} := lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. Then: (a) the limit exists and makes B♭ a perfect topological ring of characteristic p; ♯ is continuous and multiplicative; B♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} is an open subring and B♭° := lim_{x↦x^p} B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°}; B♭ is complete and Hausdorff; (b) for every ideal of definition I ⊆ B⁺ with p ∈ I (for instance I = (p, ϖ) for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ B⁺; Kedlaya asks p ∈ I^p), reduction x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod I)_n is an isomorphism of topological rings B♭⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I (discrete factors), and B♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt B⁺ p; (c) if B has a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in B° and compatible p-power roots, i.e. ϖ = ϖ♭♯ for some ϖ♭ ∈ B♭, then ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of B♭, B♭° is open and bounded with the ϖ♭-adic topology, B♭ = B♭°[1/ϖ♭], the spectral gauges satisfy |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ, and B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; this applies whenever there is a continuous ring homomorphism f: A → B from a perfectoid Tate ring A, with ϖ♭ := f♭(ϖ_A♭); the closure in B♭ of a perfect subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is then a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p; (d) a continuous ring homomorphism g: B → C of such rings induces g♭: B♭ → C♭, (x^{(n)}) ↦ (g(x^{(n)})), a continuous ring homomorphism with (g♭x)♯ = g(x♯), functorially; (e) there is a unique ring homomorphism θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ with θ_B([x]) = x♯ (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` for the p-adically complete ring B⁺), natural in B: θ_C ∘ W(g♭) = g ∘ θ_B; it is not surjective in general; (f) if B is perfectoid, B♭ with ♯, g♭ and θ_B is the tilt of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring with the sharp map, functoriality and θ of P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- B complete, Hausdorff, uniform, p topologically nilpotent in B; no perfectoid condition.
- In (c) B♭ is Tate only because ϖ has compatible p-power roots in B; without them B♭ need not be Tate (test uniformTilt_padic).

**Proof outline.**

1. (b), and the ring structure: B⁺ is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), hence I-adically complete for I = (p, ϖ) because p^N ∈ ϖB⁺ for large N; Mathlib `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` (hypotheses IsAdicComplete I B⁺ and CharP (B⁺/I) p) gives the multiplicative bijection lim B⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I, a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (the argument of P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with I in place of ϖ_0). Transport the ring structure of the perfect F_p-algebra lim_Φ B⁺/I; its sum has i-th coordinate lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} (Mathlib `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`), which does not depend on I. For I = (p) this is Mathlib `PreTilt B⁺ p` (B⁺ is p-adically complete, Stacks Tag 090T).
2. (a): Kedlaya's identity [x + y] = lim_m ([x^{p^{-m}}] + [y^{p^{-m}}])^{p^m} in W(F_p[x^{p^{-∞}}, y^{p^{-∞}}]) (Kedlaya AWS (2.7.1.2)), specialised to the coordinates of x, y ∈ B♭, gives existence of the limit, associativity and continuity of the addition on all of B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1(a)–(b) and proof); on B♭⁺ it is the ring structure of (b). B♭⁺ is the preimage of the open B⁺ under the continuous ♯, hence open; it is complete by (b), so B♭ is complete and Hausdorff. lim B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} and lim B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°} because B⁺ and B° are integrally closed in B (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
3. (c): (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯, so {x : x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NB° for i ≤ n} = ϖ♭^{Np^n}B♭°: the topology of B♭° is ϖ♭-adic, ϖ♭ is a unit (coordinatewise) and topologically nilpotent, and |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ (same set of exponents q, as in P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp). Hence B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. For f: A → B, f(ϖ_A) = (f♭ϖ_A♭)♯ has compatible roots and f(ϖ_A)^p | p in B° (continuous homomorphisms into a uniform Tate ring preserve power-bounded elements, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A closed subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is complete and Tate, and the closure of a perfect subring is perfect because x ↦ x^{1/p} (the shift of coordinates) is continuous.
4. (d): g commutes with the limit formula and with the coordinates (Mathlib `Perfection.mapMonoidHom`); continuity is coordinatewise.
5. (e): B⁺ is p-adically complete, so θ_B exists and is unique as the Witt-vector lift of x ↦ x♯ mod p (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` on PreTilt B⁺ p, via (b)); naturality follows from uniqueness. For B = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) (p odd) the image of θ_B is ℤ_p ≠ ℤ_p[p^{1/p}].
6. (f): for perfectoid B the construction and the formulas are those of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (θ is determined by θ([x]) = x♯).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt` (data): uniformTilt B : Type := Perfection B p with CommRing (limiting addition), TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, CharP p, PerfectRing, CompleteSpace and T2Space instances, for B complete Hausdorff uniform Tate with IsTopologicallyNilpotent (p : B).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.sharp` (projection): sharp : uniformTilt B →* B := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom B p 0, continuous; sharp (x^{1/p^n})^{p^n} = sharp x.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.coeff_add` (characterisation): coeff i (x + y) = lim_{n→∞} (coeff (i + n) x + coeff (i + n) y)^{p^n} (Filter.Tendsto form).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.plusEquiv` (equivalence): For an ideal of definition I of B⁺ with p ∈ I: lim B⁺ ≃+* Perfection (B⁺ ⧸ I) p, a homeomorphism for discrete factors (from Perfection.quotientMulEquiv); and lim B⁺ ≃+* PreTilt B⁺ p.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (characterisation): x ∈ (uniformTilt B)° ↔ sharp x ∈ B°; likewise x ∈ lim B⁺ ↔ sharp x ∈ B⁺.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.map` (functoriality): map g : uniformTilt B →+* uniformTilt C for g : B →+* C continuous; continuous; sharp (map g x) = g (sharp x); map_id, map_comp.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isTateRing_of_sharp` (instance): If ϖ♭ : uniformTilt B has sharp ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer of B with (sharp ϖ♭)^p ∣ p in B°, then IsTateRing (uniformTilt B), IsBounded (uniformTilt B)°, IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B), and gauge ϖ♭ x = gauge (sharp ϖ♭) (sharp x).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_closure` (other): Under isTateRing_of_sharp, the closure of the range of a ring homomorphism from a perfect ring whose range contains ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is a closed subring that is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.theta` (compatibility): theta B : 𝕎 (lim B⁺) →+* B⁺ with theta [x] = sharp x, equal to WittVector.fontaineTheta B⁺ p under plusEquiv; theta C ∘ WittVector.map (map g) = g ∘ theta B.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.equivTilt` (compatibility): For B perfectoid, uniformTilt B ≃+* tilt B (the identity of Perfection B p), a homeomorphism commuting with sharp and map (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_equiv_tilt` (compatibility): For B perfectoid, uniformTilt B and tilt B are the same ring structure on Perfection B p: the identity is a topological ring isomorphism commuting with sharp, with map and with θ.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_padic` (non-example): uniformTilt ℚ_p ≃+* 𝔽_p (Teichmüller representatives {0} ∪ μ_{p−1}, p odd) with the discrete topology: it is not a Tate ring, and ℚ_p has no pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p, so (c) does not apply; a construction asserting that the tilt of every uniform Tate ring is Tate fails here.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_charP` (degenerate): If B is a perfect uniform Tate ring of characteristic p, sharp : uniformTilt B ≃+* B is a topological ring isomorphism; uniformTilt of the zero ring is zero.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_hom` (characterisation): For f: A → B continuous with A perfectoid and B uniform, IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B), CharP (uniformTilt B) p, and map f ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer with sharp (map f ϖ♭) = f ϖ.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: the tilt B♭ of the uniform target B, the closure of f♭(A♭) in it, and θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ for the map from the untilt B₀ to B (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(ii))
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting (b): the gauge |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ on the tilt of a uniform target
- Kedlaya AWS §2.7 (Lemmas 2.7.1, 2.7.7, 2.7.8): calculations with the tilt of a pair before it is known to be perfectoid or analytic
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (a): tilts of uniform quotients of perfectoid rings (through the dense-image criterion)

**Acceptance.**

- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4: for f: A → B continuous with A perfectoid and B uniform, B♭ is a uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p receiving f♭: A♭ → B♭, and the closure of f♭(A♭) is a perfectoid Tate ring (the first two steps of P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion).
- For B = ℚ_p, B♭ ≅ 𝔽_p with the discrete topology: an element with compatible p-power roots has valuation 0, and the only units of ℤ_p with p^n-th roots for all n are the Teichmüller representatives (p odd).

<a id="p1-tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt` — The integral tilt R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p, and ♯ is PreTilt.untilt

*Comparison.* Let R be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements (e.g. R°). Then R+ satisfies Mathlib's standing hypotheses Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+) and IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), and: (a) the subring R♭+ = lim_{x↦x^p} R+ of R♭ is isomorphic as a topological ring to Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p = Perfection (ModP R+ p) p via x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod p)_n, with inverse built from Perfection.teichmuller / Perfection.quotientMulEquiv; (b) under this isomorphism x ↦ x♯ on R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt : PreTilt R+ p →* R+, and PreTilt.coeff 0 is ♯ mod p (PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero); (c) R♭ ≅ (PreTilt R+ p)[1/ϖ♭] (Localization.Away). Mathlib's PreTilt is thus the integral tilt of this layer; Mathlib has no ring structure on lim_{x↦x^p} R and no tilt of a non-field Tate ring, which this layer supplies (the field case, Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val, is compared in P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R ≠ 0 (otherwise p is a unit of R+ = 0 and Mathlib's hypothesis fails).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Both rings are lim_Φ R+/p: PreTilt R+ p by definition, R♭+ by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with ϖ_0 replaced by p, and both ring structures are the inverse-limit ones (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a) for R+ = R°, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting in general).
2. (b) PreTilt.untilt is defined as teichmuller p (span {p}), the zeroth coordinate of the inverse of the reduction map (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv), i.e. x ↦ x♯.
3. (c) R♭ = R♭+[1/ϖ♭] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b), since ϖ♭R♭° ⊆ R♭+).

**Acceptance.**

- For R = ℂ_p, PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ (ℂ_p)♭° and PreTilt.untilt p♭ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements realises 𝒪_{C}♭ through PreTilt).
- WittVector p (PreTilt R+ p) is Mathlib's A_inf(R+), the source of WittVector.fontaineTheta (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`](#p1-inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:PreTilt`, `mathlib:PreTilt.untilt`, `mathlib:PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero`, `mathlib:PreTilt.coeff`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:ModP`, `mathlib:Localization.Away`.

<a id="p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting` — Rings of integral elements correspond under tilting: R+ ↦ R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11)

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. (a) R+ ↦ R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ = {x ∈ R♭ : x♯ ∈ R+} is an inclusion-preserving bijection from rings of integral elements of R to those of R♭; the inverse sends R♭+ to the preimage in R° of the image of R♭+ in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (b) R♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ R+/ϖ compatibly with R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (c) On both sides, rings of integral elements correspond to integrally closed subrings of the common quotient R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ (equivalently of R°/R°° ≅ R♭°/R♭°°). Hence a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R+) has tilt pair (R♭, R♭+), and R° ↦ R♭°.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid; rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained in R°.

**Proof outline.**

1. An open integrally closed R+ ⊆ R° contains R°° ⊇ ϖR° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn), so R+ is the preimage of R+/ϖR° ⊆ R°/ϖR°; R+ is integrally closed in R iff R+/ϖR° is integrally closed in R°/ϖR° (lift, resp. reduce, a monic equation; ϖR° ⊆ R+), and R+ is open iff it contains ϖR° (ECD before Lemma 3.11).
2. The same holds for R♭, and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)) transports integrally closed subrings; x ∈ R♭+ iff x♯ mod ϖ ∈ R+/ϖ iff x♯ ∈ R+, and then x^{(n)} = (x^{1/p^n})♯ ∈ R+ by integral closedness, so R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.5).

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K and an open valuation subring K+ ⊆ K°, K♭+ is the open valuation subring of K♭ with the same image in the common residue field K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (Sch12 Proposition 3.6 proof).
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and R+ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = R°, R♭+ = K♭°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosedIn`.

<a id="p1-topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal` — R°° = ⋃ ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is an idempotent flat ideal

*Lemma.* Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n a pseudo-uniformizer of R with compatible p-power roots (for R perfectoid, P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). Then the ideal R°° of topologically nilpotent elements of R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal) equals ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ⋃_{q∈ℤ[1/p]_{>0}} ϖ^qR°; it satisfies (R°°)² = R°° and is flat as an R°-module (a filtered union of the free rank-one modules ϖ^{1/p^n}R°). For every ring of integral elements R+, R°° ⊆ R+ and R°° = ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R+. Hence (R°, R°°) and (R+, R°°) satisfy the hypotheses of P0/root-ideal-basic-setup.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Uniformity is used through P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0).

**Proof outline.**

1. ⊇: ϖ^{1/p^n} is topologically nilpotent and R° is power-bounded, so ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R°° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul).
2. ⊆: for x ∈ R°°, x^N ∈ ϖR° for N large because ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); for p^n ≥ N, x^{p^n} ∈ ϖR°, so (x/ϖ^{1/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° and x/ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R° by integral closedness (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).
3. Idempotence: ϖ^{1/p^n} = (ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p ∈ (R°°)². Flatness: ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ≅ R° since ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R°, and a filtered colimit of flat modules is flat.
4. R+: R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}·ϖ^{1/p^n − 1/p^{n+1}}R° ⊆ ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R+.

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K, K°° = m_K with m_K² = m_K (Bhatt notes Lemma 3.1.3(2)).
- For ℚ_p, ℤ_p°° = pℤ_p and (pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p: without p-power roots the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements is not idempotent.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`](#p0-root-ideal-basic-setup).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Almost

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD Definition 3.21, p. 19. Almost zero can be tested on the roots ϖ^{1/p^n} of a fixed ϖ.
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Bhatt notes, Lemma 3.1.3(2), p. 10. (K°°)² = K°° and K°° is flat, over a perfectoid field.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), ECD §3 preamble, p. 14. Topologically nilpotent elements lie in every open integrally closed R+.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-almost-setup"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup` — The almost setup (R°, R°°) of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD 3.21–3.23)

*Construction.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. The pair (R°, R°°) is a basic setup for almost mathematics (P0/almost-basic-setup: R°° idempotent and R°° ⊗_{R°} R°° ≅ R°° flat), and so is (R+, R°°) for every ring of integral elements R+. For an R+-module M the following are equivalent: (i) M is almost zero, R°°M = 0; (ii) ϖ'M = 0 for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ' of R; (iii) ϖ^{1/p^n}M = 0 for all n, for one (equivalently any) pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with compatible p-power roots (ECD Definition 3.21; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.9.4). The almost-zero modules form the Serre class of P0/almost-zero-serre-class, the almost categories R°a-Mod and R+a-Mod are the Serre quotients of P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (ECD Definition 3.23), and restriction of scalars along R+ → R°, which is injective with almost zero cokernel (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), induces an equivalence R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod. The construction depends only on R. For a perfectoid field K it is the classical setup (K°, m_K), with K°/m_K almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(i)).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid (compatible roots exist, P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).

**Proof outline.**

1. Basic setup: R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is idempotent and flat (P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal), so P0/root-ideal-basic-setup applies to R° and to R+.
2. (i) ⇔ (ii) ⇔ (iii): every pseudo-uniformizer lies in R°°, every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer, and R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R°.
3. R°/R+ is almost zero: for x ∈ R° and ϖ' a pseudo-uniformizer, ϖ'x is topologically nilpotent, hence in R+ (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
4. R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod: R+ → R° is an almost isomorphism of rings, so extension and restriction of scalars induce inverse equivalences of the Serre quotients (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.almostSetup` (constructor): almostSetup R : Almost.BasicSetup with ring R° and ideal topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R (P0/almost-basic-setup).
- `Perfectoid.almostSetupPlus` (constructor): almostSetupPlus (R+) : Almost.BasicSetup with ring R+ and ideal R°° ∩ R+ = R°°.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_ideal` (simp): (almostSetup R).ideal = topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_forall_pseudoUniformizer` (characterisation): M is almost zero ↔ ∀ ϖ', IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ' → ϖ' • M = 0.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_forall_root` (characterisation): M is almost zero ↔ ∀ n, ϖ^{1/p^n} • M = 0, for any ϖ♭ with compatible roots.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_powerBounded_quotient_plus` (other): R° ⧸ R+ is almost zero (as R+-module).
- `Perfectoid.almostModuleEquivPlus` (equivalence): Restriction of scalars induces an equivalence of the almost categories of R° and R+.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_ringEquiv` (functoriality): An isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings (topological) induces an isomorphism of basic setups; the setup does not depend on ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_field` (compatibility): For a perfectoid field K, almostSetup K is (K°, m_K), the field case of P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_tilt_quot` (compatibility): The isomorphism R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ carries R°°/ϖ onto R♭°°/ϖ♭, identifying the almost categories of R°/ϖ and R♭°/ϖ♭ (used in P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_residueField` (computation): For K a perfectoid field, K° ⧸ m_K is almost zero and ϖ^{1/p^n} acts by 0 on it for all n.
- `Perfectoid.not_idempotent_padic` (non-example): For ℚ_p, (pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p, so (ℤ_p, ℤ_p°°) is not a basic setup; ℤ_p/p is killed by p but not by an idempotent ideal containing p.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_of_subsingleton` (degenerate): For R = 0 every module is almost zero.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_root_test` (characterisation): For K = ℂ_p, the 𝒪-module 𝒪/m is almost zero while 𝒪/p^{1/p}𝒪 is not (p^{1/p²} does not kill it).
- `Perfectoid.almostModuleEquivPlus_test` (compatibility): For K = ℂ_p and K+ an open rank-2 valuation subring, K°a-Mod ≃ K+a-Mod.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definitions 3.21, 3.23 and Theorem 3.24: almost zero modules, R°a-mod, and almost acyclicity of O+
- PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base: its perfectoid instantiation is this node
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary, P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence: R°a-Perf and (R°a/ϖ)-Perf
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity, P2/integral-almost-acyclicity: H^i(X, O+)^a = 0
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem: almost finite étale R°a-algebras
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/higher-v-acyclicity, D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected: almost vanishing and almost faithfully flat descent over (R+/ϖ)^a

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K: the residue field K°/m_K is almost zero, and every almost zero K°-module is a k-vector space (ECD Example 3.22(i)).
- Theorem-level consumers: H^i(Spa(R, R+), O+) is almost zero for i > 0 (ECD Theorem 3.24; P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity).

<a id="p1-perfectoid-field-definition"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition` — Perfectoid fields (ECD Definition 3.6)

*Definition.* A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring K (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) whose underlying topological ring is a nonarchimedean field: K is a field, complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| defining its topology (ECD Definition 3.6). Equivalently (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation; ECD Proposition 3.8; the original definition Sch12 Definition 3.1): K is a nonarchimedean field which is not discretely valued, |p| < 1, and Frobenius is surjective on K°/p. Its value group is p-divisible (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible). In characteristic p a perfectoid field is the same as a complete perfect nonarchimedean field. A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is automatically a perfectoid field (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field). ℚ_p and all discretely valued fields are not perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Nonarchimedean field: in Lean, NontriviallyNormedField K with IsUltrametricDist K and CompleteSpace K; its Tate structure has ring of definition K° (closed unit ball) and any 0 < |ϖ| < 1 as pseudo-uniformizer.
- Residue characteristic p is forced by |p| < 1.

**Proof outline.**

1. The Tate structure of a nonarchimedean field (API isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField) is routine: K° is open and bounded, and the ϖ-adic topology on K° is the norm topology.
2. Uniformity is automatic (K° is the closed unit ball), so the definition reduces to condition (b) of ECD Definition 3.1.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField` (structure): class IsPerfectoidField (K) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] : Prop := IsPerfectoidTateRing K (for the Tate structure below).
- `Huber.isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField` (instance): A complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field is a Tate ring with ring of definition the closed unit ball and pseudo-uniformizer any 0 < |ϖ| < 1; its power-bounded subring is the closed unit ball and its topologically nilpotent ideal the open unit ball.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.toIsPerfectoidTateRing` (coercion): A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.iff` (characterisation): IsPerfectoidField K ↔ (valuation not discrete) ∧ ‖p‖ < 1 ∧ Surjective (frobenius (K°/p) p) (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.norm_p_lt_one` (projection): ‖(p : K)‖ < 1.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.exists_pow_dvd_p` (projection): ∃ ϖ, 0 < ‖ϖ‖ < 1 ∧ ‖p‖ ≤ ‖ϖ‖ ^ p.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.valueGroup_pDivisible` (characterisation): Every element of the value group |K^×| has a p-th root in it (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.iff_perfectRing` (characterisation): If CharP K p: IsPerfectoidField K ↔ PerfectRing K p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.of_isPerfectoidTateRing_of_isField` (constructor): A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field carries a nonarchimedean absolute value making it a perfectoid field (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.tilt` (compatibility): The tilt of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field of characteristic p (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_padicComplex` (example): ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p) is a perfectoid field.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidField_padic` (non-example): ¬ IsPerfectoidField ℚ_[p]: ℚ_p is discretely valued (ECD Remark 3.3), although Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is surjective.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_padicComplex_test` (computation): IsPerfectoidField (PadicComplex p): the value group is |p|^ℚ and every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_iff_perfect_laurent` (characterisation): For the completed perfection K of F_p((t)): IsPerfectoidField K holds; F_p((t)) is not perfect and not a perfectoid field.
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidField_trivial` (degenerate): The perfect field F̄_p with the trivial absolute value is not a nonarchimedean field in this sense (the absolute value must be nontrivial), so it is not a perfectoid field.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_isPerfectoidField` (compatibility): IsPerfectoidField K → IsPerfectoidTateRing K, and conversely for K a field (Kedlaya).

**Uses.**

- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements; PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: C = ℂ_p is a perfectoid field; its tilt C♭
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field: the completed perfection of F_p((t)) is a perfectoid field
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-p-adic-field: K^cycl is a perfectoid field
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field, P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields, P3/fontaine-wintenberger: tilting and Galois theory of perfectoid fields
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: completed residue fields of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid fields
- ECD Definition 3.6; Sch12 Definition 3.1; Berkeley Definition 6.1.7; Bhatt Definition 3.1.1: the definition in the sources

**Acceptance.**

- ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and the completed perfection of F_p((t)) are perfectoid fields (P1/perfectoid-examples); ℚ_p is not.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-field-characterisation"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation` — Characterisation of perfectoid fields (ECD Proposition 3.8)

*Theorem.* Let K be a nonarchimedean field. Then K is a perfectoid field iff (i) K is not discretely valued, (ii) |p| < 1, and (iii) Frobenius Φ: K°/p → K°/p is surjective (ECD Proposition 3.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9). Condition (i) cannot be dropped (ℚ_p and its unramified extensions satisfy (ii) and (iii)). Hence Sch12 Definition 3.1 agrees with ECD Definition 3.6, and a nonarchimedean field is a perfectoid ring in Kedlaya's sense iff it is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K complete with a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value.

**Proof outline.**

1. K is uniform (K° is the closed unit ball) and Tate.
2. (⇒) (ii): ϖ^p | p with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 gives |p| ≤ |ϖ|^p < 1. (iii): P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i) ⇒ (ii). (i): if K were discretely valued with uniformizer π and ϖ = uπ^k (k ≥ 1), then K°/ϖ and K°/ϖ^p are Artin local rings of lengths k and pk, so Φ could not be bijective (ECD Remark 3.3).
3. (⇐) A nondiscrete subgroup of ℝ_{>0} is dense, so there is ϖ ∈ K with |p|^{1/p} ≤ |ϖ| < 1, i.e. ϖ^p | p in K° (Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9 proof); then P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion and P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer give bijectivity of Φ: K°/ϖ → K°/ϖ^p.

**Acceptance.**

- ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) satisfy (i)–(iii) (P1/perfectoid-examples).
- ℚ_p satisfies (ii) and (iii) (Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective) but not (i); Sch12 notes that nondiscreteness is needed to exclude unramified extensions of ℚ_p.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`](#p1-frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`](#p1-perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-elements-adically-complete`](#p1-integral-elements-adically-complete), `mathlib:NontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible` — The value group of a perfectoid field is p-divisible (Sch12 Lemma 3.2)

*Lemma.* Let K be a perfectoid field with value group Γ = |K^×| ⊆ ℝ_{>0}. Then Γ is p-divisible, and it is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 (in characteristic 0).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid; in characteristic p the statement follows from perfectness.

**Proof outline.**

1. Characteristic p: every x has a p-th root x^{1/p}, so |x| = |x^{1/p}|^p.
2. Characteristic 0 (Sch12 Lemma 3.2): Γ ≠ |p|^ℤ by nondiscreteness (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), so Γ is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1; for such x choose y with |x − y^p| ≤ |p| (Frobenius surjective on K°/p); then |y|^p = |y^p| = |x|.

**Acceptance.**

- |ℂ_p^×| = |p|^ℚ is p-divisible; |ℚ_p^×| = |p|^ℤ is not, consistently with ℚ_p not being perfectoid.

<a id="p1-uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field` — A uniform Banach field over a nondiscretely valued field is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya)

*Theorem.* Let F be a nonarchimedean field whose value group |F^×| is dense in ℝ_{>0}, and let A be a uniform Banach F-algebra (complete, with topology defined by a power-multiplicative norm; equivalently the spectral seminorm |·|_sp is a norm defining the topology) whose underlying ring is a field. Then |·|_sp is multiplicative, so A is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 3.7). The criterion used: a uniform Banach field A is a nonarchimedean field iff |t|_sp |t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ∈ A^× (Remark 3.3), because then |x|_sp = |xy·y^{-1}|_sp ≤ |xy|_sp/|y|_sp.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- |F^×| dense in ℝ_{>0}; the discretely valued case is not covered by the proof (Kedlaya, Remark 3.9).
- Uniformity is essential: Kedlaya's Example 2.15 is a Banach field that is not a nonarchimedean field.
- The proof uses the Berkovich spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms: M(A) ≠ ∅ for A ≠ 0, f is a unit iff α(f) ≠ 0 for all α, and |x|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x) (Berkovich, Theorems 1.2.1 and 1.3.1), requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0.

**Proof outline.**

1. Criterion (Remark 3.3): if |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ≠ 0 then |·|_sp is multiplicative; conversely a multiplicative norm satisfies it.
2. Lemma 3.6: if A is not a nonarchimedean field, there are t ∈ A with |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp > 1 and an interval [γ, δ] meeting |F^×| such that |λ|·|(t − λ)^{-1}|_sp ≤ c² for all λ ∈ F with |λ| ∈ [γ, δ]; the proof builds a convergent sequence μ_n = Σλ_i in F by contradiction.
3. Theorem 3.7: with ρ_n ↑ δ and polynomials P_n(t) = ∏(t − λ_{n,i}) whose roots have norms in [ρ_n^-, ρ_n^+], set x_n = (Σ_{j<m_n} P_{n,j}t^j)/P_n(t) and y_n = x_1⋯x_n; estimate α(y_n − y_{n−1}) for every α ∈ M(A) with α(t) = ρ, pass to |·|_sp = max_α α, and obtain a limit y which is neither zero nor a unit, a contradiction.

**Acceptance.**

- Applied with F the completed perfection of F_p((z)) (value group dense) to a perfect uniform Banach field of characteristic p (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field).
- Kedlaya Example 2.15 (Gauss norm on F(T_1, T_2, …)): the completion is a Banach field whose norm is not multiplicative, and it is not uniform.

**Prerequisites.** `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`, `mathlib:NontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`, `mathlib:CompleteSpace`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/BanachField

**namespace.** TauCeti

**Sources.**

- [`Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018`](#source-p0-kedlaya-banachfields-2018), Kedlaya, Banach fields, Remark 3.3, p. 8. The criterion |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1.
- [`Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018`](#source-p0-kedlaya-banachfields-2018), Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7, proof, p. 10. Pointwise estimates for α ∈ M(A).
- [`Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018`](#source-p0-kedlaya-banachfields-2018), Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7, proof, p. 11. The contradiction.

<a id="p1-perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field` — A perfectoid Tate ring is a field iff its tilt is (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, general base)

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Then R is a perfectoid field (a nonarchimedean field) iff its tilt R♭ is; in that case the absolute values satisfy |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R when normalised by |ϖ♭|_{R♭} = |ϖ|_R (Sch12 Lemma 5.21 over a perfectoid base field; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.5.2 and Example 3.3.8 in characteristic 0; Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid with ϖ♭ with compatible roots; the spectral gauges are those of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

**Proof outline.**

1. A uniform Tate ring R is a nonarchimedean field iff R is a field and its spectral gauge |·|_ϖ is multiplicative (then |·|_ϖ is an absolute value defining the topology).
2. (⇒) |·|_{R♭} = |·♯|_R (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp) is multiplicative because ♯ is. R♭ is a field: for x ≠ 0, every x^{(n)} ≠ 0 (P1/sharp-map: x♯ = 0 iff x = 0, applied to x^{1/p^n}), and ((x^{(n)})^{-1})_n ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R is a multiplicative inverse (the argument of Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2).
3. (⇐) (Sch12 Lemma 5.21) Scale x, y ≠ 0 by powers ϖ^{k/p} into R° ∖ ϖ^{1/p}R°, choose x♭, y♭ ∈ R♭° with x − (x♭)♯, y − (y♭)♯ ∈ ϖR° (P1/sharp-map); then |x| = |x♭|, |y| = |y♭|, |xy| = |x♭y♭|, so multiplicativity transfers. x is a unit: |1 − x·((x♭)^{-1})♯| < 1 and R is complete.

**Acceptance.**

- (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ is the field F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- For a perfectoid field K, the product K × K♭ is perfectoid but not a field, and its tilt K♭ × K♭ is not a field.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp`](#p1-spectral-norm-under-sharp), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

<a id="p1-perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field` — A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya; ECD Remark 3.7)

*Theorem.* Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field. Then the topology of A is defined by a multiplicative absolute value, so A is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 4.2; answers ECD Remark 3.7; Berkeley Remark 6.1.8; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.1).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field (Kedlaya, Remark 4.3: such A need not be an algebra over any perfectoid field).

**Proof outline.**

1. Characteristic p: A is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) and uniform; for a pseudo-uniformizer z, A is a uniform Banach algebra over the completed perfection of F_p((z)), whose value group is dense (Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2 proof; Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.1.8), so P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field applies.
2. General case: A♭ is a field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field, (⇒) argument for fields: coordinatewise inverses in lim_{x↦x^p} A) and a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence a perfectoid field by the characteristic-p case; so A is a perfectoid field by P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field (⇐). This replaces Kedlaya's appeal to the homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(A♭) of Berkovich spectra by the spectral-gauge comparison P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp.

**Acceptance.**

- Every perfectoid Tate ring that is a field, e.g. ℚ_p^cycl or ℂ_p with their Tate topologies, is a perfectoid field; the theorem is needed when the topology is given only by a ring of definition.
- Kedlaya Remark 4.3 constructs a perfectoid ring over ℚ_p admitting quotients ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), which is not an algebra over any perfectoid field; the theorem applies to its field quotients.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field`](#p1-uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`](#p1-perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition).

<a id="p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field` — Tilt of a perfectoid field; comparison with Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val

*Construction.* Let K be a perfectoid field. Its tilt K♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) is a perfectoid field of characteristic p with absolute value |x|_♭ := |x♯|; K♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ is its valuation ring for any ϖ ∈ K with |p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1; |K♭^×| = |K^×|; K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ and K♭°/m♭ ≅ K°/m; K♭ = K if char K = p. Replacing ϖ by (ϖ♭)♯ one may assume ϖ has compatible p-power roots (Sch12 Lemma 3.4, Remark 3.5). For v : Valuation K ℝ≥0 the absolute value, O = K° and hv : v.Integers O, the tilt is isomorphic to Mathlib's Tilt K v O hv p = FractionRing (PreTilt O p), and Mathlib's valuation PreTilt.val K v O hv p satisfies PreTilt.val x = v(x♯) for x ∈ PreTilt O p ≅ K♭°.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid; ϖ | p in K° for the identification with lim_Φ K°/ϖ.

**Proof outline.**

1. K♭ is a perfectoid Tate ring (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) and a nonarchimedean field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field) with absolute value |x♯| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp).
2. K♭° = lim K° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings) is a valuation ring: x or x^{-1} lies in it according as |x♯| ≤ 1 or ≥ 1.
3. Value groups: |K♭^×| ⊆ |K^×|; conversely for x ∈ K° with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 there is y ∈ K♭° with x ≡ y♯ mod pK° (P1/sharp-map), so |x| = |y♯|, and such |x| generate |K^×| (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible, proof).
4. Residue fields: K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings), and m, m♭ are the nilradicals of these rings.
5. Mathlib: K♭° ≅ PreTilt O p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt) and K♭ = Frac(K♭°) = FractionRing (PreTilt O p); PreTilt.val x = preVal(x_n)^{p^n} for n with x_n ≠ 0, and a lift z of x_n satisfies z^{p^n} ≡ x♯ mod p^{n+1} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec), so for v(z) > v(p) both sides equal v(x♯).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.tilt_isPerfectoidField` (instance): For K a perfectoid field, tilt K is a perfectoid field (with the absolute value below).
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.norm_def` (characterisation): ‖x‖_{K♭} = ‖x♯‖_K.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.valueGroup_eq` (characterisation): The value groups |K♭^×| and |K^×| coincide as subgroups of ℝ_{>0}.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.integerEquiv` (equivalence): K♭° ≃+* lim_Φ K°/ϖ for ϖ | p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.quotEquiv` (equivalence): K♭° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* K° ⧸ (ϖ).
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.residueFieldEquiv` (equivalence): The residue fields of K♭ and K are identified.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.equivMathlibTilt` (compatibility): tilt K ≃+* Tilt K v O hv p (Mathlib), restricting to (tilt K)° ≃+* PreTilt O p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.preTiltVal_eq` (compatibility): PreTilt.val K v O hv p x = v (PreTilt.untilt x) for x ∈ PreTilt O p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.equivSelfOfCharP` (equivalence): If CharP K p then tilt K ≃+* K isometrically.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.map` (functoriality): A continuous embedding of perfectoid fields induces an isometric embedding of tilts (P1/tilt-functoriality).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.tiltField_padicComplex_pflat` (computation): In tilt ℂ_p, p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n has ‖p♭‖ = ‖p‖ and ‖ε − 1‖ = ‖p‖^{p/(p−1)}.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField_equivMathlibTilt_test` (compatibility): For K = ℂ_p: tilt ℂ_p ≃+* Tilt ℂ_p v 𝒪_{ℂ_p} hv p and PreTilt.val corresponds to the absolute value of the tilt.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField_equivSelf_laurent` (degenerate): For K the completed perfection of F_p((t)), tilt K ≃+* K.
- `Perfectoid.preTilt_padicInt_trivial` (non-example): For ℚ_p (not perfectoid), PreTilt ℤ_p p = Perfection F_p p ≅ F_p and Mathlib's Tilt ℚ_p … p ≅ F_p carries the trivial valuation: without the perfectoid hypothesis the tilt is not a nonarchimedean field.

**Uses.**

- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: O_C♭ = PreTilt O_C p, v♭(x) = v_p(x♯), Frac(O_C♭) = Tilt; ε and p♭
- PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: C♭ with its G_F-action through the action on C
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting: continuous valuations of K and K♭
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields, P3/fontaine-wintenberger: tilting finite extensions of perfectoid fields
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: tilts of completed residue fields
- Sch12 Lemma 3.4; Berkeley Remark 6.2.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.5.2: the construction in the sources

**Acceptance.**

- For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = (p, p^{1/p}, …) and t♯ = p.
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl, |(ε − 1)♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`](#p1-perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp`](#p1-spectral-norm-under-sharp), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt`](#p1-tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible`](#p1-perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible), `mathlib:Tilt`, `mathlib:PreTilt.val`, `mathlib:PreTilt.isDomain`, `mathlib:Perfection.teichmuller_spec`, `mathlib:Valuation.Integers`.

<a id="p1-continuous-valuations-under-tilting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting` — Continuous valuations of K and K♭ correspond (Sch12 Proposition 3.6)

*Lemma.* For a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, |·| ↦ |·|♭, |x|♭ := |x♯|, is a bijection between continuous valuations of K up to equivalence and continuous valuations of K♭ up to equivalence (points of Spa(K, K°) ∪ … of higher rank included); it is the field case of the tilting homeomorphism P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid; continuity in Huber's sense (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont): continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m.

**Proof outline.**

1. |·|♭ is a valuation: only the ultrametric inequality is nontrivial and follows from |x + y|♭ = lim |(x^{1/p^n})♯ + (y^{1/p^n})♯|^{p^n} ≤ max(|x♯|, |y♯|).
2. Continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m, hence to valuation subrings of K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting); this bijection is the one described.

**Acceptance.**

- The rank-one valuation of K maps to the rank-one valuation of K♭ of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; higher-rank continuous valuations correspond to valuation subrings of the common residue field K°/m.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`](#p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), `mathlib:Valuation.IsEquiv`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont`.

<a id="p1-witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring` — A_inf = W(R+) for a perfectoid pair of characteristic p: strict p-ring, (p,[ϖ])-adically complete

*Lemma.* Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then R+ is perfect, ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free, and A_inf(R, R+) := W(R+) satisfies: (a) W(R+) is p-torsion free and p-adically complete with W(R+)/p = R+ (a strict p-ring; Mathlib WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP); (b) every element is uniquely Σ_{n≥0} p^n[x_n] with x_n ∈ R+; (c) [ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor, W(R+) is [ϖ]-adically and (p,[ϖ])-adically complete and separated, and W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ; (d) Σ p^n[x_n] is a unit iff x_0 is a unit of R+; (e) the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology does not depend on ϖ; (f) W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] is the ring W^b(R) of Witt vectors with bounded Teichmüller coordinates, independent of ϖ and of R+ up to the evident inclusions; (g) for every p-adically complete ring S and ring homomorphism R+ → S/p there is a unique ring homomorphism W(R+) → S lifting it; Frobenius W(Φ) is an automorphism.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- pR = 0 and R perfectoid, so R and R+ are perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a), (b), (g): R+ is perfect, so W(R+) is the strict p-ring with residue ring R+ (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.2.1, Corollary 2.2.6, Lemma 2.2.7; Mathlib WittVector, WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP).
2. (c): [ϖ]·Σp^n[x_n] = Σp^n[ϖx_n] and ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (b)); completeness from W_r(ϖ^{p^{r−1}}R+) ⊆ [ϖ]W_r(R+) ⊆ W_r(ϖR+) and ϖ-completeness of R+ (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(ii); Bhatt Example 6.1.6).
3. (d): reduction modulo p is R+ and W(R+) is p-adically complete; (e): two pseudo-uniformizers divide powers of each other in R+; (f): [ϖ]^{-n}Σp^m[x_m] = Σp^m[ϖ^{-n}x_m] (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.2, Remark 2.3.3).

**Acceptance.**

- For R = F the perfect field of anchor Layer 6 and R+ = 𝒪_F, this is the (p,[ϖ])-adic completeness of A_inf = W(𝒪_F) packaged in anchor Layer 6.1 (P1/anchor-layer-6-compatibility).
- For R+ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}, A_inf = W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) is (p,[p♭])-adically complete; Mathlib's BDeRhamPlus 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p is built on W(PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p) ≅ this ring.

<a id="p1-primitive-degree-one-ideals"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals` — Primitive (distinguished) elements and ideals of degree 1 in W(R+) (ECD Definition 3.15)

*Definition.* Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. An element ξ = Σ_{n≥0} p^n[ξ_n] ∈ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 (distinguished) if ξ_0 is topologically nilpotent and ξ_1 is a unit of R+; equivalently ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u with u ∈ W(R+)^× (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.2.3). An ideal J ⊆ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 if it is principal with a primitive generator. Equivalently (ECD Definition 3.15), J is generated by an element p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W(R+): every such element is primitive, and every primitive element is a unit multiple of one of this form, because a topologically nilpotent element of R+ is divisible by a pseudo-uniformizer (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2; Kedlaya AWS Exercise 2.3.6). ξ = p is primitive (ξ_0 = 0): it corresponds to the untilt R itself. In the notation of an untilt S, R = S♭ and R+ = S♭+.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- ξ_0 = 0 is allowed (Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.2.5); p² and [ϖ] are not primitive.

**Proof outline.**

1. p + [ϖ]α = [ϖα_0] + p(1 + [ϖ]α') with α − [α_0] = pα'; 1 + [ϖ]α' is a unit because its reduction 1 + ϖα'_0 is a unit of the ϖ-adically complete R+ (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)).
2. Conversely ξ = [ξ_0] + pu with u a unit: u^{-1}ξ = p + [ξ_0]u^{-1}, and ξ_0 = ϖc for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2), so `u^{-1}ξ = p + [ϖ]([c]u^{-1})`.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive` (structure): For ξ : WittVector p R+: IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0 : R) ∧ IsUnit (ξ.coeff 1).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitiveIdeal` (structure): J : Ideal (WittVector p R+) with ∃ ξ, IsPrimitive ξ ∧ J = Ideal.span {ξ}.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.iff_teichmuller_add` (characterisation): IsPrimitive ξ ↔ ∃ u : (W R+)ˣ, ξ = teichmuller p (ξ.coeff 0) + p * u ∧ IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0).
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_add` (constructor): IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ → IsPrimitive (p + teichmuller p ϖ * α) for every α.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.exists_associated_p_add` (characterisation): IsPrimitive ξ → ∃ u unit, ϖ pseudo-uniformizer, α, ξ = u * (p + [ϖ] α).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.mul_unit` (other): Associates of primitive elements are primitive.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.isUnit_of_eq_mul` (relation): IsPrimitive ξ → IsPrimitive ξ' → ξ' = y * ξ → IsUnit y (P1/distinguished-element-criterion).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.isRegular` (other): Primitive elements are nonzerodivisors (P1/distinguished-element-criterion).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.map` (functoriality): For a morphism of perfectoid pairs of characteristic p, WittVector.map f carries primitive elements to primitive elements, hence primitive ideals J to generators of J·W(R'+).
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p` (example): IsPrimitive (p : W R+) (coefficients (0, 1, 0, …)).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.frobenius` (other): φ(ξ) and φ^{-1}(ξ) are primitive (ξ_0^{p^{±1}} topologically nilpotent, ξ_1^{p^{±1}} a unit).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitiveIdeal.iff_distinguished` (compatibility): A generator of ker θ is primitive iff it is distinguished in the sense of BMS1 Remark 3.11 and of PerfectoidQuotients:Q0 (the conditions coincide).

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_sub_pflat` (computation): In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}), p − [p♭] = p + [p♭]·(−1) is primitive; so is Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p} (its image in W(F̄_p) is p).
- `Perfectoid.not_isPrimitive_p_sq` (non-example): p² is not primitive (its Witt coordinate ξ_1 is 0), and neither is [ϖ]; a definition requiring only ξ ∈ (p, [ϖ]) would accept them.
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_test` (degenerate): p is primitive, and the untilt along (p) is (R, R+) itself.
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_iff_associated_test` (characterisation): In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}), Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} is a unit multiple of an element p + [ϖ]α.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 3.15 and Theorem 3.17: untilts ↔ primitive ideals of degree 1
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel: ker θ is primitive, and any primitive element of ker θ generates it
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction, P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, P1/marked-untilt: the inverse construction and the classification
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: ξ primitive of degree one, congruent to p times a unit up to [ϖ]-multiples
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta: w ∈ ker θ generates it iff its first Witt coordinate is a unit
- PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings: distinguished generators of ker θ for integral perfectoid rings
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: untilts of S as degree-one points of Y_S

**Acceptance.**

- In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): p − [p♭] and Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p} are primitive (Kedlaya AWS Examples 2.3.7–2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.5).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`](#p1-witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:WittVector`.
