<a id="p1-completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings` — Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with them (Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2)

*Construction.* Let J be a small filtered category and j ↦ R_j a functor from J to perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms φ_a: R_i → R_j (no injectivity, flatness or density assumed; characteristic 0, p or neither; no perfectoid base field). Fix j₀ ∈ J and a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ ∈ R_{j₀}♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯ (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots); on the tail J_{j₀} = Under j₀ (final in J, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`) the images of ϖ and of its roots are pseudo-uniformizers with compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in every R_j° (a compatible pseudo-uniformizer). Put A := colim_j R_j° (filtered colimit of rings, Mathlib `CommRingCat.FilteredColimits`), R_0 := its ϖ-adic completion lim_n A/ϖ^nA, and R := R_0[1/ϖ], topologised with R_0 open carrying its ϖ-adic topology. Then: (a) R is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and ring of definition R_0; ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R_0 and R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = colim_j R_j°/ϖ^n; the canonical maps ι_j: R_j → R are continuous and compatible, and the image of colim R_j is dense; for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring S and compatible continuous ring homomorphisms ψ_j: R_j → S there is a unique continuous ψ: R → S with ψ ∘ ι_j = ψ_j; R is independent of j₀ and ϖ, and replacing R_j° by rings of integral elements R_j⁺ (compatible under the φ_a) gives the same R, since ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j⁺ ⊆ R_j°; (b) R is a perfectoid Tate ring; R_0 is ϖ-adically complete and integral perfectoid, R_0 ⊆ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R_0 for all n; so R, with the ι_j, is the colimit of the R_j in perfectoid Tate rings and in complete Hausdorff uniform Tate rings; (c) tilting commutes with completed filtered colimits: the R_j♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality) form a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p with compatible pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭, and the continuous homomorphism from their completed colimit T (as in (a), with ring of definition the ϖ♭-adic completion of colim R_j♭°) to R♭ induced by the ι_j♭ is an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings, compatible with ♯; dually, for a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and a filtered system of perfectoid R′♭-algebras T_j, the untilt over R′ (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) of their completed colimit is the completed colimit of the untilts T_j♯. PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs builds the same ring from plus rings along a cofiltered diagram of pairs and P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid adds the statements about the plus ring.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- J small and filtered (hence nonempty); every R_j a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1; transition maps continuous.
- The R_j must be perfectoid: a completed colimit of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid (ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})) without its tilt being the colimit of the tilts (test completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower); such limits are tilde-limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P7).

**Proof outline.**

1. Compatible pseudo-uniformizer: continuous ring homomorphisms map units to units, topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent ones and R_{j₀}° into R_j° (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so the images of ϖ♭'s coordinates are compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in R_j°; parallel morphisms j₀ ⇉ j may give different images, which agree in A. Restricting to Under j₀ does not change the colimit (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget).
2. (a) A exists (mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A as it is a unit in each R_j. The ϖ-adic completion R_0 is ϖ-adically complete with R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = A/ϖ^nA (Stacks Tag 05GG for the finitely generated ideal ϖA; mathlib:AdicCompletion) and ϖ-torsion free (if ϖ·(x_n)_n = 0 in lim A/ϖ^n then x_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^nA, so x_n = 0). R := R_0[1/ϖ] with basis {ϖ^nR_0} is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. R_j° is open and bounded in R_j with its ϖ-adic topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero), so R_j° → A → R_0 is continuous and extends to ι_j on R_j = R_j°[1/ϖ]. Universal property: ψ_j(R_j°) ⊆ S° (S uniform), S° is open, bounded and ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so the induced A → S° extends uniquely to R_0 and to R; uniqueness from density of A in R_0. Independence: two compatible pseudo-uniformizers define cofinal filtrations on A (at a common stage each divides a power of the other), and colim R_j⁺ ⊆ A ⊆ ϖ^{-1}·colim R_j⁺ because ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j°° ⊆ R_j⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), so both completions give the same R.
3. (b) ϖ^p | p in A, hence in R_0. Φ: A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is the filtered colimit of the bijections Φ_j: R_j°/ϖ → R_j°/ϖ^p (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer, P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), hence bijective, and so is Φ: R_0/ϖ → R_0/ϖ^p since R_0/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n. By the successive-approximation argument of P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion ((i) ⇒ (ii), which uses only ϖ-adic completeness) Frobenius on R_0/p is surjective. So R_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii), P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison), and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes R = R_0[1/ϖ] a perfectoid Tate ring with R_0 ⊆ R° and R°/R_0 killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}. The colimit statement is (a) together with perfectoidness.
4. (c) The R_j♭ are perfectoid of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) with transition maps φ_a♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality); by (a) and (b) their completed colimit T is perfectoid, with ring of definition T_0 and T_0/ϖ♭ = colim_j R_j♭°/ϖ♭. The ι_j♭ induce χ: T → R♭ (universal property (a); R♭ is uniform). Modulo ϖ♭, T_0/ϖ♭ = colim R_j♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ colim R_j°/ϖ = R_0/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c), compatibly with the φ_a), and R_0/ϖ → R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ is an almost isomorphism (its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, by (b)); likewise T_0/ϖ♭ → T°/ϖ♭. So χ induces an isomorphism (T°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (R♭°/ϖ♭)^a of perfectoid (R_{j₀}♭°a/ϖ♭)-algebras, and χ is an isomorphism by P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence over the base R_{j₀}♭ (Sch12 Theorem 5.2: perfectoid algebras are determined by their reduction modulo ϖ; Bhatt Remark 6.2.9). Compatibility with ♯ holds coordinatewise.
5. (c) dual form: apply (c) to the system T_j♯, whose tilts are the T_j (counit of P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), and use full faithfulness of untilting.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit` (data): completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ : Type, for F : J ⥤ (perfectoid Tate rings, continuous homomorphisms) with J filtered and ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with roots of F.obj j₀; CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition` (structure): R_0 = AdicCompletion (span {ϖ}) (colim (F ⋙ powerBoundedSubring)), an open bounded subring with its ϖ-adic topology; R = Localization.Away ϖ R_0; R_0 ⧸ ϖ^n ≃+* colim (R_j° ⧸ ϖ^n).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ι` (constructor): ι j : F.obj j →+* completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, continuous, with (ι j).comp (F.map a) = ι i for a : i ⟶ j in Under j₀.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.lift` (universal-property): For S complete Hausdorff uniform Tate and compatible continuous ψ j : F.obj j →+* S: lift ψ continuous with (lift ψ).comp (ι j) = ψ j (lift_comp_ι), and hom_ext for two continuous maps agreeing on all ι j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): IsPerfectoidTateRing (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition_almostEq` (characterisation): R_0 ≤ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n} • R° ≤ R_0 for all n (R°/R_0 is almost zero for P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.denseRange` (other): The ring homomorphism colim F → completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ has dense range.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.tiltEquiv` (equivalence): tilt (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭) ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (F ⋙ tiltFunctor) ϖ♭.toTilt, a homeomorphism commuting with sharp and sending tilt.map (ι j) to ι j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv` (equivalence): For a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and G : J ⥤ perfectoid R′♭-algebras: the untilt over R′ of completedFilteredColimit G is isomorphic to completedFilteredColimit (G ⋙ untiltFunctor R′), naturally in G.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.equivOfChoice` (compatibility): Changing (j₀, ϖ♭) or restricting along a final functor J′ ⥤ J gives canonically isomorphic rings, compatibly with ι and lift; using compatible rings of integral elements instead of R_j° gives the same ring.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isColimit` (universal-property): The cocone (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, ι) is a colimit in the category of perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_const` (degenerate): For J with a terminal object j (in particular a one-object J), completedFilteredColimit F ≃+* F.obj j as topological rings, compatibly with ι_j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_locallyConstant` (computation): For a perfectoid field K and a profinite set S = lim S_i (finite S_i), the completed colimit of the perfectoid rings K^{S_i} = C(S_i, K) is C^0(S, K) with the sup norm, and its ring of definition is C^0(S, K°).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_tilt_algebraicClosure` (compatibility): For a perfectoid field K, tiltEquiv identifies (completion of an algebraic closure of K♭) with the tilt of the completed colimit of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L of K♭ inside it; the union of the L♯ is dense in the untilt.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower` (non-example): For p odd, the fields ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n}) are not perfectoid and their tilts in the sense of P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring are 𝔽_p, while the completion ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ is perfectoid with tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: tilting does not commute with completed colimits of non-perfectoid rings, so the hypothesis that every R_j be perfectoid cannot be dropped.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: the Krasner step: the untilt of the completed algebraic closure M of K♭ is the completed colimit of the untilts of the finite extensions of K♭ in M, (c)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit: the completed colimit of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings, with ring of definition the completed colimit of the R_j°, is perfectoid, (a)–(b)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid: perfectoidness and tilt of the completed direct limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces; P5 adds the plus rings
- Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2 and proof of Theorem 3.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22: filtered colimits of perfectoid algebras and their tilts in the sources

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 proof of Theorem 3.7 and Bhatt, proof of almost purity over a field: for M the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭, M is the completed colimit of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ and the union of the L♯ is dense in M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 4.6: the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebras is perfectoid; here without a base field.
- Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22: the completion of a filtered direct limit of Fontaine perfectoid Banach rings, for the infimum of the spectral norms, is perfectoid.

<a id="p1-perfected-tate-algebra"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra` — Perfected Tate algebras R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ in any set of variables over any perfectoid Tate ring

*Construction.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (ϖ^p | p in R°) and Σ an arbitrary set, possibly infinite. The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is A_0[1/ϖ], where A_0 is the ϖ-adic completion of the monoid algebra R°[T^a : a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}] (AddMonoidAlgebra over the finitely supported exponent vectors Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}, T^a = Π_s T_s^{a(s)}), topologised with A_0 open and ϖ-adic; equivalently the completion of the perfect polynomial ring R[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] for the topology in which R°[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] is open with its ϖ-adic topology (the Gauss norm). It is a perfectoid Tate ring with R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩° = A_0 = {Σ_a c_aT^a : c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on exponents}; R⁺⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a ring of integral elements for every R⁺. Universal property: for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and every family, indexed by s ∈ Σ, of compatible systems (t_s^{(m)})_{m≥0} in S° with (t_s^{(m+1)})^p = t_s^{(m)}, there is a unique continuous R-algebra map R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ t_s^{(m)}; for S perfectoid such families are families (x_s) in S♭°, via t_s^{(m)} = (x_s^{1/p^m})♯. Its tilt is R♭⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, so T_s♯ = T_s. The construction is functorial in Σ, and R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is the completed filtered colimit (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings) of the algebras in finitely many of the variables. For Σ = {1, …, n} it is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩, which contains Tau Ceti's R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ as the closed subring of series with exponents in ℕ^n, with a continuous R-linear retraction σ(Σ x_aT^a) = Σ_{a ∈ ℕ^n} x_aT^a; the Laurent variant R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid as well (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12 for arbitrary index sets).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid with no base field; Σ any set (Σ = ∅ gives R).
- Infinite Σ is used: P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base takes Σ = C♭° (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21), and Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7 takes Σ = C♭⁺.

**Proof outline.**

1. A_0 is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (a completed free R°-module on the monomials, with c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter), with A_0/ϖ = (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ]; Φ: A_0/ϖ → A_0/ϖ^p is bijective coefficientwise (R° perfectoid) and on monomials (a ↦ pa is bijective on ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}), and Frobenius on A_0/p is surjective; so A_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)) and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes A_0[1/ϖ] perfectoid with A_0 ⊆ A° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_0.
2. A° = A_0: if ϖ^{1/p^m}x ∈ A_0 for all m then every coefficient c_a satisfies ϖ^{1/p^m}c_a ∈ R° for all m, hence c_a ∈ R° (R° = its own almost elements, P1/almost-integral-dictionary (a)).
3. Universal property: T^a ↦ Π_s (t_s^{(m)})^{k_s} for a = (k_s/p^m)_s is a well-defined R°-algebra map R°[T^a] → S° (compatibility of the systems; continuous maps into the uniform S send R° into S°, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); it is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, and S° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so it extends uniquely to A_0 and to A_0[1/ϖ]; uniqueness from density of R[T_s^{1/p^∞}].
4. Tilt: the ring map R♭°⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → lim_{x↦x^p} A_0, T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, reduces modulo ϖ♭ to the identity of (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] = (R♭°/ϖ♭)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); both sides are ϖ♭-adically complete and torsion free, so it is an isomorphism; invert ϖ♭ (P1/sharp-map for T_s♯ = T_s).
5. Finitely many variables: for finite Σ_0 ⊆ Σ, A_0(Σ_0) ⊆ A_0(Σ), the union is dense and A_0(Σ)/ϖ^n = colim_{Σ_0} A_0(Σ_0)/ϖ^n, which is the description of the completed colimit in P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (a). A map g: Σ → Σ′ induces T_s ↦ T_{g(s)} by the universal property.
6. The subring R⟨T⟩ and σ for Σ = {1, …, n}: σ is continuous and R-linear and splits the inclusion (it is not multiplicative).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra` (data): perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ : Type for Σ : Type*, with CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances and an R-algebra structure.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): IsPerfectoidTateRing (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X` (constructor): X s a = T_s^a for s : Σ and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}; X s (a + b) = X s a * X s b, (X s (a/p))^p = X s a, X s a ∈ A°.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.powerBoundedSubring_eq` (characterisation): (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ)° = {Σ c_a T^a | c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}}.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift` (universal-property): For a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and a family t : Σ → Perfection S° p (compatible p-power roots in S°), the unique continuous R-algebra map with X s (1/p^m) ↦ coeff m (t s); lift_X and uniqueness (hom_ext).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.liftTilt` (universal-property): For S perfectoid: continuous R-algebra maps perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ → S correspond to maps Σ → (tilt S)°, x ↦ lift (fun s ↦ x s), with sharp (tilt.map (liftTilt x) (X s 1)) = sharp (x s).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tiltEquiv` (equivalence): tilt (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ) ≃+* perfectedTateAlgebra (tilt R) Σ, a homeomorphism with sharp (X s a) = X s a.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.mapIndex` (functoriality): For g : Σ → Σ′, the continuous R-algebra map with X s a ↦ X (g s) a; mapIndex id = id, mapIndex (g′ ∘ g) = mapIndex g′ ∘ mapIndex g.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.equivCompletedColimit` (compatibility): perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (Σ₀ ↦ perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ₀) over finite subsets Σ₀ ⊆ Σ (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.restrictedIncl` (compatibility): For Σ = Fin n: the continuous injective R-algebra map from TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R (R⟨T⟩) with closed image, T_i ↦ X i 1.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.retraction` (other): For Σ = Fin n: the continuous R-linear map σ onto integral exponents with σ ∘ restrictedIncl = id (the frame of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.plus` (constructor): For a ring of integral elements R+, R+⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a ring of integral elements; the resulting perfectoid pair.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.laurent` (other): The Laurent variant R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is perfectoid.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.emptyEquiv` (example): perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_empty_test` (degenerate): perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R as topological rings.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X_pow` (computation): (X s (1/p^{m+1}))^p = X s (1/p^m), and Frobenius on A_0/ϖ sends the class of X s (1/p) to that of X s 1; for Σ = ℕ the series Σ_k ϖ^k X k 1 converges while Σ_k X k 1 does not.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tilt_cyclotomic` (compatibility): tilt (ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≃+* (tilt ℚ_p^cycl)⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (ECD Example 3.4(iii); Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_fin_test` (compatibility): For Σ = Fin n, perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ of the AdicSpacesPartII request, restrictedIncl embeds TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R with retraction σ, and for Fin n ⊆ ℕ the map perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) → perfectedTateAlgebra R ℕ is a strict inclusion.
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_restricted` (non-example): For n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0, R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is not perfectoid: T_1 is not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift_one` (characterisation): lift with t_s^{(m)} = 1 for all s, m is evaluation at T = 1, a continuous R-algebra map to R; two continuous R-algebra maps agreeing on all X s (1/p^m) are equal.

**Uses.**

- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings (request (a) to P1): R̃⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over an arbitrary perfectoid R̃ with ι and σ is a perfectoid frame of R⟨T⟩ (Σ = {1, …, n})
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: the perfectoid relative ball B^{N,perf}_X = Spa(A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, A+⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: the perfectoid polydisc
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base: the perfectoid ring B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩ in infinitely many variables and its universal property, mapping densely to B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21)
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13: C̃ = A⟨T_s^{p^{-∞}} : s ∈ C♭⁺⟩ surjecting onto C, for completed tensor products of perfectoid rings
- ECD Example 3.4(iii); Sch12 Proposition 5.20; Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12: the example in the sources

**Acceptance.**

<a id="p1-cyclotomic-perfectoid-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field` — The completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field; its tilt and primitive ideal

*Theorem.* The completion ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is a perfectoid field: its valuation ring is the p-adic completion ℤ_p^cycl of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}], its value group |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)} is nondiscrete and Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective. Its tilt is the completed perfection of F_p((t)) with t = ε − 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …), with |t♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (Berkeley Example 6.2.4), and it is the untilt of (F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^) along the primitive ideal generated by Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[1 + t]^{i/p} (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.8). ℤ_p^× acts compatibly, by γ(t) = (1 + t)^γ − 1 on the tilt.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- p any prime; ζ_{p^n} a compatible system of primitive p^n-th roots of unity.

**Proof outline.**

1. ℤ_p[ζ_{p^n}] is the valuation ring of ℚ_p(ζ_{p^n}) with |ζ_{p^n} − 1| = |p|^{1/(p^{n−1}(p−1))}, so the value group is nondiscrete and |p| < 1.
2. Every element of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}] is Σa_iζ^i with a_i ∈ ℤ_p and ζ ∈ μ_{p^n}, and Σa_iζ^i ≡ (Σa_iζ'^i)^p mod p for ζ'^p = ζ, as a^p ≡ a mod p for a ∈ ℤ_p; so Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.5.12: "trivial to check") and P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation applies.
3. Tilt: ε ∈ lim ℤ_p^cycl, t = ε − 1 has |t♯| = lim|ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)} < 1, is a pseudo-uniformizer, and K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
4. Primitive generator: z = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} maps to p under W(K♭°) → W(F_p), so z_1 is a unit, and θ(z) = Σ_{i<p}ζ_p^i = 0; hence ker θ = (z) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c)).

**Acceptance.**

- For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}) is the finite extension K·ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p^cycl, perfectoid by stability of perfectoid fields under finite extension (Sch12 Theorem 3.7(i), Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.5.6), the P3 node P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.
- v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1) in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation`](#p1-perfectoid-field-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`](#p1-fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals`](#p1-primitive-degree-one-ideals), `mathlib:Padic`, `mathlib:PadicInt`.

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples` — Examples and non-examples of perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Remark 3.3, Example 3.4)

*Application.* The following are perfectoid Tate rings, each a declaration of the library: (1) ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p), a perfectoid field whose tilt contains p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) with (p♭)♯ = p; (2) the completion K_1 of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), a perfectoid field with valuation ring the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}] and tilt F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t♯ = p, the untilt along (p − [t]) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7); (3) the completed perfection F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, a perfectoid field of characteristic p equal to its own tilt; (4) ℚ_p^cycl (P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); (5) ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (P1/perfected-tate-algebra); (6) the ring R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ϖ^p = T divides p in R°), which does not contain a nonarchimedean field (ECD Example 3.4(iv); Berkeley Example 6.1.5(4)); (7) products such as K × K♭ for a perfectoid field K, where p is a nonzero nonunit. Non-examples: ℚ_p and every discretely valued nonarchimedean field (ECD Remark 3.3), F_p((t)) (not perfect), ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) (not uniform), R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ for n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0 (T_1 not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Each example is checked against ECD Definition 3.1 through the criteria of this layer.

**Proof outline.**

1. (1) ℂ_p is algebraically closed with value group |p|^ℚ, so every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(2)); P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation.
2. (2) K_1° = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^ is generated by the p^{1/p^n}, whose classes are p-th powers modulo p (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(1)); its tilt is computed by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field and it is the untilt along (p − [t]) (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals).
3. (3) P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. (4) P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field. (5) P1/perfected-tate-algebra.
4. (6) R° is the displayed ring (bounded); ϖ = T^{1/p} has ϖ^p = T and p = T·(p/T) with p/T ∈ R°; Frobenius R°/T^{1/p} → R°/T is surjective as all topological generators T^{1/p^n}, (p/T)^{1/p^n} and ℤ_p^cycl have p-th roots modulo p (ECD Example 3.4(iv)).
5. (7) API IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras. Non-examples: P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation, P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced, P1/perfected-tate-algebra.

**Acceptance.**

- These realise the tests of the stage: completed F_p((t^{1/p^∞})), cyclotomic and compatible-root mixed-characteristic fields, perfected Tate balls and tori, and a non-field perfectoid Tate ring.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation`](#p1-perfectoid-field-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra`](#p1-perfected-tate-algebra), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field`](#p1-cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`](#p1-untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), `mathlib:PadicComplex`, `mathlib:Padic`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Padic.isTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PadicInt.not_isTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`.

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/anchor-layer-6-compatibility` — Compatibility with the anchor's perfect field F and A_inf = W(𝒪_F) (Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6.1)

*Comparison.* Let F be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of characteristic p with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, as in anchor Layer 6.1. Then (a) F is a perfectoid field of characteristic p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), its tilt is F itself with ♯ the identity (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), and (F, 𝒪_F) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p; (b) the anchor's A_inf = W(𝒪_F), with pair of definition (A_inf, (p, [ϖ])), is the ring W(F♭+) = W(𝒪_F) of this layer, and the anchor's (p, [ϖ])-adic completeness and separatedness of W(𝒪_F) is P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring for (F, 𝒪_F); (c) the untilts of F are the pairs (W(𝒪_F)[1/[ϖ]]/(ξ), W(𝒪_F)/(ξ)) for primitive ξ ∈ A_inf (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). The anchor's curve 𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf) and its Frobenius windows are not re-planned; P1 only identifies the input objects.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- F as in anchor Layer 6 (no algebraic closedness).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) A complete nontrivially valued perfect field is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid; its value group is p-divisible (perfectness), so not discrete.
2. (b) Same ring; the completeness statements coincide.
3. (c) The classification with (R, R+) = (F, 𝒪_F).

**Acceptance.**

- For F the completed perfection of F_p((t)): untilts include ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ (ξ = p − [t]) and ℚ_p^cycl (ξ = Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}).

<a id="p2"></a>

## P2. Rational localization, sheafiness and perfectoid spaces

Use the anchor’s spectra and rational localizations to prove the tilting homeomorphism and perfectoidness of rational localizations, stable uniformity and sheafiness, with almost acyclicity of the integral structure sheaf. Define perfectoid spaces inside the existing adic-space category, glue tilts, and construct relative and absolute products using R0. Fibre products over an analytic base are distinguished from products over a perfectoid field.

**Coverage (`source_decomposed`; packet P0).** All targets of the RS-05-narrowed stage that P2a owns are realised for arbitrary perfectoid Tate pairs (ECD Definition 3.1, no base field): the tilting map and homeomorphism identifying rational subsets, perfectoid rational localisations with explicit almost integral model and tilt (the AdicSpacesPartII request), restriction maps and plus rings, the approximation lemma, stable uniformity and sheafiness, integral almost acyclicity on rational coverings, the almost Čech-to-sheaf passage, the sheaf theorem (ECD 3.18, 3.24), completed residue fields, and the p-finite/completed-direct-limit arguments of Sch12 kept for P3/P5 and AdicEtaleGeometry:A3. Anchor Layers 2-4 and AdicSpacesPartII R0/R3, DiamondsAndVStacks D0 are imported, not re-planned. Perfectoid spaces: affinoid perfectoid spaces and perfectoid spaces as full subcategories of the anchor's adic spaces (Perfd, Perf), the affinoid perfectoid basis and open subspaces, the characteristic-p criterion (Mihara), the glued tilt (KEEP id, now a construction over an arbitrary perfectoid space) and ECD Corollary 3.20 with its pair-level lemma, completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs (characteristic p, general, plus-ring almost formula, uniform version over any Tate base, dense-image criterion), affinoid and global fibre products (KEEP id, generalised from a perfectoid field to arbitrary perfectoid spaces) with tilting compatibility, fibre products over a non-perfectoid analytic base (in Perfd), absolute products in Perf with a corrected chart construction, and the comparison with Scholze's spaces over a perfectoid field. The adic-space carriers of anchor Layers 2–5 are requests; the unread inputs (BGR 7.3.2, a general-base write-up of Sch12 Lemmas 6.4–6.5, the tilt of completed residue fields) are gaps.

**Planets.** The tilting homeomorphism; Rational localization; The sheaf theorem; Perfectoid space; Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces; Fibre products of perfectoid spaces.

<a id="p2-tilting-map-of-spectra"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra` — The tilting map x ↦ x♭ from Spa(R, R⁺) to Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)

*Construction.* Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺) and sharp map ♯ : R♭ → R (continuous and multiplicative, not additive), X = Spa(R, R⁺), X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺). For x ∈ X with valuation v_x : R → Γ_x ∪ {0}, the composite v_x ∘ ♯ : R♭ → Γ_x ∪ {0} is a continuous valuation of R♭ with v_x(f♯) ≤ 1 for all f ∈ R♭⁺; its class is a point x♭ ∈ X♭, characterised by |f(x♭)| ≤ |g(x♭)| ⟺ |f♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)| for all f, g ∈ R♭ (written |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|). The tilting map τ_R : X → X♭, x ↦ x♭, satisfies: (a) supp(x♭) = {f ∈ R♭ : f♯ ∈ supp(x)}; (b) τ_R is continuous: if f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭ and some f_i is a unit of R♭ (for instance f_n = (ϖ♭)^N), then f₁♯, …, f_n♯ generate the unit ideal of R and τ_R⁻¹(U(f₁, …, f_n / g)) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯); every rational subset of X♭ has a presentation with f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺ and f_n = (ϖ♭)^N for some N; (c) τ is natural: for a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with tilt φ♭, τ_R ∘ Spa(φ) = Spa(φ♭) ∘ τ_S; (d) if pR = 0 then (R♭, R♭⁺) = (R, R⁺) with ♯ = id and τ_R = id. That τ_R is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets; here only the map and its first properties are constructed.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (R, R⁺) a perfectoid Tate pair (stage conventions); no base field.
- For (b): some numerator f_i is a unit of R♭, which makes f_i♯ = (f_i)♯ a unit of R because ♯ is multiplicative with 1♯ = 1; without such a normalisation the unit-ideal condition on f♯ is not automatic before the homeomorphism is known.
- For (c): φ continuous, φ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺, and φ♭ its tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), so that φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭.

**Proof outline.**

1. Valuation axioms: v_x(0♯) = 0, v_x(1♯) = 1 and multiplicativity come from ♯ being multiplicative with 0♯ = 0, 1♯ = 1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).
2. Strong triangle inequality: by the addition law of the tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) (f + g)♯ = lim_n z_n with z_n = ((f^{1/p^n})♯ + (g^{1/p^n})♯)^{p^n}; v_x(z_n) ≤ M := max(v_x(f♯), v_x(g♯)). If M ≠ 0, continuity of v_x makes {w : v_x(w) < M} an open neighbourhood of 0, so v_x((f + g)♯ − z_n) < M for large n and v_x((f + g)♯) ≤ M; if M = 0 then all z_n lie in supp(v_x), which is closed (an intersection of the open, hence closed, subgroups {v_x < γ}), so (f + g)♯ ∈ supp(v_x) (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.12; Sch12 proof of Proposition 3.6).
3. Continuity of v_x ∘ ♯: {f : v_x(f♯) < γ} = ♯⁻¹{v_x < γ} is open because ♯ is continuous; v_x(f♯) ≤ 1 on R♭⁺ because (R♭⁺)♯ ⊆ R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting: R♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺). Hence x♭ ∈ X♭ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff`); equivalent valuations give equivalent composites, so τ_R is well defined on classes, and (a) is the definition of the support.
4. (b): if f_i is a unit of R♭ then f_i♯ is a unit of R, so f♯ generates the unit ideal and U(f♯/g♯) is rational; x ∈ τ⁻¹U(f/g) iff |f_j♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)| ≠ 0 for all j, i.e. x ∈ U(f♯/g♯). Normalisation: on the quasi-compact rational U = U(f/g) the function g is a unit of O(U), so |(ϖ♭)^N(y)| ≤ |g(y)| on U for N large, and adding (ϖ♭)^N to the numerators does not change U (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`; Sch12 Remark 2.8); multiplying all parameters by a power of ϖ♭ puts them into R♭⁺ (`rationalSubset_image_mul_right`). Continuity follows because rational subsets form a basis of X♭ (Tau Ceti `isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`).
5. (c): φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), so for y ∈ Spa(S, S⁺) both composites send y to the class of v_y ∘ φ ∘ ♯_R. (d): in characteristic p the tilt of (R, R⁺) is (R, R⁺) with ♯ = id (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt` (data): The map spa R⁺ → spa R♭⁺, x ↦ x♭, sending the valuation v_x to v_x ∘ ♯.
- `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_vle_iff` (characterisation): For f g : R♭, (spaTilt x).vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯.
- `PerfectoidSpace.supp_spaTilt` (projection): The support of spaTilt x is the preimage under ♯ of the support of x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.continuous_spaTilt` (other): spaTilt is continuous.
- `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset` (compatibility): If some f_i ∈ T is a unit of R♭, then spaTilt ⁻¹' rationalSubset R♭⁺ T s = rationalSubset R⁺ (T.image ♯) s♯.
- `PerfectoidSpace.exists_rationalSubset_eq_insert_pseudoUniformizer_pow` (other): Every rational subset of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) equals rationalSubset R♭⁺ (insert ((ϖ♭)^N) T) s with T ⊆ R♭⁺, s ∈ R♭⁺, for some N.
- `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_comp_spaComap` (functoriality): For a morphism φ of perfectoid Tate pairs, spaTilt ∘ φ.spaComap = φ♭.spaComap ∘ spaTilt.
- `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_eq_id_of_charP` (simp): If pR = 0, then spaTilt = id under the identification of R with its tilt.

**Unit tests.**

- `spaTilt_test_perfectoidDisc_point` (computation): For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and x the point T ↦ ϖ, spaTilt x is the point T ↦ ϖ♭ of Q_p^cycl♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: |T(x♭)| = |T♯(x)| = |ϖ(x)|.
- `spaTilt_test_charP_eq_id` (degenerate): For R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (characteristic p), spaTilt is the identity of Spa(R, R⁺).
- `spaTilt_test_preimage_disc` (compatibility): On the perfectoid disc over Q_p^cycl, spaTilt ⁻¹' U({T, ϖ♭}/ϖ♭) = U({T, ϖ}/ϖ), the instance of spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset with f₂ = ϖ♭.
- `spaTilt_test_no_ringHom` (non-example): There is no ring homomorphism Q_p^cycl♭ → Q_p^cycl, so spaTilt is not Pair.Hom.spaComap of any morphism of Huber pairs; a definition of x♭ as the pullback of x along a ring map cannot typecheck in mixed characteristic.
- `spaTilt_test_vle_characterisation` (characterisation): x♭ is the unique point y of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) with y.vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯ for all f g; two points of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) with the same relation coincide.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: the map whose bijectivity and openness is proved there; (b) gives continuity and the preimage formula
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization: Spa of the untilt of O_{X♭}(U) maps into τ⁻¹(U) by naturality (c)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: the completed residue field of x tilts to that of x♭
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction: the homeomorphisms Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U intertwine the tilting maps
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting (P2b): the underlying map |X| → |X♭| of the glued tilt is τ on affinoid charts
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity: the étale sites are compared over the identification |X| = |X♭|
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4 (Zariski closed subsets and tilting): the tilt of a Zariski closed subset is its image under τ
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1, D4 (underlying spaces of perfectoid spaces and diamonds): |X| = |X♭| naturally in X

**Acceptance.**

- For K = Q_p^cycl (the completion of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}), a perfectoid field) and R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, the point x of evaluation at T^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n} tilts to the point of R♭ = K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ given by evaluation at T ↦ ϖ♭, and τ⁻¹{|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|} = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}.
- The map is not Spa of a morphism of Huber pairs: for K = Q_p^cycl there is no ring homomorphism K♭ → K at all (K♭ has characteristic p, K characteristic 0).

<a id="p2-rational-localization-in-characteristic-p"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p` — Rational localisations of perfectoid Tate pairs of characteristic p are perfect, with an explicit almost integral model

*Lemma.* Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with pR = 0 (so R is a perfect complete Tate ring and R⁺ is perfect; ECD Proposition 3.5), ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudo-uniformizer, X = Spa(R, R⁺), f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R⁺ with f_n = ϖ^N, and U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g). Then: (i) the rational localisation (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) (anchor Layer 3.1) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p: Frobenius is bijective on O_X(U) and on O_X⁺(U); (ii) let A_U be the ϖ-adic completion of the subring R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^m} : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0] of R[1/g]; then A_U is perfect and ϖ-torsion free, A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)° inside O_X(U) = A_U[1/ϖ], and both quotients O_X(U)°/A_U and O_X⁺(U)/A_U are almost zero (killed by ϖ^{1/p^k} for all k); (iii) the surjection ψ : R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^∞}], T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i/g)^{1/p^m}, has kernel containing the ideal I generated by the elements g^{1/p^m} T_i^{1/p^m} − f_i^{1/p^m} (i ≤ n, m ≥ 0), and ker ψ / I is almost zero; (iv) consequently every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p is stably uniform.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- pR = 0; (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair (equivalently R perfect, complete, Tate: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
- f_i, g ∈ R⁺ and f_n = ϖ^N: every rational subset has such a presentation (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b), applied with R = R♭).
- Almost zero is with respect to the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of R⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); in a perfect R⁺ it is generated by the ϖ^{1/p^k}.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) Frobenius: the composite R → R → O_X(U) of Φ⁻¹ with the structure map is continuous, sends g to g^{1/p}, a unit of O_X(U), and f_i/g to (f_i/g)^{1/p}, which is power-bounded; by the universal property of the rational localisation (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`) it extends uniquely to σ : O_X(U) → O_X(U). Φ ∘ σ and σ ∘ Φ are continuous and restrict to the structure map on R, so both are the identity by uniqueness (Kedlaya AWS proof of Theorem 2.5.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.1.7). A perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid, in particular uniform (ECD Proposition 3.5). O_X⁺(U) is perfect because it is integrally closed in the perfect ring O_X(U).
2. (iii) The ideal I is stable under p-th roots of its generators, so P := R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]/I is perfect; ψ induces a surjection P → R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}] which becomes an isomorphism after inverting ϖ, because inverting ϖ inverts g (g · (f_n/g) = ϖ^N), so that R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}][1/ϖ] = R[1/g] and P[1/ϖ] = R[1/g] as well; hence its kernel is ϖ^∞-torsion in the perfect ring P, and ϖ^k x = 0 implies (ϖ^{k/p^m} x)^{p^m} = 0, so ϖ^{k/p^m} x = 0 since perfect rings are reduced (Sch12 proof of Lemma 6.4(i) in characteristic p; Bhatt Lemma 9.2.3(2)).
3. (ii) A_U is perfect and ϖ-torsion free as the ϖ-adic completion of a perfect ϖ-torsion-free ring. The cokernel of R⁺[f/g] → R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}] is killed by ϖ^{nN} (Bhatt Lemma 9.2.3(3): a product ∏(f_i/g)^{a_i} with a_i ∈ [0,1) times ϖ^{nN} lies in R⁺[f/g] because ϖ^N/g = f_n/g), so both ϖ-adic completions give the same Tate ring after inverting ϖ, and R⁺⟨f/g⟩[1/ϖ] = O_X(U) because R⁺ is a ring of definition of R (R uniform) and f₁, …, f_n generate the unit ideal. A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) since its generators have absolute value ≤ 1 on U = Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) and O_X⁺(U) is closed. Since A_U is open and bounded, O_X(U)° ⊆ ϖ^{-c}A_U for some c; for y ∈ O_X(U)° and k ≥ 0, (ϖ^{c/p^k} y)^{p^k} ∈ A_U, and A_U contains the p-th roots (unique in O_X(U)) of its elements, so ϖ^{c/p^k} y ∈ A_U: O_X(U)°/A_U is almost zero.
4. (iv) By (i) every rational localisation of (R, R⁺) is perfectoid, hence uniform (ECD Definition 3.1).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization: applied to (R♭, R♭⁺); its presentation (iii) and model (ii) are untilted there
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: perfectness of the rings O_{X♭}(V) makes the completed residue fields of X♭ perfect, hence perfectoid
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity: Frobenius is bijective on every term of the characteristic-p integral Čech complex
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy: stable uniformity in characteristic p
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: rational subsets of relative balls over characteristic-p perfectoid bases are perfect

**Acceptance.**

- For K = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ (t-adic completion) and R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, U = {|T| ≤ |t|}: O_X(U) = K⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_U = K°⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_X(U)° exactly; for the annulus U = {|t| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}, O_X(U) = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (t/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfect.
- The perfectness in (i) fails for non-perfect rings: for the Tate algebra F_p((t))⟨T⟩ (not perfectoid) the rational localisation at {|T| ≤ |t|} is F_p((t))⟨T/t⟩, which is not perfect; the lemma uses that R is perfect.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`](#p0-almost-zero-serre-class), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`.

<a id="p2-almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer` — Almost exactness lifts from reduction modulo ϖ for torsion-free complete complexes

*Lemma.* Let V be a ring, m ⊆ V an ideal with m² = m, ϖ ∈ V an element, and call a V-module almost zero if it is killed by m (these form a Serre class, closed under arbitrary products and filtered colimits; PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class). (a) Let C be a bounded complex of V-modules whose terms are ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete and separated. If every cohomology module of C/ϖC is almost zero, so is every cohomology module of C. (b) Conversely, if the terms of C are ϖ-torsion free and every cohomology module of C is almost zero, so is every cohomology module of C/ϖC. (c) Let α : M → N be V-linear with M ϖ-adically separated, N ϖ-torsion free, coker α almost zero, and α ⊗ V/ϖ with almost zero kernel and cokernel. Then ker α and coker α are almost zero.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- m² = m (basic setup ideal, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup); in the application V = R⁺ for a perfectoid Tate pair and m its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements, with ϖ ∈ m.
- Completeness and separatedness are ϖ-adic; the inverse limit C = lim_n C/ϖ^n C has surjective transition maps.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Termwise torsion-freeness gives short exact sequences of complexes 0 → C/ϖ^n → C/ϖ^{n+1} → C/ϖ → 0 (first map multiplication by ϖ); by induction and the long exact cohomology sequence all H^q(C/ϖ^n) are almost zero (the class is closed under extensions because m² = m).
2. Since C = lim_n C/ϖ^n with surjective transition maps, the Milnor sequence 0 → lim¹_n H^{q−1}(C/ϖ^n) → H^q(C) → lim_n H^q(C/ϖ^n) → 0 is exact. lim_n of almost zero modules is almost zero (a submodule of the product), and lim¹_n is a quotient of ∏_n H^{q−1}(C/ϖ^n), which is killed by m; so the derived-limit term is controlled, not discarded, and H^q(C) is almost zero. This is Sch12's 'by flatness and completeness'.
3. (b) The long exact sequence of 0 → C → C → C/ϖ → 0 places H^q(C/ϖ) between H^q(C) and H^{q+1}(C).
4. (c) (Bhatt, footnote in the proof of Lemma 9.2.5) Replace N by the image of α (its quotient is almost zero); L = ker α satisfies L/ϖL ⊆ ker(α ⊗ V/ϖ) because N is ϖ-torsion free, so L is almost ϖ-divisible, while L ⊆ M is ϖ-adically separated; an almost ϖ-divisible separated module is almost zero.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity: the tilting reduction: almost exactness of the tilted complex modulo ϖ♭ transfers to the original complex
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization: (c) makes the comparison map an almost isomorphism once it is one modulo ϖ
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate: completion preserves almost exactness
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity: the same tilting reduction for étale Čech complexes

**Acceptance.**

- Completeness cannot be dropped: for V = Z_p, m = 0 (so almost zero means zero) and C = [Q_p → 0], C/pC = 0 is exact while C is not; Q_p is p-torsion free but not p-adically separated.
- In PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity, (b) is applied to the characteristic-p integral Čech complex and (a) to the characteristic-0 one after identifying both modulo ϖ.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup`](#p0-almost-basic-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`](#p0-almost-zero-serre-class), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.ExactAt`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Almost/LiftModPseudoUniformizer

**namespace.** TauCeti.Almost

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.14 (characteristic 0), p. 38. Statement (a) as used by Scholze (in the almost category).
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 9, footnote 1 in the proof of Lemma 9.2.5, p. 100. Statement (c).
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), Section 3, after Example 3.22, p. 19. The Serre-class property used in the induction.

<a id="p2-almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization` — Untilted rational localisations: explicit almost integral model, perfectoidness and tilt

*Lemma.* Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺) and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ as in the stage conventions. Let f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g) ⊆ X♭ and U♯ := τ_R⁻¹(U) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) ⊆ X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b)). Then: (i) the ϖ-adic completion A of the subring R⁺[(f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯ : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0] of R[1/g♯] is ϖ-torsion free and Frobenius induces an almost isomorphism A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ, i.e. A^a is a perfectoid R⁺ᵃ-algebra; (ii) O_X(U♯) = A[1/ϖ] is a perfectoid Tate ring and A ⊆ O_X⁺(U♯) ⊆ O_X(U♯)° with almost zero quotients; (iii) the map R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → A, T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯, is surjective modulo ϖ with kernel modulo ϖ almost equal to the image of the ideal generated by (g^{1/p^m})♯ T_i^{1/p^m} − (f_i^{1/p^m})♯; (iv) (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) is the untilt over (R, R⁺) of (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)): there is a unique isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) compatible with the structure maps from (R♭, R♭⁺) and with ♯.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; no base field; ϖ♭ with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R°.
- The normalisation f_n = (ϖ♭)^N makes f₁♯, …, f_n♯ generate the unit ideal of R, so U♯ is a rational subset with the displayed presentation.
- The untilt of (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) over (R, R⁺) exists by the tilting equivalence over the perfectoid base R (ECD Theorem 3.13; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt); no base field is used.

**Proof outline.**

1. Characteristic p: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p applied to (R♭, R♭⁺) and U gives O_{X♭}(U) perfectoid, the model A♭ = R♭⁺⟨(f/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩ almost equal to O_{X♭}⁺(U), and the presentation P♭ = R♭⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]/I♭ with almost zero kernel onto R♭⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}].
2. Untilt and comparison map: let (S, S⁺) be the perfectoid (R, R⁺)-algebra with (S, S⁺)♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting). By naturality of τ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (c)) every point of Spa(S, S⁺) maps to τ⁻¹(U) = U♯, so the universal property of the rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`) gives (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) → (S, S⁺) over (R, R⁺); composing, R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}] →a A →d S⁺.
3. Modulo ϖ: since ♯ induces ring isomorphisms R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ and S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ natural in the pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings), the reduction of d ∘ a modulo the ideal (I, ϖ) is identified with the characteristic-p map P♭/ϖ♭ → O_{X♭}⁺(U)/ϖ♭, which is an almost isomorphism by the first step; the generators (g^{1/p^m})♯T^{1/p^m} − (f^{1/p^m})♯ reduce to g^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m} − f^{1/p^m} because ♯ is additive modulo ϖ.
4. Lifting: a is surjective (surjective before completion); the ϖ-adic completion of P is ϖ-adically separated and S⁺ is ϖ-torsion free, so d ∘ a, being an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ, is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer (b); Bhatt, footnote in the proof of Lemma 9.2.5). With a surjective, a and d are almost isomorphisms; A is ϖ-torsion free (a completion of a torsion-free ring), so the almost zero kernel of d vanishes and A ⊆ S⁺ with almost zero cokernel. This gives (i) and (iii), since S⁺ᵃ is a perfectoid R⁺ᵃ-algebra (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary).
5. (ii): as in the characteristic-p case the cokernel of R⁺[f♯/g♯] → R⁺[(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}] is killed by ϖ^{nN} (1/g♯ = ϖ^{-N} f_n♯/g♯), so A[1/ϖ] = R⁺⟨f♯/g♯⟩[1/ϖ] = O_X(U♯); hence O_X(U♯) ≅ S is perfectoid, A ⊆ O_X⁺(U♯) (generators of absolute value ≤ 1 on U♯) and O_X(U♯)°/A ≅ S°/A is almost zero (S°/S⁺ is almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
6. (iv): the map μ : (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) → (S, S⁺) is an isomorphism of topological rings by (ii); on plus rings, tilting the inclusion (A[1/ϖ], A) → (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) shows that g divides f_i in the tilt of O_X⁺(U♯), so the tilt of Spa(O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯)) maps into U and the universal property over (R♭, R♭⁺) gives (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)) → (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭, whose untilt inverts μ; uniqueness holds because the structure maps from (R, R⁺) are epimorphisms of complete Tate pairs (Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5(4); Sch12 Lemma 6.4(iii)).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc: the almost integral model of O_X(U_c♯) on the perfectoid polydisc
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids: every rational subset is some U♯, so (ii) and (iv) give the general rational localisation theorem
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation (request to P2): perfectoidness of R̃⟨ι(T)/ι(s)⟩ for a perfectoid frame without base field, through the rational localisation node

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid Tate ring R₀ and the perfected Tate algebra R = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), g ∈ R♭⁺ homogeneous and U_c = {|g| ≤ |ϖ♭|^c} (c ∈ Z[1/p]_{≥0}), the lemma gives O_X(U_c♯)°ᵃ = R°⟨(g♯/ϖ^c)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ, the formula consumed by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc.
- Over a perfectoid field K this is Sch12 Lemma 6.4 (i)-(iii) and Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5; for R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}, O_X(U♯) = Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ with tilt Q_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- The model is almost, not exactly, integral: for R⁺ ≠ R° (e.g. R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) and U = X, A = R⁺ while O_X(X)° = R°.

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc` — Approximation of homogeneous functions on a perfectoid polydisc over a perfectoid Tate ring

*Lemma.* Let R₀ be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R₀♭, ϖ♭ ∈ R₀♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R₀°, and let P = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ be the perfected Tate algebra, with P° = R₀°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ graded by total degree in T with values in Z[1/p]_{≥0} (R₀° in degree 0), and tilt P♭ = R₀♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, where T_i♯ = T_i. Let f ∈ P° be homogeneous of degree d. Then for every rational c ≥ 0 and every ε ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε < 1 there is g ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d such that for all x ∈ Spa(P, P°): |f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|). In particular max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) for all x.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R₀ a perfectoid Tate ring (no base field; Sch12 Lemma 6.5 is the case R₀ = K a perfectoid field).
- P is perfectoid with P° = R₀°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and tilt R₀♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12).
- Homogeneity refers to the Z[1/p]-grading of R₀°[T^{1/p^∞}] by total T-degree, extended to the completion as convergent sums of homogeneous terms of one degree.

**Proof outline.**

1. Fix ε ∈ Z[1/p] ∩ (0, 1) and f; prove by induction on c, in steps c → c' = c + a with a fixed a ∈ Z[1/p], 0 < a < ε, that there are ε(c) ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε(c) ≤ ε − a and g_c ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d with |f − g_c♯| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε+ε(c)}| max(|f|, |ϖ^c|) on Spa(P, P°); c = 0 holds with ε(0) = ε and g₀ ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d with g₀♯ ≡ f modulo ϖP° (lift f coefficientwise through R₀♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R₀°/ϖ), since then |f − g₀♯| ≤ |ϖ| and max(|f|, |ϖ^0|) = 1 on Spa(P, P°); each induction step loses a small constant through almost mathematics.
2. On U_c♯ = {|g_c♯| ≤ |ϖ^c|} = {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} (the two agree by the induction hypothesis), h := f − g_c♯ ∈ ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c)} O⁺(U_c♯); by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization, O(U_c♯)°ᵃ = P°⟨(g_c♯/ϖ^c)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ, and homogeneity puts h almost into the ϖ-adic completion of ⊕_{i ∈ Z[1/p] ∩ [0,1]} ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c)} (g_c♯/ϖ^c)^i P°_{deg = d − di}; choose 0 < ε(c') < ε(c) and write h = Σ_i ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c')} (g_c♯/ϖ^c)^i r_i with r_i ∈ P° homogeneous of degree d − di, r_i → 0.
3. Choose s_i ∈ P♭° homogeneous of degree d − di with s_i → 0 and ϖ | r_i − s_i♯: coefficientwise lifting through R₀♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R₀°/ϖ, using that ♯ is additive modulo ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Put g_{c'} = g_c + Σ_i (ϖ♭)^{c+1−ε+ε(c')} (g_c/(ϖ♭)^c)^i s_i.
4. Estimate: where |f(x)| > |ϖ^c(x)|, |g_c♯(x)| = |f(x)| and each correction term has absolute value ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε+ε(c')}(x)||f(x)| (maximal at i = 1); where |f(x)| ≤ |ϖ^c(x)|, f − g_{c'}♯ ≡ f − g_c♯ − h = 0 modulo ϖ^{c+1} O(U_c♯)°, and c + 1 > c' + 1 − ε + ε(c'). This is Sch12's proof of Lemma 6.5 with K replaced by R₀; it uses only the grading, the model of O(U_c♯) and ♯ modulo ϖ.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: the universal case to which an arbitrary f ∈ R is pulled back along R⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_c^{1/p^∞}⟩ → R

**Acceptance.**

- Field case (Sch12 Lemma 6.5, Bhatt Lemma 9.2.6): R₀ = K perfectoid field, P = K⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- For f = T₀ one may take g = T₀ for every c. For f = T₀ + ϖT₁ (homogeneous of degree 1), g = T₀ + ϖ♭T₁ satisfies f ≡ g♯ modulo ϖP° because ♯ is additive modulo ϖ, which gives the estimate for c = 0; for c > 0 the locus {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} requires the inductive corrections.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization`](#p2-almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 9, Lemma 9.2.6 and the paragraph before it, p. 101. Field-case statement of the polydisc approximation.

<a id="p2-approximation-lemma"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma` — Approximation lemma: every function on a perfectoid affinoid is approximated by a sharp

*Lemma.* Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺), ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ as in the stage conventions, X = Spa(R, R⁺). (i) For every f ∈ R, every rational c ≥ 0 and every ε ∈ Z[1/p] with 0 < ε < 1 there is g ∈ R♭ such that for all x ∈ X: |f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|); in particular max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|). (ii) For f, h ∈ R and an integer c ≥ 0 there are a, b ∈ R♭ with {x ∈ X : |f(x)| ≤ |h(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |h(x)|} = {x ∈ X : |a♯(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|}. The field version is Sch12 Corollary 6.7(i); the general version holds with the same proof over the base R, and independently by Witt-vector Euclidean division (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.17).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; no base field.
- The estimate is pointwise in the value group Γ_x ∪ {0} of each x ∈ X, with |ϖ^r(x)| := |((ϖ♭)^r)♯(x)| for r ∈ Z[1/p].

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduction to R⁺ = R°: every point of X has a unique rank-one generization, which lies in Spa(R, R°); if the estimate holds at rank-one points with ε' < ε, it holds strictly there, and a strict inequality |u(y)| < |v(y)| with v(y) ≠ 0 at the rank-one generization y of x gives |u(x)| ≤ |v(x)| (u/v is topologically nilpotent in the completed residue field of y) (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(i)).
2. Reduction to f ∈ R° and c an integer: replace f by ϖ^k f and c by c + k; enlarging c only weakens the bound. Write f = g₀♯ + ϖg₁♯ + … + ϖ^c g_c♯ + ϖ^{c+1} f_{c+1} with g_j ∈ R♭° (successive approximation through R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); the term ϖ^{c+1}f_{c+1} does not affect the estimate, so assume f_{c+1} = 0.
3. Universal case: the continuous R-algebra map μ : P = R⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_c^{1/p^∞}⟩ → R, T_j^{1/p^m} ↦ (g_j^{1/p^m})♯ (universal property of the perfected Tate algebra, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples) sends the homogeneous degree-one element F = Σ ϖ^j T_j to f; its tilt μ♭ sends T_j to g_j (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality). PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc (base R₀ = R) gives G ∈ P♭° with the estimate for F on Spa(P, P°); pull it back along Spa(μ) : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(P, P°) using μ(G♯) = (μ♭(G))♯, and set g = μ♭(G).
4. (ii) (Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(2)): choose b with |h − b♯| < max(|h|, |ϖ^c|) and a with max(|f|, |ϖ^c|) = max(|a♯|, |ϖ^c|) by (i) (with ε < 1, the strict form following from ε < 1 and ε(c) > 0); the equality of the two sets is a case distinction with the strong triangle inequality: where |ϖ^c| ≤ |h|, |b♯| = |h|, and conversely.
5. Alternative proof without the polydisc: write R⁺ = W(R♭⁺)/(ξ) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals) and approximate a lift of f by a prepared Witt vector via Euclidean division by ξ (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(b); Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.9, 2.6.17).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: (ii) shows that every rational subset of X is τ⁻¹ of a rational subset of X♭, whence injectivity and openness
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7 (Frobenius-controlled towers): approximation of functions by sharps in tilde-limit arguments (Sch12 §7, 'the analogue of Lemma 6.5 holds true')
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/integral-approximation-of-generators: approximating local generators on rational subsets of perfectoid spaces

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Corollary 6.7(i) and Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(1) are the case of a perfectoid affinoid algebra over a perfectoid field K.
- For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and f = T + ϖ, g = T + ϖ♭ satisfies f ≡ g♯ modulo ϖR°, which is the estimate for c = 0; for c ≥ 1 the lemma provides g with {|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} = {|g♯| ≤ |ϖ^c|} (Sch12 Remark 6.6), a rational subset of X that is a preimage from X♭.
- Consequence consumed by the tilting homeomorphism: every rational subset of X is the preimage of a rational subset of X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, step 2).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc`](#p2-approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra`](#p2-tilting-map-of-spectra), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`](#p1-tilt-functoriality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`](#p1-untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.

<a id="p2-tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets` — The tilting homeomorphism Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) identifies rational subsets

*Theorem.* Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; no perfectoid base field) with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺). Then the tilting map τ_R : X = Spa(R, R⁺) → X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra), is a homeomorphism, natural in morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs. A subset U ⊆ X is rational if and only if τ_R(U) ⊆ X♭ is rational; explicitly, for f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, τ_R(U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)) = U(f₁, …, f_n / g), and every rational subset of X can be written as U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) for such f_i, g. Consequently τ_R preserves the specialisation order, quasi-compact opens and rank-one (maximal) points, and restricts, for every rational U ⊆ X, to a homeomorphism U ≅ τ_R(U) identifying rational subsets of U and of τ_R(U).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair; characteristic 0, p, or mixed (ECD Example 3.4(iv)).
- Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) and Corollary 6.7(iii) prove the statement over a perfectoid field; ECD Theorem 3.12 states it for perfectoid Tate rings, with the remark after Theorem 3.13 that the proof works in general; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.16 and Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.1 prove it for Fontaine perfectoid (Tate, resp. analytic) rings.

**Proof outline.**

1. Continuity and the preimage formula: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (b).
2. Every rational subset of X is a preimage: normalise U = U(h₁, …, h_n / h) with h_i, h ∈ R⁺ and h_n = ϖ^c (Tau Ceti `rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`, `rationalSubset_image_mul_right`); then U = ⋂_{i<n} {|h_i| ≤ |h|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |h|} (Tau Ceti `rationalSubset_inter`), and each set in the intersection is {|a_i♯| ≤ |b_i♯|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |b_i♯|} = τ⁻¹U(a_i, (ϖ♭)^c / b_i) by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma (ii) (Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(3)).
3. Injectivity: X is spectral (Tau Ceti instance `SpectralSpace (spa Aplus)`), hence T₀, and its rational subsets form a basis; since every rational subset is τ-saturated, two points with the same image lie in the same open sets and coincide (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(iii)).
4. Surjectivity: for y ∈ X♭ the completed residue affinoid field (k(y)^, k(y)^+) is perfect (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p: the O_{X♭}(V), V ∋ y, are perfect) and complete, hence a perfectoid field of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation). Untilt R♭ → k(y)^ over R: the tilting equivalence over R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) gives a perfectoid R-algebra L with L♭ ≅ k(y)^, a perfectoid field, and the open valuation ring L⁺ corresponding to k(y)^+ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting); the point x : R → L → Γ ∪ {0} lies in X and x♭ = y by naturality of ♯ (Sch12 proof of Corollary 6.7(iii): untilt the field, then the valuation).
5. Openness and rational images: by bijectivity and the preimage formula, τ(U(f♯/g♯)) = U(f/g); since every rational subset of X has this form, τ maps a basis of opens to opens and is a homeomorphism; a subset U ⊆ X is rational iff τ(U) is. The remaining assertions (specialisation, maximal points, restriction to rational U) are formal consequences of being a homeomorphism that preserves rational subsets, together with Tau Ceti's description of rational subsets of a rational subset (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2)).
6. Naturality: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra (c).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids: every rational subset of X is τ⁻¹ of a rational subset of X♭, so the untilted localisation lemma applies to all rational U
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity: a finite rational covering of U ⊆ X is transported to a finite rational covering of τ(U), with intersections
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: points of X and X♭ correspond, so residue fields can be compared
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting (P2b): |X| ≅ |X♭| glues to the underlying homeomorphism of the tilt of a perfectoid space
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity: X_ét ≅ X♭_ét starts from |X| ≅ |X♭| and rational subsets
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4, P5, P6: Zariski closed subsets, cofiltered limits and pro-étale maps are compared with their tilts through this homeomorphism
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1, D6: |X| = |X♭| for affinoid perfectoid X, and the diamond of Spa(R, R⁺) has underlying space |X♭|

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) (perfectoid affinoid K-algebras over a perfectoid field) is a special case.
- For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: τ({|T| ≤ |ϖ|}) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}, the Gauss point goes to the Gauss point, and the classical point T ↦ ϖ goes to T ↦ ϖ♭.
- The theorem applies to ECD Example 3.4(iv), R = Z_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p}, which lives over no field: its spectrum contains points with |p(x)| = 0 and points with |p(x)| ≠ 0, and both kinds are matched with points of the characteristic-p space X♭.
- Without the approximation lemma one only obtains that rational subsets of X are preimages of quasi-compact opens of X♭ (Bhatt Remark 9.2.8); the statement that images of rational subsets are rational needs the approximation lemma.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra`](#p2-tilting-map-of-spectra), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma`](#p2-approximation-lemma), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p`](#p2-rational-localization-in-characteristic-p), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`](#p1-tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`](#p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting`](#p1-continuous-valuations-under-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation`](#p1-perfectoid-field-characterisation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`](#p1-tilt-functoriality), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_inter`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`.
