<a id="p3-finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p` — Almost purity in characteristic p: finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (equivalently a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect; no base field), ϖ ∈ R a pseudouniformiser (it has all p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} in R°), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, and S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology and plus ring S⁺ = integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S is perfect, complete and uniform, hence a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, and (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair; (ii) S° is the integral closure of R° in S and S°/S⁺ is almost zero, so S°a = S⁺a; (iii) S°a is an almost finite étale R°a-algebra (almost finitely presented projective and unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S lies in (S°a ⊗_{R°a} S°a)_*); (iv) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° whose composite is multiplication by ε; (v) if S is faithfully flat over R, then Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° and R°a → S°a is almost faithfully flat and almost split. The statement specialises to Scholze 2012 Proposition 5.23 for R a perfectoid K-algebra, K a perfectoid field of characteristic p, and to the finite separable extensions of a perfectoid field of characteristic p.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfect, complete, Tate, characteristic p; no perfectoid base field.
- Almost mathematics for the basic setup (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), equivalently the ideal (ϖ^{1/p^∞}); almost finite étale in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras (Gabber–Ramero §3.1).
- Not claimed: S° finite, flat or étale over R°; S free over R.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): S is perfect by P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect; complete Tate with its natural topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) and uniform (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform; alternatively PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform, S being perfect and complete); perfect complete uniform Tate rings of characteristic p are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect); (S, S⁺) is a Huber pair by A1.
2. (ii): S° = integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b)); S°° ⊆ S⁺ since S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
3. (iii) unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S satisfies ϖ^N e ∈ im(S° ⊗_{R°} S°) for some N; as Frobenius is bijective on S° ⊗_{R°} S° (both perfect), ϖ^{N/p^m} e ∈ im(S° ⊗ S°) for every m, so e is an almost element (Scholze 2012 proof of 5.23; Bhatt Proposition 4.3.4).
4. (iv): write ϖ^N e = Σ_{i=1}^n x_i ⊗ y_i with x_i, y_i ∈ S°; then ϖ^{N/p^m} e = Σ x_i^{1/p^m} ⊗ y_i^{1/p^m} with the same n. For a finite étale algebra and e = Σ a_i ⊗ b_i one has Σ_i Tr_{S/R}(f a_i) b_i = f (Bhatt Construction 4.3.3: Tr of the diagonal factor is 1), so s ↦ (Tr(s x_i^{1/p^m}))_i, (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i y_i^{1/p^m} are maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° (Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c)) composing to ϖ^{N/p^m}: uniform almost finite projectivity. Almost finitely presented projective with an almost idempotent is almost finite étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).
5. (v): Tr(S) = R for faithfully flat S, so ϖ^c = Tr(f) with f ∈ S°; compatibility of the trace with Frobenius gives ϖ^{c/p^n} = Tr(f^{1/p^n}) with f^{1/p^n} ∈ S°, whence R°° ⊆ Tr(S°°) up to almost zero and R°a → S°a is almost split (Bhatt Remark 4.3.5).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence: essential surjectivity of A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹]
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor: the characteristic-p leg of the untilting functor
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: the characteristic-p case
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: in characteristic p étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale

**Acceptance.**

- Reviewer-authored test (no source example): for K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ and the Artin–Schreier extension S = K[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1}), S is a perfectoid field and S°a is finite étale and uniformly almost finite projective (n = p) over K°a; S° is not finite free over K° at any finite level, and this is not claimed.
- The bound n on the number of generators is independent of ε (uniformity); for S of constant rank d one can take n = d², and n = d after localising where S is free.
- A non-field instance: R = 𝔽_p[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] (the characteristic-p analogue of ECD Example 3.4(iv)) and S = R[u]/(u^p − u − T^{-1}): the theorem applies without any perfectoid base field.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`](#p3-etale-over-perfect-is-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform`](#p3-finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform`](#p1-perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobenius`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/CharP

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §5, Proposition 5.23, p. 28. The statement over a perfectoid field; the proof uses no property of the field beyond ϖ^{1/p^∞}.
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Proposition 4.3.4, p. 27. Bhatt's primitive version for arbitrary perfect rings R and t ∈ R (here t = ϖ): no base field.

<a id="p3-characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence` — Characteristic p: inverting ϖ is an equivalence between almost finite étale R°a-algebras and finite étale R-algebras

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser ϖ. Let (R°a)_afet be the category of almost finite étale R°a-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). Then the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* the ring of almost elements, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints), with its natural topology, is an equivalence of categories, compatible with tensor products; a quasi-inverse is S ↦ S°a. Moreover every A ∈ (R°a)_afet is uniformly almost finite projective, A_* is perfect, ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete, and A_* is the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; almost faithful flatness of A corresponds to faithful flatness of A_*[ϖ⁻¹].

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfect complete Tate of characteristic p; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).
- This is Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.28 for V = R°, ε = ϖ (V perfect, m = ∪ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}V).

**Proof outline.**

1. Well defined: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective over R (almost finite projective modules become finite projective after inverting ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and unramified (the almost idempotent becomes an idempotent), hence finite étale.
2. Essential surjectivity: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] with S°a ∈ (R°a)_afet by P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p.
3. Full faithfulness (Bhatt Lemma 4.3.7): A ≅ T^a for T the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]. A is perfect (the almost version of P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect, almost finite étale maps being weakly étale), so A_* is perfect; ϖ is a non-zero-divisor on A_* (almost flatness). For f ∈ T, the R-span of f^ℕ lies in ϖ^{-c}A_*, so ϖ^{c/pⁿ} f ∈ A_* for all n by perfectness, i.e. f ∈ A_*; conversely almost finite generation gives ϖ g^ℕ ⊆ ϖ^{-c}T, whence g ∈ T_*. As T is functorial in the R-algebra A_*[ϖ⁻¹], the functor is fully faithful.
4. Uniformity and completeness: P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv) for S = A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; A_* = S° is ϖ-adically complete.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor: FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence: the characteristic-p case

**Acceptance.**

- R = K a perfectoid field of characteristic p: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) ≃ finite products of finite separable extensions L, via L ↦ L°a.
- Degenerate: A = R°a ↦ R, A = 0 ↦ 0, A = (R°a)ⁿ ↦ Rⁿ.
- Non-example of the integral statement: the functor from finite étale R°-algebras (honest, not almost) to FÉt(R) is not essentially surjective — the Artin–Schreier cover of 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ has no finite étale model over the valuation ring.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`](#p3-finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`](#p3-etale-over-perfect-is-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`](#p0-almost-hom-and-adjoints), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

<a id="p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor` — The untilting functor on finite étale algebras, T ↦ T♯, via almost finite étale integral structures

*Construction.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) and choose a pseudouniformiser ϖ♭ ∈ R♭ with ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯ satisfying ϖ^p | p in R° (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), so that R♭°/ϖ♭ = R°/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Define the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) as the composite FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), T ↦ T°a ↦ T°a/ϖ♭ ↦ A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] =: T♯, where the first equivalence is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence, the middle equivalence is the unique flat deformation of almost finite étale algebras along the ϖ-adically complete flat R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), and the last functor inverts ϖ (natural module topology on T♯). Properties: T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring, finite étale over R, with a canonical isomorphism (T♯)♭ ≅ T of R♭-algebras (so (−)♯ is inverse to tilting on its image; compatible with the untilting of perfectoid algebras of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt); (T♯)°a = A is almost finite étale over R°a; the functor is independent of ϖ♭ up to canonical isomorphism, preserves tensor products, finite products, ranks (rank of T♯ at x ∈ Spa R equals the rank of T at x♭) and faithful flatness; and it commutes with base change along every map of perfectoid Tate rings R → R' (for example a rational localisation or the completed residue field at a point): (T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'. Equivalently (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 3.6.20, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.10) T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ for a generator ξ of ker(θ: W(R♭⁺) → R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction), which shows finite étaleness without almost mathematics.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.
- ϖ♭ with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p; different choices give canonically isomorphic functors.

**Proof outline.**

1. Middle identification: the categories of almost finite étale algebras over R♭°a/ϖ♭ and R°a/ϖ coincide because the rings coincide (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings) and R♭°a = R♭⁺a, R°a = R⁺a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
2. Lifting: R°a is flat over the basic setup and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary), so reduction modulo ϖ is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 5.3.27), and the lift A is flat and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete).
3. Perfectoidness and tilt: A/ϖ = T°a/ϖ♭ is a perfectoid (R°a/ϖ)-algebra (relative Frobenius isomorphism, P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect (b)); A is its unique flat deformation, hence a perfectoid R°a-algebra, and A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is a perfectoid R-algebra whose tilt has the same reduction modulo ϖ♭, i.e. is T (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).
4. Finite étale: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective and unramified after inverting ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
5. Base change: each step commutes with base change along R°a → R'°a (flat deformations are unique, reduction modulo ϖ and inverting ϖ commute with tensor products); the tilt of R → R' is R♭ → R'♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality).
6. Ranks: the rank of an almost finite projective module is read off modulo ϖ and after inverting ϖ, and Spa R ≅ Spa R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets).

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt` (constructor): The functor CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R♭ ⥤ CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R, T ↦ T♯.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_isPerfectoid` (instance): T♯ with its natural topology is a perfectoid Tate ring.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.tiltUntiltIso` (equivalence): (T♯)♭ ≅ T naturally in T.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_almostFiniteEtale` (projection): (T♯)°a is almost finite étale over R°a, uniformly almost finite projective.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltBaseChangeIso` (functoriality): For a map of perfectoid Tate rings R → R', (T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_rank` (simp): rank_x(T♯) = rank_{x♭}(T) for x ∈ Spa R.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltTensorIso` (structure): (T₁ ⊗ T₂)♯ ≅ T₁♯ ⊗ T₂♯ (monoidal functor).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_faithfullyFlat_iff` (characterisation): T♯ is faithfully flat over R iff T is faithfully flat over R♭.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltIsoWitt` (compatibility): T♯ ≅ W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ with ξ a generator of ker θ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_independent` (other): Different choices of ϖ♭ give canonically isomorphic functors.

**Unit tests.**

- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_self` (degenerate): untilt R (R♭ as a finite étale R♭-algebra) ≅ R, and untilt 0 = 0, untilt (T₁ × T₂) ≅ untilt T₁ × untilt T₂.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_quadratic` (computation): For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t♯ = p and p odd: untilt (K♭[u]/(u² − t)) ≅ K[u]/(u² − p).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_tilt` (compatibility): tilt (untilt T) ≅ T as R♭-algebras, and untilt T agrees with PerfectoidSpaces:P1's untilt of the perfectoid R♭-algebra T.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_mod_varpi` (characterisation): untilt T is the unique finite étale R-algebra S with (S°a)/ϖ ≅ (T°a)/ϖ♭ as (R°a/ϖ)-algebras.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_not_basechange` (non-example): There is no ring map R♭ → R along which untilt T = T ⊗ R: the sharp map is multiplicative but not additive, and for R = ℚ_p^cycl the untilt of the Artin–Schreier extension is not obtained by substituting ♯ into an equation.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the functor whose full faithfulness is proved
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence: untilting the local finite étale algebras T_U over O(U♭)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: untilting finite extensions of K♭
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 5.25: the fully faithful functor R♭_fét → R_fét
- Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 3.6.21 / AWS Lemma 2.8.11: the untilting functor whose essential surjectivity is the tilting equivalence

**Acceptance.**

- The untilt of R♭ is R, of R♭ × R♭ is R × R, of 0 is 0.
- For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p, and p odd: the untilt of K♭(t^{1/2}) is K(p^{1/2}) (Bhatt Example 3.2.9).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`](#p3-characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`](#p3-etale-over-perfect-is-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete`](#p0-finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`](#p1-almost-integral-dictionary), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`](#p1-tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`](#p1-tilt-functoriality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction`](#p1-untilt-construction), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`](#p2-tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 6, §6.2, construction of functors after Theorem 6.2.10, p. 49. Bhatt constructs the same chain of functors (a)–(d).

<a id="p3-tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful` — The untilting functor FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) is fully faithful, inverse to tilting on its image, with image the S having almost finite étale integral structure

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field). The untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is fully faithful and, on its essential image, inverse to tilting: for S = T♯, S is perfectoid and S♭ ≅ T. Its essential image consists exactly of the finite étale R-algebras S such that S (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a; for such S, S°a is uniformly almost finite projective over R°a. The functor preserves degrees (rank functions), tensor products and faithful flatness. For R = K a perfectoid field this is the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; for R of characteristic p (R♭ = R) it is the identity.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No claim of essential surjectivity here; that is P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence (ECD 6.1(ii)).
- Neither étaleness of S° over R° nor freeness of S over R is asserted or needed.

**Proof outline.**

1. Full faithfulness: each functor in the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor except the last is an equivalence; the last, (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹], is fully faithful because A_* is recovered functorially as the total integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* is the power-bounded subring of the perfectoid, uniform A_*[ϖ⁻¹], PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; almost finite generation gives the reverse inclusion; Bhatt, proof of Theorem 6.2.10, functor (d)).
2. Image: T♯ has the stated properties (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor). Conversely, if S ∈ FÉt(R) is perfectoid with S°a almost finite étale, then S°a/ϖ is almost finite étale over R°a/ϖ = R♭°a/ϖ♭; let T := the characteristic-p finite étale algebra with T°a/ϖ♭ ≅ S°a/ϖ (P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence and PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras on the tilt side); uniqueness of flat lifts gives S°a ≅ (T♯)°a and S ≅ T♯.
3. Uniformity: uniform almost finite projectivity lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi, for the root setup of ϖ^{1/p^∞}) from the characteristic-p case (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)).
4. Degrees, tensor products, faithful flatness: P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence: full faithfulness over O(U) and O(U_ij) in the gluing
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: full faithfulness over K
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: Sch12 5.25 for the completed tower

**Acceptance.**

- For R = K a perfectoid field this gives a fully faithful, degree-preserving functor FÉt(K♭) → FÉt(K), the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; when K♭ is algebraically closed its image is all of FÉt(K) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and T = R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − t) (ℓ ≠ p prime, t♯ = T): T♯ ≅ R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), a Kummer cover, in the image with S°a almost finite étale.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`](#p3-characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`](#p3-finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi`](#p0-uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`](#p1-almost-integral-dictionary), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §5, Theorem 5.25, p. 29. The statement over a perfectoid field; the proof uses only R°a, ϖ and Scholze's Theorem 4.17 (= PerfectoidSpaces:P0 lifting).
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 6, proof of Theorem 6.2.10 over a field, p. 49. Full faithfulness and degree preservation of untilting.

<a id="p3-untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field` — If the tilt of a perfectoid field is algebraically closed, so is the field

*Lemma.* Let K be a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) with tilt K♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field). If K♭ is algebraically closed (Mathlib `IsAlgClosed K♭`), then K is algebraically closed.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid field of any characteristic (in characteristic p, K♭ = K and the statement is trivial).

**Proof outline.**

1. Let P ∈ K°[X] be monic irreducible of degree d ≥ 1. The Newton polygon of P is a line (P irreducible over the complete field K, unique extension of the absolute value: Mathlib `spectralNorm`), and as |K^×| = |K♭^×| is divisible (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) one may rescale so that |a₀| = 1.
2. Choose Q ∈ K♭°[X] monic with the same image in K°/ϖ[X] = K♭°/ϖ♭[X] (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field) and a root y ∈ K♭° of Q (K♭ algebraically closed). Then P(y♯) ≡ 0 modulo ϖ (sharp map, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).
3. P(X + y♯) is irreducible with constant term P(y♯); rescale P₁(X) = c^{-d}P(cX + y♯) with |c|^d = |P(y♯)| ≤ |ϖ|, integral again by the straight Newton polygon; iterate to get a Cauchy sequence x_n with |P(x_n)| ≤ |ϖ|ⁿ converging to a root of P (Scholze 2012 Proposition 3.8; Kedlaya's argument in Bhatt Proposition 3.2.10).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: the untilt of the completed algebraic closure of K♭ is algebraically closed

**Acceptance.**

- The completed algebraic closure ℂ_p of ℚ_p is algebraically closed, with tilt ℂ_p♭ algebraically closed; this lemma recovers the first from the second.
- The converse also holds (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), `mathlib:IsAlgClosed`, `mathlib:spectralNorm`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §3, Proposition 3.8, p. 17. The statement ('K [' is the extraction's K♭).
- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §3, proof of Proposition 3.8, p. 18. The approximation argument.
- [`Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017`](#source-p0-bhatt-perfectoidnotes-2017), Chapter 3, Proposition 3.2.10, p. 14. The same statement with Kedlaya's proof.

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p3-finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields` — Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid, and tilting is a degree-preserving equivalence of finite extensions

*Theorem.* Let K be a perfectoid field (characteristic 0 or p) with tilt K♭. (i) Every finite extension L/K, with its natural topology (the unique extension of the absolute value, Mathlib `spectralNorm`), is a perfectoid field. (ii) The untilting functor (−)♯ of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is an equivalence FÉt(K♭) ≃ FÉt(K) with quasi-inverse L ↦ L♭; it restricts to an equivalence between finite field extensions of K♭ and of K, preserving degrees, automorphism groups and Galois extensions. (iii) K is algebraically closed if and only if K♭ is. (iv) For every finite extension L/K, L°a is almost finite étale over K°a (Tate, Gabber–Ramero §6.6 for deeply ramified fields), uniformly almost finite projective.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid field; finite extensions carry their natural topology; finite étale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`).
- An alternative, ramification-theoretic proof (Gabber–Ramero Propositions 6.6.2 and 6.6.6: L°a/K°a étale for deeply ramified K; 6.3.6: finite projectivity) is not the route planned here.

**Proof outline.**

1. Characteristic p: (i) and (iv) are P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p for R = K; (ii) is the identity; (iii) trivial.
2. (ii) full faithfulness and degrees: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for R = K.
3. Essential surjectivity: let M be the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭ (perfect and complete, hence a perfectoid field); its untilt M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) is a perfectoid field over K (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field: R is a perfectoid field iff R♭ is) and algebraically closed (P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field).
4. The union N ⊆ M♯ of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭ is a subfield algebraic over K and dense in M♯ (M is the completed colimit of the perfectoid fields L, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ over K, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (c), and the colimit of the L♯ is dense in it, (a)); by Krasner's lemma (Mathlib `IsKrasner.of_completeSpace`, applied over finite subextensions of N/K, which are complete) N is separably closed; as K has characteristic 0 in this step, every finite extension F/K is separable and embeds in some L♯ with L/K♭ finite Galois.
5. L♯/K is Galois with Gal(L♯/K) ≅ Gal(L/K♭) (untilting preserves degrees and automorphisms); F = (L♯)^H for a subgroup H, and F♭ := L^H satisfies (F♭)♯ ⊆ (L♯)^H = F with equal degrees, so F is an untilt. General finite étale K-algebras are finite products of such F.
6. (i): F ≅ (F♭)♯ is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) and a field; its topology is the natural one (finite-dimensional K-vector space).
7. (iii): if K♭ is algebraically closed, apply P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field; if K is, every finite extension of K♭ untilts to a finite extension of K of the same degree, hence is trivial, so K♭ (perfect) is algebraically closed.
8. (iv): L is in the essential image of (−)♯, so L°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence: the field case at each completed residue field
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger: Galois groups
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: ℂ_p♭ algebraically closed

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ and 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ have equivalent categories of finite extensions (P3/fontaine-wintenberger).
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd), L is perfectoid, L♭ is a quadratic extension of K♭, and L°a/K°a is almost finite étale although L°/K° is ramified (the different of K(p^{1/2p^n})/K_n has valuation 1/(2pⁿ) → 0, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).
- Non-example: ℚ_p is not perfectoid and its finite extensions are not either (discretely valued, ECD Remark 3.3); the theorem needs K perfectoid.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`](#p3-tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field`](#p3-untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`](#p3-finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`](#p1-perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`](#p1-tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings`](#p1-completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings), `mathlib:IsKrasner.of_completeSpace`, `mathlib:spectralNorm.nontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`, `mathlib:IsGalois`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §3, Theorem 3.7 (i), p. 17. Statement (i).
- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §3, Theorem 3.7 (ii), p. 17. Statement (ii).

<a id="p3-cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension` — The completed cyclotomic extension of a finite extension of ℚ_p is perfectoid

*Lemma.* Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p inside a fixed algebraic closure, and C its completion. The closure L of K(μ_{p^∞}) in C is a perfectoid field: L = K·ℚ_p^cycl is the compositum of K with the completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), a finite extension of ℚ_p^cycl of degree at most [K : ℚ_p], and K(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in it. Its tilt is the finite extension of (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ corresponding to L under the tilting equivalence of finite extensions.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K a finite extension of ℚ_p; no ramification hypothesis.
- The perfectoid condition is checked once, for ℚ_p^cycl (P1), and transported along the finite extension L/ℚ_p^cycl by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.

**Proof outline.**

1. K·ℚ_p^cycl is a finite extension of the complete field ℚ_p^cycl (generated by a primitive element of K over ℚ_p), hence complete for the unique extension of the absolute value; so it is closed in C.
2. K(μ_{p^∞}) = K·ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in K·ℚ_p^cycl: ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in ℚ_p^cycl and K·ℚ_p^cycl = Σ K·ℚ_p^cycl over a K-basis, so L = K·ℚ_p^cycl.
3. ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); a finite extension of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field and tilting matches finite extensions (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (i), (ii)).

**Uses.**

- AdicSpacesPartII:R5: request (b) of AdicSpacesPartII to PerfectoidSpaces P1: the completed cyclotomic field of a finite K/ℚ_p as a perfectoid base for coefficient algebras and weight spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field: the case K = ℚ_p, proved directly in P1

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p this is ℚ_p^cycl itself.
- For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}), L = ℚ_p^cycl(p^{1/p}) is a perfectoid field of degree p over ℚ_p^cycl (a Kummer extension: p^{1/p} ∉ ℚ_p^cycl because ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p is abelian and ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) is not Galois over ℚ_p), while K itself is not perfectoid.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field`](#p1-cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`](#p3-finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension`.

<a id="p3-completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed` — The completed tensor product of plus rings need not be integrally closed

*Lemma.* Let K be a perfectoid field with algebraically closed residue field, for instance the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) with ℚ̆_p the completion of the maximal unramified extension of ℚ_p, let ℓ be a prime with ℓ ∤ p(p − 1), and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), a cyclic Galois extension of degree ℓ which is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields) with trivial residue extension. With A = K, B = C = L and plus rings the rings of integers, D = L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ and D⁺ = (L°)^ℓ, while L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ is injective and not surjective. So the map from the ϖ-adic completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ to D⁺ in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) is an almost isomorphism that is not an isomorphism, and the completed tensor product of plus rings is not integrally closed in D, hence not a ring of integral elements.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid with algebraically closed residue field; ℓ a prime not dividing p(p − 1).
- The perfectoidness of L is the finite-extension theorem of this layer; the rest is the formula of P2.

**Proof outline.**

1. (iv) K contains μ_ℓ (Hensel's lemma over the algebraically closed residue field) and p^{1/ℓ} ∉ K (1/ℓ is not in the value group (p − 1)⁻¹ℤ[1/p]), so L/K is cyclic of degree ℓ and L ⊗_K L ≅ L^ℓ, a ⊗ b ↦ (a g(b))_g. As the value group of K is dense, 𝔪_K L° = 𝔪_L, so L°/𝔪_K L° is the residue field of L, which equals that of K. If L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ (injective, the source being K°-flat) were surjective, K° → L° would be a Galois extension of rings with group Gal(L/K), hence L° would be finite projective, thus free, of rank ℓ over the local ring K°, contradicting dim L°/𝔪_K L° = 1.
2. The formula of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) identifies D⁺ with (L°)^ℓ up to the almost isomorphism, which is therefore not an isomorphism.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces: the plus ring of a fibre product is the completed integral closure, not the completed tensor product of plus rings
- Kedlaya AWS notes, proof of Lemma 2.8.7: the counterexample to its plus-ring claim, recorded as a source issue

**Acceptance.**

- The example with K the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), ℓ ∤ p(p − 1).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula`](#p2-completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p2-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`](#p3-finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CompletedTensor

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017`](#source-p0-kedlaya-awsnotes-2017), §2.8, proof of Lemma 2.8.7, p. 71. The plus-ring claim this example refutes: the completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is D⁺ only up to almost isomorphism (see sourceIssues).

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p3-fontaine-wintenberger"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger` — Fontaine–Wintenberger: the absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and of its tilt are isomorphic

*Theorem.* Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K♭. Fix an algebraic closure K̄ of K with completion C, so that C♭ is an algebraically closed perfectoid field containing K♭ (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)), and let K♭^sep be the separable closure of K♭ in C♭. Then L ↦ L♭ (for finite Galois L/K inside K̄, with L♭ ⊆ C♭ by functoriality of tilting) defines an isomorphism of profinite groups Gal(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K♭^sep/K♭) (Mathlib `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` up to the choice of closures), compatible with the Galois correspondences (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`): finite subextensions of K̄/K correspond to finite subextensions of K♭^sep/K♭ with the same degrees. Application (Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1): the absolute Galois groups of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and of 𝔽_p((t)) are canonically isomorphic; this uses in addition that an algebraic extension F of a complete field and its completion F̂ have the same absolute Galois group (FÉt(F) ≃ FÉt(F̂), F° being henselian: P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b)), and that 𝔽_p((t)) → 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) is purely inseparable (Frobenius twists do not change finite étale algebras, P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K perfectoid field; closures fixed as described; continuity is part of the claim (isomorphism of profinite groups).

**Proof outline.**

1. For finite Galois L/K ⊆ K̄, L is perfectoid and L♭/K♭ is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ Gal(L♭/K♭) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii): equivalence preserving degrees and automorphisms).
2. The embeddings: L ⊆ C induces L♭ ⊆ C♭, landing in K♭^sep (L♭ is separable over K♭); every finite separable extension of K♭ inside C♭ arises (essential surjectivity), and inclusions correspond.
3. Gal(K̄/K) = lim_L Gal(L/K) over finite Galois subextensions (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.algEquivToLimit`), likewise for K♭; the isomorphisms of the finite quotients are compatible with restriction (functoriality), so their limit is an isomorphism of profinite groups.
4. Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_K for K its completion, and G_{𝔽_p((t))} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{K♭} (completion and purely inseparable extension), then apply the main statement with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p.

**Uses.**

- PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: G_K acting through G_{K♭}

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}.
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})), G_K ≅ G_{K♭} with K♭ ≅ 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t = ε − 1 for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ K♭°: the Fontaine–Wintenberger field-of-norms isomorphism.
- Consequence: for C algebraically closed perfectoid, Spa(C, C⁺) and Spa(C♭, C♭⁺) both have trivial finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`](#p3-finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`](#p3-henselian-finite-etale-approximation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection`](#p3-finite-etale-under-completed-perfection), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-field), `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`, `mathlib:InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`, `mathlib:InfiniteGalois.algEquivToLimit`, `mathlib:IsGalois`, `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2. The application (the extraction drops the superscript ∞ of p^{1/p^∞}).
- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §1, discussion after Theorem 1.1, p. 2. The reduction to the completions, whose justification is spelled out in this node.
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.3, Theorem 7.3.1 (2), p. 50. The Galois-group consequence.

<a id="p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence` — Tilting is an equivalence between finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring and over its tilt (ECD 6.1(ii))

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭. Then the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse the tilting functor S ↦ S♭ (S being perfectoid). It is compatible with tensor products, with base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings (in particular rational localisations and completed residue fields), and preserves ranks and faithful flatness. For every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R° with tilt R♭⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), it induces an equivalence between finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) and (R♭, R♭⁺) → (S♭, S♭⁺) (plus rings the integral closures; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), i.e. between finite étale affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(R, R⁺) and over Spa(R♭, R♭⁺).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.
- The gluing uses rational coverings of Spa(R, R⁺) and the effective descent of finite étale algebras along them (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent), which needs no sheafiness; the sheaf property of O is not used.

**Proof outline.**

1. Full faithfulness: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful.
2. Local essential surjectivity: fix S ∈ FÉt(R), X = Spa(R, R⁺), x ∈ X. The completed residue field k(x)^ is a perfectoid field with tilt k(x♭)^ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). By P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii), S ⊗_R k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ for some T_x ∈ FÉt(k(x♭)^). By P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X♭ there are a rational U♭ ∋ x♭ and T_U ∈ FÉt(O_{X♭}(U♭)) with T_U ⊗ k(x♭)^ ≅ T_x; U♭ is the tilt of a rational U ∋ x with O_X(U) perfectoid of tilt O_{X♭}(U♭) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
3. Then (T_U)♯ ∈ FÉt(O_X(U)) satisfies (T_U)♯ ⊗ k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ ≅ S ⊗ k(x)^ (base change compatibility of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor); by the full faithfulness half of P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X, after shrinking U, (T_U)♯ ≅ S ⊗_R O_X(U).
4. Quasi-compactness of X (anchor Layer 2) gives a finite rational covering X = ∪ U_i with T_i ∈ FÉt(O(U_i♭)) and φ_i: T_i♯ ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i). On the rational U_ij = U_i ∩ U_j, φ_j⁻¹ ∘ φ_i descends uniquely to T_i ⊗ O(U_ij♭) ≅ T_j ⊗ O(U_ij♭) (full faithfulness over the perfectoid O(U_ij), whose tilt is O(U_ij♭)); the cocycle condition holds by faithfulness over U_ijk.
5. Glue: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent on X♭ gives T ∈ FÉt(R♭) with T ⊗ O(U_i♭) ≅ T_i compatibly; then T♯ ⊗ O(U_i) ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i) compatibly on overlaps, and the full faithfulness of descent on X gives T♯ ≅ S.
6. Quasi-inverse: T♯ is perfectoid with (T♯)♭ ≅ T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor), so S ↦ S♭ is quasi-inverse. Plus rings: the integral closure of R⁺ in S tilts to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭, both being the elements of absolute value ≤ 1 at the points over Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid: every S is an untilt
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: tilting of finite étale maps
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale: finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings

**Acceptance.**

- For R = K a perfectoid field this is P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩): the finite étale R-algebras are the untilts of finite étale algebras over the characteristic-p ring; e.g. the Kummer cover R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), ℓ ≠ p, is the untilt of R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − T♭).
- The non-field example of ECD Example 3.4(iv), R = ℤ_p^cycl⟦T^{1/p^∞}⟧⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T], is covered: no base field is used.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`](#p3-tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`](#p3-finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`](#p3-residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`](#p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`](#p2-tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

<a id="p3-finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid` — Finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid (ECD 6.1(i))

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) and S a finite étale R-algebra (Mathlib `Module.Finite R S`, `Algebra.Etale R S`) with its natural topology as a finite R-module. Then S is a perfectoid Tate ring; S ≅ (S♭)♯ with S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); for every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R°, with S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S (the finite étale pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S` of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair whose tilt (S♭, S♭⁺) has S♭⁺ the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭. Consequently Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is a finite étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces. This serves AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.5(1), Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 2.15(a)).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale as a ring; the topology on S is the natural module topology (complete, since S is finite projective).

**Proof outline.**

1. By P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S ≅ T♯ for T := S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor).
2. The natural topology on S agrees with the topology of T♯ (both are the natural finite R-module topology; any R-linear isomorphism of finite projective modules is a homeomorphism).
3. Plus rings: as in the last step of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S⁺ corresponds to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭ under PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.
4. (S, S⁺) is sheafy (perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so Spa(S, S⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space finite étale over Spa(R, R⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism).

**Uses.**

- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale: R̃ ⊗_R S is perfectoid for R̃ perfectoid and S finite étale (the AdicSpacesPartII request)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale: adic spaces finite étale over perfectoid spaces are perfectoid
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids: preimages of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: a rational subset of a finite étale space over a perfectoid is perfectoid

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and S = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): S is a perfectoid field (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R[u]/(u² − (1 + pT)) (p odd; étale since 1 + pT is a unit and 2 is invertible): S is perfectoid.
- Non-example (why étale matters): S = R[u]/(u²) is finite but not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid; S = R[u]/(u² − p) over R = ℚ_p^cycl is finite étale and perfectoid, but the analogous extension ℚ_p(√p) of the non-perfectoid ℚ_p is not perfectoid.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`](#p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`](#p2-perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1 (i), p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). The statement for an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring.
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.4.5, and its sketch, p. 53. (1) is deduced from (2): every S is an untilt.

<a id="p3-almost-finite-etale-equivalence"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence` — Almost purity, categorical form: (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) by inverting ϖ, compatibly with tilting

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p, and R⁺ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then: (a) the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (natural topology), is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse S ↦ S°a = S⁺a, compatible with tensor products and base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings; (b) the six categories FÉt(R) ≃ (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet ≃ (R♭°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R♭) of Scholze's diagram are equivalent by the functors of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor, and the composite is the tilting equivalence of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence; (c) (R⁺a)_afet = (R°a)_afet, since R⁺a = R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup; ECD Definition 3.23). In Bhatt's notation: inverting p (resp. t) gives R°a_afet ≃ R_fet (resp. S°a_afet ≃ S_fet) and tilting gives R°a_afet ≃ S°a_afet for S = R♭.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).

**Proof outline.**

1. Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is T♯ for some T (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), so S°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the essential image consists of S with almost finite étale S°a).
2. A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is fully faithful (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful, proof) and essentially surjective: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] since (S°a)_* = S° for perfectoid S (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; S perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).
3. (b): each functor of the chain is an equivalence: P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence on the tilt side, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras for the two reductions modulo ϖ, (a) on the untilt side.
4. (c): S⁺ ⊆ S° with S°/S⁺ almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii) applied to the perfectoid S).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale: the objectwise statement
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity: (S ⊗_R S)°a = S°a ⊗ S°a for the Čech complex of a finite étale cover
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations: Ô^{+a}(W̃) as a completed tensor product via almost purity
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: almost faithfully flat descent of the almost finite étale integral structures

**Acceptance.**

- R = K a perfectoid field: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) via L ↦ L°a (Berkeley Theorem 7.3.2 and the diagram following it).
- Characteristic p: this is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence (Gabber–Ramero 3.5.28).
- Non-example: the analogous functor on honest (non-almost) finite étale R°-algebras is not essentially surjective: over K = ℚ_p^cycl, K(p^{1/2})° is not étale over K°.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`](#p3-tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p3-finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`](#p3-characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`](#p1-almost-integral-dictionary), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

<a id="p3-integral-closure-almost-finite-etale"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale` — The integral closure is almost finite étale: S° over R° for S finite étale over a perfectoid Tate ring R (ECD 6.1(iii))

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, ϖ a pseudouniformiser, S ∈ FÉt(R) and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S° is the integral closure of R° in S, S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S°, and S°a = S⁺a is an almost finite étale R°a = R⁺a-algebra: almost finitely presented, almost projective, and unramified (the diagonal idempotent of S ⊗_R S is an almost element of S° ⊗_{R°} S°); (ii) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° composing to multiplication by ε; (iii) Tr_{S/R}(S°) ⊆ R° and the trace pairing induces an almost isomorphism S°a → alHom_{R°a}(S°a, R°a); (iv) if S is faithfully flat over R, S°a is almost faithfully flat over R°a, Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° (up to almost zero), and R°a → S°a is almost split. Not claimed, and false in general: S° finite, flat or étale over R°, or S free over R.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence, S ≅ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] with A almost finite étale and A = S°a; S° is the integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b), S being uniform); S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S° as S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
2. (ii): uniformity holds in characteristic p (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)) and lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi) through the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.
3. (iii): an almost finite projective algebra is almost finite étale iff its trace pairing is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 4.1.14); Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c).
4. (iv): faithful flatness of S is positivity of ranks, preserved by tilting; in characteristic p, R°a → S°a is almost split with trace surjective onto R°° (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (v)); reduce modulo ϖ and lift: almost splitting modulo ϖ of an almost projective map lifts, and trace surjectivity is checked modulo ϖ by Nakayama for the ϖ-adically complete R°.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids: every finite étale map of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity: almost faithful flatness of O⁺ along finite étale covers
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations: Ô_Y⁺(U) almost flat over the perfectoid base
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: descent of the integral structure S⁺a

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): L°a is almost finite étale over K°a though L°/K° is ramified; the trace of L° contains every element of positive valuation (Tate's computation, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).
- Kedlaya–Liu's formulation: o_B is uniformly almost finite projective and almost étale over o_A for B ∈ FÉt(A), A perfectoid (Theorem 5.5.9); Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.24: Tr: B°° → A°° surjective for B faithfully finite étale.
- For R of characteristic p this is P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`](#p3-almost-finite-etale-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform`](#p3-finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`](#p3-finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`](#p3-finite-etale-untilting-functor), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`](#p0-finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`](#p0-almost-flat-projective-finiteness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion`](#p0-trace-form-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi`](#p0-uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:integralClosure`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1 (iii), p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). The statement for an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring.
- [`KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015`](#source-p0-kedlayaliu-relativefoundations-2015), §5.5, Theorem 5.5.9, p. 133. Uniform almost finite projectivity (ii) and almost étaleness, for perfectoid ℚ_p-algebras.
- [`KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015`](#source-p0-kedlayaliu-relativefoundations-2015), §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132. The factorisation form of (ii).

<a id="p3-almost-purity-theorem"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem` — The almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Theorem 6.1)

*Theorem.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1; characteristic 0, p, or neither; no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭, and FÉt(R) the category of finite étale R-algebras with their natural topologies. (i) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid). (ii) Tilting S ↦ S♭ is an equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭), with quasi-inverse the untilting functor (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence). (iii) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S° is almost finite étale over R° (equivalently S⁺a over R⁺a for any ring of integral elements and S⁺ its integral closure), and uniformly almost finite projective (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale); categorically, A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence). The three conclusions are distinct statements: (iii) is about the integral structure up to almost zero and is neither étaleness of S° over R° nor finite freeness of S over R. Consequences recorded elsewhere: every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale); for R = K a perfectoid field, (i)–(iii) are P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid.
2. (ii): P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.
3. (iii): P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale, with the categorical form P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence.
4. The declaration bundles the three conclusions as consumers cite them (ECD Theorem 6.1).

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: v-descent of (finite) étale maps rests on (i)–(iii)
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: finite étale covers of the perfectoid tower
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations: almost purity for Ô⁺
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: étale over perfectoid is perfectoid
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: almost purity and the finite étale site
- VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3: pro-étale local systems rest on almost purity

**Acceptance.**

- Every finite étale R-algebra S, for R perfectoid, is itself perfectoid with S°a almost finite étale over R°a; 'almost finite étale' means finite étale in the almost category, not étaleness of S° over R°.
- R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ with the Kummer cover S = R[T^{1/ℓ}] (ℓ ≠ p) and a wildly ramified Artin–Schreier–Witt-type cover: both have S°a uniformly almost finitely generated over R°a.
- Faltings' original almost purity (toric charts over a discretely valued field) is recovered by base change to the perfectoid tower (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 5.5.10).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p3-finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`](#p3-integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`](#p3-almost-finite-etale-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

<a id="p3-perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy` — Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy; perfectoid spaces are locally strongly sheafy

*Lemma.* Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. For every n ≥ 0 the Tate algebra R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ (Tau Ceti `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R`) is stably uniform, hence sheafy for every ring of integral elements; that is, R is strongly sheafy in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (`Huber.IsStronglySheafy R`). Consequently every perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) is a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy`), and every rational localisation and every finite étale algebra of a perfectoid Tate ring is strongly sheafy. This makes available, for perfectoid spaces, A1's local-to-global description of finite étale maps, fibre products of étale maps inside adic spaces, and the étale and finite étale sites with their structure sheaves.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R perfectoid Tate (ECD Definition 3.1); p is topologically nilpotent in R because ϖ^p | p, so R is a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra.

**Proof outline.**

1. The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), hence stably uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy).
2. R⟨T⟩ → R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ splits as a map of topological R⟨T⟩-modules: R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the completed direct sum of the free rank-one modules R⟨T⟩·T^b over b ∈ (ℤ[1/p] ∩ [0, 1))ⁿ, and the projection onto b = 0 is continuous and R⟨T⟩-linear.
3. A complete Tate ring admitting a topologically split map to a stably uniform complete Tate ring is stably uniform, hence sheafy by Buzzard–Verberkmoes (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy; anchor Layer 4).
4. Closure under rational localisation and finite étale algebras: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b), (d); alternatively they are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids, P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and the first step applies.
5. Locally strongly sheafy: a perfectoid space is covered by Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale: A1's local-to-global theorem over perfectoid affinoids
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space: A1's site applies to perfectoid spaces
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair: A1 defers the membership of perfectoid rings to PerfectoidSpaces

**Acceptance.**

- ℚ_p^cycl⟨T_1, T_2⟩ is sheafy (it is even strongly noetherian); the content is for non-noetherian R such as ℚ_p^cycl⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨T⟩ and the ring of ECD Example 3.4(iv).
- Non-example of the hypothesis: Buzzard–Verberkmoes' non-sheafy uniform Tate rings are not strongly sheafy; perfectoidness is what excludes them.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`](#p2-perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/StronglySheafy

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 6, §6.3, Proposition 6.3.3 (3), p. 47. The Tate algebras over a perfectoid ring are split in perfectoid rings ('RhT1, …, Tn i' is R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩).
- [`ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020`](#source-p0-scholzeweinstein-berkeley-2020), Lecture 6, §6.3, Proposition 6.3.4, p. 48. Split in a perfectoid ring ⇒ stably uniform ⇒ sheafy.

<a id="p3-finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces` — Finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(i))

*Definition.* Let X, Y be perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: the full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces locally of the form Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid). A morphism f: Y → X is finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f`) if it is finite étale as a morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism: X has a cover by open affinoids V = Spa(A, A⁺) with f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺) over V, B ∈ FÉt(A) with its natural topology and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺). No second notion is introduced: `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` is A1's `AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` of the underlying morphism. ECD's defining condition — for every open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X the preimage f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid with R → S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S — is equivalent (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale), as are Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (a cover of X by such affinoids) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1). X_fét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces finite étale over X (all X-morphisms); for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, global sections give X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. Conventions: the plus ring is the integral closure, never S° when R⁺ ≠ R°; f need not be surjective; the degree x ↦ dim_{k(x)}(O_Y ⊗ k(x)) is locally constant.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X, Y perfectoid; for Y an arbitrary adic space with Y → X finite étale, Y is automatically perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f := AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` on the underlying morphism (perfectoid spaces are analytic, their charts being Tate).
2. The affinoid model Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(R), R perfectoid, is an affinoid perfectoid space: S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and sheafy.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class on morphisms of perfectoid spaces: A1's AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale of the underlying morphism.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_adic` (compatibility): IsFiniteEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f.toAdicSpaceHom.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_forall_affinoidPerfectoid` (characterisation): ECD Definition 6.2(i): for every open affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ X the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with integral-closure plus ring (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_exists_cover` (characterisation): Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii): the same condition over the members of one open affinoid perfectoid cover of X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.spa` (constructor): For R perfectoid and S ∈ FÉt(R), Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is finite étale (S⁺ the integral closure).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of finite étale morphisms are finite étale (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along any morphism of perfectoid spaces is finite étale, with affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C, D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.of_comp` (other): If g and g ∘ f are finite étale, so is f.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f is finite étale iff f♭ is (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.isStronglyFiniteEtale` (relation): Finite étale morphisms are strongly finite étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.finiteEtaleAffinoidEquiv` (equivalence): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X_fét ≃ (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R)ᵒᵖ via global sections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.isFinite` (projection): Finite étale morphisms are finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) and hence closed; they are open (étale).

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_fold` (degenerate): For every perfectoid space X, X ⊔ X → X and ∅ → X are finite étale, and the identity is finite étale of degree 1.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_kummer` (computation): Over X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩), Spa(R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) → X (ℓ ≠ p prime) is finite étale of degree ℓ, and its source is perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_rational` (non-example): The inclusion of the rational subset {|T| ≤ |p|} into the perfectoid closed disc is étale but not finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_plus_ring` (non-example): For (K, K⁺) with K⁺ ⊊ O_K of rank 2, Spa(K × K, O_K × O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺) is not finite étale although K → K × K is a finite étale ring map: the plus ring must be the integral closure (K⁺ × K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): IsFiniteEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f.toAdicSpaceHom (definitional).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_ecd` (characterisation): IsFiniteEtale f iff for every open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(R) and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ (ECD Definition 6.2(i)).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces: the middle factor of the local description of étale maps
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space: objects of X_fét
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid: finite étale morphisms descend along étale covers
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: the prestack of finite étale perfectoid spaces
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected: finite étale covers of strictly totally disconnected spaces split
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover: the finite étale factor of an étale map, affinoid perfectoid over rational subsets
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale: finite étale covers of perfectoid spaces

**Acceptance.**

- The fold map X ⊔ X → X and ∅ → X are finite étale; an open immersion that is not closed is not.
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) and ℓ ≠ p, the Kummer cover T ↦ T^ℓ (Spa of R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) is finite étale of degree ℓ.

<a id="p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces` — Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(ii))

*Definition.* A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f`) if it is étale in A1's local sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`): every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood V ⊆ Y such that f|_V factors as V ↪ W → U ↪ X with V → W an open immersion, W → U finite étale (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces) and U ⊆ X open. W is then automatically perfectoid. This is ECD Definition 6.2(ii) (whose printed condition 'y ∈ Y' is read as y ∈ V), Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(iii) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(2). Equivalent local form: U may be taken a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid open of X, W = Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(O(U)), and V a rational subset of W; so étale morphisms are locally composites 'rational embedding, finite étale, rational embedding' of affinoid perfectoid spaces. X_ét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces étale over X (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). Étale morphisms need not be separated or quasi-compact.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X, Y perfectoid; an adic space étale over a perfectoid X is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f := AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f` on the underlying morphism.
2. W perfectoid: W → U finite étale with U perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid, locally on U); rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class on morphisms of perfectoid spaces: A1's local description.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.iff_adic` (compatibility): IsEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f.toAdicSpaceHom.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_isOpenImmersion` (instance): Open immersions are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_isFiniteEtale` (instance): Finite étale morphisms are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.exists_standardAffinoid` (characterisation): Local standard form: rational ⊆ finite étale over rational ⊆ affinoid perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of étale morphisms are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along any morphism of perfectoid spaces is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_comp` (other): If g and g ∘ f are étale, so is f.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.isOpenMap` (projection): Étale morphisms are open on underlying spaces.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f is étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.isStronglyEtale` (relation): Étale morphisms are strongly étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.isPerfectoid_of_isEtaleLocalDescription` (instance): An adic space étale over a perfectoid space is perfectoid.

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_openImmersion` (degenerate): Open immersions of perfectoid spaces are étale; the identity is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_rational_in_cover` (computation): For R perfectoid, S ∈ FÉt(R) and a rational subset V ⊆ Spa(S, S⁺), the composite V → Spa(R, R⁺) is étale (standard affinoid étale map).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_not_finite` (non-example): The inclusion of the open unit disc (a non-quasi-compact open) into the closed perfectoid disc is étale but not finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_proetale` (non-example): Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) → Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl) is not étale (it is pro-étale, PerfectoidSpaces:P6), nor is the Zariski closed immersion {T = 0} into the perfectoid disc (not open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): IsEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f.toAdicSpaceHom (definitional).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_standard` (characterisation): IsEtale f iff f is locally on Y a composite of a rational embedding, a finite étale map and a rational embedding of affinoid perfectoid spaces.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space: objects of X_ét
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: étale maps tilt to étale maps
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: the prestack of separated étale perfectoid spaces
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison: Y_ét of the perfectoid covers
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover: ECD Definition 6.2(ii) and its local standard form
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map: affinoid étale maps as building blocks of pro-étale maps

**Acceptance.**

- Open immersions and finite étale morphisms are étale.
- Two copies of the perfectoid closed disc glued along the complement of the origin map étale, not separatedly, to the disc.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, Definition 6.2 (ii), continued, p. 26. The factorisation.
