<a id="p3-strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change` — Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces; tilting invariance and base change

*Definition.* (Scholze 2012 Definition 7.2, over an arbitrary perfectoid base) A morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) of perfectoid Huber pairs is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale (S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology, S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale f`) if X has a cover by open affinoid perfectoid V with f⁻¹(V) affinoid perfectoid and (O_X(V), O⁺_X(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O⁺_Y(f⁻¹V)) strongly finite étale; strongly étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale f`) if locally on Y it factors as an open immersion, a strongly finite étale map and an open immersion. Properties: (a) f is strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭ is (the almost finite étale condition is transported by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b)); (b) base change along arbitrary maps Z → X of perfectoid spaces preserves both classes, with affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C (already complete, being finite projective over C), D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺ in D, and |Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| surjective (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(i)–(ii), with the printed |X ×_Z Y| read as the fibre product of the base change); (c) composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.8); (d) in characteristic p every (finite) étale map is strongly (finite) étale, and by almost purity this holds in general (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale), so the strong classes coincide with P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces and P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Perfectoid spaces without base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) on each chart (R°a = R⁺a).

**Proof outline.**

1. Definition: the affinoid condition is stable under restriction to rational subsets (base change of almost finite étale algebras, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras, and rational localisation of the perfectoid pair, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction), so the global notion is well defined.
2. (b), affinoid case: A ⊗_B C is finite projective over C, hence complete; it is finite étale over C and D°a = A°a ⊗ C°a is almost finite étale (base change); the universal property among perfectoid spaces follows from that of Spa of a finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv)); surjectivity on points from Huber's argument (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).
3. (a): the tilting slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence) matches affinoid perfectoid covers; strongly finite étale affinoid maps correspond under P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class: affinoid-locally strongly finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class: locally open immersion, strongly finite étale, open immersion.
- `Perfectoid.Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (data): The affinoid condition on a map of perfectoid pairs: finite étale with S°a almost finite étale over R°a.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f strongly finite étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f strongly étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Stable under base change along any map of perfectoid spaces, with the affinoid formula.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Stable under base change; surjective on topological fibre products.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of strongly finite étale maps are strongly finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.isOpenMap` (projection): Strongly étale maps are open.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.iff_isFiniteEtale` (characterisation): Strongly finite étale ↔ finite étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.iff_isEtale` (characterisation): Strongly étale ↔ étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_charp` (characterisation): For X of characteristic p, IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsFiniteEtale f (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.test_open` (degenerate): Open immersions are strongly étale; they are strongly finite étale only when also closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_tilt` (compatibility): IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsStronglyFiniteEtale f♭.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_plus_ring` (non-example): (K, K⁺) → (K × K, O_K × O_K) with K⁺ ⊊ O_K is not strongly finite étale: the plus ring is not the integral closure.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_basechange` (computation): For Spa(A, A⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) strongly finite étale and Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺), the fibre product is Spa(A ⊗_B C, integral closure of C⁺).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids: the affinoid statement is about this class
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: the strong classes are manifestly tilting invariant
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: in characteristic p étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p: strongly étale maps and their base change
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv: base change of affinoid étale maps
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover: strongly finite étale pieces

**Acceptance.**

- The strong notion is a priori stronger: it requires S°a almost finite étale; in characteristic 0 the equality with finite étale is a theorem (almost purity), not part of the definition.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`](#p0-almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction`](#p2-perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §7, after Definition 7.2, p. 40. Property (a).
- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §7, Lemma 7.3 (ii), p. 40. Property (b), affinoid formula.

<a id="p3-strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids` — Preimages of affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with strongly finite étale ring map

*Lemma.* Let f: Y → X be a finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), or more generally a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces with X perfectoid, and let V = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X be an open affinoid perfectoid subspace (arbitrary perfectoid Tate R, no base field). Then f⁻¹(V) is affinoid perfectoid: f⁻¹(V) = Spa(S, S⁺) with S = O_Y(f⁻¹V) ∈ FÉt(R) perfectoid and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S, and (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) is strongly finite étale (S°a almost finite étale over R°a). Global sections give an equivalence V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op, and strongly finite étale covers of V correspond to finite étale R-algebras (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.6 and Theorem 7.9(i)–(ii), Bhatt Proposition 10.0.6 and Corollary 10.0.7, in general). In particular every finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces satisfies ECD Definition 6.2(i). Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.7 (in characteristic p, étale maps are locally base changes of étale maps of noetherian affinoid adic spaces) is not needed for this.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid; f finite étale in A1's sense; V affinoid perfectoid open.

**Proof outline.**

1. R is strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), so AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (a), (c) gives f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S`) with S ∈ FÉt(R), and V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. (The descent of finite étale algebras along the rational cover of V on which f is known to be affinoid is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent; Scholze's noetherian approximation, via P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit and p-finite affinoids, is replaced by it.)
2. S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), so the map of pairs is strongly finite étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale: ECD's 'for all affinoids' form
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects: finite étale covers of affinoid perfectoids are algebraic
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4: affinoid finite étale pieces over the limit
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover: W_y affinoid perfectoid with finite étale ring map

**Acceptance.**

- A finite étale cover of the perfectoid closed disc glued from covers of two rational pieces with compatible gluing is Spa of a single finite étale algebra over R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, with plus ring the integral closure of R⁺.
- Openness of strongly étale maps follows (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); it is not assumed.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`](#p3-perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p3-finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`](#p3-integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`](#p3-strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

<a id="p3-etale-is-strongly-etale"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-is-strongly-etale` — Every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale)

*Lemma.* Let f: Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then f is finite étale iff it is strongly finite étale, and étale iff it is strongly étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change). In characteristic p this is P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p; in general it is a consequence of almost purity (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale). Hence the tilting invariance and base-change properties of the strong classes hold for all (finite) étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X, Y perfectoid spaces over no fixed base.

**Proof outline.**

1. Strongly ⇒ plain: by definition.
2. Finite étale ⇒ strongly finite étale: over each affinoid perfectoid V ⊆ X, P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids.
3. Étale ⇒ strongly étale: the finite étale factor W → U of the local description is strongly finite étale by the previous step.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: étale maps tilt because strongly étale maps do
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}), Spa(L) → Spa(K) is strongly finite étale although L° is not étale over K°.

<a id="p3-perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale` — Comparison of perfectoid finite étale and étale morphisms with AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and with finite étale algebras

*Comparison.* Let X be a perfectoid space. (a) (Perfectoidness) If g: Y → X is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of analytic adic spaces in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), then Y is a perfectoid space. (b) (Morphism classes) For morphisms of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: finite étale in A1's sense (= P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); ECD Definition 6.2(i) (for every open affinoid perfectoid U the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with integral-closure plus ring); Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (for one open affinoid perfectoid cover); Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1); strongly finite étale. Likewise étale in A1's sense ⇔ ECD 6.2(ii) ⇔ Scholze 2012 7.1(iii) ⇔ Berkeley 7.5.1(2) ⇔ strongly étale. (c) (Algebraic comparison) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, the functors X_fét → FÉt(R)^op (global sections), FÉt(R) → {finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)} (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`, plus ring forced to be the integral closure) and the latter → Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` (forget topology and plus ring) are equivalences; every finite étale R-algebra is perfectoid for its natural topology. (d) (Sites) The category of perfectoid spaces étale (resp. finite étale) over X is the small étale (resp. finite étale) site of the underlying adic space in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site), with the same coverings; A1's structure sheaves O, O⁺ on it (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), its Galois category of finite étale objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category) and its basis of affinoid objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison) apply. (e) (Base change from adic spaces; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv) and Proposition 7.10) If Y' → X' is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (e.g. locally noetherian ones) and Z → X' is a morphism from a perfectoid space, then Y' ×_{X'} Z exists, is perfectoid, and is finite étale (resp. étale) over Z; for affinoids its ring is D = A ⊗_B C with D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid, hence locally strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy); A1's notions are defined for all analytic adic spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): locally on X, Y is Spa(S, S⁺) with S finite étale over a perfectoid R (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global over the strongly sheafy affinoid perfectoid charts), perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid; for étale maps, Y is locally an open subspace of such a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. (b): A1 ⇔ Scholze 7.1(ii) by definition; A1 ⇒ ECD 6.2(i) by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids; ECD 6.2(i) ⇒ A1 trivially; ⇔ strongly by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale; Berkeley 7.5.1(1) quantifies over opens of the target and is equivalent by the same lemma. The étale case follows from the finite étale case and the definitions.
3. (c): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv) (morphisms of the pairs are the algebra maps); the forgetful functor to CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R is an equivalence because the topology and the plus ring are determined.
4. (d): objects étale over X in A1's sense are perfectoid by (a); the morphism classes agree by (b); coverings are jointly surjective families in both.
5. (e): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change for the fibre product with locally strongly sheafy Z; perfectoidness by (a) applied over Z; it is the fibre product in perfectoid spaces over the analytic base X' of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base (the uniform completion is unnecessary, the algebra being finite projective over the perfectoid factor).

**Uses.**

- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover: ECD 6.2(i) for W_y
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation: étale maps over perfectoid covers stay perfectoid
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison: the perfectoid étale site is A1's

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) and the pullback of the Kummer cover 𝔾_m → 𝔾_m, z ↦ z^ℓ, of the rigid torus along X → Spa(ℚ_p⟨T^{±1}⟩): the fibre product is Spa(R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)), perfectoid and finite étale over X ((e)).
- For X = Spa(C, C⁺), C algebraically closed perfectoid: X_fét is equivalent to finite sets (every finite étale C-algebra is split, Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.equivOfIsSepClosed`).
- Non-example: a finite étale map of adic spaces over a non-perfectoid base (Spa ℚ_p(p^{1/2}) → Spa ℚ_p) has non-perfectoid source; (a) requires X perfectoid.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`](#p3-perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p3-finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`](#p3-strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-is-strongly-etale`](#p3-etale-is-strongly-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base`](#p2-fibre-products-over-analytic-base), `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.equivOfIsSepClosed`.

<a id="p3-etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open` — Étale and finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces: composition, base change, cancellation, openness, tilting

*Lemma.* For morphisms of perfectoid spaces (Berkeley Proposition 7.5.2; ECD after Definition 6.2; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.8, Proposition 7.10): (1) composites of (finite) étale morphisms are (finite) étale; (2) for f: Y → X (finite) étale and any g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces, the fibre product Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is (finite) étale over X', agrees with A1's fibre product of adic spaces, has the affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C, D⁺ = integral closure of C⁺ (no completion needed), and |Y ×_X X'| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| is surjective; (3) if g and g ∘ f are (finite) étale, so is f; (4) f is (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭: Y♭ → X♭ is; (5) étale morphisms are open; quasi-compact étale morphisms have quasi-compact open image; the diagonal of an étale morphism is an open immersion, and of a finite étale morphism an open and closed immersion.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- All spaces perfectoid; fibre products in perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2.

**Proof outline.**

1. (1), (3), (5): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal, applied to the underlying adic spaces (locally strongly sheafy by P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), with P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale identifying the classes.
2. (2): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change gives the fibre product of adic spaces with its affinoid formula; it is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)) and therefore satisfies the universal property among perfectoid spaces, so it is the perfectoid fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property); surjectivity on points from A1.
3. (4): by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale, f is (finite) étale iff strongly (finite) étale, and the strong classes are tilting invariant (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (a)) — on affinoids by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence with plus rings, and the tilting slice equivalence PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence matches open covers.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space: the site axioms
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: étale maps tilt
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4: finite étale and affinoid étale objects are stable under base change
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site: étale maps of perfectoid spaces as building blocks

**Acceptance.**

- For X' = Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) → X at a point x, the fibre of a finite étale Y → X is Spa of the finite étale k(x)^-algebra O_Y(f⁻¹V) ⊗ k(x)^.
- For the Kummer cover f of the perfectoid torus over ℚ_p^cycl, f♭ is the Kummer cover u ↦ u^ℓ of the tilted torus over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`](#p3-perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`](#p3-perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-is-strongly-etale`](#p3-etale-is-strongly-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`](#p3-strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property`](#p2-perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`](#p2-tilting-slice-equivalence).

<a id="p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space` — The étale site X_ét and the finite étale site X_fét of a perfectoid space

*Construction.* Let X be a perfectoid space. Its étale site X_ét (`PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale X`) is the small étale site of the underlying locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site; P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy): objects the adic spaces étale over X — all perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)), i.e. the perfectoid spaces étale over X of ECD — with all X-morphisms (étale by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (3)), and the topology generated by jointly surjective families (on all points, including higher-rank ones). The finite étale site X_fét is the full subcategory of finite étale objects with the induced jointly-surjective topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). Structure: (i) X_ét has finite limits (fibre products of perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and a basis X_ét^aff of affinoid perfectoid objects étale over X, closed under rational subsets, finite étale maps and fibre products (Kedlaya–Liu 8.3.1: perfectoid spaces are stably adic), which is a dense subsite (Mathlib `Functor.IsDenseSubsite`); (ii) a morphism g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces induces a morphism of sites X'_ét → X_ét by base change, functorially; a morphism X → Y to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (e.g. locally noetherian) induces a morphism of sites X_ét → Y_ét (Scholze 2012 after Definition 7.11); (iii) O_{X_ét}: U ↦ O_U(U) and O⁺_{X_ét}: U ↦ O⁺_U(U) are sheaves of rings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), as are O⁺/ϖ and O^{+a}; (iv) for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op; (v) for X connected and a geometric point, X_fét is a Galois category with fundamental group π₁(X) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category), and for X = Spa(K, K⁺), K a perfectoid field, π₁ = Gal(K^sep/K).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid; sites are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 with the coverings of ECD (jointly surjective).

**Proof outline.**

1. Take A1's site of the underlying adic space; perfectoidness of all objects and the equality of the morphism classes is P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale.
2. Site axioms, morphisms of sites: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (i)–(iv) with the fibre products identified by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (2).
3. Basis: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison; affinoid objects are affinoid perfectoid by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids.
4. Sheaves: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf; O⁺/ϖ and the almost sheaves by sheafification (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale` (constructor): The category of perfectoid spaces étale over X (A1's AdicSpace.smallEtale of the underlying adic space).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtaleTopology` (structure): The Grothendieck topology of jointly surjective families.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.isPerfectoid` (instance): Every object of X_ét is a perfectoid space.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.hasFiniteLimits` (instance): X_ét has finite limits, computed by perfectoid fibre products.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtaleAffinoid` (data): The dense subsite of affinoid perfectoid objects étale over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.map` (functoriality): A morphism X' → X induces the base change functor X_ét → X'_ét and a morphism of sites, with map_id and map_comp.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.toAdic` (functoriality): A morphism X → Y to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space induces a morphism of sites X_ét → Y_ét.
- `PerfectoidSpace.structureSheafEtale` (data): The sheaves O_{X_ét} and O⁺_{X_ét}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale` (constructor): The finite étale site X_fét.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale.affinoidEquiv` (equivalence): For X = Spa(R, R⁺): X_fét ≃ (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R)ᵒᵖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory` (instance): For connected X, X_fét is a Galois category.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.adicEquiv` (compatibility): X_ét ≃ AdicSpace.smallEtale of the underlying adic space, compatible with coverings.

**Unit tests.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_point` (computation): For K a perfectoid field, Spa(K, O_K)_fét ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets (via AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category and P3/fontaine-wintenberger).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_empty` (degenerate): For X = ∅ the site has a single object (∅) covered by the empty family; for X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every finite étale object is a finite disjoint union of copies of X, so X_fét ≃ FintypeCat.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale X = AdicSpace.smallEtale X.toAdicSpace as sites (same objects up to the full embedding of perfectoid spaces, same coverings).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_basis` (characterisation): The affinoid perfectoid objects form a dense subsite: Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_not_fpqc` (non-example): Spa(ℂ_p) → Spa(ℚ_p^cycl) is not a covering in X_ét (not étale), although it is a v-cover: X_ét is not the pro-étale or v-site.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence: the sites compared
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity: cohomology on X_ét
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: ν: X_proét → X_ét and the sheaves O, O⁺ on X_ét
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected: étale covers of a perfectoid space
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison: X_ét for the perfectoid charts of Y^◇
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: X_ét → X_fét and cohomology of F_p on the perfectoid tower
- ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2: étale topoi of perfectoid spaces over algebraically closed fields

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every covering of X in X_ét has a member with a section near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).
- For X = Spa(K, O_K), K perfectoid field, X_fét ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`](#p3-perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`](#p3-perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`](#p3-etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`](#p3-strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-basis), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology`](#p0-almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.GaloisCategory`.

<a id="p3-etale-descent-perfectoid"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid` — Étale descent for finite étale morphisms and finite projective modules on perfectoid spaces

*Theorem.* Let X be a perfectoid space with étale site X_ét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). (a) (Locality) A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is finite étale if, for some covering {X_i → X} in X_ét, every base change Y ×_X X_i → X_i is finite étale; étaleness of f is local on Y and on X for open coverings. (b) (Stack) The prestack U ↦ U_fét (finite étale perfectoid spaces over U, with isomorphisms) on X_ét is a stack for the étale topology (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`): finite étale spaces with descent data along an étale covering descend uniquely. (c) (Vector bundles; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22(b), (d)) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, M ↦ M ⊗_R O_{X_ét} is an equivalence between finitely generated projective R-modules and finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules, and M ⊗ O is a sheaf on X_ét with M ⊗ O(Y) = M ⊗_R O(Y) on affinoid perfectoid Y ∈ X_ét. Descent along v-covers is not part of this node (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid; coverings jointly surjective families of étale maps.

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduction: every covering in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object can be refined by composites of rational coverings and single surjective finite étale maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction, after Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.20 and de Jong–van der Put); it suffices to prove the claims for these two kinds of coverings.
2. Rational coverings: effective descent of finite étale algebras (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent) and of finite projective modules (Kiehl gluing on sheafy Tate affinoids, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing; perfectoid pairs are sheafy).
3. Surjective finite étale Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺): R → S is faithfully flat; faithfully flat descent of modules (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`, `ModuleCat.reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.4) descends the module and its multiplication; finiteness, projectivity and étaleness descend (Mathlib `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, `Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.5). The descended algebra is finite étale over R, hence perfectoid with the integral-closure plus ring (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (c)); finite projective modules descend along the sheafy finite étale surjection by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent.
4. (a) follows from (b) applied to the base-changed family with its canonical descent datum, together with full faithfulness (the equaliser property of O, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf).

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: the étale-local step of v-descent
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors/three-descriptions-of-G-torsors: vector bundles are étale sheaves (Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22(c), (d))
- VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3: pro-étale local systems and vector bundles on perfectoid spaces

**Acceptance.**

- For a finite Galois étale cover Y → X with group G and a G-equivariant finite étale Y' → Y, Y' descends to a finite étale X' → X with Y' = X' ×_X Y (Galois descent).
- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every finite locally free O_{X_ét}-module is free (c).

<a id="p3-etale-site-tilting-equivalence"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence` — Tilting identifies the étale sites: X_ét ≃ X♭_ét, compatibly with affinoids, fibre products, coverings and O⁺/ϖ

*Comparison.* Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting). The tilting functor Y ↦ Y♭ of the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence: perfectoid spaces over X ≃ perfectoid spaces over X♭) restricts to equivalences of categories X_ét ≃ X♭_ét and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). These equivalences preserve and reflect affinoid perfectoid objects (with Spa(S, S⁺)♭ = Spa(S♭, S♭⁺)), fibre products, and covering families (|Y| ≅ |Y♭| compatibly with the maps to |X| ≅ |X♭|); hence they are equivalences of sites and induce equivalences of topoi Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X♭_ét) (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`). They are functorial in X: compatible with the morphisms of sites induced by maps X' → X and their tilts. For a pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ of X (locally), they identify the sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ and O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and the almost sheaves O⁺a/ϖ and O⁺a_{X♭}/ϖ♭, on the identified sites. For affinoid X = Spa(R, R⁺) the restriction to X_fét is the tilting equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭) of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid over no fixed base; ϖ chosen on affinoid perfectoid opens as in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

**Proof outline.**

1. Objects: Y → X is étale iff Y♭ → X♭ is (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (4)); essential surjectivity from the slice equivalence (every perfectoid space over X♭ is Y♭ for a perfectoid Y over X).
2. Affinoid perfectoid objects: Spa(S, S⁺) ↦ Spa(S♭, S♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting); finite étale objects over affinoids correspond by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.
3. Coverings: |Y| ≅ |Y♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, glued), compatibly with the projections, so joint surjectivity is preserved; fibre products are preserved by the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products).
4. Topoi: an equivalence of sites preserving and reflecting coverings induces an equivalence of sheaf categories (Mathlib `Equivalence.sheafCongr`).
5. O⁺/ϖ: on affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(S, S⁺), S⁺/ϖ = S♭⁺/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, ECD Lemma 3.11), compatibly with rational restriction and finite étale base change; sheafify.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity: first half of ECD 6.3
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: tilting preserves affinoid perfectoid objects and commutes with base change
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison: Y^◇_ét is computed on tilts
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: X_∞,ét ≅ X_∞♭,ét

**Acceptance.**

- The site isomorphism is compatible with the homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭| (open subspaces correspond to open subspaces).
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl), X_ét ≃ X♭_ét recovers Fontaine–Wintenberger (P3/fontaine-wintenberger) on the finite étale part.
- Non-example: tilting is not a morphism of ringed sites (O_X and O_{X♭} are not identified; only O⁺/ϖ is).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`](#p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`](#p3-etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`](#p2-tilting-slice-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`](#p2-perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`](#p2-tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products`](#p2-tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`](#p1-rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`.

<a id="p3-etale-almost-acyclicity"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity` — Almost acyclicity of O⁺ and acyclicity of O on the étale site of an affinoid perfectoid space

*Theorem.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space (R perfectoid Tate, no base field) with étale site X_ét, and write H^i(X_ét, −) for sheaf cohomology of abelian sheaves on X_ét (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). Then: (a) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is almost zero (killed by R°°) for i > 0; (b) H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0; (c) for every finite covering {U_j → U} in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object U by affinoid perfectoid objects, the augmented Čech complex of O⁺ is almost exact and that of O is exact; (d) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)^a = (R⁺/ϖ)^a and H^i(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ) is almost zero for i > 0; (e) for every finitely generated projective R-module M, H^i(X_ét, M ⊗_R O) = 0 for i > 0. The same holds on the analytic site (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity) and for every affinoid perfectoid object of X_ét.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; almost zero = killed by every pseudouniformiser (ECD Definition 3.21).

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduction to Čech complexes: the affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis of X_ét stable under fibre products (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space); by the Čech-to-derived comparison on an acyclic basis (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison; its almost version PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology) and the covering reduction of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.21), it suffices to show (c) for rational coverings and for single surjective finite étale maps Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺).
2. Rational coverings: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity for O⁺, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy (c) for O.
3. Surjective finite étale R → S: S is faithfully flat and finite étale; the n-fold fibre products are Spa of S^{⊗_R n} with plus rings whose almost versions are (S⁺a)^{⊗ n} over R⁺a (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence: the equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) respects tensor products). The Čech complex of O⁺ is the Amitsur complex of R⁺a → S⁺a, which is almost faithfully flat (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale (iv)), hence almost exact (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact, within PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent); the complex of O is the Amitsur complex of the faithfully flat R → S, exact (Mathlib `CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat` in degree 0; faithfully flat descent).
4. H⁰ exactly: O⁺ is a sheaf with O⁺(X) = R⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), not merely almost.
5. (b) from (a) by inverting ϖ on the Čech complexes of finite coverings (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion), or directly from the exactness in (c).
6. (d): O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free; the long exact sequence of 0 → O⁺ → O⁺ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (multiplication by ϖ) and (a). (e): M ⊗ O is a direct summand of Oⁿ.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity: second half of ECD 6.3
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét feeds the pro-étale computation
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: H^j(X_ét, O) = 0 in characteristic p
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors/three-descriptions-of-G-torsors: vector bundles are acyclic étale sheaves

**Acceptance.**

- For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and O⁺(Y)^G = R⁺ (the Čech complex of the cover is the complex of inhomogeneous cochains).
- In characteristic p, H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i ≥ 1 gives, with the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → 𝔽_p → O → O → 0, H^i(X_ét, 𝔽_p) = 0 for i ≥ 2 (used by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion).
- For X = Spa(K, O_K), K a perfectoid field, H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is the Galois cohomology H^i(Gal(K̄/K), O_{K̄}) of the discrete module O_{K̄}; it is almost zero for i > 0 because each finite Galois L/K has L°a almost finite étale and almost faithfully flat over K°a (Tate's computation, recovered from almost purity).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`](#p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`](#p3-almost-finite-etale-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`](#p3-integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology`](#p0-almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent`](#p0-almost-faithfully-flat-descent), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact`](#p0-almost-amitsur-complex-exact), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`](#p2-perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-integral-almost-acyclicity), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, `mathlib:CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

<a id="p3-etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity` — ECD Theorem 6.3: the tilting equivalence of étale sites and the almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét

*Comparison.* (ECD Theorem 6.3, over an arbitrary perfectoid base.) Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭. (i) Tilting induces an equivalence of sites X_ét ≃ X♭_ét (and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét), functorial in X, preserving affinoid perfectoid objects, fibre products and coverings, identifying O⁺/ϖ with O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and inducing an equivalence of étale topoi (P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence). (ii) If X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and the R⁺-modules H^i(X_ét, O⁺) are almost zero for i > 0; moreover H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0, and the sheaf U ↦ O_U(U) on X_ét is a sheaf (P3/etale-almost-acyclicity). Here X_ét is the étale site of P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space (= A1's site of the underlying adic space).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X perfectoid; no base field; cohomology is sheaf cohomology on X_ét.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence.
2. (ii): P3/etale-almost-acyclicity (a), (b); the sheaf property is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf via P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space.
3. The declaration bundles the two halves as ECD Theorem 6.3 and its consumers cite them.

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected: étale covers of perfectoid spaces and their tilts
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison: X_ét ≃ X♭_ét
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: tilting of the étale site of the perfectoid tower and Artin–Schreier
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison: étale topoi of perfectoid spaces
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: ECD Theorem 6.3
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: the finite étale site

**Acceptance.**

- For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O_Y⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and (O_Y⁺(Y))^G = O_X⁺(X) (a special case of the Čech statement).
- The site equivalence is compatible with the homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭| and, for X of characteristic p, is the identity.
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 7.12 and Proposition 7.13 (over a perfectoid field K) are the instance X over Spa(K, K°).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence`](#p3-etale-site-tilting-equivalence), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity`](#p3-etale-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`](#p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`.

<a id="p4"></a>

## P4. Morphisms and perfectoid quotients

Decompose ECD §5: injections, immersions, Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions, universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspaces, diagonals and separatedness. Prove the direction from a given surjective perfectoid quotient. The reverse ECD 5.8 is owned by PerfectoidQuotients Q4 and used only later in P6; it is not an input to the P4 construction on which Q4 depends.

**Coverage (`source_decomposed`; packet P0).** ECD §5 (Definition 5.1 – Proposition 5.11) is decomposed in full, in the generality of perfectoid spaces without a base field: injections with the (K, K⁺)- and (C, C⁺)-point, residue-field and finality criteria (5.3, Berkeley 8.3.3), the qcqs isomorphism criterion (5.4), base change and universal injectivity (5.5), immersions (5.6), Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions (5.7) with the universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace of Scholze's Lemma II.2.2 built from a general intersection-of-rational-subsets construction, the direction strongly Zariski closed ⇒ Zariski closed proved here; the converse, ECD 5.8, is PerfectoidQuotients Q4's, which is built on this layer, and no node of P4 uses it (the comparison that records it is PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed), diagonals (5.9), separatedness (5.10) and the valuative criterion (5.11) with the general-pair uniqueness of ECD 10.10 for perfectoid spaces. Comparisons: open immersions and closed immersions with the anchor's Layer 5 carriers, tilting of all notions (Scholze II.2.7) with plus-ring and topological formulas, base change (II.2.9), and the non-examples separating closed from Zariski closed immersions. The integral perfectoid criteria (almost and exact forms, BMS1 3.21, Sch12 5.6 in Tate generality) serve compatible-root annuli (RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0) and the Zariski closed construction. DiamondsAndVStacks' request (ECD 5.3, 5.4, 5.11) is served by P4/injection-criteria, P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion and P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness. RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0's request addressed to P4 ('the perfectoid structure sheaf and its acyclicity') is P2 content (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity); P4 supplies the integral criterion for its chart cover.

**Planets.** Injection of perfectoid spaces; Immersion of perfectoid spaces; Zariski closed immersion; Universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace; Separated map of perfectoid spaces; Valuative criterion for separatedness.

<a id="p4-affinoid-perfectoid-field-points"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points` — Affinoid perfectoid fields and (K, K⁺)-valued points of perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* An affinoid perfectoid field is a pair (K, K⁺) of a perfectoid field K (a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field, ECD Definition 3.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) and an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K; equivalently K⁺ is a valuation subring with K°° ⊂ K⁺ ⊂ K° = O_K, so (K, K⁺) is a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) and Spa(K, K⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space. It is algebraically closed if K is. A morphism (K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺) is a morphism of Huber pairs (a continuous field homomorphism carrying K⁺ into L⁺), also called an extension of affinoid perfectoid fields. The points of Spa(K, K⁺) are the valuation subrings V with K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°; they form a chain under inclusion, K⁺ is the unique closed point, K° is the unique rank-one point, every point is a specialization of K° and a generalization of K⁺, and the quasicompact open subsets are the Spa(K, K'⁺) for valuation subrings K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K°. For a perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) the set of (K, K⁺)-valued points is X(K, K⁺) := Hom_Perfd(Spa(K, K⁺), X); it is covariant in X, contravariant in (K, K⁺), and carries the closed-point map X(K, K⁺) → |X|. For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X(K, K⁺) is the set of morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺), and the closed-point map sends φ to spaComap φ of the closed point.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- p is a fixed prime; perfectoid fields are those of ECD Definition 3.6, of either characteristic, with no base field.
- K⁺ is a valuation subring. Open integrally closed subrings that are not valuation subrings (they occur in ECD Lemma 9.9) do not give affinoid perfectoid fields.

**Proof outline.**

1. Open and bounded subrings of K lie between K°° and K°: an open integrally closed subring contains every topologically nilpotent element (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`) and a bounded one consists of power-bounded elements; conversely K°° is open and K° bounded because K is a nonarchimedean field.
2. Points of Spa(K, K⁺): a continuous valuation v with v ≤ 1 on K⁺ has valuation ring V ⊇ K⁺; if x ∈ V had |x|_K > 1 then x⁻¹ would be topologically nilpotent, so v(x⁻¹) < 1 by continuity, contradicting v(x) ≤ 1; hence V ⊆ K°. Overrings of the valuation ring K⁺ are its localizations at primes, hence a chain. Quasicompact opens are the rational subsets {|f| ≤ 1}, f ∈ K, which are the Spa(K, K⁺[f]) (anchor Layer 2 rational subsets).
3. The description of X(K, K⁺) for affinoid X is the universal property of affinoid adic spaces (morphisms W → Spa(R, R⁺) are the morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_W(W), O_W⁺(W)); requested from the anchor, Layer 5) applied to W = Spa(K, K⁺), with O(W) = K and O⁺(W) = K⁺.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField` (structure): A perfectoid field K together with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.toPair` (coercion): The underlying Tau Ceti Huber pair (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.ofRankOne` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid field (K, K°).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.spa` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid space Spa(K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.closedPoint` (data): The point K⁺ of |Spa(K, K⁺)|, its unique closed point; every point specializes to it.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.mem_spa_iff` (characterisation): Points of Spa(K, K⁺) correspond to valuation subrings V with K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°; they form a chain with maximum K°, the unique rank-one point.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.isOpen_iff` (characterisation): The quasicompact open subsets of Spa(K, K⁺) are the Spa(K, K'⁺) with K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K° a valuation subring; every open subset is a union of these.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints` (data): X(K, K⁺) := Hom(Spa(K, K⁺), X) for a perfectoid space X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.map` (functoriality): A morphism f : Y → X induces f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺); map_id and map_comp hold.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.restrict` (functoriality): An extension (K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺) induces X(K, K⁺) → X(L, L⁺), natural in X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.closedPointImage` (projection): The natural map X(K, K⁺) → |X| sending a point to the image of the closed point.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv` (universal-property): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X(K, K⁺) ≃ Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺).

**Unit tests.**

- `AffinoidField.subsingleton_spa_ofRankOne` (computation): For every perfectoid field K, |Spa(K, K°)| has exactly one point.
- `AffinoidField.card_spa_eq_two` (computation): If K⁺ ⊊ K° is the preimage of a rank-one valuation ring k⁺ ⊊ k of the residue field k = K°/K°°, then |Spa(K, K⁺)| has exactly two points and only K⁺ is closed.
- `AffinoidField.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv_closedPoint` (compatibility): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) = Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺), the closed-point image of φ is Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap φ` applied to the closed point of Spa(K, K⁺).
- `AffinoidField.not_padic` (non-example): (ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is not an affinoid perfectoid field, because ℚ_p is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `AffinoidField.not_of_intersection` (non-example): If the residue field k of a perfectoid field K has incomparable nontrivial valuation rings k₁⁺, k₂⁺, the preimage K⁺ of k₁⁺ ∩ k₂⁺ is open, bounded and integrally closed but not a valuation subring, and Spa(K, K⁺) has at least two closed points.

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 5.3 (ii), Lemma 5.4 (iii)-(iv), Proposition 5.11 (iii): the injection, isomorphism and separatedness criteria are tests on (K, K⁺)-valued points
- Berkeley Lectures Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 and Proposition 17.4.4: injectivity is tested on algebraically closed affinoid fields (C, C⁺); the valuative criterion for v-sheaves
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks, D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves: the isomorphism criteria for diamonds and v-stacks reduce to (K, K⁺)-points of qcqs perfectoid spaces
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness: the valuative criterion for v-stacks uses the same lifting problems Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺)
- ECD Proposition 1.15 and Lemma 7.19: connected components of totally disconnected spaces are Spa(K, K⁺); rank-one points are Spa(C, O_C)

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(K, K°) is a single point, and for X affinoid perfectoid X(K, K°) is the set of continuous ring maps R → K with R⁺ → K°.
- If K⁺ has rank two, Spa(K, K⁺) has exactly two points: the open rank-one point K° and the closed point K⁺.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring`.

<a id="p4-maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing` — Morphisms of perfectoid spaces are generalizing and spectral

*Lemma.* Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (more generally of analytic adic spaces). Then the continuous map |f| : |Y| → |X| is generalizing (Mathlib `GeneralizingMap`: for y ∈ Y and a generalization x' of f(y) there is a generalization y' of y with f(y') = x'), and it is spectral on spectral opens (for open affinoids V ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, V → U is a spectral map, Mathlib `IsSpectralMap`). Consequently the image of every morphism, and of every quasicompact open under a morphism, is stable under generalization, and the image of a quasicompact open is pro-constructible in any spectral open containing it.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X and Y are perfectoid spaces, so every point is analytic (every point of Spa of a Tate ring is analytic, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isAnalyticPoint_of_isTateRing`).

**Proof outline.**

1. Generalizations of an analytic point: for y ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) with B Tate, the generalizations of y form a chain in bijection with the valuation subrings V of the completed residue field with K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° (vertical generalization; horizontal generalizations do not occur at analytic points). This description is requested from the anchor, Layer 2.
2. Lifting: with x = f(y), the field map K(x) → K(y) satisfies K(y)⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and K(y)° ∩ K(x) = K(x)°. A generalization x' of x is a valuation ring V' with K(x)⁺ ⊆ V' ⊆ K(x)°; it is the localization of K(x)⁺ at a prime 𝔭. The extension K(x)⁺ ⊆ K(y)⁺ of valuation rings is local, so Spec K(y)⁺ → Spec K(x)⁺ is a surjective order-preserving map of chains; let 𝔮 be the largest prime over 𝔭. It contains 𝔪(K(y)°), which lies over 𝔪(K(x)°) ⊆ 𝔭, so V := K(y)⁺_𝔮 satisfies K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° and V ∩ K(x) = V'. The point y' given by V is the required lift.
3. Spectrality: the preimage of a rational subset under a morphism of affinoid adic spaces is rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`), and quasicompact opens of an affinoid are finite unions of rational subsets; for spectral (qcqs) opens cover by finitely many affinoids.
4. Images: a generalizing map has generalization-stable image; the image of a pro-constructible subset under a spectral map of spectral spaces is pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets).

**Acceptance.**

- The inclusion of a rational subset U ⊆ X is generalizing: U is open, hence stable under generalization.
- For the map Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, K⁺) induced by an extension of perfectoid fields, the image is the rank-one point, which is stable under generalization but not closed when K⁺ ≠ K°.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:GeneralizingMap`, `mathlib:IsSpectralMap`, `mathlib:StableUnderGeneralization`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isAnalyticPoint_of_isTateRing`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields).

<a id="p4-quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps` — Quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms of perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* A perfectoid space X is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated) if |X| is quasicompact (resp. a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`). A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is quasicompact if f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every quasicompact open U ⊆ |X|, equivalently for every open affinoid U ⊆ X; it is quasiseparated if the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal` in the category of perfectoid spaces, whose fibre products are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is quasicompact; qcqs means both. Equivalently, f is quasiseparated if and only if for every open affinoid U ⊆ X and all open affinoids V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) the intersection V ∩ W is quasicompact; if X is affinoid (or quasiseparated), f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is quasiseparated. By ECD Proposition 8.3 these agree with the topos-theoretic notions of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos for the sheaves represented by perfectoid spaces.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), and open affinoids of a fibre product V ×_U W are the affinoid perfectoid spaces given by the P2 affinoid formula.

**Proof outline.**

1. Quasicompactness is local on the target and testable on affinoids because affinoids form a basis of quasicompact opens stable under finite intersection inside an affinoid (rational subsets, anchor Layer 2).
2. Diagonal criterion: the open subsets V ×_U W (V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) affinoid, U ⊆ X affinoid) cover Y ×_X Y and are affinoid; Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_U W) = V ∩ W; so Δ_f is quasicompact if and only if all V ∩ W are quasicompact.
3. If X is quasiseparated the same criterion shows that f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact` (structure): f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every quasicompact open U ⊆ |X|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated` (structure): The diagonal Δ_f is quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiCompact_iff_affinoid` (characterisation): f is quasicompact iff f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every open affinoid U ⊆ X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiSeparated_iff_affinoid_inter` (characterisation): f is quasiseparated iff V ∩ W is quasicompact for all open affinoids V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U), U ⊆ X open affinoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace` (compatibility): For X quasiseparated, f is quasiseparated iff |Y| is a Mathlib QuasiSeparatedSpace.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact.comp` (structure): Composites of quasicompact morphisms are quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated.comp` (structure): Composites of quasiseparated morphisms are quasiseparated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact.baseChange` (functoriality): The base change of a quasicompact morphism along any morphism is quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated.baseChange` (functoriality): The base change of a quasiseparated morphism along any morphism is quasiseparated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiCompact_of_affinoid` (instance): Morphisms between affinoid perfectoid spaces are quasicompact and quasiseparated.

**Unit tests.**

- `quasiCompact_affinoid` (computation): Every morphism Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces is quasicompact and quasiseparated.
- `not_quasiCompact_openDisc` (non-example): The open immersion of the open unit disc ⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|} into Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is not quasicompact (the preimage of the whole disc is not quasicompact).
- `quasiSeparated_id` (degenerate): The identity of any perfectoid space is qcqs.
- `quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace` (compatibility): For X affinoid, f : Y → X is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`.

**Uses.**

- ECD Lemma 5.4: the isomorphism criterion is stated for qcqs morphisms
- ECD Proposition 5.11 (iii): the valuative criterion assumes f quasiseparated
- ECD Lemma 11.11 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks: qcqs maps of diamonds are tested against qcqs perfectoid spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5 (ECD Proposition 6.4): finite-stage descent is stated for qcqs étale objects
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base: quasicompact separated maps to a strictly totally disconnected base

**Acceptance.**

- Every morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is qcqs.
- The inclusion of the open unit disc (the union of the rational subsets {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|}) into the perfectoid closed unit disc is quasiseparated but not quasicompact.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:CompactSpace`, `mathlib:QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `mathlib:IsQuasiSeparated`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos`.

<a id="p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces` — Injections of perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for every perfectoid space Z the map f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective (ECD Definition 5.1). It suffices to test affinoid perfectoid Z, because two morphisms Z → Y that agree on an open affinoid cover of Z agree. In the category Perfd of perfectoid spaces this says exactly that f is a monomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`), and, fibre products existing in Perfd (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), it is equivalent to the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y being an isomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`). Injections are not determined by |f| being injective: the characterisations on points, residue fields and underlying spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (ECD Definition 3.19): adic spaces of the anchor, locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring; Perfd is a full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduction to affinoid Z: morphisms of adic spaces are determined locally on the source (anchor Layer 5 gluing).
2. Mono ⇔ Δ_f iso is Mathlib `pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff` applied in Perfd, which has pullbacks by P2.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection` (structure): f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective for every perfectoid space Z.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isInjection_iff_mono` (compatibility): IsInjection f ↔ Mono f in Perfd.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_affinoid` (constructor): If f_* is injective on Hom(Z, −) for every affinoid perfectoid Z, then f is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isInjection_iff_isIso_diagonal` (characterisation): f is an injection iff Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an isomorphism.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.id` (instance): Identities, and more generally isomorphisms, are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.comp` (structure): Composites of injections are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_comp` (other): If g ∘ f is an injection then f is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_isSplitMono` (instance): Split monomorphisms (for instance sections and diagonals) are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.fieldPoints_injective` (relation): An injection induces injective maps Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes of injections are injections (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition).

**Unit tests.**

- `isInjection_rationalOpen` (computation): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and U ⊆ X rational, the open immersion U → X is an injection.
- `isInjection_diagonal` (degenerate): For every morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces, Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an injection.
- `not_isInjection_quadraticExtension` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K and a separable quadratic extension L/K (L is perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is bijective on underlying spaces but not an injection: the two K-embeddings of L into a completed algebraic closure C give distinct (C, O_C)-points with the same image.
- `isInjection_iff_mono` (compatibility): IsInjection f ↔ CategoryTheory.Mono f in the category of perfectoid spaces.

**Uses.**

- ECD Example 5.2: the residue-field points i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X are injections
- ECD Definition 5.6: immersions are injections whose underlying map is a locally closed immersion
- ECD Proposition 11.3 / Berkeley Proposition 8.3.4: an equivalence relation R → X × X is an injection
- ECD Lemma 7.19, Lemma 9.9: maps over (strictly) totally disconnected bases and compactifications of étale maps are shown to be injections before being identified
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness and D4 isomorphism criteria: injections of v-sheaves restrict to injections of perfectoid spaces

**Acceptance.**

- Rational open immersions U ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺) are injections (universal property of rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`).
- Diagonals are injections, being split monomorphisms (Mathlib instance `IsSplitMono (pullback.diagonal f)`).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Mono`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`.

<a id="p4-almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion` — Almost integral perfectoid criterion: a ϖ-complete ring with almost bijective Frobenius gives a perfectoid Tate ring

*Lemma.* Let A⁺ be a ring and ϖ ∈ A⁺ a non-zero-divisor such that (i) ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} ∈ A⁺ and ϖ^p divides p in A⁺; (ii) A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete and separated; (iii) the Frobenius Φ : A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ, x ↦ x^p, is an almost isomorphism for the basic setup (A⁺, 𝔪) with 𝔪 = ⋃ₙ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup): its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Let A := A⁺[1/ϖ], topologized so that A⁺ is open with the ϖ-adic topology. Then A is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 with pseudouniformizer ϖ; its power-bounded subring is A° = A⁺_* := {x ∈ A : ϖ^{1/pⁿ}x ∈ A⁺ for all n}; A⁺ ⊆ A° and A°/A⁺ is almost zero; the integral closure of A⁺ in A is a ring of integral elements; and Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is an isomorphism. This is the Tate-ring form of Sch12 Lemma 5.6 (stated there over a perfectoid field K for perfectoid K°ᵃ-algebras).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No base field: A⁺ is an arbitrary ring; in characteristic p the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous.
- Almost mathematics is taken for the idempotent ideal 𝔪 = ⋃ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (flat because ϖ is a non-zero-divisor).

**Proof outline.**

1. A⁺_* = (A⁺ᵃ)_* is the module of almost elements; for the ϖ-torsion-free A⁺ it is {x ∈ A : εx ∈ A⁺ for all ε ∈ 𝔪}, ϖ-torsion free, ϖ-adically complete, and almost equal to A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion; Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii),(iv)).
2. Φ : A⁺_*/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺_*/ϖ is injective: if x ∈ A⁺_* and x^p ∈ ϖA⁺_*, almost injectivity gives ε^{1/p}x ∈ ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* for all ε ∈ 𝔪, so x ∈ (ϖ^{1/p}A⁺)_* = ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).
3. If x ∈ A and x^p ∈ A⁺_* then x ∈ A⁺_* (Sch12 Lemma 5.7): with y = ϖ^{k/p}x ∈ A⁺_*, injectivity of Φ lowers k by one while k ≥ 1, using that A⁺_* has no ϖ-torsion.
4. A° = A⁺_*: elements of A⁺_* are power-bounded; if x is power-bounded then εx is topologically nilpotent for ε ∈ 𝔪, so (εx)^{p^N} ∈ A⁺_* for large N, hence εx ∈ A⁺_* by the previous step, for all ε; hence x ∈ A⁺_*. In particular A° ⊆ ϖ⁻¹A⁺ is bounded, so A is uniform, complete and Tate with pseudouniformizer ϖ.
5. Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is surjective: it is almost surjective, so for x ∈ A° there is y ∈ A° with ϖ^{1/p}x ≡ y^p mod ϖA°; z := y/ϖ^{1/p²} has z^p ∈ A° and x ≡ z^p mod ϖ^{(p−1)/p}A°, hence z ∈ A° by the root lemma, and the residual error lies in 𝔪A°, which gives surjectivity modulo ϖ (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).
6. ϖ^p divides p in A°, and Φ is an isomorphism A°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A°/ϖ; replacing ϖ by ϖ^{1/p} is harmless, so A satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). The integral closure of A⁺ is open (it contains A⁺) and contained in A° (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`).

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field C with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting p-power roots and A⁺ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective, and A = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid with A° = A⁺.
- Non-example: for A⁺ = O_C⟨T⟩ Frobenius modulo ϖ^{1/p} is not almost surjective (no element ϖ^εT is a p-th power modulo ϖ), and C⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid.
- The ϖ-adic completion of a filtered colimit of rings of integral elements of perfectoid pairs satisfies the hypotheses (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`](#p0-root-ideal-basic-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`](#p0-almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`](#p1-almost-integral-dictionary), `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`sch12-perfectoid`](#source-p0-sch12-perfectoid), §5, Definition 5.1 (ii), p. 21. The integral hypotheses (completeness, flatness = ϖ-torsion freeness, almost bijective Frobenius).

<a id="p4-integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli` — Integral perfectoid criterion: integral perfectoid rings give perfectoid Tate rings (compatible-root annuli)

*Lemma.* Let R₀ be a ring and π ∈ R₀ a non-zero-divisor with π^p | p such that R₀ is π-adically complete, and suppose that R₀ is an integral perfectoid ring (BMS1 Definition 3.5, PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings) — for instance because Frobenius R₀/π → R₀/π^p is an isomorphism (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)). Then R := R₀[1/π], with the π-adic topology on R₀, is a complete Tate ring that is perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1), R₀ ⊆ R°, πR° ⊆ R₀, and after replacing π by a unit multiple admitting compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9) the cokernel R°/R₀ is killed by every π^{1/pⁿ}. The criterion is about the pair (R₀, π): it is never inferred from the name of an integral model. Application (compatible-root period annuli): for a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{>0}, the ϖ-adic completion A⁺ of R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) satisfies the hypotheses (it is free over R° on the monomials T^α, S^β modulo the relations, and Frobenius is bijective from A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} to A⁺/ϖ on that basis; for a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊊ R° in place of R° it is almost bijective and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion applies), so the annulus ring A⁺[1/ϖ] = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^a/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; the same holds after base change of an annulus along a compatible-root extension, which is how perfectoidness of the chart cover of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 is checked. Without the roots of T the Frobenius criterion fails and R⟨T, ϖ^a/T⟩ is not perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- π is a non-zero-divisor; without this the localization loses information and the conclusion fails.
- Integral perfectoid is the BMS1 notion (π-adically complete for some π with π^p | p, Frobenius surjective on R₀/p, ker θ principal), owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; its comparison with rings of integral elements of perfectoid Tate rings (BMS1 Lemma 3.20) is PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison.

**Proof outline.**

1. BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i),(ii) (inside PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison): an integral perfectoid R₀ has Φ : R₀/π → R₀/π^p an isomorphism, and conversely a π-torsion-free π-complete R₀ with that isomorphism is integral perfectoid.
2. Replace π by uπ, u ∈ R₀^×, with compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9, 'moreover' part).
3. Apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion with A⁺ = R₀ and ϖ = π: Frobenius is bijective, a fortiori almost bijective; this gives R perfectoid, R° = (R₀)_* and R°/R₀ almost zero; since π·(R₀)_* ⊆ R₀ one gets πR° ⊆ R₀ (BMS1 Lemma 3.21, whose proof is 'as in Sch12 Lemma 5.6').
4. Annuli: R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ}) is a free R°-module on the monomials T^α (α ≥ 0) and S^β (β > 0) in ℤ[1/p], hence ϖ-torsion free; Frobenius sends c·T^α to c^p·T^{pα}, and R°/ϖ^{1/p} → R°/ϖ is bijective (ECD Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2 for the pseudouniformizer ϖ^{1/p}), so Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective.

**Acceptance.**

- Perfectoid annulus: for C a perfectoid field and a = 1, R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{1/pⁿ}) gives the perfectoid ring of the annulus |ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1, which is the rational localization C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
- BMS1 Example 3.6: ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is integral perfectoid, and ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/p] is perfectoid (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).
- Non-example: R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) has compatible roots of T, but Φ : R₀/ϖ^{1/p} → R₀/ϖ kills the nonzero class of T^{1/p}; R₀[1/ϖ] = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) is not reduced, hence not perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion`](#p4-almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion), `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`](#p1-integral-perfectoid-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018`](#source-p0-bms-integralpadichodge-2018), §3.2, Lemma 3.21 and proof, p. 27. The integral comparison R₀ ⊆ R° up to fractional powers of π.
