<a id="p4-intersection-of-rational-subsets"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets` — The perfectoid space attached to a filtered intersection of rational subsets

*Construction.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space, ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformizer with ϖ^p | p admitting compatible p-power roots (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), and 𝒰 a nonempty family of rational subsets of X that is filtered (for U, V ∈ 𝒰 some W ∈ 𝒰 lies in U ∩ V); put T := ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U ⊆ |X|. Let S⁺_𝒰 be the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U) and S_𝒰 := S⁺_𝒰[1/ϖ], topologized by the ϖ-adic topology on S⁺_𝒰, and let ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 := Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) → X be induced by the compatible maps O_X(U) → S_𝒰. Then: (a) S_𝒰 is a perfectoid Tate ring, S⁺_𝒰 is a ring of integral elements, S⁺_𝒰 ⊆ S_𝒰° with almost zero cokernel, S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ = colim_U O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ, and each O_X(U) → S_𝒰 has dense image; (b) |ι_𝒰| is a homeomorphism of |Z_𝒰| onto T with its subspace topology, and T is pro-constructible and stable under generalization; (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_𝒰 if and only if |g|(|W|) ⊆ T, and then uniquely; in particular ι_𝒰 is an injection and Z_𝒰 is the limit of the U ∈ 𝒰 in the category of perfectoid spaces; (d) Z_𝒰 depends, up to unique isomorphism over X, only on the subset T. The residue-field points of ECD Example 5.2 and the universal Zariski closed subspaces of Scholze's torsion paper Lemma II.2.2 are the cases 𝒰 = {rational neighbourhoods of x} and 𝒰 = {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; the family 𝒰 consists of rational subsets and is filtered; no base field.
- Completions are ϖ-adic; they do not depend on the choice of ϖ among pseudouniformizers of R.

**Proof outline.**

1. Valuative description of the colimit: s ∈ O_X(U₀) (U₀ ∈ 𝒰) has image in colim O⁺ iff |s| ≤ 1 on T. Indeed {x ∈ U₀ : |s(x)| ≤ 1} is a rational subset, O⁺_X(U) = {f : |f| ≤ 1 on U} (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one` on O(U)), and by compactness of the constructible topology (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets) T ⊆ V for a quasicompact open V forces some U ∈ 𝒰 to lie in V.
2. Frobenius: each (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is a perfectoid pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so Φ : O⁺(U)/ϖ^{1/p} → O⁺(U)/ϖ is an almost isomorphism (bijective on O(U)°, and O(U)°/O⁺(U) is almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii), PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). Filtered colimits and ϖ-adic completion preserve almost isomorphisms modulo ϖ, ϖ-torsion freeness and ϖ^p | p; apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion to A⁺ = S⁺_𝒰.
3. Points: a point z of Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) restricts to each O(U) with |O⁺(U)| ≤ 1, hence (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`) to a point of every U, so to a point of T; conversely a point x ∈ T defines compatible continuous valuations on the O(U), bounded by 1 on colim O⁺(U), which extend continuously to the completion. The resulting continuous bijection |Z_𝒰| → T is spectral and generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), T is spectral as a pro-constructible subset (anchor Layer 1.3), so it is a homeomorphism (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient).
4. Ring of integral elements: S⁺_𝒰 is open; if s ∈ S_𝒰 is integral over S⁺_𝒰 then |s| ≤ 1 on Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰); approximating s modulo ϖS⁺_𝒰 by s₀ in the image of some O(U) gives |s₀| ≤ 1 on T, so s₀, and then s, lies in S⁺_𝒰 by the valuative description.
5. Universal property: for W = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid with |g| ⊆ T, g factors uniquely through every U ∈ 𝒰 (rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), the compatible maps O⁺(U) → A⁺ extend uniquely to S⁺_𝒰 because A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete; general W by gluing (anchor Layer 5). Uniqueness makes ι_𝒰 an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Hom(W, Z_𝒰) = lim Hom(W, U).
6. Independence: the universal property depends only on T.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid space Z_𝒰 = Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰).
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.ι` (data): The morphism ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.plus_mod_pow` (simp): S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ ≅ colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ for every n.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.range_ι` (characterisation): |ι_𝒰| is a homeomorphism onto ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U with the subspace topology.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.lift` (universal-property): For g : W → X with |g| ⊆ ⋂𝒰, the unique lift W → Z_𝒰; lift_ι and lift_unique.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isInjection` (other): ι_𝒰 is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isLimit` (universal-property): Z_𝒰 with the maps to the U ∈ 𝒰 is a limit cone in Perfd.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.congr` (extensionality): If ⋂𝒰 = ⋂𝒱 then Z_𝒰 ≅ Z_𝒱 uniquely over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isPerfectoid` (instance): S_𝒰 is a perfectoid Tate ring and S⁺_𝒰 a ring of integral elements.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.denseRange` (other): O_X(U) → S_𝒰 has dense image for U ∈ 𝒰.

**Unit tests.**

- `proRationalSubspace_singleton` (degenerate): For 𝒰 = {U}, ι_𝒰 is isomorphic over X to U → X.
- `proRationalSubspace_rationalNhds` (compatibility): For 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x ∈ X, Z_𝒰 ≅ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) over X, compatibly with PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection.
- `proRationalSubspace_annulusClosure` (computation): For X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) and 𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|} : n ≥ 0}: S_𝒰 = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and S⁺_𝒰 is the ϖ-adic completion of O_C[T^{1/p^∞}] + 𝔪_C[T^{−1/p^∞}]; T is the annulus {|T| = 1} together with the rank-two point y with |T(y)| = 1⁻.
- `proRationalSubspace_empty` (degenerate): If ⋂𝒰 = ∅ then S_𝒰 = 0.
- `proRationalSubspace_not_open` (non-example): For 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of the Gauss point η of the perfectoid disc, T = {η} is not open, so ι_𝒰 is an injection that is not an open immersion.

**Uses.**

- ECD Example 5.2: the completed residue field point is the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods
- Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.2 and ECD Remark 7.9: a Zariski closed subset is the limit of the rational subsets {|f₁|, …, |f_k| ≤ 1}, f_i ∈ I
- ECD Lemma 7.6 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid: pro-constructible generalizing subsets of totally disconnected spaces are intersections of {|f| ≤ 1}
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: the special case of a cofiltered system of rational open immersions into a fixed affinoid
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed: the closure of an annulus is the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski closed

**Acceptance.**

- 𝒰 = {U}: Z_𝒰 = U.
- 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of a point x: Z_𝒰 = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (ECD Example 5.2).
- If T = ∅ then S_𝒰 = 0 and Z_𝒰 is empty.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion`](#p4-almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`](#p4-maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`](#p1-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`](#p1-perfectoid-almost-setup), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction`](#p2-perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`.

<a id="p4-residue-field-point-injection"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection` — The completed residue field point i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X

*Construction.* For a perfectoid space X and a point x ∈ X, the completed residue field K(x) with its open and bounded valuation subring K(x)⁺ is an affinoid perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), and there is a canonical morphism i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X sending the closed point to x: on an affinoid perfectoid neighbourhood U = Spa(R, R⁺) of x it is given by (R, R⁺) → (K(x), K(x)⁺), independently of U. Moreover (ECD Example 5.2): (a) i_x is isomorphic over U to the pro-rational subspace ι_𝒰 for 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x in U (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets), so K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V) and K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ; (b) i_x is an injection and |i_x| is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of x; (c) every (K, K⁺)-valued point φ of X whose closed point maps to x factors uniquely as φ = i_x ∘ φ' with φ' : Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) given by a morphism of affinoid perfectoid fields; (d) for f : Y → X and y ∈ Y with f(y) = x, f ∘ i_y = i_x ∘ Spa(K(x) → K(y)).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X is a perfectoid space; x is any point (not necessarily of rank one).

**Proof outline.**

1. Independence of U: two affinoid neighbourhoods contain a common rational neighbourhood, and restriction maps are compatible with the maps to K(x) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields).
2. (a),(b): the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods of x is the set of generalizations of x (in a spectral space the generalizations of x are the intersection of its quasicompact open neighbourhoods); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets, whose ring S⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim O⁺(V), which is K(x)⁺ (ECD Example 5.2).
3. (c): φ maps |Spa(K, K⁺)| into the generalizations of x (the closed point goes to x, every point of Spa(K, K⁺) generalizes the closed point, and continuous maps preserve specialization), so it factors uniquely through i_x by the universal property of (a); the factorization is a morphism (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) because both are affinoid.
4. (d) follows from the construction of completed residue fields and uniqueness in (c).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint` (constructor): The morphism i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (simp): i_x maps the closed point to x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_isInjection` (other): i_x is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.range_residueFieldPoint` (characterisation): |i_x| is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_factor` (universal-property): A (K, K⁺)-point with closed point x factors uniquely through i_x via a morphism (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_naturality` (functoriality): f ∘ i_y = i_{f(y)} ∘ Spa(K(f(y)) → K(y)) for f : Y → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_plus_mod` (simp): K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` (compatibility): i_x is the pro-rational subspace of the rational neighbourhoods of x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_isRankOne_iff` (characterisation): x is a rank-one point iff K(x)⁺ = K(x)° iff |Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| is a single point.

**Unit tests.**

- `residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (degenerate): For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x the closed point, i_x is the identity of X.
- `residueFieldPoint_gauss` (computation): For the Gauss point η of Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), K(η) is the completion of C(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm and K(η)⁺ = K(η)°; |i_η| has image {η}.
- `residueFieldPoint_not_isOpenImmersion` (non-example): i_η is an injection whose image {η} is not open (and not locally closed), so i_η is not an immersion.
- `residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` (compatibility): i_x is isomorphic over X to ι_𝒰 for 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x in an affinoid neighbourhood.

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 5.3, proof of (ii) ⇒ (iii) and (iii) ⇒ (iv): base change along i_x reduces to X = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)
- ECD Lemma 5.4, proof of (ii) ⇔ (iii): every (K, K⁺)-point factors over the immersion i_x
- ECD Proposition 5.11, proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii): specializations are witnessed by injections Spa(K, K⁺) → Y ×_X Y
- ECD Lemma 7.3 and Proposition 1.15: connected components of totally disconnected spaces are Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field: (K, K⁺)-points are determined by their closed point and a map of residue fields

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x its closed point, i_x is the identity.
- For the Gauss point η of the perfectoid closed unit disc over a perfectoid field C, K(η) is the completion of C(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm and K(η)⁺ = K(η)°.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets`](#p4-intersection-of-rational-subsets), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`](#p4-affinoid-perfectoid-field-points), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`](#p4-maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space).

<a id="p4-qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point` — A qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)

*Lemma.* Let X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated perfectoid space with a unique closed point x. Then i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X is an isomorphism; in particular X is affinoid, O_X(X) = K(x) and O⁺_X(X) = K(x)⁺.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X qcqs (|X| is then a spectral space, being quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally spectral).

**Proof outline.**

1. In the spectral space |X| every point specializes to a closed point, which is x; so every open neighbourhood of x is all of X.
2. An affinoid open neighbourhood U of x therefore equals X, so X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid, and every rational neighbourhood of x is X.
3. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (a), K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺(V) = R⁺, hence K(x)⁺ = R⁺, K(x) = R and i_x is the identity.

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(K, K⁺) itself.
- A quasicompact open subset of Spa(K, K⁺) containing the closed point is all of Spa(K, K⁺).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`](#p4-residue-field-point-injection), `mathlib:SpectralSpace`, `mathlib:specializes_iff_mem_closure`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space`.

<a id="p4-fibre-product-points-surjective"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective` — Points of fibre products of perfectoid spaces surject onto compatible pairs

*Lemma.* Let Y₁ → X ← Y₂ be morphisms of perfectoid spaces and W = Y₁ ×_X Y₂ their fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then |W| → |Y₁| ×_{|X|} |Y₂| is surjective, and it is spectral on spectral opens. Consequently, for points y₁ ∈ Y₁, y₂ ∈ Y₂ with the same image x ∈ X there are an affinoid perfectoid field (L, L⁺) and (L, L⁺)-valued points ỹ_i ∈ Y_i(L, L⁺) whose closed points map to y_i and whose images in X(L, L⁺) agree: take w ∈ W over (y₁, y₂), (L, L⁺) = (K(w), K(w)⁺) and ỹ_i = pr_i ∘ i_w.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Fibre products are those of Perfd (the uniform completion of the completed tensor product on affinoids).

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduce to affinoid X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺) containing y_i (open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products).
2. W = Spa(D, D⁺) with D the uniform completion of B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ (P2 affinoid formula); uniformization does not change the adic spectrum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d)), and the adic spectrum of a completion is that of the uncompleted pair.
3. Amalgamation: there is a valuation v on B₁ ⊗_A B₂ restricting to y₁ and y₂ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation); restricting v to the convex subgroup generated by the value groups of y₁, y₂ gives a continuous valuation bounded by 1 on the image of B₁⁺ ⊗ B₂⁺, hence on its integral closure, as in the proof of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points.
4. Spectrality: preimages of rational subsets are rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`).
5. The (L, L⁺)-points: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection applied to w.

**Acceptance.**

- For a separable quadratic extension L/K of perfectoid fields, |Spa(L, O_L) ×_{Spa(K, O_K)} Spa(L, O_L)| has two points over the single point of |Spa(L, O_L)| × |Spa(L, O_L)|: the map is surjective and not injective.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`](#p4-residue-field-point-injection), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FibreProductPoints

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

<a id="p4-algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field` — Every affinoid perfectoid field embeds into an algebraically closed one, and (K, K⁺)-points are detected there

*Lemma.* Let (K, K⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid field. (a) Let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of K and C⁺ ⊆ C° the preimage of a valuation subring of the residue field of C° dominating the image of K⁺. Then C is an algebraically closed perfectoid field, (C, C⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid field, K → C is a morphism (K, K⁺) → (C, C⁺), and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺. (b) The induced map π : Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) sends the closed point to the closed point. (c) For every perfectoid space Y the restriction map Y(K, K⁺) → Y(C, C⁺), φ ↦ φ ∘ π, is injective. In particular a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is injective on (K, K⁺)-points for all affinoid perfectoid fields as soon as it is injective on (C, C⁺)-points for all algebraically closed ones.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No assumption on the characteristic of K.

**Proof outline.**

1. C is perfectoid: its value group is divisible, it is not discretely valued, and Frobenius is surjective on C°/p because every element of the ring of integers of the algebraic closure has a p-th root (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition).
2. C is algebraically closed: in characteristic 0 by Mathlib `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange` applied to the dense algebraic closure; in characteristic p this is the classical continuity-of-roots argument (Krasner), not covered by that Mathlib lemma (recorded gap).
3. C⁺: K⁺ is the preimage of a valuation ring k⁺ of the residue field k = K°/K°°; the residue field k_C of C° is an algebraic closure of k; a valuation subring k_C⁺ of k_C dominating the local ring of the integral closure of k⁺ exists (Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`), and k_C⁺ ∩ k = k⁺ because valuation rings are maximal for domination; put C⁺ = preimage of k_C⁺. It contains C°°, so it is open and bounded.
4. (b): the closed point of Spa(C, C⁺) is C⁺ and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺.
5. (c): if φ ∘ π = ψ ∘ π then φ and ψ send the closed point to the same y (by (b)), so both factor through i_y (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)) by morphisms (K(y), K(y)⁺) → (K, K⁺) whose composites with the injective map K → C agree; hence φ = ψ.

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed) and K⁺ = K°, C = ℂ_p and C⁺ = O_{ℂ_p}.
- If K⁺ has rank two, C⁺ has rank two and π is a bijection on closed points and on rank-one points.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`](#p4-affinoid-perfectoid-field-points), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`](#p4-residue-field-point-injection), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`](#p1-perfectoid-field-definition), `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange`, `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring`, `mathlib:LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`.

<a id="p4-completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel` — Completed tensor products over a nonarchimedean field preserve kernels and strictness

*Lemma.* Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value (an analytic field) and V, W, X Banach K-modules, with ⊗̂_K the completed projective tensor product. (a) V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective. (b) For a bounded K-linear f : V → W with f_X := f ⊗̂ id_X : V ⊗̂_K X → W ⊗̂_K X, the natural map ker(f) ⊗̂_K X → ker(f_X) is a bijection. (c) If f is strict then so is f_X. Consequently, for an isometric embedding K → L of analytic fields and every Banach K-module V, the map V → L ⊗̂_K V is injective; in particular L ⊗̂_K V = 0 implies V = 0.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; Banach modules are complete normed K-vector spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 2.2.9: all three parts reduce to Banach modules containing dense subspaces of countable dimension; there (a) follows from Schauder bases of V and W, and (b), (c) from a Schauder basis of X ([Ked10, Lemma 1.3.11], unread; the reduction to countable type is recorded as a gap).
2. Consequence: apply (b) to the inclusion K → L (injective and strict) tensored with V: the kernel of V = K ⊗̂_K V → L ⊗̂_K V is 0 ⊗̂_K V = 0.

**Acceptance.**

- For V finite-dimensional over K, V ⊗̂_K X = V ⊗_K X and (b) is the exactness of V ⊗_K − over a field.
- For a closed subspace V' ⊆ V, V' ⊗̂_K X → V ⊗̂_K X is injective with closed image.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/countable-type-closed-subspace-section`.

<a id="p4-rank-one-residue-field-rigidity"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity` — A map of perfectoid fields that is injective on geometric points is an isomorphism

*Lemma.* Let K → L be a continuous homomorphism of perfectoid fields (it is injective and, after normalisation, isometric). Suppose that for every algebraically closed perfectoid field C, any two continuous homomorphisms L → C that agree on K are equal; equivalently Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is injective on (C, O_C)-valued points. Then K → L is an isomorphism. The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is required for all perfectoid fields C instead of algebraically closed ones.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Both fields perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.6), of the same characteristic.

**Proof outline.**

1. D := L ⊗̂_K L is a perfectoid Tate ring, already uniform before any uniformization (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; KL15 Proposition 3.6.11 for ℚ_p-algebras; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).
2. For a ∈ L the element a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a maps to 0 in K(z) for every rank-one point z of Spa(D, D°): K(z) is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), it embeds into an algebraically closed perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), and the two composites L → C agree on K.
3. Hence its spectral seminorm, the maximum over the Gel'fand spectrum, i.e. over the rank-one points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm), vanishes, and it is 0 because D is uniform. So the multiplication D → L, whose kernel is topologically generated by these elements, is an isomorphism, and inl : L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism.
4. With V := L/K (a K-Banach space, K being closed in L), the strict exact sequence 0 → K → L → V → 0 stays strict exact after L ⊗̂_K − (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel (b), (c)); as L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism, V ⊗̂_K L = 0, hence V = 0 and K = L.

**Acceptance.**

- For a nontrivial finite separable extension L/K, the hypothesis fails: two distinct K-embeddings L → C exist.
- For K → K the hypothesis holds trivially and the conclusion is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel`](#p4-completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`](#p4-algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p2-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/InjectionCriteria

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

<a id="p4-field-points-of-residually-injective-maps"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps` — (K, K⁺)-points of a map that is injective on points with isomorphic rank-one residue fields

*Lemma.* Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is injective and, for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x, the map of completed residue fields K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism. Then for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective, and its image consists of the φ whose closed point maps into f(|Y|).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X, Y perfectoid spaces; the hypothesis is condition (iii) of ECD Proposition 5.3.

**Proof outline.**

1. Every φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) factors uniquely through i_x, x = image of the closed point (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)); replace X by X' := Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by Y' := Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. The hypothesis passes to Y' → X': Y' → Y is a base change of the injection i_x; along a chain of generalizations the completed residue fields coincide, and by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective each point of |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| has exactly one preimage, because the fibre product of two affinoid fields with the same field over a third is Spa of that field with the larger of the two valuation rings.
3. Now |Y'| ⊆ |X'| is stable under generalization (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing) inside the chain |X'|; every quasicompact open V ⊆ Y' has a unique closed point v, so V = Spa(K(v), K(v)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point) with K(v) = K(x); thus Y' is an increasing union of open subspaces Spa(K(x), K'⁺) ⊆ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points).
4. For each such open, Spa(K(x), K'⁺)(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)(K, K⁺) is injective with image the morphisms (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) carrying K'⁺ into K⁺, i.e. those whose closed point lands in Spa(K(x), K'⁺). Taking the union gives the claim for Y' → X', hence for Y → X.

**Acceptance.**

- For f = i_x, (K, K⁺)-points of Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) are the (K, K⁺)-points of X whose closed point is a generalization of x.

<a id="p4-stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer` — The stalk of O⁺/ϖ at x is K(x)⁺/ϖ

*Lemma.* Let X be a perfectoid space (more generally an analytic adic space), U ⊆ X open, ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(U) a pseudouniformizer and x ∈ U. The natural map O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺ has dense image, its kernel I satisfies I = ϖI, and the induced map O⁺_{X,x}/ϖ → K(x)⁺/ϖ is an isomorphism. Consequently the stalk at x of the sheaf O⁺_X/ϖ is K(x)⁺/ϖ.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- O⁺_X(V) = {f ∈ O_X(V) : |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ V} (anchor Layer 3.3).

**Proof outline.**

1. Dense image: the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x} is dense in K(x), and O⁺_{X,x} maps onto a dense subring of K(x)⁺ (completed residue field construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). Since ϖK(x)⁺ is open, O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺/ϖ is surjective.
2. Kernel: if f ∈ O⁺_X(V) has f(x) = 0 then V' := {y ∈ V : |f(y)| ≤ |ϖ(y)|} is a rational neighbourhood of x on which f/ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(V') with (f/ϖ)(x) = 0; so I = ϖI.
3. Injectivity modulo ϖ: if g ∈ O⁺_{X,x} maps into ϖK(x)⁺, lift the quotient to h ∈ O⁺_{X,x}; then g − ϖh ∈ I = ϖI.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x the closed point, O⁺_{X,x} = K⁺ and the lemma is trivial.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §II.3.1, before Lemma II.3.1. The generality; the proof uses only a pseudouniformizer, so it holds on any analytic adic space.

<a id="p4-isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs` — A homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue pairs is an isomorphism

*Lemma.* Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is a homeomorphism and, for every y ∈ Y with x = f(y), the map (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K(y), K(y)⁺) is an isomorphism of affinoid perfectoid fields. Then f is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No quasicompactness is assumed: over an open affinoid U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to U, hence qcqs.

**Proof outline.**

1. Work over a rational subset U ⊆ X with pseudouniformizer ϖ; put V = f⁻¹(U). By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer the map of sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖ) on |U| is an isomorphism on stalks (f is a homeomorphism), hence an isomorphism; by dévissage along 0 → O⁺/ϖ^{n−1} → O⁺/ϖⁿ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free) so is O⁺_X/ϖⁿ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ).
2. Taking sections: O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity), and O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) is injective; comparing through the isomorphism H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) ≅ H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) shows that O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ is an almost isomorphism.
3. Both O⁺_X(U) and O⁺_Y(V) are ϖ-adically complete (V is covered by finitely many affinoids); passing to the limit (the lim and lim¹ of almost zero systems are almost zero) and inverting ϖ gives O_X(U) ≅ O_Y(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
4. The valuations at y and f(y) agree by hypothesis, O⁺ = {|·| ≤ 1} on both sides, so f is an isomorphism of structure sheaves compatible with the stalk valuations over the homeomorphism |f|, i.e. an isomorphism in the anchor's category of adic spaces (anchor Layers 3.4 and 5).

**Acceptance.**

- The identity of any perfectoid space.
- Non-example: Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite extension L ≠ K is a homeomorphism of one-point spaces but K → L is not an isomorphism.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer`](#p4-stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-integral-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`](#p0-almost-inversion-and-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields).

<a id="p4-qcqs-isomorphism-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion` — Isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps: bijectivity on points and on (C, C⁺)-points

*Theorem.* Let f : Y → X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated morphism of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps). The following are equivalent: (i) f is an isomorphism; (ii) |f| : |Y| → |X| is bijective and for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x the map K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism; (iii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is a bijection; (iv) for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺) the map Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺) is a bijection. (ECD Lemma 5.4.)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- f quasicompact and quasiseparated; this is used in (ii)+(iii) ⇒ (i) to make |f| a spectral map of spectral spaces over an affinoid.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) ⇒ (ii), (iii), (iv) are clear; (iii) ⇒ (iv) is trivial.
2. (ii) ⇒ (iii): a (K, K⁺)-point of X with closed point x factors through i_x (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); replace X by Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by the base change. Then Y has a unique closed point y, so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point); K(x) = K(y) by (ii), and bijectivity of |f| forces K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.
3. (iii) ⇒ (ii): it suffices that Y ×_X Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) is an isomorphism; (iii) gives a unique section; i_y for its image y still satisfies (iii), so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺), and K(x) → K(y) → K(x) composing to the identity forces K(y) = K(x) and K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.
4. (iv) ⇒ (ii): |f| is surjective (extend (K(x), K(x)⁺) to an algebraically closed (C, C⁺) with C⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and lift, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field); |f| is injective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective gives two (L, L⁺)-points with equal image, extended to (C, C⁺)); for rank-one y ↦ x, Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (C, O_C)-points because f and i_y are, so K(x) = K(y) by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity. (ECD argues instead by Galois equivariance; see sourceIssues.)
5. (ii) + (iii) ⇒ (i): reduce to X affinoid, so Y is qcqs; |f| is a bijective, generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), spectral map of spectral spaces, hence a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient) and a homeomorphism; the residue pairs agree by the proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii), so f is an isomorphism by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs.

**Acceptance.**

- ECD Lemma 7.19: a qcqs map to a strictly totally disconnected space that is a bijective injection is an isomorphism.
- Quasicompactness is needed: for an infinite profinite set S and X = S × Spa(C, O_C) = Spa(C⁰(S, C), C⁰(S, O_C)), the map Y = ⊔_{s∈S} Spa(C, O_C) → X is bijective on underlying sets and on all (K, K⁺)-points (Spa(K, K⁺) is connected) but is not an isomorphism; it is not quasicompact.
- A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is qcqs and bijective on points but fails (ii) and (iv).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`](#p4-quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`](#p4-affinoid-perfectoid-field-points), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`](#p4-residue-field-point-injection), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point`](#p4-qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`](#p4-algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`](#p4-fibre-product-points-surjective), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity`](#p4-rank-one-residue-field-rigidity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`](#p4-maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs`](#p4-isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §5, Lemma 5.4 (iv), p. 23. The test on algebraically closed (C, C⁺).

<a id="p4-injection-criteria"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria` — Characterisations of injections of perfectoid spaces

*Theorem.* Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces); (ii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺), Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective; (ii') the same for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺); (iii) |f| is injective and K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x; (iv) |f| is injective and, for every perfectoid space Z, Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) ×_{C⁰(|Z|, |X|)} C⁰(|Z|, |Y|) is a bijection, i.e. f is final among morphisms g : Z → X for which |g| factors through a continuous map |Z| → |Y|. In particular injections Y → X are determined, up to unique isomorphism over X, by the continuous injection |Y| → |X|; |Y| need not carry the subspace topology of |X|. (ECD Proposition 5.3; (ii') is Berkeley Lectures Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3).)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No quasicompactness hypothesis.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (ii') are clear; (ii') ⇒ (ii) is PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field (c); (iv) ⇒ (i) is clear.
2. (ii) ⇒ (iii), injectivity of |f|: if y₁ ≠ y₂ map to x, base change along i_x and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective give (L, L⁺)-points ỹ₁ ≠ ỹ₂ with the same image.
3. (ii) ⇒ (iii), residue fields: for rank-one y ↦ x, g : Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (K, K⁺)-points because f and the injection i_y are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); conclude by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity.
4. (iii) ⇒ (iv): by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps, f_* is injective on (K, K⁺)-points with image the points whose closed point lies in f(|Y|). Given g : Z → X with |g| factoring continuously through |Y|, work locally on Z so that X, Y, Z are affinoid; the qcqs map Y ×_X Z → Z is then bijective on all (K, K⁺)-points, hence an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion), and its inverse gives the unique factorization; uniqueness glues.
5. Determination by |Y| → |X| is (iv).

**Acceptance.**

- Rational open immersions and the residue-field points i_x satisfy (iii).
- Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite separable extension L ≠ K fails (ii') and (iii) although |f| is injective.
- ECD Lemma 9.9 applies (ii) together with the valuative criterion to recognise an injection.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`](#p4-affinoid-perfectoid-field-points), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`](#p4-residue-field-point-injection), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`](#p4-algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`](#p4-fibre-product-points-surjective), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity`](#p4-rank-one-residue-field-rigidity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps`](#p4-field-points-of-residually-injective-maps), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion`](#p4-qcqs-isomorphism-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

<a id="p4-injections-base-change-composition"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition` — Base change of injections, and the underlying space of a pulled-back injection

*Theorem.* Let f : Y → X be an injection of perfectoid spaces and X' → X any morphism, with base change f' : Y' = X' ×_X Y → X'. Then f' is an injection, and the natural map |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is a homeomorphism (the target with the fibre product topology). Moreover composites of injections are injections, and if g ∘ f is an injection then so is f. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (i).)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- f an injection; X' → X arbitrary.

**Proof outline.**

1. f' is an injection: monomorphisms are stable under pullback (in any category with pullbacks).
2. |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is injective because |f| and |f'| are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii)); it is surjective and spectral (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective) and generalizing, both sides being generalization-stable subsets of |X'| (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing).
3. On spectral opens a bijective generalizing spectral map of spectral spaces is a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient), hence a homeomorphism.
4. Composition and cancellation are formal from the definition.

**Acceptance.**

- For f a rational open immersion U ⊆ X, Y' is the preimage of U in X' with its open subspace structure.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`](#p4-injection-criteria), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`](#p4-fibre-product-points-surjective), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`](#p4-maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Mono`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

<a id="p4-injection-iff-universally-injective"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-iff-universally-injective` — Injections are exactly the universally injective maps

*Theorem.* A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if and only if it is universally injective: for every morphism X' → X the base change f' : X' ×_X Y → X' is injective on underlying spaces. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (ii).)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- None beyond the existence of fibre products.

**Proof outline.**

1. ⇒: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii).
2. ⇐: given g : Z → X, pull back along g to reduce to Z = X; it suffices that f has at most one section. A section h is an injection (split monomorphism), and |X| → |Y| → |X| is the identity with both maps injective, so |h| is a homeomorphism with inverse |f|.
3. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv) applied to h, every morphism into Y factors uniquely through h; so h is an isomorphism, f is its inverse, and the section is unique.

**Acceptance.**

- A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is injective on points but not universally injective: its self-fibre product has two points over one.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition`](#p4-injections-base-change-composition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`](#p4-injection-criteria), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces).

<a id="p4-perfectoid-immersion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion` — Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces) and |f| : |Y| → |X| is a locally closed immersion, i.e. a topological embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`) with locally closed image (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed`). It is an open immersion (resp. closed immersion) if moreover |f| is an open (resp. closed) embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`) (ECD Definition 5.6). The definition is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent structure: an injection is determined by its image as a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)), so an immersion is determined up to unique isomorphism over X by the locally closed subset f(|Y|). These notions live in the namespace `PerfectoidSpace` and are compared with the anchor's open and closed immersions in PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/anchor-closed-immersion-comparison; closed immersions are strictly more general than Zariski closed immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Topology of |Y| is its own spectral-space topology; the embedding condition says it is the subspace topology.

**Proof outline.**

1. The definition is a conjunction of an injection with a topological condition; nothing to construct.
2. Uniqueness given the image: two immersions with the same image are injections with homeomorphic images, hence uniquely isomorphic over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is an embedding with locally closed range.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is an open embedding.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is a closed embedding.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion.isImmersion` (relation): Open immersions are immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion.isImmersion` (relation): Closed immersions are immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.isInjection` (projection): Immersions are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.isLocallyClosed_range` (projection): The image of an immersion is locally closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.ext` (extensionality): Two immersions into X with the same image are uniquely isomorphic over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.stableUnderGeneralization_range` (other): The image of an immersion is stable under generalization.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` (instance): Closed immersions are quasicompact: the preimage of a quasicompact open is closed in it.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.comp` (structure): Composites of (open, closed) immersions are (open, closed) immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes of (open, closed) immersions are (open, closed) immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion.of_isOpen` (constructor): For U ⊆ |X| open, the open perfectoid subspace U → X is an open immersion.

**Unit tests.**

- `isOpenImmersion_rationalSubset` (computation): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and U ⊆ X rational, U → X is an open immersion.
- `isClosedImmersion_origin` (computation): The point T^{1/pⁿ} = 0 (all n), i.e. Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), is a closed immersion.

- `not_isImmersion_residueFieldPoint` (non-example): For the Gauss point η of the perfectoid disc, i_η is an injection but not an immersion: {η} is not locally closed (every open neighbourhood of η contains all but finitely many of its rank-two specializations).

- `isImmersion_iff_scheme_analog` (compatibility): Like Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion` (embedding with locally closed range plus a local condition), IsImmersion f ↔ IsInjection f ∧ IsEmbedding |f| ∧ IsLocallyClosed (range |f|); here the local condition is the injection property.

- Diagonals are immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

<a id="p4-immersions-base-change-and-composition"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition` — Immersions are stable under base change and composition; closed immersions are quasicompact

*Lemma.* Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces are stable under composition and under base change along arbitrary morphisms; for an immersion f : Y → X and X' → X, the image of the base change is the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|. Closed immersions are quasicompact; an immersion is a closed immersion if and only if its image is closed.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Morphisms of perfectoid spaces; fibre products as in P2.

**Proof outline.**

1. Base change: by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition the base change f' is an injection and |Y'| ≅ |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|; since |Y| → |X| is an embedding, the fibre product topology is the subspace topology of the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|, which is locally closed (open, closed) when f(|Y|) is.
2. Composition: composites of injections are injections, and composites of embeddings with locally closed (open, closed) images have locally closed (open, closed) images (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed.image` for embeddings with locally closed range).
3. Quasicompactness: for a quasicompact open U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to the closed subset f(|Y|) ∩ U of U.

**Acceptance.**

- The preimage of a rational subset under any morphism is rational, and the base change of its inclusion is that rational open immersion.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`](#p4-perfectoid-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition`](#p4-injections-base-change-composition), `mathlib:IsLocallyClosed`, `mathlib:Topology.IsEmbedding`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Immersion

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §5, Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24. The input from which base change of immersions follows.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §5, before Definition 5.6, p. 24. The role of Corollary 5.5 for the immersion notions.

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P4`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p4-open-immersion-comparison"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison` — Open immersions of perfectoid spaces agree with the anchor's open immersions

*Comparison.* For a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: (a) f is an open immersion in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion; (b) f is an open immersion of adic spaces in the sense of the anchor (Layer 5.1): an isomorphism onto the open adic subspace X|_U, U = f(|Y|). Every open subset U ⊆ |X| underlies the perfectoid open subspace X|_U (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are open affinoid perfectoid subspaces, and the open immersions into X correspond bijectively to the open subsets of |X|.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Perfectoid spaces are adic spaces of the anchor (P2), so both notions apply to the same morphisms.

**Proof outline.**

1. (b) ⇒ (a): X|_U → X is a monomorphism, because a morphism Z → X factors through X|_U if and only if |Z| lands in U, and then uniquely (anchor Layer 5.1 universal property of open subspaces); |X|_U| → |X| is an open embedding.
2. (a) ⇒ (b): X|_U → X is an injection with the same image and topology as f, so Y ≅ X|_U over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(R, R⁺) and U = X(T/s) rational, (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is the rational localization and U → X is an open immersion in both senses.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`](#p4-perfectoid-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`](#p4-injection-criteria), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §10, after Remark 10.8, p. 51. The same compatibility recorded one level up, for pro-étale stacks.

<a id="p4-zariski-closed-immersion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion` — Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions into affinoid perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. For an ideal I ⊆ R put V(I) := {x ∈ |X| : |g(x)| = 0 for all g ∈ I}; a subset Z ⊆ |X| is Zariski closed if Z = V(I) for some ideal I (Scholze torsion paper Definition II.2.1). A morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces is a Zariski closed immersion (defined by I) if f is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion) and f(|Z|) = V(I) (ECD Definition 5.7 (i)). Conventions: V(I) depends only on the closure of I and on its radical; V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F with U_F := {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F} rational, because I is an ideal and |ϖ(x)|ⁿ → 0 cofinally at every continuous valuation; V(I) is closed, pro-constructible and stable under generalization; V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J) and V(IJ) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J). Every Zariski closed subset is the image of exactly one Zariski closed immersion up to unique isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal). A Zariski closed immersion defined by I is not Spa(R/I, ·): the perfectoid structure on V(I) kills all compatible p-power roots.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; the global notion over non-affinoid X (locally Zariski closed) is PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding.

**Proof outline.**

1. V(I) = ⋂ U_F: '⊆' is clear; if |g(x)| ≠ 0 for some g ∈ I then |ϖ^{−n}g(x)| > 1 for n large, as |ϖ(x)|ⁿ is eventually below every element of the value group of the continuous valuation x (anchor Layer 1.5), and ϖ^{−n}g ∈ I.
2. Closedness: V(I) = ⋂_{g∈I} {|g| = 0} and each {|g| = 0} is the complement of ⋃_n {|ϖⁿ| ≤ |g|}, a union of rational subsets; pro-constructibility and generalization-stability follow from the intersection formula.
3. The formula V(I) = image of the anchor's quotient pair: Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom` identifies {v : I ⊆ supp v} with V(I).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus` (data): V(I) ⊆ |Spa(R, R⁺)| for an ideal I ⊆ R.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_eq_iInter_rational` (characterisation): V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isClosed_zeroLocus` (other): V(I) is closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.stableUnderGeneralization_zeroLocus` (other): V(I) is stable under generalization.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_sup` (simp): V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_mul` (simp): V(I·J) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_closure` (simp): V(closure I) = V(I) and V(√I) = V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosed` (structure): A subset of |X| of the form V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion` (structure): f : Z → Spa(R, R⁺) is a closed immersion with f(|Z|) = V(I) for some ideal I.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` (projection): Zariski closed immersions are closed immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.iso_zariskiClosedSubspace` (characterisation): A Zariski closed immersion defined by I is uniquely isomorphic over X to Z_I → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes along maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are Zariski closed, defined by IR'.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.of_isStronglyZariskiClosed` (relation): Strongly Zariski closed immersions are Zariski closed.

**Unit tests.**

- `zeroLocus_T` (computation): For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V((T)) = {origin}, and the Zariski closed immersion is Spa(C, O_C) → X; its kernel is the closure of the ideal generated by all T^{1/pⁿ}, not (T).
- `zeroLocus_T_sub_one` (computation): For C ∋ μ_{p^∞}, V((T − 1)) ⊆ Spa(C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) is homeomorphic to ℤ_p (compatible systems of p-power roots of unity).
- `zeroLocus_bot_top` (degenerate): V(0) = |X| and V(R) = ∅.
- `not_isZariskiClosed_annulusClosure` (non-example): The closure of the annulus {|T| = 1} in the perfectoid closed disc is closed, generalizing and the image of a closed immersion, but it is not Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed).
- `zeroLocus_eq_range_quotient` (compatibility): V(I) equals the range of Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap (quotientHom S I)`, i.e. {v : I ⊆ supp v}.

**Uses.**

- ECD Theorem 5.8 and PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed: the statement that Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed
- ECD Remark 7.9 and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale: Zariski closed immersions of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid pro-étale
- ECD Proposition 5.9: diagonals of maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are Zariski closed
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: the global notion is local on the target
- Scholze torsion paper §§II.3, III.2 and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties: Hodge-type Shimura varieties at infinite level are Zariski closed in the Siegel case, hence perfectoid
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: comparison with Fargues–Scholze's Zariski closed immersions into relative balls

**Acceptance.**

- For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V((T)) is the single point T = 0, and V((T − 1)) is the profinite set of classical points (T^{1/pⁿ}) = (ζ_{pⁿ}^a)_n, a ∈ ℤ_p, when C contains all p-power roots of unity.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`](#p4-perfectoid-immersion), `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space).

<a id="p4-strongly-zariski-closed-immersion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion` — Strongly Zariski closed immersions: surjective perfectoid quotients

*Definition.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. A morphism f : Z → X is strongly Zariski closed if Z = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, f is induced by a morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with R → S surjective, and S⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺ in S (ECD Definition 5.7 (ii)). Equivalently (by the open mapping theorem, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), with I := ker(R → S) closed, (S, S⁺) is isomorphic to the anchor's quotient pair Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I` and R/I is perfectoid. The plus-ring clause is part of the definition: it is what makes a strongly Zariski closed map a closed immersion. Scholze's earlier Definition II.2.6 (R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective) omits it and is strictly weaker (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; S perfectoid is part of the data (a quotient R/I of a perfectoid R is perfectoid iff it is uniform, Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4(a)).

**Proof outline.**

1. Equivalence with the quotient pair: R → S is a continuous surjection of complete Tate rings, hence open (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`), so R/I ≅ S topologically, I closed; the plus rings agree by definition of Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` (integral closure of the image of R⁺).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed` (structure): Z = Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) with R → S surjective and S⁺ the integral closure of the image of R⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.surjective` (projection): R → S is surjective.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.plus_eq` (projection): S⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.isClosed_ker` (other): ker(R → S) is closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.iff_quotient` (compatibility): Equivalent to being Spa of the anchor quotient pair Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I with R/I perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.isZariskiClosedImmersion` (relation): Strongly Zariski closed maps are Zariski closed immersions defined by ker(R → S).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.almostSurjective_plus` (relation): R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.comp` (structure): Composites are strongly Zariski closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes along maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are strongly Zariski closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.tilt` (compatibility): f is strongly Zariski closed iff its tilt is (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-tilting).

**Unit tests.**

- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_origin` (computation): C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C, T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0, with plus rings O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → O_C, is strongly Zariski closed.
- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_id` (degenerate): The identity of X and the map from the empty space Spa(0, 0) are strongly Zariski closed.
- `not_isStronglyZariskiClosed_ofPowerBounded` (non-example): For R⁺ ⊊ R°, Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺) has R → R surjective and R⁺ → R° almost surjective (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), but R° is not the integral closure of R⁺, so it is not strongly Zariski closed (nor a closed immersion).
- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_iff_quotient` (compatibility): f is strongly Zariski closed iff (S, S⁺) ≅ Tau Ceti Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) (ker(R → S)) over (R, R⁺) with S perfectoid.

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 5.9: the diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed
- ECD Theorem 5.8 via PerfectoidQuotients:Q4: Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: affinoid étale perfectoid spaces embed strongly Zariski closed into perfectoid relative balls
- Scholze torsion paper §III (boundary of Shimura varieties): the boundary is strongly Zariski closed
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: the affinoid pieces of a Zariski-closed embedding

**Acceptance.**

- The diagonal Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(S, S⁺) ×_{Spa(R, R⁺)} Spa(S, S⁺) of any map of affinoid perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotientHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

<a id="p4-surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings` — A surjection of perfectoid Tate rings is almost surjective on integral elements

*Lemma.* Let ψ : R → S be a surjective continuous homomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings and R⁺ ⊆ R°, S⁺ ⊆ S° rings of integral elements with ψ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺. Then R° → S° and R⁺ → S⁺ are almost surjective: for every pseudouniformizer ϖ of R admitting compatible p-power roots, S°/ψ(R°) and S⁺/ψ(R⁺) are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Equivalently, the quotient seminorm on S induced by the spectral norm of R equals the spectral norm of S. In particular, for a strongly Zariski closed Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺), R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.8).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R, S perfectoid Tate rings of any characteristic, not necessarily over a field or over ℚ_p.

**Proof outline.**

1. Promote R and S to uniform Banach rings with their spectral norms; ψ is submetric, and by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`) the quotient norm is at most c times the spectral norm of S for some c > 1.
2. Improvement c ↦ c^{1/p}: given b ∈ S, lift b^p to a₀ with |a₀| ≤ c|b|^p, approximate a₀ by a sharp element ♯(x) with x ∈ R♭ and α(a₀ − ♯(x)) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a₀), |b|^p} for every α in the Gel'fand spectrum of R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (d); Kedlaya AWS (2.8.5.1), whose factor p⁻¹ is α(p) for the normalisation |p| = p⁻¹), and take a = ♯(x^{1/p}) (♯ is multiplicative, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map); the p-th power map estimate in a nonarchimedean field gives |b − ψ(a)| ≤ p^{−1/p}|b| at every point of the Gel'fand spectrum, the case β(p) = 0 being trivial (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.5, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(c)).
3. Iterating, the quotient norm is ≤ c^{1/pⁿ}·(spectral norm) for all n, so it equals the spectral norm; hence ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°) + ϖS° for all n, and completeness gives ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°).
4. For plus rings: ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S⁺ ⊆ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R°) ⊆ ψ(R°°) ⊆ ψ(R⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S = C (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0): R° → S° = O_C is surjective.
- Characteristic p: a strict surjection of perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebras is almost optimal (KL15 Remark 3.1.6(a)).

<a id="p4-surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting` — Surjectivity and closed ideals with perfectoid quotient under tilting

*Lemma.* Let f : A → B be a continuous homomorphism of Tate rings with A perfectoid. (a) If B is uniform and f is surjective then B is perfectoid. (b) If B is perfectoid then f is surjective if and only if its tilt f♭ : A♭ → B♭ is surjective. (c) I ↦ I♭ := ker(A♭ → (A/I)♭) is a bijection between closed ideals I ⊆ A with A/I uniform (equivalently perfectoid) and closed perfect ideals of A♭; the inverse sends J to the closure of the ideal generated by {♯(x) : x ∈ J}. (d) A closed ideal I ⊆ A has A/I perfectoid if and only if I is the closure of the ideal generated by ♯(x^{1/pⁿ}) for x in some subset of A♭ and all n ≥ 0. (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4, Corollaries 2.4.5–2.4.6.)

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Tate rings; A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): a uniform ring with a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3(a) via Lemma 2.8.4).
2. (b) ⇐: θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺ is surjective, so the composite W(A♭) → W(B♭) → B is surjective when f♭ is (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel). ⇒: from PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings, lift ♯(b) with norm ≤ p^{1/2}|b| and correct by sharp approximations (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c), with (e) bounding ♯(b) − ♯(f♭(a)) − ♯(b − f♭(a))); iterating lifts every b ∈ B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.6, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(d)).
3. (c): by (b), closed ideals with perfectoid quotient correspond to surjections of perfectoid rings, hence to surjections of their tilts, i.e. to closed ideals of A♭ with perfect uniform quotient; a quotient of a perfect uniform ring by a closed perfect ideal is perfect and uniform (x̃^{1/p} lifts x^{1/p}), and conversely the kernel of a map to a perfect ring is perfect.
4. (d) follows from (c) with the subset {♯(x) : x ∈ I♭}.

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I the closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0), A/I = K and I♭ is the closure of (T♭^{1/pⁿ}).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings`](#p4-surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion`](#p2-perfectoid-dense-image-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`](#p1-tilt-functoriality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma`](#p1-sharp-approximation-lemma), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`](#p1-sharp-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`](#p1-fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

<a id="p4-universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed` — The universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset

*Construction.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and I ⊆ R an ideal. Let 𝒰_I := {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}, U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}, and let ι_I : Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) → X be the pro-rational subspace of 𝒰_I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets): S_I⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_F O⁺_X(U_F) and S_I = S_I⁺[1/ϖ]. Then: (a) Z_I is affinoid perfectoid and R → S_I has dense image; (b) |ι_I| is a homeomorphism onto V(I); (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_I if and only if g^*(h) = 0 in O_W(W) for all h ∈ I, if and only if |g| lands in V(I), and then uniquely; (d) ι_I is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion); (e) I^perf := ker(R → S_I) is a closed ideal containing I, equal to {h ∈ R : |h| = 0 on V(I)}, and Z_{I^perf} = Z_I; (f) Z_I depends only on V(I). In characteristic-free generality this is Scholze's Lemma II.2.2 with Remark II.2.3 (stated over a perfectoid field) and Bhatt's Proposition 9.4.1 (1)–(3). Surjectivity of R → S_I is ECD Theorem 5.8 and is imported (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed); it is not used in this construction.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid with a pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots; I arbitrary (not necessarily closed or finitely generated).

**Proof outline.**

1. V(I) = ⋂ U_F (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion), and 𝒰_I is filtered (U_F ∩ U_G = U_{F∪G}); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets for (a), (b) and the topological universal property.
2. (c): if |g| lands in V(I), each g^*(h), h ∈ I, vanishes at every point of W; on an affinoid perfectoid open of W (uniform) its spectral seminorm, a maximum over points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm), is 0, so g^*(h) = 0. Conversely g^*(h) = 0 forces |h| = 0 on the image.
3. (d): ι_I is an injection with |ι_I| a homeomorphism onto the closed subset V(I), hence a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion), with image V(I).
4. (e), (f): h ∈ ker(R → S_I) iff |h| = 0 on |Z_I| = V(I) (S_I uniform); both Z_I and Z_{I^perf} are pro-rational subspaces with intersection V(I) = V(I^perf).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace` (constructor): Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) for an ideal I ⊆ R.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.ι` (data): ι_I : Z_I → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.range_ι` (characterisation): |ι_I| is a homeomorphism onto V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.lift` (universal-property): A morphism W → X killing I factors uniquely through ι_I; lift_ι, lift_unique.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.isZariskiClosedImmersion` (relation): ι_I is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.denseRange` (other): R → S_I has dense image.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.ker_eq` (characterisation): ker(R → S_I) = {h : |h| = 0 on V(I)}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.congr` (extensionality): V(I) = V(J) ⇒ Z_I ≅ Z_J uniquely over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace_sup` (simp): Z_{I+J} ≅ Z_I ×_X Z_J.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.plus_mod` (simp): S_I⁺/ϖ = colim_F O⁺_X(U_F)/ϖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (simp): Z_0 = X, Z_R = ∅.

**Unit tests.**

- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T` (computation): R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, I = (T): S_I = C, and ker(R → S_I) is the closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) ⊋ (T); R/(T) is not reduced (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T_sub_one` (computation): C = ℂ_p, R = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, I = (T − 1): S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p), with T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ (γ ↦ ζ_{pⁿ}^γ) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.10).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (degenerate): Z_0 = X and Z_R = ∅.
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_ne_quotient` (non-example): Spa(R/I, ·) is not Z_I in general: for I = (T), R/I is not uniform, so Spa(R/(T), ·) is not a perfectoid space, while Z_I = Spa(C, O_C).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_eq_proRational` (compatibility): Z_I is the pro-rational subspace of the family {U_F}; if I is generated by g₁, …, g_k admitting compatible p-power roots g_i = ♯(g_i♭), then S_I = R/J with J the closure of the ideal generated by all g_i^{1/pⁿ} (R/J is perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (d), and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed identifies Spa(R/J, ·) with Z_I).

**Uses.**

- Scholze torsion paper §III.3 (Hodge type): Zariski closed subsets of perfectoid Siegel spaces are perfectoid
- ECD Remark 7.9 and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale: Z = lim U_F is a pro-étale presentation
- PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed: the closed perfectoid quotient R' = S_perfd[1/ϖ] is identified with S_I
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: affinoid Zariski-closed subsets are affinoid perfectoid
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8 (compatible-root closed locus): the kernel of R → S_I kills all compatible roots

**Acceptance.**

- For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I = (T): S_I = C, and I^perf is the closure of the ideal generated by all T^{1/pⁿ}.
- For I = 0: Z_I = X; for I = R: Z_I = ∅.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets`](#p4-intersection-of-rational-subsets), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`](#p4-zariski-closed-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`](#p4-perfectoid-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space).

<a id="p4-zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal` — Every Zariski closed immersion is the universal one

*Lemma.* Let f : Z → X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a Zariski closed immersion defined by an ideal I. Then there is a unique isomorphism Z ≅ Z_I over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed). Consequently Z is affinoid perfectoid, Z = lim_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F, and a Zariski closed immersion is determined by its image V(I).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof outline.**

1. f and ι_I are injections whose underlying maps are homeomorphisms onto the same subset V(I) with its subspace topology (f is a closed immersion; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed (b)).
2. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv), injections into X are determined up to unique isomorphism by the continuous injection of underlying spaces.

**Acceptance.**

- The Zariski closed immersion Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) at the origin is Z_{(T)}.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed`](#p4-universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`](#p4-zariski-closed-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`](#p4-injection-criteria).

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §II.2, after Remark II.2.3, p. 14. The identification of a Zariski closed subset with its universal perfectoid space.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §7, Remark 7.9, p. 32. The consumer: the limit presentation of an arbitrary Zariski closed immersion.

<a id="p4-strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed` — A surjective perfectoid quotient is a Zariski closed immersion (the direction proved here)

*Lemma.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be affinoid perfectoid, ψ : R → S a surjective continuous homomorphism onto a perfectoid Tate ring, I := ker ψ and S⁺ the integral closure of ψ(R⁺). Then: (a) I is closed and (S, S⁺) ≅ Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`; (b) Z := Spa(S, S⁺) → X is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I, and |Z| → V(I) is a homeomorphism; (c) Z ≅ Z_I over X, so S = S_I and I = I^perf. Thus every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed. The converse is ECD Theorem 5.8, imported in PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- S perfectoid; ψ surjective.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): ψ is open by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), so S ≅ R/I topologically; I is closed as the kernel of a continuous map to a Hausdorff ring; S⁺ matches Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` by definition.
2. (b): maps W → Z from affinoid perfectoid W are morphisms (S, S⁺) → (O_W(W), O⁺_W(W)); as ψ is surjective they are determined by the composite with ψ, so Z → X is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces). |Z| → |X| is a closed embedding with image {v : I ⊆ supp v} = V(I) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`).
3. (c): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal.

**Acceptance.**

- The diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).
- C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C, T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0: Z = Z_{(T)}.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`](#p4-strongly-zariski-closed-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`](#p4-zariski-closed-immersion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal`](#p4-zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p4-injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`](#p4-perfectoid-immersion), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotientHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space).
