<a id="p5-finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects` — Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii))

*Theorem.* For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). The base change functor Φ: 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs is an equivalence of categories (ECD 6.4(ii)), and it restricts to equivalences 2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét (ECD 6.4(i)) and 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep (ECD 6.4(iii)) on the full subcategories X_fét ⊆ X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs (a finite étale space over an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid perfectoid, hence quasicompact and separated). In explicit form: (full faithfulness) colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_j, Y_j') → Hom_X(Y, Y') is bijective for Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs; (essential surjectivity) every qcqs, resp. quasicompact separated, resp. finite étale, étale Y → X is the base change of a qcqs, resp. quasicompact separated, resp. finite étale, Y_i → X_i; (recognition) a morphism of (X_i)_ét,qcqs whose base change to X is surjective, resp. an isomorphism, is so over some X_j (P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection), and a qcqs étale Y_i whose base change is separated is separated over some X_j (P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage). Part (iv), affinoid étale objects, is AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv and is not claimed here; the cardinal bound of ECD 6.4 is P5/limit-cardinal-bounds.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- The standing setting; no noetherian or characteristic hypothesis.
- The henselian approximation used for (i) is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (Elkik, Gabber–Ramero).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation.
2. (ii): P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent.
3. (iii): P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent.
4. Compatibility: finite étale spaces over affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), affinoid perfectoid spaces are quasicompact and separated, the inclusions commute with base change, and restriction of an equivalence to full subcategories that it matches is an equivalence (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories, API fullSubcategory).

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected: a splitting of an étale cover over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover: an étale cover of the limit comes from a finite stage and becomes split at the next
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: a surjection of the pro-étale site is an étale surjection at a finite level
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: spreading out qc separated étale objects and descent data to a finite level
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons: the three 2-colimit equivalences for diamonds are deduced by v-descent
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4: ECD 6.4 assembled: (o)-(iii) from here, (iv) from A3

**Acceptance.**

- A finite étale cover of a limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the pullback of one at a finite stage, unique up to unique isomorphism at a further stage; an étale surjection over the limit is an étale surjection at a finite stage.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons: for diagrams of diamonds the same three equivalences are deduced from this theorem by v-descent.
- Profinite sets: finite étale, qcqs étale and qc separated étale spaces over S × Spa(K, O_K) are locally on S constant.

<a id="p6"></a>

## P6. Affinoid approximation and pro-étale presentations

Keep cardinal arithmetic in D0, while recording κ-small and uniformly κ-small perfectoid presentations and the corrected singular-cardinal forms. Assemble the affinoid finite-stage theorem from A3 with P5, then define and prove the basic affinoid and local pro-étale calculus. These arguments use neither v-descent nor a diamond atlas; disconnected covers and the actual pro-étale/v sites belong to D1–D3.

**Coverage (`source_decomposed`; packet P0).** All targets of the stage text are realised by 31 nodes. Set-theoretic bounds (ECD 4.2–4.4 with DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal and D0/completion-cardinality-bound): κ-small and uniformly κ-small perfectoid spaces, the cover criterion, closure under open subspaces, disjoint unions, fibre products and tilting, κ-smallness of cofiltered limits, the size of the affinoid étale site, and κ-small perfectoid sub-pairs. ECD Proposition 4.4's converse and its 'stable under finite products' hold only with a uniform bound when κ is singular, and the cutoff cardinal κ(ω₁) constructed in ECD's proof of Lemma 4.1 is singular; the nodes state the corrected forms and the counterexamples (sourceIssue PerfectoidSpaces/E40). ECD 6.4(iv) is imported from AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv and assembled with P5's (i)–(iii), with descent of surjectivity and the relative form the §7 proofs use; P5's qcqs result is not cited for affinoidness. Pro-étale calculus (ECD 7.8–7.11, the DiamondsAndVStacks request): affinoid pro-étale and pro-étale maps as actual cofiltered limits of affinoid étale maps, X × S, the geometric-point example, Zariski closed immersions in the rational-intersection form and diagonals and graphs, the pro-category equivalence with its κ-bounded form, and composition, base change, cancellation, sections, cofiltered and all small limits, both affinoid and local. A comparison with Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects serves ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H2/H4. No proof uses v-descent, a diamond atlas or the analytic-diamond comparison. Totally disconnected, w-local and strictly totally disconnected spaces, w-localization and the strictly totally disconnected cover are DiamondsAndVStacks:D1 nodes and are not planned here. AdicSpacesPartII:R0 enters through completed tensor products in the fibre-product size bound; AdicSpacesPartII:R5 enters only through AdicEtaleGeometry:A3.

**Planets.** κ-small perfectoid space; Affinoid pro-étale morphism; Pro-étale morphism; Product with a profinite set; Pro-category equivalence; Stability of pro-étale morphisms.

<a id="p6-kappa-small-perfectoid-space"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space` — κ-small perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* Fix a cardinal κ with ℵ₀ < κ that is a strong limit (2^λ < κ for every cardinal λ < κ); every cutoff cardinal of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (ECD Lemma 4.1) is one. A perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: an adic space locally isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) for a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field) is κ-small if (i) its underlying set |X| has cardinality #|X| < κ, and (ii) for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X (so A = O_X(U)) the ring A has cardinality #A < κ. The full subcategory of κ-small perfectoid spaces is written Perfd_κ, and for a κ-small X the category of κ-small perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X is X_proét,κ (ECD Definition 8.1). Conventions: cardinalities are those of underlying sets; the plus rings carry no condition (A⁺ ⊆ A); clause (ii) quantifies over all open affinoid subspaces, and there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ of them, so no separate count of charts is imposed; the predicate is invariant under isomorphism and monotone in κ. The bound in (ii) is not uniform over the charts: the stronger notion with a single bound λ < κ is PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space, and for quasicompact X the two agree.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- κ is an uncountable strong limit cardinal; ECD notes that this is all §4 needs. Mathlib's `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts ℵ₀ as a strong limit, so ℵ₀ < κ is a separate hypothesis.
- The cofinality clauses (ii) and (iii) of the cutoff lemma are not part of the definition; they are used only in the limit statements (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits) and in D1's countable iteration.
- Clause (ii) is not implied by clause (i) (a one-point space with a large field), and clause (i) is not implied by clause (ii) (a disjoint union of κ points): both are needed.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `IsKappaSmall κ X` as the conjunction of #|X| < κ and #O_X(U) < κ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X, using the open affinoid subspaces of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space.
2. Record invariance under isomorphisms of perfectoid spaces (an isomorphism induces a bijection of points and of open affinoid subspaces with isomorphic rings) and monotonicity in κ.
3. Record the affinoid characterisation #A < κ and the cover criterion, which are the theorems PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion.
4. Essential smallness of Perfd_κ: a κ-small X is determined up to isomorphism by the topological space |X| (a set of cardinality < κ) and the restriction of (O_X, O_X⁺) with its valuations to the basis of open affinoid subspaces, whose rings have cardinality < κ; transporting all of these along injections into κ shows that the isomorphism classes of κ-small perfectoid spaces form a set, so Perfd_κ is essentially small (mathlib `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall` (structure): IsKappaSmall κ X: #|X| < κ and #O_X(U) < κ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.card_lt` (projection): If X is κ-small then #|X| < κ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.card_sections_lt` (projection): If X is κ-small and U ⊆ X is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace, then #O_X(U) < κ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.of_iso` (compatibility): If X ≅ Y as perfectoid spaces and X is κ-small, then Y is κ-small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.mono` (relation): If κ ≤ κ' (both uncountable strong limits) and X is κ-small, then X is κ'-small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isKappaSmall_affinoid_iff` (characterisation): For X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid: IsKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.of_cover` (constructor): If X has a cover by open affinoid subspaces Spa(A_j, A_j⁺) with #A_j < κ and #|X| < κ, then X is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.isOpen` (functoriality): An open subspace of a κ-small perfectoid space is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.tilt_iff` (compatibility): X is κ-small iff its tilt X♭ is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-tilting).
- `PerfectoidSpace.KappaSmall` (structure): Perfd_κ: the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces on the κ-small objects.
- `PerfectoidSpace.KappaSmall.essentiallySmall` (instance): Perfd_κ is essentially small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.empty` (example): The empty perfectoid space is κ-small.

**Unit tests.**

- `isKappaSmall_spa_Cp` (computation): For every cardinal κ with ℵ₀ < κ and κ a strong limit, Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is κ-small: it has one point and #C_p = 2^ℵ₀ < κ.
- `isKappaSmall_empty` (degenerate): The empty perfectoid space is κ-small for every κ.
- `isKappaSmall_affinoid_iff` (characterisation): For an affinoid perfectoid space X = Spa(A, A⁺), IsKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ.
- `not_isKappaSmall_bigField` (non-example): Let K be the completion, for the Gauss norm, of the perfection of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < κ); K is a perfectoid field with #K ≥ κ. Then Spa(K, K°) has one point but is not κ-small: clause (i) does not imply clause (ii).
- `not_isKappaSmall_sigma` (non-example): The disjoint union of κ copies of Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is not κ-small, although each of its open affinoid subspaces (a finite union of copies) has a ring of cardinality 2^ℵ₀: clause (ii) does not imply clause (i).
- `isKappaSmall_not_uniform` (non-example): If cf κ = ω₁ (as for the cutoff cardinals κ(µ) with cf µ = ω₁ built in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and K_α (α < ω₁) are perfectoid fields with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, then ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°) is κ-small, but no λ < κ bounds the cardinalities of the rings of all its open affinoid subspaces.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1(i)–(iii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site, D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site): the big pro-étale site and the v-site are topologies on Perfd_κ, and X_proét,κ is the site of κ-small pro-étale X-spaces
- ECD Proposition 8.2 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence): pullback c*_{κ,κ'} from X_proét,κ to X_proét,κ' for a κ-small X; the proof writes κ'-small affinoids as limits of κ-small ones
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the strictly totally disconnected cover X̃ of a κ-small affinoid X can be taken κ-small
- ECD Corollary 7.22 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps): κ-small affinoid pro-étale spaces over a strictly totally disconnected X correspond to spectral data of cardinality < κ
- ECD Proposition 6.4, set-theoretic clause (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits): a small cofiltered limit of uniformly κ'-small affinoid perfectoid spaces is κ-small
- ECD Proposition 7.10 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations): κ-small affinoid pro-étale X-spaces correspond to Pro_κ(X_ét^aff)
- ECD Lemma 11.22, Proposition 11.23, Lemma 12.17 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5): κ-smallness of cofiltered limits of diamonds and of v-sheaves admitting a surjection from a κ-small perfectoid space

**Acceptance.**

- For every uncountable strong limit κ, Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) and the perfectoid disc Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) are κ-small: their rings have cardinality 2^ℵ₀ < κ.
- The empty perfectoid space is κ-small.

**Prerequisites.** `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), `mathlib:Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`.

<a id="p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality` — Cardinality of complete Tate rings with a dense subring, and of their rational localisations, finite étale algebras and completed tensor products

*Lemma.* Let A be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`, with its topology complete and separated). (a) If D ⊆ A is a dense subset with #D ≤ λ for an infinite cardinal λ, then #A ≤ λ^ℵ₀ ≤ 2^λ. (b) Consequently, with λ_A := #A + ℵ₀: (b1) for a rational subset U = R(T/s) of Spa(A, A⁺), the rational localisation A⟨T/s⟩ (Tau Ceti `completionLocObj`) has cardinality ≤ λ_A^ℵ₀, as the image of A[1/s] is dense; (b2) a finite étale A-algebra B with its canonical topology has #B ≤ λ_A, being a quotient of some Aⁿ; (b3) for morphisms of complete Tate pairs A → B and A → C, the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) and its uniformisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) have cardinality ≤ (#B·#C·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀, as the image of B ⊗_A C is dense. (c) If κ is an uncountable strong limit and λ < κ, each of these bounds is < κ. This is the Tate-ring instance of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound (the conditional form of ECD Remark 4.3): the first countability it needs holds because the sets ϖⁿA₀ form a countable basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- A Hausdorff: without it the limit of a sequence is not unique and the bound fails.
- Completeness is not needed for (a) (only Hausdorff and first countable); it is part of the setting of (b).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): by first countability every a ∈ A is the limit of a sequence in D; as A is Hausdorff the limit map from the set of convergent sequences in D to A is well defined and surjective, so #A ≤ #D^ℵ₀ ≤ λ^ℵ₀ (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound), and λ^ℵ₀ ≤ (2^λ)^ℵ₀ = 2^{λ·ℵ₀} = 2^λ (mathlib `Cardinal.power_mul`, `Cardinal.power_le_power_right`).
2. (b1): A⟨T/s⟩ is the completion of A[1/s] for the localisation topology, and #A[1/s] ≤ #A·ℵ₀.
3. (b2): B is generated as an A-module by finitely many elements, so it is a quotient of Aⁿ.
4. (b3): the image of B ⊗_A C, a quotient of the free abelian group on B × C, is dense in the completion; uniformisation is a separated completion of a quotient, so the same bound applies.
5. (c): 2^λ < κ for λ < κ.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion: bounds the rings of rational subsets of the charts
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound: bounds the rings of affinoid étale spaces through rational and finite étale pieces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure: bounds the rings of fibre products
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the size of the fibre products X_J and of their limit

**Acceptance.**

- A = C_p with the dense countable subfield of algebraic numbers: #C_p ≤ ℵ₀^ℵ₀ = 2^ℵ₀.
- A = C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with dense subring Q̄_p[T^{1/p^∞}]: # ≤ 2^ℵ₀.
- Without the Hausdorff hypothesis the bound fails: in K[T] with the Gauss-norm topology the ideal (T − c) with |c| > 1 is dense, and K[T]/(T − c) ≅ K with the quotient topology has the dense subset {0}.

**Prerequisites.** `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product`, `mathlib:FirstCountableTopology`, `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`, `mathlib:Cardinal.power_mul`, `mathlib:Cardinal.power_le_power_right`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §4, proof of Proposition 4.4, pp. 20–21. Part (b1): rational localisations have a dense subalgebra finitely generated over the base.

<a id="p6-uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space` — Uniformly κ-small perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. A perfectoid space X is uniformly κ-small if there is a cardinal λ < κ such that #|X| ≤ λ and #O_X(U) ≤ λ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X; equivalently, X is κ'-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space) for some cardinal κ' < κ (take κ' = λ⁺, which is < κ because κ is a limit cardinal). Properties: (a) uniformly κ-small implies κ-small; (b) a quasicompact κ-small perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small, so the two notions have the same affinoid and the same qcqs objects; (c) if κ is regular (a strongly inaccessible cardinal) the two notions agree; (d) they differ for every κ of cofinality ω₁, in particular for the cutoff cardinals κ(µ) with cf µ = ω₁ constructed in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1: ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°), with perfectoid fields K_α whose cardinalities are < κ and cofinal in κ, is κ-small and not uniformly κ-small. The uniformly κ-small spaces satisfy the cover criterion and the stability under fibre products that ECD Proposition 4.4 states for κ-small spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- κ uncountable strong limit; the class is intended for the cutoff cardinals of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal, which are in general singular.
- ECD's own set-theoretic statements (Proposition 6.4, Lemma 11.22) are formulated with such a uniform bound κ' < κ; this node names that hypothesis.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X` as ∃ λ < κ, #|X| ≤ λ ∧ ∀ U open affinoid, #O_X(U) ≤ λ, and prove the equivalence with ∃ κ' < κ, IsKappaSmall κ' X using λ⁺ < κ.
2. (a) is immediate. (b): cover a quasicompact κ-small X by finitely many open affinoids V_1, …, V_n; an open affinoid U ⊆ X is covered by finitely many rational subsets W_k of the V_j contained in U, #O(W_k) ≤ (#O(V_j)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality), and O(U) embeds into ∏_k O(W_k) because O_X is a sheaf (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity); so λ := max(#|X|, max_j (#O(V_j)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀) < κ works.
3. (c): there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ open affinoid subspaces, and for regular κ a supremum of fewer than κ cardinals below κ is below κ (mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord` with cf κ = κ).
4. (d): the space has ℵ₁ points; each open affinoid subspace is a finite union of components, whose ring is a finite product of fields K_α of cardinality < κ, so the space is κ-small; any common bound λ would be ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ. Perfectoid fields K_α with λ_α ≤ #K_α ≤ λ_α^ℵ₀ exist for every cardinal λ_α (completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), and κ(ω₁) of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1 has cofinality ω₁.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall` (structure): ∃ λ < κ, #|X| ≤ λ and #O_X(U) ≤ λ for all open affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isUniformlyKappaSmall_iff_exists_lt` (characterisation): IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ ∃ κ' < κ, IsKappaSmall κ' X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isKappaSmall` (relation): Uniformly κ-small spaces are κ-small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall.of_isKappaSmall_of_compactSpace` (constructor): A quasicompact κ-small perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall.of_isRegular` (constructor): For regular κ every κ-small perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isUniformlyKappaSmall_affinoid_iff` (characterisation): For X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid: IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isOpen` (functoriality): Open subspaces of uniformly κ-small spaces are uniformly κ-small, with the same λ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall.fibreProduct` (functoriality): Fibre products of uniformly κ-small spaces over any perfectoid space are uniformly κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure).

**Unit tests.**

- `isUniformlyKappaSmall_disc` (computation): Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is uniformly κ-small with λ = 2^ℵ₀ for every uncountable strong limit κ.
- `isUniformlyKappaSmall_empty` (degenerate): The empty perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small with λ = 1: its point set is empty and its ring of sections on the empty affinoid open is the zero ring, whose underlying set has one element.
- `isUniformlyKappaSmall_iff_isKappaSmall_of_compactSpace` (characterisation): For a quasicompact perfectoid space X, IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ IsKappaSmall κ X.
- `not_isUniformlyKappaSmall_of_cof_omegaOne` (non-example): For κ with cf κ = ω₁ and perfectoid fields K_α (α < ω₁) with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°) is κ-small and not uniformly κ-small.
- `isUniformlyKappaSmall_of_isRegular` (compatibility): If κ is regular, IsKappaSmall κ X → IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X for every perfectoid space X.

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 4.4, 'In particular' (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site): stability of the underlying category of the sites under fibre products, which holds for this class for every cutoff cardinal
- ECD Proposition 6.4, set-theoretic clause, and Lemma 11.22 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits, DiamondsAndVStacks:D5): the hypothesis 'all X_i are κ′-small for one κ′ < κ'
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the countable iteration keeps a uniform bound below κ at each step

**Acceptance.**

- Every κ-small affinoid perfectoid space is uniformly κ-small with λ the cardinality of its ring raised to ℵ₀.
- The example of (d) separates the notions for κ = κ(ω₁).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `mathlib:Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`, `mathlib:Cardinal.IsRegular`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`.

<a id="p6-adic-spectrum-cardinality"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality` — The adic spectrum of A has at most 2^{#A·#A} points

*Lemma.* Let A be a Huber ring and A⁺ ⊆ A a subring. Then #Spa(A, A⁺) ≤ 2^{#A·#A}: a point of Spv A is determined by its valuative relation {(a, b) ∈ A × A : |a(x)| ≤ |b(x)|} (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.ext'`), so Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ Spv A injects into the power set of A × A. For A infinite this is 2^{#A}. Consequently, if κ is an uncountable strong limit and #A < κ then #Spa(A, A⁺) < κ, and a perfectoid space covered by a family of open affinoids Spa(A_j, A_j⁺), j ∈ J, has at most #J · sup_j 2^{#A_j·#A_j} points.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No hypothesis on A⁺ or on the topology is needed: the bound is for Spv A.

**Proof outline.**

1. The map Spv A → Set (A × A), x ↦ {(a, b) : x.vle a b}, is injective by `ValuationSpectrum.ext'`; restrict it to spa A⁺ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`).
2. #Set (A × A) = 2^{#A·#A} (mathlib `Cardinal.mk_set`, `Cardinal.mk_prod`), and #A·#A = #A for A infinite (mathlib `Cardinal.mul_eq_self`).
3. For a cover, the union bound #⋃_j |U_j| ≤ #J · sup_j #|U_j| (mathlib `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion: bounds #|X| from a cover by charts
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound: bounds #|Y| for affinoid étale Y

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) has one point, well below the bound 2^{2^ℵ₀}.
- A bound in terms of #A alone is needed and attained in order of magnitude: the classical points of Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) alone number #K°.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.ext'`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_prod`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mul_eq_self`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_le_of_injective`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`.

**Imports from Tau Ceti roadmaps.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`.

<a id="p6-kappa-small-cover-criterion"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion` — Cover criterion for κ-smallness (ECD Proposition 4.4, corrected for singular κ)

*Theorem.* Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal and X a perfectoid space. (a) If X is κ-small, then X is covered by fewer than κ open affinoid subspaces Spa(A, A⁺) with #A < κ (namely by all of them: there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ). (b) If X has a cover {U_j = Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)}_{j∈J} by open affinoid subspaces with #A_j < κ for all j, then every open affinoid subspace U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X has #A < κ; so such an X is κ-small as soon as #|X| < κ. (c) If moreover #J < κ and sup_j #A_j < κ — automatic when J is finite, or when #J < cf κ — then #|X| < κ, and X is κ-small, indeed uniformly κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space). (d) In particular an affinoid perfectoid space Spa(A, A⁺) is κ-small iff #A < κ, and a quasicompact perfectoid space is κ-small iff it has a finite cover by open affinoid subspaces whose rings have cardinality < κ. (e) The converse of (a) as printed in ECD Proposition 4.4 — a cover by fewer than κ open affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ, without a uniform bound, implies κ-small — holds for regular κ and fails whenever cf κ ≤ #J: for κ of cofinality ω₁ (such as the cutoff cardinal κ(ω₁) of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and perfectoid fields K_α, α < ω₁, with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs Spa(K_α⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K_α°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is covered by ω₁ < κ open affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ and has at least κ points.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- κ uncountable strong limit. Part (c) needs the uniform bound; part (e) records exactly where the printed statement needs it.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): the open subsets of |X| number at most 2^{#|X|} < κ, open affinoid subspaces cover X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space), and each has ring of cardinality < κ by definition.
2. (b): U is quasicompact (Tau Ceti `spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`); each U ∩ U_j is a union of rational subsets of U_j, so finitely many rational subsets W_k ⊆ U ∩ U_{j_k} cover U. #O(W_k) ≤ (#A_{j_k}·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality (b1)), and A = O_X(U) embeds into ∏_k O(W_k) since O_X is a sheaf (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity).
3. (c): #|U_j| ≤ 2^{#A_j·#A_j} ≤ 2^λ with λ := sup_j #A_j + ℵ₀ < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality), hence #|X| ≤ #J · 2^λ < κ; if #J < cf κ then sup_j #A_j < κ by mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`.
4. (d): take J a singleton, respectively finite, and use (b), (c).
5. (e): for regular κ, cf κ = κ > #J and (c) applies. For the counterexample, the points x_a : T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ a^{1/pⁿ} (a ∈ K_α°) of the disc over K_α (characteristic p, perfect) are pairwise distinct, so #|X| ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ, while each disc ring has cardinality ≤ #K_α^ℵ₀ < κ; the fields K_α are completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples).

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site, D2/cutoff-independence: recognising κ-small spaces from affinoid covers
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure: fibre products are recognised from charts U ×_W V

**Acceptance.**

- Affinoid instance (ECD's use in §7–§8): Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is κ-small for every cutoff cardinal κ, its ring having cardinality 2^ℵ₀.
- A countable disjoint union of copies of Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is κ-small for every cutoff κ by (c) (#J = ℵ₀ < cf κ).
- The counterexample of (e) for κ = κ(ω₁).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality`](#p6-adic-spectrum-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, `mathlib:Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set`.

<a id="p6-kappa-small-closure"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure` — Closure properties of κ-small perfectoid spaces: open subspaces, disjoint unions, fibre products

*Theorem.* Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. (a) An open subspace of a κ-small (resp. uniformly κ-small) perfectoid space is κ-small (resp. uniformly κ-small). (b) A disjoint union ⊔_{j∈J} X_j is uniformly κ-small if #J < κ and all X_j are κ'-small for one κ' < κ; finite disjoint unions of κ-small spaces are κ-small. (c) (ECD Proposition 4.4, 'in particular') For morphisms X → Z ← Y of perfectoid spaces with X and Y uniformly κ-small (Z arbitrary), the fibre product X ×_Z Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is uniformly κ-small: if #|X|, #|Y| ≤ λ and all open affinoid rings of X and Y have cardinality ≤ λ (λ ≥ ℵ₀), then X ×_Z Y is covered by at most 2^λ open affinoids U ×_W V with rings of cardinality ≤ λ^ℵ₀ and has at most 2^{2^λ} points. In particular fibre products of κ-small quasicompact (for instance affinoid) perfectoid spaces are κ-small, and the κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces are stable under fibre products. (d) For κ of cofinality ω₁ the unrestricted statement fails: for a perfectoid field L of characteristic p and perfectoid fields K_α ⊇ L (α < ω₁) that are completed perfections of L(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm, with λ_α < κ cofinal in κ, X := ⊔_α Spa(K_α, K_α°) is κ-small but X ×_{Spa(L, L°)} X is not, since Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) has at least λ_α points.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- κ uncountable strong limit; Z need not be κ-small in (c).
- The fibre product is that of perfectoid spaces over a general perfectoid Tate base (P2), with affinoid charts given by the uniform completed tensor product.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): points and open affinoid subspaces of an open V ⊆ X are points and open affinoid subspaces of X.
2. (b): apply PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (c) to the cover by the charts of the X_j.
3. (c): the triples (U, V, W) of open affinoids with U ⊆ X, V ⊆ Y, W ⊆ Z and U, V mapping into W give an open cover of X ×_Z Y by the U ×_W V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces); choosing one W per pair (U, V) uses at most 2^λ·2^λ charts. The ring of U ×_W V is the uniform completed tensor product of O(U) and O(V) over O(W), of cardinality ≤ (λ·λ·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = λ^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality (b3)); then PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (c) and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality give the bounds. Quasicompact κ-small spaces are uniformly κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space (b)).
4. (d): X is κ-small (ℵ₁ points; each open affinoid is a finite union of components). For β < λ_α choose a perfectoid field C ⊇ L and elements c_γ ∈ C (γ < λ_α) of absolute value 1 with residues algebraically independent over the residue field of L; x_γ ↦ c_γ and x_γ ↦ d_γ (d_γ = c_γ for γ ≠ β, d_β = c_β + t) are isometric L-embeddings K_α → C, and together they give a point p_β of Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) with |x_β ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_β|(p_β) = |t| and |x_γ ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_γ|(p_β) = 0 for γ ≠ β; so the p_β are pairwise distinct and #|X ×_{Spa L} X| ≥ sup_α λ_α = κ.

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site, D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site: the pretopologies on Perfd_κ pull covers back along arbitrary maps
- ECD Proposition 11.4 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds): products and fibre products of perfectoid spaces used to form fibre products of diamonds

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Y = Z = Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, …), X ×_Z Y = X is κ-small.
- Spa(C_p) ×_{Spa(K)} Spa(C_p) for K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧ has infinitely many points and ring of cardinality 2^ℵ₀, hence is κ-small for every cutoff κ.
- The counterexample (d) shows that ECD's 'stable under finite products' needs the uniform or quasicompact hypothesis for singular κ.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion`](#p6-kappa-small-cover-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality`](#p6-adic-spectrum-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`](#p2-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`](#p1-perfectoid-examples), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`.

<a id="p6-kappa-small-tilting"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-tilting` — Tilting preserves κ-smallness

*Lemma.* For a perfectoid Tate ring A with tilt A♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), #A♭ ≤ (#A)^ℵ₀ and #A ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀·ℵ₀. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit κ and a perfectoid space X with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting), X is κ-small iff X♭ is κ-small, and X is uniformly κ-small iff X♭ is; tilting restricts to an equivalence between κ-small perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid space S and κ-small perfectoid spaces over S♭.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- No base field; any characteristic.

**Proof outline.**

1. #A♭ ≤ (#A)^ℵ₀: as a multiplicative monoid A♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} A ⊆ A^ℕ (ECD Definition 3.9, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).
2. #A ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀·ℵ₀: A°/ϖ ≅ A♭°/ϖ♭ for a compatible pseudouniformiser (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); each ϖᵏA°/ϖ^{k+1}A° is a quotient of A°/ϖ, so #A°/ϖⁿ ≤ (#A°/ϖ)ⁿ; A° is ϖ-adically complete, so A° = lim A°/ϖⁿ has cardinality ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀; and A = ⋃_n ϖ^{-n}A°.
3. Spaces: |X| ≅ |X♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), and U ↦ U♭ is a bijection between open affinoid perfectoid subspaces with O(U♭) = O(U)♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting); since κ is a strong limit, λ^ℵ₀ < κ for λ < κ.

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2 and D6 (Perf_κ versus Perfd_κ): the v-site of characteristic-p perfectoid spaces and its untilts respect the cutoff

**Acceptance.**

- C_p and its tilt, the completed algebraic closure of F_p((t)), both have cardinality 2^ℵ₀.
- The tilt of a κ-small affinoid perfectoid space is κ-small: the diamond Spd of DiamondsAndVStacks:D6 keeps κ-small objects κ-small.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`](#p1-tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`](#p2-perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`](#p2-tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), `mathlib:Cardinal.power_le_power_right`.

<a id="p6-kappa-small-cofiltered-limits"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits` — Cofiltered limits of uniformly bounded κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces are κ-small (set-theoretic clause of ECD Proposition 6.4)

*Lemma.* Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). (a) If #Mor(I) ≤ λ and #R_i ≤ λ for all i, with λ infinite, then #R ≤ λ^ℵ₀; so for an uncountable strong limit κ > λ, X is κ-small (and uniformly κ-small). (b) (ECD) If κ is a cutoff cardinal (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal), I is λ-small for some λ < κ and all X_i are κ′-small for one strong limit κ′ < κ, then X is κ-small; if κ′ = κ_λ is a strong limit of cofinality > λ (clause (iii) of the cutoff lemma), then X is even κ_λ-small, so the bound does not grow with the diagram. (c) The uniform bound cannot be dropped: for κ of cofinality ω₁ and a tower of perfectoid fields K_0 ⊆ K_1 ⊆ … ⊆ K_α ⊆ … (α < ω₁) with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, the X_α = Spa(K_α, K_α°) are κ-small, I = ω₁ has fewer than κ elements, and the limit (the completed union) is not κ-small.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- The ring-level bound #R ≤ (#Mor(I)·sup_i #R_i)^ℵ₀ is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds; this node states it for P6's κ-small notion.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): colim R_i⁺ has cardinality ≤ #Mor(I)·λ ≤ λ, and R⁺ is its ϖ-adic completion (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), in which it is dense, so #R⁺ ≤ λ^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality); R = R⁺[1/ϖ]; then PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
2. (b): with λ' := max(λ, κ′) < κ apply (a). For κ′ = κ_λ of cofinality > λ, sup_i #R_i < κ_λ (mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`), and #R ≤ (sup)^ℵ₀ < κ_λ as κ_λ is a strong limit.
3. (c): the completed union has cardinality ≥ sup_α #K_α = κ.

**Uses.**

- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): κ-smallness of X_∞ and of the countable iterate X̃
- ECD Lemma 11.22 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons): κ-smallness of cofiltered limits of diamonds
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations: a pro-étale presentation indexed by fewer than κ objects gives a κ-small limit

**Acceptance.**

- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): X_∞ = lim_J X_J over the finite subsets J of fewer than κ affinoid étale covers is κ-small, with a bound depending only on #O(X).
- The tower of (c) shows the necessity of 'one κ′ for all i'.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds`](#p5-limit-cardinal-bounds), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion`](#p6-kappa-small-cover-criterion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space`](#p6-uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound`, `mathlib:Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`.

<a id="p6-affinoid-etale-size-bound"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound` — Size of the affinoid étale site: rings bounded by #O(X)^ℵ₀, fewer than κ isomorphism classes

*Lemma.* Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and μ(X) := (#R + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀. (a) Every affinoid perfectoid space Y étale over X (Y ∈ X_ét^aff, étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces) has #O_Y(Y) ≤ μ(X) and #|Y| ≤ 2^{μ(X)}. (b) X_ét^aff is essentially small: it has at most 2^{μ(X)} isomorphism classes of objects, and #Hom_X(Y, Y') ≤ 2^{μ(X)} for all objects. (c) If κ is an uncountable strong limit and X is κ-small, then every object of X_ét^aff is κ-small, X_ét^aff has fewer than κ isomorphism classes of objects, and all its Hom-sets have fewer than κ elements; in particular the isomorphism classes of affinoid étale surjections onto X form a set of cardinality < κ (the count in ECD's proof of Lemma 7.18).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; no size hypothesis in (a), (b).

**Proof outline.**

1. Local structure (ECD Definition 6.2(ii)): every y ∈ Y has a neighbourhood V ⊆ Y that is a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid W finite étale over a rational subset U ⊆ X (shrink the open sets of the definition; W is affinoid by ECD Definition 6.2(i), PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids); Y is quasicompact, so finitely many such V_1, …, V_n cover Y.
2. Cardinalities (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality): #O(U) ≤ (#R·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = μ; #O(W) ≤ #O(U)·ℵ₀; #O(V_k) ≤ (#O(W)·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ = μ; O(Y) embeds into ∏_k O(V_k) (O_Y is a sheaf, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), so #O(Y) ≤ μⁿ = μ; #|Y| ≤ 2^μ by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality.
3. Counting: an object is determined up to isomorphism by a Tate ring structure on a set of cardinality ≤ μ (ring operations, a ring of definition and a pseudouniformiser), a plus subring, and a continuous ring map R → O(Y): at most (2^μ)^4·μ^{#R} = 2^μ classes; Hom_X(Y, Y') injects into the ring maps O(Y') → O(Y), at most μ^μ = 2^μ.
4. (c): #R < κ gives μ ≤ 2^{#R+ℵ₀} < κ and 2^μ < κ; κ-smallness of Y by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).

**Uses.**

- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): fewer than κ affinoid étale surjections onto a κ-small X
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence: X_ét^aff is essentially small, so Pro(X_ét^aff) and the canonical presentation are defined
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations: Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) and κ-small objects

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(C, O_C) with C algebraically closed: X_ét^aff is equivalent to finite sets (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point), with countably many isomorphism classes.
- X = Spa(K, O_K) for a perfectoid field K: the objects are finite disjoint unions of Spa(L, O_L) with L/K finite separable (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), each of cardinality #K.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`](#p3-strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/adic-spectrum-cardinality`](#p6-adic-spectrum-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion`](#p6-kappa-small-cover-criterion), `mathlib:Cardinal.power_mul`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

<a id="p6-kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs` — Every affinoid perfectoid space is the cofiltered limit of its κ-small perfectoid quotients (κ-bounded form of ECD Proposition 6.5)

*Lemma.* Let (S, S⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1) with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p divides p in S°, and let A ⊆ S be a subset. Then there is a closed subring S' ⊆ S containing A ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}} with #S' ≤ (#A + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ such that, with the subspace topology, S' is a perfectoid Tate ring, S'° = S' ∩ S°, and (S', S' ∩ S⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit κ and a morphism Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces with #R < κ, the set P_κ(Y/X) of closed subrings S' ⊆ S of cardinality < κ that contain the image of R and for which (S', S' ∩ S⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair, ordered by inclusion, satisfies: (a) it is directed, and every subfamily of cardinality ≤ λ whose members have cardinality ≤ λ, for a λ < κ, has an upper bound of cardinality ≤ λ^ℵ₀; in particular it is ω₁-directed; (b) ⋃ S' = S and ⋃ (S' ∩ S⁺) = S⁺; (c) Y = lim_{S' ∈ P_κ(Y/X)} Spa(S', S' ∩ S⁺) in perfectoid spaces over X, a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoid perfectoid spaces over X whose colimit of plus rings is already complete. For countable A this recovers the final statement of ECD Proposition 6.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition). P_κ(Y/X) is not κ-directed when κ is singular, so the directedness in (a) is the uniformly bounded one.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (S, S⁺) perfectoid; no base field. The upper bound in (a) needs the uniform bound λ on the members.

**Proof outline.**

1. Construction: A_0 := the subring generated by A ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}}; A_{n+1} := the subring generated by A_n and, for each x ∈ A_n ∩ S°, one chosen y_x ∈ S° with y_x^p − x ∈ ϖ^p S° (it exists because Φ : S°/ϖ → S°/ϖ^p is surjective, ECD Definition 3.1, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); A' := ⋃_n A_n, so #A' ≤ #A + ℵ₀; S' := the closure of A' (mathlib `Subring.topologicalClosure`), of cardinality ≤ (#A + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality).
2. S' is a complete Tate ring with ring of definition S' ∩ S_0 and pseudouniformiser ϖ, and ϖⁿ(S' ∩ S_0) = S' ∩ ϖⁿS_0 as ϖ^{-1} ∈ S'; bounded subsets of S' are those bounded in S, so S'° = S' ∩ S° (Tau Ceti `powerBoundedSubring`), which is bounded: S' is uniform; p/ϖ^p ∈ S' ∩ S° = S'°.
3. Frobenius on S'°/ϖ is injective: if y ∈ S'° and y^p ∈ ϖ^p S'° then (y/ϖ)^p ∈ S°, so y/ϖ ∈ S° (S° is integrally closed, Tau Ceti `isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`) and y/ϖ ∈ S'. Surjective onto S'°/ϖ^p: for x ∈ S'° choose x_n ∈ A' with x − x_n ∈ ϖ^p S°; then x_n ∈ A' ∩ S°, y := y_{x_n} ∈ A' ∩ S°, and y^p − x ∈ ϖ^p S° ∩ S' = ϖ^p S'°. S' ∩ S⁺ is open, integrally closed and contained in S'°.
4. (a): apply the construction to the union of the family (cardinality ≤ λ·λ). (b): each s ∈ S lies in the S' generated by {s} and the image of R. (c): by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces the limit is Spa of the ϖ-adic completion of ⋃ (S' ∩ S⁺) = S⁺, which is already complete; each Spa(S', S' ∩ S⁺) is κ-small by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
5. Singular κ: a family of cf κ members with cardinalities cofinal in κ has no upper bound in P_κ(Y/X).

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 8.2 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence): κ'-small affinoid perfectoid spaces over a κ-small X as cofiltered limits of κ-small ones
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations: the analogous statement for affinoid pro-étale X-spaces

**Acceptance.**

- For S = K⟨T_β^{1/p^∞} : β < µ⟩ (perfectoid polydisc in µ ≥ κ variables over a perfectoid field K with #K < κ), the subrings K⟨T_β^{1/p^∞} : β ∈ F⟩ for countable F lie in P_κ, and Y is their limit.
- ECD's use in the proof of Proposition 8.2: a κ′-small affinoid over X is a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoids over X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition`](#p5-countably-generated-decomposition), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`](#p6-complete-tate-ring-cardinality), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion`](#p6-kappa-small-cover-criterion), `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:Subring.topologicalClosure`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Cardinality

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29. The countable case, whose sub-pair construction the node makes explicit and bounds by κ.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §8, proof of Proposition 8.2, p. 39. The κ-bounded form used in DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence; (a) states the directedness that holds.

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p6-affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly` — ECD Proposition 6.4(iv) in the form used by the pro-étale calculus: affinoid étale objects and surjectivity descend to a finite stage

*Comparison.* Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces over a small index category, with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺, R = R⁺[1/ϖ]). For a perfectoid space T write T_ét^aff for the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over T (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces). (a) (ECD Proposition 6.4(iv), which is AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv) The base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét^aff → X_ét^aff. (b) (Descent of surjectivity) If Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff and Y_i ×_{X_i} X → X is surjective, there is j_0 → i such that Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j → X_j is surjective for every j → j_0. (c) (Relation to the quasicompact separated stage of P5) If Y ∈ X_ét^aff and Z_i → X_i is a qcqs étale model of Y (Z_i ×_{X_i} X ≅ Y; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects, ECD 6.4(ii)), then Z_i ×_{X_i} X_j is affinoid perfectoid and isomorphic over X_j to the model given by (a) for all j beyond some j_0. Affinoidness at a finite stage is the content of (a) and is not a consequence of ECD 6.4(ii)–(iii) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations (c)). (d) (Relative form) If B is an affinoid perfectoid space and the X_i → B are compatible étale maps (for instance a pro-étale presentation of X over B), then every Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff and every Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j lies in B_ét^aff, so the finite-stage models of (a) are affinoid étale over B. (e) The equivalences of ECD 6.4 (i)–(iv) are compatible with the inclusions X_fét ⊆ X_ét^aff ⊆ X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs (AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4). No step uses v-descent, a diamond atlas or the comparison of analytic adic spaces with diamonds.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X_i affinoid perfectoid of any characteristic, over no base field; I small and cofiltered.
- The equivalence (a) is imported from AdicEtaleGeometry:A3; this node adds the consequences (b)–(d) that the proofs of ECD Lemma 7.11(i), Lemma 7.18 and Proposition 8.5 use.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a): cite AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv (full faithfulness from ECD 6.4(ii); essential surjectivity in characteristic p through Huber's standard étale presentation, transported by tilting).
2. (b): the image V_i of |Y_i| in |X_i| is a quasicompact open (étale maps are open, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open; Y_i is quasicompact). Since |Y_i ×_{X_i} T| → |Y_i| ×_{|X_i|} |T| is surjective for étale Y_i → X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), the image of |Y| in |X| is the preimage of V_i, which is |X| by hypothesis. The preimages C_j of the closed set |X_i| ∖ V_i in |X_j| (j → i) form a cofiltered system of spectral spaces along spectral maps whose limit is its preimage in |X| = lim |X_j| (P5, ECD 6.4(o)), which is empty; so some C_{j_0} is empty (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces), and then C_j = ∅ for j → j_0, which by the same surjectivity means Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j → X_j is surjective.
3. (c): AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations (c).
4. (d): composites of étale maps are étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open) and fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
5. (e): AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4.

**Uses.**

- ECD proof of Lemma 7.11(i) (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition): affinoid étale maps to a limit Y = lim Y_i descend to some Y_i and so become affinoid étale over the base
- ECD proof of Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the countable iteration kills every affinoid étale cover at the next level
- ECD proof of Proposition 8.5 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves): surjective affinoid étale maps to a pro-étale presentation descend to a finite level
- ECD proof of Proposition 7.16 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected): splittings of étale covers extend to neighbourhoods of a component

**Acceptance.**

- ECD Lemma 7.18: an affinoid étale cover of X_∞ = lim_J X_J comes from some X_J by (a) and stays a cover there by (b); it splits over X_{J'} for J' ⊋ J containing it.
- ECD Proposition 8.5(ii): for a pro-étale presentation Y = lim Y_j and a surjective affinoid étale Ỹ → Y, Ỹ is the pullback of a surjective affinoid étale Ỹ_j → Y_j for j large (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves).
- Constant system X_i = X: every functor is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects`](#p5-finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`](#p3-etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`](#p3-strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`.

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, Proposition 6.4(iv), p. 27. Part (a).
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 28. The division of labour between P5's (ii) and A3's essential surjectivity recorded in (c).

<a id="p6-affinoid-pro-etale-map"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map` — Affinoid pro-étale morphisms and pro-étale presentations

*Definition.* Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space). f is affinoid pro-étale if Y = Spa(S, S⁺) and X = Spa(R, R⁺) are affinoid perfectoid and there are a small cofiltered category I, a functor i ↦ (Y_i → X) from I to X_ét^aff (affinoid perfectoid spaces Y_i = Spa(S_i, S_i⁺) with an étale structure map to X in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2, and X-morphisms as transition maps) and an X-isomorphism Y ≅ lim_i Y_i, the limit being taken in perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: S⁺ ≅ the ϖ-adic completion of colim S_i⁺ for a pseudouniformiser ϖ of R, and S = S⁺[1/ϖ]). The data (I, (Y_i), the isomorphism) is a pro-étale presentation of f. Conventions: the transition maps are X-morphisms between étale X-spaces and hence étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); they are not required to be surjective or finite étale, which distinguishes these presentations from those of Scholze 2013 used in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism; I is small but of arbitrary size; being affinoid pro-étale is the existence of a presentation. X_proét^aff denotes the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces over X on the affinoid pro-étale X-spaces. Basic facts recorded with the definition: every étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid pro-étale (constant presentation); |Y| = lim |Y_i| (ECD 6.4(o)); the image of |Y| in |X| is the intersection of the quasicompact open images of the |Y_i|, hence pro-constructible and stable under generalisation.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X and Y affinoid perfectoid is part of the definition; perfectoidness of the limit is supplied by P5.
- ECD writes Y = lim Y_i; in a formalisation the presentation is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces over X together with the étaleness of its legs' index objects.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `ProEtalePresentation f` as a structure with fields: a small cofiltered category I, a functor I ⥤ X_ét^aff, and an isomorphism over X from Y to the limit of its composite with the forgetful functor to perfectoid spaces; define `IsAffinoidProEtale f` as its nonemptiness.
2. Constant presentation: for Y ∈ X_ét^aff take I = ∗.
3. Underlying space: |Y| ≅ lim |Y_i| by P5 (ECD 6.4(o)); the image of |Y| → |X| equals ⋂_i im(|Y_i| → |X|): for x in the intersection the fibres of |Y_i| over x are nonempty spectral spaces with spectral transition maps, so their limit, the fibre of |Y|, is nonempty (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); each image is a quasicompact open (étale maps are open, P3).

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtalePresentation` (structure): A pro-étale presentation of f : Y → X: a small cofiltered I, a functor I ⥤ X_ét^aff and an X-isomorphism of Y with its limit.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale` (structure): f is affinoid pro-étale: Nonempty (ProEtalePresentation f).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.of_presentation` (constructor): A pro-étale presentation makes f affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.of_isEtale` (constructor): An étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.id` (example): The identity of an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtalePresentation.isLimit` (universal-property): The cone Y → Y_i is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtalePresentation.plusModEquiv` (characterisation): O⁺(Y)/ϖ ≅ colim_i O⁺(Y_i)/ϖ for a pseudouniformiser ϖ of O(X).
- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtalePresentation.homeomorphLimit` (compatibility): |Y| ≃ₜ lim_i |Y_i|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.range_eq_iInter` (characterisation): The image of |Y| in |X| is the intersection of the quasicompact open images of the |Y_i|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.isProConstructible_range` (other): The image of |Y| in |X| is pro-constructible and stable under generalisation.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isAffinoidProEtale_iff_canonical` (characterisation): f is affinoid pro-étale iff Y → lim_{(T,t) ∈ E_Y} T is an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidProEtale` (structure): X_proét^aff: the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces over X on the affinoid pro-étale X-spaces.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces preserves affinoid pro-étale maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidProEtale.of_comp` (functoriality): An X-map between affinoid pro-étale X-spaces is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation).

**Unit tests.**

- `isAffinoidProEtale_rationalSubset` (computation): For a rational subset U = X(f_1, …, f_n / g) of an affinoid perfectoid X, the inclusion U ↪ X is affinoid pro-étale with the presentation indexed by a point.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_id` (degenerate): The identity of an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid pro-étale.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_origin` (computation): For K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧ and X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), the origin Spa(K, K°) ↪ X is affinoid pro-étale with the presentation (X_n = {|T| ≤ |p|ⁿ})_n, and it is not étale (its image is not open).
- `not_isOpenMap_of_isAffinoidProEtale` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K and an infinite profinite set S with a non-isolated point x, the map Spa(K, O_K) × {x} → Spa(K, O_K) × S is affinoid pro-étale and not open (Berkeley Remark 8.2.3): affinoid pro-étale maps are not étale-local products.
- `not_isAffinoidProEtale_openUnitDisc` (non-example): The open unit disc {|T| < 1} of the perfectoid closed disc is étale, hence pro-étale, over it but not affinoid pro-étale: it is not quasicompact, hence not affinoid.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013` (compatibility): For an affinoid perfectoid U = lim U_i in the pro-étale site of a locally noetherian adic space over a perfectoid field (Scholze 2013) and V = lim V_k pro-étale over U by rational and finite étale pieces, V̂ → Û is affinoid pro-étale with presentation (V̂_k) (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison).

**Uses.**

- ECD Remark 7.9, Proposition 7.10, Lemma 7.11 (this stage): the pro-étale calculus
- ECD Proposition 7.12 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization): X^wl → X is an inverse limit of finite disjoint unions of rational subsets, hence affinoid pro-étale
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): X̃ → X is affinoid pro-étale
- ECD Lemma 7.19 and Corollary 7.22 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base, D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps): qc separated pro-étale maps over a strictly totally disconnected base are affinoid pro-étale; the image of an affinoid pro-étale map is pro-constructible and generalizing
- ECD Proposition 8.5(ii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves): (ν*F)(Y) = colim_i F(Y_i) along a pro-étale presentation
- ECD Proposition 8.2 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence): κ-bounded presentations of affinoid pro-étale X-spaces
- ECD Example 11.12 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds): Z ×_{π0 Z} (π0 Z ×_T S) is affinoid pro-étale over Z

**Acceptance.**

- Rational subsets, finite étale maps of affinoids and their composites are affinoid pro-étale.
- Zariski closed immersions are affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale).
- X × S → X for a profinite set S (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`](#p3-etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit`.

<a id="p6-pro-etale-map"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map` — Pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces

*Definition.* A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale if for every y ∈ Y there are an open neighbourhood V ⊆ Y of y and an open subset U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U such that V and U are affinoid perfectoid and f|_V : V → U is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map). Conventions: V and U can be chosen rational inside any given neighbourhoods of y and f(y) (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); X_proét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X with all X-morphisms, which are automatically pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits); for κ-small X, X_proét,κ is its full subcategory of κ-small objects. Pro-étale morphisms need not be open, need not be locally of finite type, and being pro-étale is local on the source and, for open covers, on the target, but not local on the target for the pro-étale topology. This is not Mathlib's pro-étale site of a scheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`, defined by weakly étale maps) nor Scholze 2013's X_proét of a locally noetherian adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- f an arbitrary morphism of perfectoid spaces, over no base field.
- The definition asks for affinoid V and U; ECD's 'open subset U' is taken affinoid, as the restriction f|_V must be affinoid pro-étale.

**Proof outline.**

1. Define `IsProEtale f` by the stated local condition with V and U open affinoid perfectoid subspaces.
2. Record: affinoid pro-étale maps are pro-étale; étale maps are pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); pro-étaleness is local on the source and for open covers of the target.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale` (structure): f is pro-étale: locally on source and target affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.of_isAffinoidProEtale` (constructor): Affinoid pro-étale maps are pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.of_isEtale` (constructor): Étale maps are pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.of_openCover` (constructor): If X = ⋃ U_α is an open cover and every f⁻¹(U_α) → U_α is pro-étale, then f is pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.restrict` (functoriality): For open U ⊆ X and open V ⊆ f⁻¹(U), f|_V : V → U is pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isProEtale_iff_exists_rational` (characterisation): f is pro-étale iff each y has rational neighbourhoods V ∋ y, U ∋ f(y) with f(V) ⊆ U and V → U affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of pro-étale maps are pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change of a pro-étale map along any morphism is pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.of_comp` (functoriality): An X-morphism between pro-étale X-spaces is pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsProEtale.diagonal` (other): The diagonal of any morphism of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/diagonals-are-pro-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtaleOver` (structure): X_proét: perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X, with all X-morphisms.
- `PerfectoidSpace.ProEtaleOver.hasPullbacks` (instance): X_proét has fibre products, computed in perfectoid spaces.

**Unit tests.**

- `isProEtale_openImmersion` (computation): The inclusion of the open unit disc {|T| < 1} into the perfectoid closed disc over a perfectoid field is pro-étale.
- `isProEtale_id` (degenerate): The identity of any perfectoid space is pro-étale.
- `isProEtale_prod_locallyProfinite` (computation): For a perfectoid space X and a locally profinite set S (e.g. Q_p), X × S := ⋃ X × S_c over the compact open S_c ⊆ S is pro-étale over X (Berkeley Example 8.2.2).
- `not_isOpenMap_of_isProEtale` (non-example): Spa(K, O_K) × {x} → Spa(K, O_K) × S (x a non-isolated point of a profinite S) is pro-étale and not open (Berkeley Remark 8.2.3).
- `isProEtale_iff_isAffinoidProEtale_of_etale_affinoid` (characterisation): An étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is pro-étale and affinoid pro-étale.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1(i)–(ii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site, D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site): pro-étale covers and the small pro-étale site X_proét
- ECD Definition 10.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks): quasi-pro-étale maps are those whose pullbacks to strictly totally disconnected spaces are pro-étale
- ECD Definition 11.1 and Proposition 11.4 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond, D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds): pro-étale equivalence relations; the diagonal of a representable map is pro-étale
- ECD Proposition 7.12 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization): X^wl → X is pro-étale for qcqs X
- ECD Lemma 7.19 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base): fibrewise criterion for pro-étale maps over strictly totally disconnected spaces

**Acceptance.**

- Every étale morphism of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale.
- X × S → X for a locally profinite S (Berkeley Example 8.2.2).
- Diagonals of arbitrary morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/diagonals-are-pro-etale).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`](#p6-affinoid-pro-etale-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`.

<a id="p6-product-with-profinite-set"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set` — The product X × S of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set, and its relative form X ×_{S₀} S

*Construction.* Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, φ : |X| → S₀ a continuous map to a profinite set and S → S₀ a continuous map of profinite sets. Write S → S₀ as a cofiltered limit of maps of finite discrete sets S_k → S₀,k (k ∈ K) compatible with S → S₀ (mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, `DiscreteQuotient`). Each φ_k : |X| → S₀,k is locally constant, so X = ⊔_{t∈S₀,k} X_{k,t} with X_{k,t} := φ_k⁻¹(t) open and closed, hence a rational subset cut out by an idempotent of O(X) (O_X is a sheaf, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity); X ×_{S₀,k} S_k := ⊔_{s∈S_k} X_{k,image(s)} is affinoid perfectoid and affinoid étale over X. Define X ×_{S₀} S := lim_k X ×_{S₀,k} S_k (limit in perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), and X × S := X ×_∗ S = lim_k X × S_k (ECD, after Definition 7.8). Properties: (a) universal property: for every perfectoid space T over X, X-morphisms T → X ×_{S₀} S correspond to continuous maps |T| → S over S₀; in particular the construction is independent of the presentation and functorial in S → S₀; (b) X ×_{S₀} S → X is affinoid pro-étale with the above pro-étale presentation; (c) |X ×_{S₀} S| = |X| ×_{S₀} S; (d) O⁺(X × S) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X)) and O(X × S) = C⁰(S, O(X)), continuous maps for the ϖ-adic topology on O⁺(X) (for X = Spa(K, O_K) this is ECD's Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K))); (e) for a morphism T → X, T ×_X (X ×_{S₀} S) = T ×_{S₀} S; (f) (X × S)♭ = X♭ × S; (g) for S locally profinite, X × S is glued from the X × S_c over the compact open subsets S_c ⊆ S and is pro-étale, not affinoid unless S is compact, over X.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; S, S₀ profinite (locally profinite in (g)).
- X × S is not the disjoint union of #S copies of X when S is infinite.

**Proof outline.**

1. Presentation: by `Profinite.asLimit`, S₀ = lim of its finite discrete quotients and S = lim of those finite discrete quotients of S compatible with them; K is cofiltered.
2. Clopen decomposition: an open and closed U ⊆ |X| gives O(X) = O(U) × O(X ∖ U) by the sheaf property, hence an idempotent e with U = {|e| ≥ 1}, a rational subset.
3. (a): X-morphisms T → X × S_k are decompositions of T into open and closed pieces indexed by S_k, i.e. locally constant maps |T| → S_k; passing to the limit gives continuous maps |T| → S (maps to a profinite set are compatible systems of maps to its finite quotients); the relative case adds compatibility with φ.
4. (b): each X ×_{S₀,k} S_k is a finite disjoint union of rational subsets of X, hence in X_ét^aff.
5. (c): P5 (ECD 6.4(o)) and the computation for finite S_k.
6. (d): colim_k Map(S_k, O⁺(X)) is the ring of locally constant maps S → O⁺(X), and its ϖ-adic completion is lim_n C⁰(S, O⁺(X)/ϖⁿ) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X)) (mathlib `LocallyConstant`, `ContinuousMap`).
7. (e): limits commute with fibre products (P2 fibre products, P5 limits). (f): tilting commutes with cofiltered limits and finite disjoint unions (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting).
8. (g): glue along the open and closed inclusions X × S_c ⊆ X × S_{c'}.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite` (constructor): X × S for X affinoid perfectoid and S profinite.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fibreProdProfinite` (constructor): X ×_{S₀} S for a continuous |X| → S₀ and a map of profinite sets S → S₀.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.fst` (projection): The projection X × S → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.isAffinoidProEtale` (other): X ×_{S₀} S → X is affinoid pro-étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.homEquiv` (universal-property): For T over X, Hom_X(T, X ×_{S₀} S) ≃ {continuous |T| → S over S₀}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.homeomorph` (compatibility): |X ×_{S₀} S| ≃ₜ |X| ×_{S₀} S.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.plusEquiv` (characterisation): O⁺(X × S) ≅ C⁰(S, O⁺(X)) and O(X × S) ≅ C⁰(S, O(X)).
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.map` (functoriality): A continuous map S → S' induces X × S → X × S', with map_id and map_comp.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.baseChange` (compatibility): T ×_X (X ×_{S₀} S) ≅ T ×_{S₀} S.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.tilt` (compatibility): (X × S)♭ ≅ X♭ × S.
- `PerfectoidSpace.prodProfinite.ofFinite` (example): For finite S, X × S ≅ ⊔_{s∈S} X.

**Unit tests.**

- `prodProfinite_finite` (computation): For a finite discrete S, X × S ≅ ⊔_{s∈S} X and O(X × S) = O(X)^S.
- `prodProfinite_punit` (degenerate): X × {pt} ≅ X and X × ∅ = ∅.
- `prodProfinite_Zp_sections` (computation): O(Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) × Z_p) = C⁰(Z_p, C_p) and O⁺ = C⁰(Z_p, O_{C_p}).
- `prodProfinite_homEquiv_connected` (characterisation): For X with |X| connected (e.g. Spa(K, O_K)), the sections of X × S → X are the points of S: Hom_X(X, X × S) ≃ S.
- `not_prodProfinite_eq_sigma` (non-example): For infinite S, X × S is not ⊔_{s∈S} X: the latter is not quasicompact and its ring of global sections is ∏_{s∈S} O(X) ≠ C⁰(S, O(X)).
- `prodProfinite_tilt` (compatibility): (X × S)♭ ≅ X♭ × S, compatibly with the projections.

**Uses.**

- ECD after Definition 7.8 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point): affinoid pro-étale spaces over a geometric point are X × S
- ECD Lemma 7.19 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base): the factorisation Y → X ×_{π0 X} π0(Y) → X and the fibres x × S_x
- ECD Example 11.12 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds): S × Spa(K, O_K) = Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K)) and Z ×_{π0 Z}(π0 Z ×_T S)
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/locally-profinite-torsors: trivial torsors X × G under a locally profinite group G
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product: the uniform completed self-product of a completed torsor tower is C⁰(G, Â_∞)

**Acceptance.**

- X × {pt} = X; X × ∅ = ∅; X × {1, …, n} = ⊔ⁿ X.
- ECD Example 11.12: S × Spa(K, O_K) = Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K)).
- ECD Lemma 7.19: X ×_{π0(X)} π0(Y) → X is affinoid pro-étale for strictly totally disconnected X.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`](#p6-affinoid-pro-etale-map), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`](#p2-sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`](#p2-rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p2-fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`](#p2-perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting), `mathlib:Profinite`, `mathlib:Profinite.asLimit`, `mathlib:DiscreteQuotient`, `mathlib:FintypeCat.toProfinite`, `mathlib:ContinuousMap`, `mathlib:LocallyConstant`.
