<a id="p7-perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers` — The perfectoid Frobenius criterion: Frobenius-controlled towers have perfectoid tilde-limits

*Theorem.* Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower) with generic fibres (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) and completion (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion). Then: (i) A_∞ is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (complete, uniform, with the pseudouniformiser ϖ satisfying ϖ^p | p in A_∞° and Φ: A_∞°/ϖ ≅ A_∞°/ϖ^p), of characteristic 0 or p according to A_0⁺, and (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair; (ii) the restriction map identifies |Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)| with lim_m |Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)|, and, when the A_m are sheafy (for instance strongly noetherian, as for affinoids of rigid spaces), X_∞ := Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m X_m in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, X_∞ is unique up to unique isomorphism, and it represents lim_m Hom(−, X_m) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) global form: let (𝔛_m) be a tower of flat ϖ-adic formal schemes (over a ϖ-adically complete base) with generic fibres X_m analytic adic spaces, and suppose 𝔛_{m_0} has an affine open cover by Spf A_{m_0}⁺ whose preimages Spf A_m⁺ (m ≥ m_0) form Frobenius-controlled towers compatibly with restriction; then the generic fibres have a perfectoid tilde-limit X_∞ ~ lim X_m, glued from the Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing), which is the generic fibre of the formal scheme lim 𝔛_m (limit in formal schemes, affine-locally Spf A_∞⁺). This theorem concerns towers whose finite levels are not perfectoid; the case of perfectoid finite levels is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Frobenius-controlled integral tower (the eventual Frobenius lifting modulo ϖ^p is the only input beyond flatness and completeness).
- For (ii)-(iii), the generic fibres are adic spaces (sheafy coordinate rings) so that the tilde-limit is defined.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound gives that A_∞⁺ is integral perfectoid, A_∞ uniform with A_∞° almost equal to A_∞⁺, and A_∞ perfectoid in Fontaine's sense (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.21), which is ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A_∞⁺⁺ is open (contains A_∞⁺), integrally closed and contained in A_∞°.
2. (ii): the tower of pairs satisfies the hypotheses of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{m,0} = A_m⁺ and I_m = ϖA_m⁺, whose completed direct limit is (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (iii)); perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so X_∞ is a perfectoid space and the final clause of that lemma gives X_∞ ~ lim X_m; uniqueness and representability are PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness.
3. (iii): on each affine piece apply (ii); the pieces are compatible with restriction (rational localisation commutes with the construction on both sides, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction) and glue by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii)-(iii). The formal-scheme limit is affine-locally Spf of the ϖ-adic completion of colim A_m⁺, whose generic fibre is Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: for 0 ≤ ε < 1/2 there are unique perfectoid spaces X_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_m X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a (and similarly X*, A) over Q_p^cycl, the transition maps of the integral models X(p^{-m}ε) agreeing with relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε}.
- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(1): X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_n X_{Γ_0*(p^n)}(ε)_a for Hilbert modular varieties, via Lemma 5.12 (relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ}).
- Compatible-root disc and torus: the towers R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ and R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩ over a perfectoid Tate pair give Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩) and Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩) (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Example 4.4 for the torus over a perfectoid field).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`](#p7-frobenius-controlled-integral-tower), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`](#p7-frobenius-tower-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`](#p7-frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`](#p7-tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`](#p7-tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction`](#p7-tilde-limit-rational-restriction), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`](#p7-tilde-limit-gluing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`](#p7-perfectoid-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`](#p1-integral-perfectoid-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`](#p2-perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`](#p2-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Criterion

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 42. The eventual Frobenius lifting condition in the source: transition maps equal to relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p with ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}.

<a id="p7-frobenius-tower-tilt"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-tilt` — The tilt of the limit of a Frobenius-controlled tower

*Lemma.* Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower and (S_•⁺, t, m_0, w′) a Frobenius-controlled integral tower of characteristic p (p = 0 in S_0⁺), together with ring isomorphisms α_m: A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ S_m⁺/t^p for m ≥ m_0 compatible with the transition maps (and with the w, w′). Then the perfectoid Tate ring S_∞ = S_∞⁺[1/t] of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers is perfect, and S_∞ is the tilt of A_∞: there is a unique isomorphism A_∞♭ ≅ S_∞ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) carrying ϖ♭ to a unit multiple of t and inducing the colimit of the α_m modulo ϖ and t, namely A_∞⁺/ϖ = colim A_m⁺/ϖ ≅ colim S_m⁺/t = S_∞⁺/t; under it, Spa(S_∞, S_∞⁺⁺) is the tilt of Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺), and in the global form of the criterion the tilt of X_∞ is the limit of the characteristic-p tower.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- The comparison α is given only modulo ϖ^p and t^p (it need not lift).

**Proof outline.**

1. A_∞⁺/ϖ^p = colim A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ colim S_m⁺/t^p = S_∞⁺/t^p (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (i)).
2. S_∞⁺ is perfect: Φ: S_∞⁺/t → S_∞⁺/t^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound) and S_∞⁺ is t-adically complete and t-torsion-free, so Frobenius is bijective on S_∞⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
3. Tilt: A_∞♭⁺ ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} A_∞⁺/ϖ up to almost zero (ECD Lemma 3.10, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); via α this is lim_Φ S_∞⁺/t = S_∞⁺ (perfect and t-complete), compatibly with the rings of integral elements; invert ϖ♭ ↔ t (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: the tilt of X*_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a is the open subset of the perfection X′*perf where |Ha| ≥ |t|^ε, using X′*(p^{-m}ε)/t^{1−ε} = X*(p^{-m}ε)/p^{1−ε} (Theorem III.2.15(i)).
- For the compatible-root disc over R, the characteristic-p tower R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ with α_m induced by R⁺/ϖ^p ≅ R♭⁺/(ϖ♭)^p gives the tilt R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ of R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`](#p7-perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`](#p7-frobenius-tower-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`](#p7-frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`](#p1-tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`](#p1-tilt-integral-subrings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`](#p1-tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Tilt

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43. The tilt identification from the congruence of the two towers.
- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §III.2.3, before Definition III.2.18, p. 42. The characteristic-p side is a perfection.

<a id="p7-perfection-tilde-limit"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit` — The perfection of a characteristic-p adic space as a tilde-limit along relative Frobenius

*Lemma.* Let k be a perfect complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser t (more generally a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p with t ∈ k° admitting all p-power roots), (S, S⁺) a complete Tate pair over (k, k°) with S⁺ flat over k° and t-adically complete, and Φ: S → S^{(p)} ≅ S the relative Frobenius over k (an isomorphism of the base, k being perfect). (i) The tower S⁺ →Φ S⁺ →Φ ⋯ (level m carrying the k°-structure twisted by Φ_k^{-m}) is a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with ϖ = t and w_m the canonical base-change isomorphisms (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower, constructor from relative Frobenius); (ii) its completion is S^{perf⁺} := the t-adic completion of colim_Φ S⁺ with S^{perf} = S^{perf⁺}[1/t], a perfect, hence perfectoid, Tate ring; (iii) if S is sheafy, Y^{perf} := Spa(S^{perf}, S^{perf⁺⁺}) ~ lim_Φ Y for Y = Spa(S, S⁺), the maps |Y^{perf}| → |Y| are homeomorphisms, and Y^{perf} is the unique perfectoid space over k with this property; (iv) for an analytic adic space Y over k covered by such affinoids, the Y^{perf} glue to a perfectoid space Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing). The corresponding statement for flat t-adic formal schemes 𝔜: lim_Φ 𝔜 is representable by the perfect flat formal scheme 𝔜^{perf}, locally Spf(R^{perf}), compatibly with generic fibres.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Base perfect of characteristic p so that relative Frobenius is k-linear and the Frobenius twist is isomorphic to the original algebra; S⁺ flat over k°.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): relative Frobenius over a perfect base satisfies the source form of the definition: the twist S⁺/t ⊗_{k°/t, Φ} k°/t^p is S⁺/t^p after identifying k°/t ≅ k°/t^p by Frobenius.
2. (ii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion; perfectness of the completion and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5: in characteristic p, perfectoid = perfect complete Tate).
3. (iii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers (ii); Frobenius induces homeomorphisms on adic spectra (a valuation is determined by its values on p-th powers), so all transition maps and the projections are homeomorphisms.
4. (iv) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing, since the construction commutes with rational localisation.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Definition III.2.18: X′*perf over F_p((t^{1/(p−1)p^∞})) is the tilde-limit of the Siegel space X′* along relative Frobenius.
- For Y = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩), Y^{perf} = Spa(k⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, k°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), and the étale topoi of Y^{perf} and Y agree (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`](#p7-frobenius-controlled-integral-tower), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`](#p7-frobenius-tower-completion), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`](#p7-perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`](#p7-tilde-limit-gluing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`](#p1-characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

**namespace.** TauCeti.Perfectoid

**Sources.**

- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42. Statement (iii)-(iv) over the base of the source.
- [`Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015`](#source-p0-scholze-torsionlocallysymmetric-2015), §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42. The tilde-limit is the one of Scholze–Weinstein.

<a id="p7-limit-of-perfectoid-tower"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower` — Towers of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps have perfectoid tilde-limits

*Theorem.* Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of perfectoid spaces whose transition maps are affinoid (for every a: j → i and every affinoid open V ⊆ X_i, f_a^{-1}(V) is affinoid; hence qcqs). Then: (i) the limit X := lim_i X_i exists in the category of perfectoid spaces; (ii) X ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), and X represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) for i_0 ∈ I and an affinoid perfectoid open V = Spa(R_{i_0}, R_{i_0}⁺) ⊆ X_{i_0} with preimages V_a = Spa(R_a, R_a⁺), the preimage of V in X is Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_a R_a⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ] (ϖ a compatible pseudouniformiser), and R is perfectoid; (iv) |X| ≅ lim_i |X_i|; (v) if I is ω_1-cofiltered, colim R_a → R and colim R_a⁺ → R⁺ are bijective. This is the easy limit theorem, in which every finite level is already perfectoid; it is distinct from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers, whose finite levels are not perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Every X_i perfectoid; affinoid transition maps (as for finite étale or pro-étale towers of affinoids).

**Proof outline.**

1. Affinoid case: PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4(o), 6.5) gives the limit Spa(R, R⁺), the formula and the homeomorphism; the perfectoidness of (R, R⁺) is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid (each R_a⁺ integral perfectoid by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.20; bijective Frobenius modulo ϖ and ϖ-torsion-freeness pass to the colimit and its completion; Lemmas 3.10(ii) and 3.21), the same argument as PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound with w_m replaced by the inverse Frobenius at each level.
2. Tilde-limit on affinoids: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{a,0} = R_a⁺.
3. Global case: cover X_{i_0} by affinoid perfectoids V; affinoid transition maps make every V_a affinoid perfectoid; glue the affinoid limits by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii) (uniqueness on overlaps from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness), which also gives (ii) and (iv).
4. (v) as in ECD Proposition 6.5 (a Cauchy sequence lives at a finite stage).

**Acceptance.**

- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11(2): the finite étale tower X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)∩Γ_1*(p^n)}(ε)_a of perfectoid spaces has the perfectoid tilde-limit X_{Γ_1*(p^∞)}(ε)_a.
- A pro-étale G-tower of perfectoid spaces X_j → X with X_∞ = lim X_j (PerfectoidSpaces:P9/profinite-galois-tower in the perfectoid case).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`](#p5-cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`](#p1-integral-perfectoid-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`](#p7-frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`](#p7-tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`](#p7-tilde-limit-gluing), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`](#p7-tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`](#p7-perfectoid-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`](#p2-affinoid-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`](#p5-completed-colimit-is-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid).

**namespace.** TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace

**Sources.**

- [`BHW-OverconvergentHilbert-2023`](#source-p0-bhw-overconvergenthilbert-2023), §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1749. The statement in the source's words.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, Proposition 6.5, p. 29. The affinoid case.
- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29. The universal property on affinoids.

<a id="p7-residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change` — Étale base change of residue-field tilde-limits, and bijectivity suffices (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16)

*Lemma.* Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit), i_0 ∈ I and g: Y → X_{i_0} an étale morphism of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces. Put Y_a := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j (a: j → i_0) and Y_X := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X, a perfectoid space étale over X. Then (i) Y_X ~′ lim_a Y_a; (ii) (the remark in the proof) in Definition 7.14, if |X| → lim |X_i| is bijective and the residue-field condition (c) holds, then |X| → lim |X_i| is already a homeomorphism, i.e. X ~′ lim X_i.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X_i and Y qcqs locally noetherian analytic; g étale (Huber's étale = A1's local description, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison).

**Proof outline.**

1. Existence of Y_X, perfectoid and étale over X: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii), Proposition 7.10).
2. Bijectivity of |Y_X| → lim_a |Y_a|, fibrewise over x ∈ X with images x_j: points over x are the extensions of the valuation of x to the finite étale k(x)^-algebra obtained from the fibre (étale maps are locally quasi-finite with finite étale fibres over completed residue fields); by (c) and henselian approximation (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^), and the valuation ring k(x)⁺ and its extensions are determined on the dense subfield colim k(x_j); so the fibres correspond.
3. Residue-field density for points of Y_X: residue fields of Y_X are finite separable over those of X and are the base changes of those of the Y_a, so density is preserved.
4. Homeomorphism (ii): Scholze refers to Huber's Remark 2.4.3 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). A route through public inputs: over an affinoid perfectoid W ⊆ X the map W → lim |X_i| is spectral (W qc, X_i qs); spectral bijections are homeomorphisms for the constructible topologies (Stacks Lemma 5.23.3 and 5.24.5), and generalising maps of spectral spaces that are surjective are quotient maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient); generalisations of an analytic point are its vertical generalisations, i.e. valuation rings between k(x)⁺ and k(x)°, which by (c) correspond to those of colim k(x_j).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for U → X étale, U ×_X X_∞ ~′ lim U ×_X X_i for the universal cover tower.
- For an open immersion Y ⊆ X_{i_0}, Y_X is the open subspace φ_{i_0}^{-1}(Y) (compare PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`](#p3-strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`](#p3-henselian-finite-etale-approximation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`](#p3-residue-field-finite-etale-colimit).

<a id="p7-tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent` — Qcqs étale spaces over a residue-field tilde-limit descend to a finite level

*Lemma.* Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit with all X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} → X_{ét,qcqs} between qcqs étale adic spaces over the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), and likewise 2-colim_i (X_i)_{fét} → X_{fét}; (ii) a finite family of morphisms (Z^k_i → Y_i)_k in (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} is jointly surjective after base change to X if and only if it is so after base change to some X_j. This is the perfectoid-limit analogue of ECD Proposition 6.4(i)-(ii) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects), with the X_i locally noetherian instead of affinoid perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid; ~′ (hence also ~).

**Proof outline.**

1. Finite étale over neighbourhoods of a point: for x ∈ X, 2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(U) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^) (Berkeley Lemma 7.4.6, via k(x)^⁺ = the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U ∋ x} O⁺(U) and Theorem 7.4.8; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), and the same at x_j ∈ X_j; by (c), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^) (the colimit of the k(x_j)^ is dense in k(x)^ and topologically henselian; finite étale algebras are finitely presented). Hence a finite étale cover of a neighbourhood of x is, near x, pulled back from a neighbourhood of some x_j, uniquely up to shrinking.
2. Faithfulness and fullness: as in ECD Proposition 6.4(ii) — graphs of maps between étale spaces are quasicompact open immersions (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal); two quasicompact opens of Z_i = Y_i ×_{X_i} Y′_i with the same preimage in Z_X agree in some Z_j, because |Z_X| → lim |Z_j| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change) and quasicompact opens of a limit of spectral spaces descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces); morphisms whose base change is an isomorphism become isomorphisms at a finite stage (surjectivity of f and of Δ_f descend).
3. Essential surjectivity: a qcqs étale Y → X is covered by finitely many pieces that are rational subsets of finite étale covers of rational subsets of X (local structure, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); quasicompact opens descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 through |X| ≅ lim |X_i|), finite étale covers descend by the first step and quasi-compactness, and the pieces glue at a finite stage by full faithfulness (X qcqs).
4. (ii): images of étale maps are open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); joint surjectivity is an equality of quasicompact opens, which descends by Stacks Lemma 5.24.6(3) and the surjectivity of |Y_X| → lim |Y_j|.

**Acceptance.**

- For the compatible-root disc tower over a perfectoid field K, every finite étale cover of the perfectoid disc is pulled back from some K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ (the disc's finite étale site is the 2-colimit).
- For the universal pro-finite-étale tower of a connected affinoid X over Q_p, the limit X_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, proof of Theorem 4.9, citing Lemma 7.5(i) of Scholze 2012).

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`](#p3-henselian-finite-etale-approximation), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`](#p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`](#p2-completed-residue-fields), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects`](#p5-finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`](#p5-quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`](#p3-residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`](#p3-finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit`](#p3-finite-etale-completed-direct-limit).

- [`Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds`](#source-p0-scholze-etalecohomologydiamonds), §6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 28. The graph argument for fullness.

<a id="p7-tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison` — Tilde-limits X ~ lim X_i of noetherian adic spaces and the comparison of etale topoi

*Comparison.* Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; no perfectoid base field is assumed, and the X_i may lie over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) while X lies over a perfectoid field), X a perfectoid space and X ~′ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit; this holds whenever X ~ lim X_i, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) |X| is a spectral space and X is qcqs (Scholze 2012 Remark 7.15); (ii) (Theorem 7.17) the étale topos X_ét^~ of the perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space) is the projective limit of the fibred topos (X_{i,ét}^~)_i of the étale topoi of the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, equal to Huber's): X_ét^~ is equivalent to the topos of sheaves on the colimit site colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} (objects qcqs étale over some X_i, morphisms the filtered colimits of Hom sets, coverings the families that are coverings at some finite level), compatibly with the pullback morphisms X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~; (iii) (Corollary 7.18) for i_0 ∈ I and a sheaf of abelian groups F_{i_0} on X_{i_0,ét}, with pullbacks F_j to X_{j,ét} (j → i_0) and F to X_ét, the natural map colim_j H^n(X_{j,ét}, F_j) → H^n(X_ét, F) is bijective for all n ≥ 0 (for sheaves of sets, n = 0; for sheaves of groups, n ≤ 1). When X is itself locally noetherian (and not assumed perfectoid), the corresponding statements are Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6, supplied by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity; this node is their perfectoid extension. Corollary 7.19 is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- All X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid (its étale site is that of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.11 / ECD Definition 6.2); no base field (Scholze 2012 states the result over a perfectoid field K; Scholze's rigid paper applies it to X_i over Q_p).
- Proofs follow Huber [Hub96] Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6 with Scholze's modification; the step through Huber's unpublished text is recorded as a gap, and the steps below use public inputs.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): Remark 7.15 via DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces.
2. (ii): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent identifies X_{ét,qcqs} with the colimit site, including coverings; since X is qcqs, the qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X form a generating subcategory of X_ét stable under fibre products, so X_ét^~ is the topos of the colimit site; a filtered colimit of coherent sites with finite-limit- and covering-preserving pullbacks has as topos the projective limit of the fibred topos (SGA 4 VI.8.2.3; request to DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).
3. Scholze's modification of Huber's proof: instead of Huber's Corollary 1.7.3, étale maps factor locally as an open immersion followed by a finite étale map (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison on the X_i; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces on X), and finite étale maps descend to a finite level by henselian approximation (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).
4. (iii): cohomology on a projective limit of coherent topoi of sheaves pulled back from a stage is the colimit of the cohomologies (SGA 4 VI.8.7.7, as in Huber's Corollary 2.4.6); on the colimit site this is DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites applied to the filtered colimit of the pulled-back sheaves, the cohomology of each stage being computed on its qcqs étale site.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim_n Spa K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ and Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩ (compatible-root disc and torus).
- Theorem 1.12/8.5's (P^n)^{ad} ~ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad} (Frobenius tower) is the source's application; in this case Cor. 7.19 does not apply but Thm 7.17 does.
- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for the universal cover X_∞ ~ lim X_i of a connected affinoid noetherian X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) (X_i finite étale over X, over Q_p; X_∞ over C_p), H^j(X_{∞,ét}, L) = colim_i H^j(X_{i,ét}, L) for all j ≥ 0 (the use made by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion). The tower satisfies X_∞ ~ lim X_i also in the sectionwise sense, by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit`](#p7-tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent`](#p7-tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity`](#p3-etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`](#p3-etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`](#p3-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`](#p3-henselian-finite-etale-approximation), `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.limit`, `mathlib:TopCat.Presheaf`, [`PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`](#p5-quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

<a id="p7-etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers` — Towers with homeomorphic, purely inseparable transition maps do not change the étale topos (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.19)

*Lemma.* In the situation of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (X ~′ lim X_i, X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic, X perfectoid), assume that every transition map X_j → X_i induces a homeomorphism |X_j| → |X_i| and purely inseparable extensions of completed residue fields. Then for every i the pullback X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~ is an equivalence of topoi; in particular H^n(X_ét, F) = H^n(X_{i,ét}, F_i) for every abelian sheaf F_i on X_{i,ét} with pullback F.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Transition maps homeomorphisms on underlying spaces with purely inseparable residue-field extensions (a universal-homeomorphism condition, typically relative Frobenius in characteristic p).

**Proof outline.**

1. For such a transition map, pullback X_{i,ét}^~ → X_{j,ét}^~ is an equivalence: Scholze refers to the remark after Huber's Proposition 2.3.7 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). This is the adic analogue of the topological invariance of the étale site (SGA 4 VIII.1.1).
2. The projective limit of a system of equivalences of topoi is equivalent to each member (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- Perfection: for Y an analytic adic space of characteristic p locally noetherian over a perfect field, Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y along relative Frobenius (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit), and Y^{perf}_ét ≃ Y_ét.
- Non-example: the Frobenius tower T ↦ T^p of P^n in characteristic 0 (Scholze 2012 Theorem 8.5) has non-inseparable residue extensions; there only the limit statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison applies.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison`](#p7-tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`](#p7-residue-field-tilde-limit), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit`](#p7-perfection-tilde-limit).

<a id="p7-regular-finite-flat-residue-tower"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower` — Finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.1)

*Theorem.* Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring with residue field k. There is a filtered direct system of finite flat R-algebras R_i such that each (R_i, mR_i) is a regular local ring and (lim→ R_i, m·lim→ R_i) is a regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field. If k is separably closed of characteristic p > 0, the R_i may be chosen of p-power rank over R. The colimit is Noetherian; it is not claimed to be complete.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- R complete regular local, of any characteristic. The proof uses the three Cohen presentations: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (equal characteristic); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ with W a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p (p ∈ m∖m²); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (p ∈ m²).
- Reuse Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing at the pin; do not reconstruct the regular-local-ring predicate. The Cohen presentations and the required regularity/normality, power-series, quotient and filtered-colimit comparison theorems remain supplier obligations (gap).
- The p-power clause needs k separably closed: then k̄/k is purely inseparable, and its finite subextensions have p-power degree.

**Proof outline.**

1. Equal characteristic: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (Matsumura 29.7). Let k_i range over the finite subextensions of k̄/k and put R_i := k_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, free of rank [k_i : k] over R. The m-adic completion of lim→ R_i is k̄⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, so lim→ R_i is Noetherian (Stacks 033E, 05UU, 00MK), hence a regular local ring.
2. Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m∖m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧. There is an integral extension W′/W of discrete valuation rings with uniformizer p and residue field k̄ (Matsumura, proof of 29.1). With W_i ranging over the finite discrete valuation ring subextensions of W′/W, put R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧; as before, the colimit has completion Ŵ′⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and is regular local.
3. Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (Matsumura 29.3 and the proof of 29.8(ii)). Each R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) is a finite flat R-algebra and a regular local ring. By the previous case lim→ W_i⟦x⟧ is regular local with regular system of parameters (p, x_1, …, x_n), so lim→ R_i is regular local with regular system of parameters (x_1, …, x_n).
4. p-power ranks: in all three cases rank_R R_i = [k_i : k] (= [W_i : W]); if k is separably closed of characteristic p, this is a power of p.

**Uses.**

- Česnavičius 2019, proof of Theorem 5.3 (PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 route 16): reduction of Brauer purity to an algebraically closed residue field

**Acceptance.**

- Non-example: the colimit is not complete. For R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧ the colimit is lim→ 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧, whose completion 𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧ is strictly larger.
- The p-power clause needs k separably closed: for k = 𝔽_p the stages 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧ have rank n.
- Ramified case: R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = ℤ_p[√p] has p ∈ m², R_i = W(𝔽_{p^i})[√p] with i ranging over the positive integers ordered by divisibility, and the colimit is regular with parameter x = √p.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `mathlib:IsRegularLocalRing`.

**Proposed library location (part record).** **module.** TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/RegularTower

<a id="p7-regular-finite-flat-perfectoid-tower"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/regular-finite-flat-perfectoid-tower` — Finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.2)

*Theorem.* Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field k, and W := W(k). There is a tower {R_m}_{m≥0} of finite flat R-algebras R_m of p-power rank over R, each a regular local ring, such that the p-adic completion R̂_∞ of R_∞ := lim→_m R_m is perfectoid (integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5, so R̂_∞[1/p] is a perfectoid Tate ring). Explicitly: if p ∈ m∖m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and R_m := W[p^{1/p^m}]⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧; if p ∈ m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² and R_m := W⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧/(p − f). The finite stages are not perfectoid, and R_∞ is not complete.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- k perfect, so W ≅ W(k) in the Cohen presentations of P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower; mixed characteristic (0, p).
- The criterion used is Česnavičius's Lemma 4.7: for a p-torsion-free ring S with (ϖ^p) = (p) for some ϖ ∈ S, if S is integrally closed in S[1/p] then x ↦ x^p : S/ϖ → S/p is injective, and if moreover every element of S/p is a p-th power then the p-adic completion of S is perfectoid. PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 route 7 plans that lemma at PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, which is not upstream of P7, so step 1 proves the instance needed here.

**Proof outline.**

1. Criterion. If x ∈ S and x^p = ϖ^p s with s ∈ S, then x/ϖ ∈ S[1/ϖ] = S[1/p] satisfies (x/ϖ)^p = s, so x/ϖ ∈ S by integral closedness, that is x ∈ ϖS. Since Ŝ/ϖ ≅ S/ϖ and Ŝ/p ≅ S/p, Frobenius Ŝ/ϖ → Ŝ/p is bijective, and Ŝ is integral perfectoid; P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid gives the Tate ring.
2. Each R_m is regular local and finite free of p-power rank over R: in the first case it is a power series ring over the discrete valuation ring W[p^{1/p^m}] (rank p^{m(n+1)}), and in the second it is the quotient of the regular ring W⟦x^{1/p^m}⟧ by p − f, which is not in the square of its maximal ideal (rank p^{mn}). Being regular, each R_m is a normal domain, so R_∞ is a normal domain, integrally closed in R_∞[1/p], and p-torsion free.
3. p ∈ m∖m²: take ϖ := p^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, since k is perfect and p and the x_i have compatible p-power roots in R_∞. Apply step 1.
4. p ∈ m²: by step 1 it suffices to find u ∈ R_∞^× with up a p-th power in R_∞, and then ϖ := (up)^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power and p ∈ m_∞², so p = Σ_i (s_i^p + p t_i)(s′_i^p + p t′_i) with s_i, s′_i ∈ m_∞ and t_i, t′_i ∈ R_∞. Hence p = s^p + pt with s, t ∈ m_∞, and u := 1 − t is a unit of the local ring R_∞ (Česnavičius follows Shimomoto's argument, [Shi16, 4.9]).

**Uses.**

- Česnavičius 2019, proof of Theorem 5.3, mixed characteristic case (PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 route 16): the perfectoid cover R̂_∞[1/p] on which the p-primary Brauer group vanishes
- PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24/037: the same towers, with the presentation R ≅ W(k)⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧/(p − f)

**Acceptance.**

- R = ℤ_p (n = 0): R_m = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}], and R̂_∞ is the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}], a perfectoid ring.
- Non-example, R = ℤ_p: for m ≥ 1, R_m/p ≅ 𝔽_p[T]/(T^{p^m}) and T is not a p-th power, so Frobenius is not surjective. At m = 0, R_0 = ℤ_p and Frobenius on R_0/p = 𝔽_p IS surjective, but no ϖ ∈ ℤ_p has (ϖ^p)=(p), since p·v_p(ϖ)=1 is impossible. Thus every finite stage in this example fails the perfectoid criterion, for different reasons at stage zero and positive stages.
- The residue field must be perfect: k is a quotient of R_∞/p, so if every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, every element of k is one.
- The completion is p-adic. R_∞ is not complete, and its m_∞-adic topology is not the one used.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower`](#p7-regular-finite-flat-residue-tower), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`](#p1-perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`](#p1-integral-perfectoid-comparison), `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosedIn`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:IsRegularLocalRing`.

<a id="p8"></a>

## P8. Finite quotients and closed loci in towers

Begin with invariant Huber pairs, continuity of valuations and invariant spectra, then prove finite-group quotient results, including groups of order divisible by p. Distinguish invariant-chart quotients from the separatedness hypotheses that produce charts, and distinguish rigid from perfectoid quotients. Develop analytic separatedness, Zariski closed loci and good towers. Finite towers need integral-algebra perfectoidization from the pending PerfectoidQuotients Part II; Q4’s semiperfectoid theorem alone does not supply it.

**Coverage (`planned`; packet P8).** Every definition and theorem of Hansen–Johansson §5.1, Hansen 2016, CGJ §2.1 and KL16 3.3.26 is a node, together with the closed-locus perfectoidization of Scholze's torsion II.2 and IV.1.1 in the form ECD 5.8 makes true. The stage text's 'Hansen–Johansson §5's invariant affinoid-cover hypothesis' is Hansen 2016's hypothesis; Hansen–Johansson replace it by analytic separation and prove that an invariant affinoid cover exists a posteriori, which is how this packet meets the completion contract to prove invariant-affinoid-cover existence before applying the quotient theorem. Groups of order divisible by p are included throughout: the invariants theorem (norm estimates and Sylow reduction) and the rational-localisation theorem (binomial coefficients prime to p and tilting) divide by no multiple of p.

**Remaining coverage obligations.**

- Install the PerfectoidQuotients Part II (generated id PerfectoidQuotientsPartII, DESIGN-PerfectoidQuotientsPartII, issue #3362) and import BS22 Theorem 10.11 with the continuous Tate-pair universal property (recorded gap).
- Requests to DiamondsAndVStacks D2, D4, D5, AdicSpacesPartII R0, R1 and to Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layers 3 and 5 are open; the nodes name exactly the statements they import, and the statements that supplier packets already contain are cited as nodes.

**Planets.** Invariant Huber pair; Invariants of a perfectoid ring; Quotient of an affinoid perfectoid space; Finite quotient of a perfectoid space; Good tower; Zariski-closed loci in perfectoid towers.

<a id="p8-invariant-huber-pair"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P8/invariant-huber-pair` — The invariant Huber pair (A^G, A^{+G}) of a finite group action

*Construction.* Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate–Huber pair and G a finite group acting on A on the left by continuous ring automorphisms with g(A⁺) = A⁺ for all g ∈ G. Put A^G = {a ∈ A : g·a = a for all g} with the subspace topology and A^{+G} = A⁺ ∩ A^G. Then: (i) A^G is a closed subring and a complete Tate ring: for every pseudouniformizer ϖ of A the norm N(ϖ) = ∏_{g∈G} g(ϖ) is a G-invariant pseudouniformizer of A and of A^G, G-stable rings of definition A₀ ⊆ A exist (the subring generated by the translates g(A₁) of any ring of definition A₁), and A₀^G is a ring of definition of A^G; (ii) (A^G)° = (A°)^G = A° ∩ A^G; (iii) A^{+G} is open and integrally closed in A^G and contained in (A^G)°, so (A^G, A^{+G}) is a complete Tate–Huber pair; (iv) A is integral over A^G, each a ∈ A being a root of the monic polynomial ∏_{g∈G}(T − g·a) ∈ A^G[T]; (v) A⁺ is the integral closure of A^{+G} in A. The construction is functorial in G-equivariant continuous maps of pairs, and for a subgroup H ≤ G it gives inclusions A^G ⊆ A^H, A^{+G} ⊆ A^{+H}.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (A, A⁺) complete Tate–Huber pair; G finite; G acts by continuous ring automorphisms preserving A⁺.
- No hypothesis on the order of G: p may divide |G|, and |G| need not be invertible in A.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) A^G is the intersection of the equalizers of the continuous maps id and g, hence closed since A is Hausdorff; it is complete as a closed subset of a complete ring. Each g(ϖ) is a topologically nilpotent unit because g is a continuous automorphism, so N(ϖ) is a topologically nilpotent unit fixed by G.
2. The subring generated by finitely many bounded subrings g(A₁) is additively generated by the bounded set ∏_g g(A₁), hence bounded, and it is open because it contains A₁; it is G-stable by construction. Then A₀^G = A₀ ∩ A^G is open and bounded in the subspace topology; N(ϖ) is topologically nilpotent, so some power N(ϖ)^m lies in A₀, and N(ϖ)^m·A₀^G is an ideal of definition.
3. (ii) A subset of A^G is bounded in A^G if and only if it is bounded in A, because the topology is induced and N(ϖ)ⁿA₀^G = N(ϖ)ⁿA₀ ∩ A^G; so a ∈ A^G is power-bounded in A^G if and only if it is in A.
4. (iii) A^{+G} = A⁺ ∩ A^G is open in the subspace topology; an element of A^G integral over A^{+G} is integral over A⁺, hence lies in A⁺ ∩ A^G.
5. (iv) The coefficients of ∏_g (T − g·a) are symmetric functions of the translates g·a, hence G-invariant; this is the integrality statement of Algebra.IsInvariant for the fixed subring of a finite group.
6. (v) (Hansen, Theorem 3.1, Step 3.) A⁺ is integral over A^{+G} by (iv) applied to elements of A⁺ (the coefficients lie in A⁺ ∩ A^G), so A⁺ ⊆ (A^{+G})^{icl}; conversely A^{+G} ⊆ A⁺ and A⁺ is integrally closed in A.

**API.**

- `Huber.Pair.invariants` (data): The pair (A^G, A^{+G}) with the subspace topology, for a finite group acting by continuous automorphisms preserving A⁺.
- `Huber.Pair.invariants_toSubring` (compatibility): The underlying subring of A^G is Mathlib's FixedPoints.subring G A.
- `Huber.Pair.normPseudoUniformizer` (constructor): For a pseudouniformizer ϖ of A, ∏_{g∈G} g(ϖ) is a G-invariant pseudouniformizer of A and of A^G.
- `Huber.Pair.exists_stable_ringOfDefinition` (constructor): A G-stable ring of definition A₀ exists, and A₀^G is a ring of definition of A^G.
- `Huber.Pair.powerBounded_invariants` (characterisation): (A^G)° = (A°)^G.
- `Huber.Pair.isIntegral_invariants` (other): A is integral over A^G; Algebra.IsInvariant (A^G) A G holds.
- `Huber.Pair.plus_eq_integralClosure_invariants` (characterisation): A⁺ is the integral closure of A^{+G} in A.
- `Huber.Pair.invariants_map` (functoriality): A G-equivariant continuous map of pairs induces a map of invariant pairs, with map_id and map_comp.
- `Huber.Pair.invariants_mono` (relation): For H ≤ G, A^G ⊆ A^H and A^{+G} ⊆ A^{+H}.
- `Huber.Pair.isClosed_invariants` (instance): A^G is closed in A, hence complete.

**Unit tests.**

- `invariants_trivialGroup` (degenerate): For the trivial group, Huber.Pair.invariants returns (A, A⁺).
- `invariants_swap_prod` (computation): For A = K × K, A⁺ = K⁺ × K⁺ and Z/2 swapping the factors, A^G is the diagonal copy of K, A^{+G} the diagonal copy of K⁺, and the norm of (ϖ, ϖ) is (ϖ², ϖ²).
- `invariants_toSubring_eq_fixedPoints` (compatibility): The underlying subring of Huber.Pair.invariants G (A, A⁺) is FixedPoints.subring G A, and A is Algebra.IsInvariant over it.
- `trace_image_ne_invariants` (non-example): For the trivial action of G = Z/p on a Tate ring A of characteristic p, the trace a ↦ Σ_g g·a is zero while A^G = A: the invariant ring is not the image of a trace or averaging operator when p divides |G|.

**Uses.**

- Hansen 2016, Theorem 1.2 and §3: the quotient Spa(A,A⁺)/G is computed as Spa(A^G, A^{+G})
- Hansen–Johansson, proofs of Theorems 5.3 and 5.8: V_x/H_x ≅ Spa(A^{H_x}, A^{+H_x}) for an H_x-stable affinoid V_x
- Caraiani–Gulotta–Johansson, Proposition 2.1.1: X_G = Spd(A^G, A^{+G}) is the v-sheaf quotient
- Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 3.3.26: A^G is perfectoid, with the norm pseudouniformizer
- PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S4: finite-group quotients of towers at infinite level are formed chartwise from invariant pairs

**Acceptance.**

- For the swap action of Z/2 on K × K the pair is the diagonal (K, K⁺).
- For G = {1} the pair is (A, A⁺).

<a id="p8-extensions-of-valuations-are-conjugate"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P8/extensions-of-valuations-are-conjugate` — Extensions of a valuation along a normal algebraic extension exist and are conjugate

*Lemma.* Let L/K be a normal algebraic extension of fields with Aut(L/K) finite, and v a valuation on K (any rank). Then v extends to a valuation of L, the extension is unique along the purely inseparable subextension K ⊆ L^{Aut(L/K)}, and Aut(L/K) acts transitively on the equivalence classes of valuations of L extending v.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- Arbitrary value groups; this is the classical statement for valuations, not for rank-one absolute values or places of function fields.

**Proof outline.**

1. Existence: the valuation ring O_v is a local subring of L, dominated by a valuation subring of L (Chevalley); for L/K algebraic its restriction to K is O_v.
2. Let B be the integral closure of O_v in L. The valuation rings of L extending O_v are the localisations B_𝔪 at the maximal ideals 𝔪 of B over 𝔪_v (valuation rings of L over O_v contain B, and are dominated by and dominate a localisation of B).
3. G = Aut(L/K) acts on B; B^G is the integral closure of O_v in the purely inseparable K′ = L^G, which is local (unique extension along purely inseparable extensions: x ↦ x^{p^n} lands in K), and B is integral over B^G with B^G = the fixed ring. Mathlib's transitivity of G on the primes of B over a prime of B^G gives transitivity on the maximal ideals over 𝔪_v, hence on the extensions.

**Acceptance.**

- K = ℚ_p, L = ℚ_p(i) (p ≡ 3 mod 4): one extension; K = ℚ, L = ℚ(i), v the 5-adic valuation: two extensions swapped by complex conjugation.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`, `mathlib:ValuationSubring`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `mathlib:Algebra.IsInvariant.exists_smul_of_under_eq`, `mathlib:Algebra.IsInvariant.isIntegral`.

**Sources.**

- [`han16`](#source-p8-han16), Theorem 3.1, Step 1, p. 4 (PDF p. 4) (continues on p. 5, PDF p. 5). Step 1 of the proof of Theorem 3.1 cites [ZS75, Corollary VI.7.3] for the transitivity.
- [`chj17`](#source-p8-chj17), Proposition 6.24, p. 54 (PDF p. 54). The proof of Proposition 6.24 cites Bourbaki V.2.2 Theorem 2 and Zariski–Samuel VI.7 Corollary 3 for the same step.

<a id="p8-continuous-valuations-over-invariants"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P8/continuous-valuations-over-invariants` — Continuous valuations restrict surjectively to the invariants, with G-orbits as fibres

*Lemma.* With (A, A⁺) and G as in the invariant Huber pair, the restriction map φ: Cont(A) → Cont(A^G), v ↦ v|_{A^G}, is surjective, and two continuous valuations of A have the same restriction if and only if they lie in the same G-orbit for the action v ↦ v ∘ g.

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- A complete Tate ring with a continuous action of a finite group G; A^G with the subspace topology.

**Proof outline.**

1. Fix the G-invariant pseudouniformizer ϖ = N(ϖ₁). Continuity criterion: a valuation v of a Tate ring R with pseudouniformizer ϖ and ring of definition R₀ ∋ ϖ is continuous if and only if v(ϖ) is cofinal in the value group and v(ϖx) < 1 for every x ∈ R₀ (Huber 1993, Theorem 3.1, as quoted by Hansen).
2. Supports: Spec A → Spec A^G is surjective with fibres the G-orbits, because A is integral over A^G (lying over, and transitivity of G on the primes over a given prime). For v ∈ Cont(A^G) with support p choose q over p; L = Frac(A/q) is algebraic and quasi-Galois over K = Frac(A^G/p), and the decomposition group G_q surjects onto Aut(L/K).
3. Extension and continuity on A: let w be a valuation of L extending v (it exists by the extension lemma) and view it as a valuation of A through A → A/q ⊆ L. Γ_w/Γ_v is torsion (L/K algebraic), so w(ϖ) is cofinal. Let A₀ be a G-stable ring of definition containing the invariant ϖ, and a ∈ A₀. Then ϖa is a root of ∏_g (T − ϖ·g(a)) = T^N + Σ_{i≥1} ϖ^i e_i T^{N−i} with e_i ∈ A₀^G, and v(ϖ^i e_i) < 1 because ϖ^i e_i is topologically nilpotent in A^G and v is continuous. If w(ϖa) ≥ 1, the leading term would strictly dominate every other term, which is impossible for a root. So w(ϖa) < 1 on A₀, and w is continuous on A by the criterion. (The source proves continuity only on the field L; see sourceIssues.)
4. Fibres: G acts transitively on the supports over p, and G_q (through Aut(L/K)) acts transitively on the extensions of v to L (extensions of valuations along a normal extension are conjugate).
5. The continuity criterion is assembled from the library: continuity from a cofinal value dominating the ideal of definition, and cofinality and v(ϖx) < 1 from continuity at topologically nilpotent elements.

**Acceptance.**

- For the swap action on K × K the two points of Cont(K × K) over a point of Cont(K) form one orbit.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P8/invariant-huber-pair`](#p8-invariant-huber-pair), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P8/extensions-of-valuations-are-conjugate`](#p8-extensions-of-valuations-are-conjugate), `mathlib:Ideal.exists_ideal_over_prime_of_isIntegral`, `mathlib:Algebra.IsInvariant.exists_smul_of_under_eq`, `mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_surjective`, `mathlib:Valuation`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isContinuous_of_forall_le_of_cofinalValue`, `tauceti:Valuation.IsContinuous.cofinalValue_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `tauceti:Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`.

**Sources.**

- [`han16`](#source-p8-han16), Theorem 3.1, Step 1, p. 4 (PDF p. 4) (continues on p. 5, PDF p. 5). Step 1 of the proof of Theorem 3.1, including the continuity criterion it quotes.
- [`chj17`](#source-p8-chj17), Proposition 6.24, p. 54 (PDF p. 54). The same fibre argument for classical affinoid algebras (Bourbaki V.2.2 Theorem 2, Zariski–Samuel VI.7 Corollary 3).

**Realises.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P8`; **implementation status:** `unchecked`.

<a id="p8-invariant-spectrum-homeomorphism"></a>

### `PerfectoidSpaces:P8/invariant-spectrum-homeomorphism` — |Spa(A, A⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A^G, A^{+G})|

*Theorem.* With (A, A⁺) and G as above, the continuous map q: |Spa(A, A⁺)| → |Spa(A^G, A^{+G})|, v ↦ v|_{A^G}, is surjective with fibres the G-orbits and induces a homeomorphism |Spa(A, A⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A^G, A^{+G})| for the quotient topology. Moreover Spa(A, A⁺) is the full preimage of Spa(A^G, A^{+G}) in Cont(A), and for every rational subset U = U(f₁, …, f_n / s) of Spa(A^G, A^{+G}) (f_i, s ∈ A^G generating an open ideal) the preimage q^{-1}(U) is the G-stable rational subset U(f₁, …, f_n / s) of Spa(A, A⁺).

**Hypotheses and scope.**

- (A, A⁺) complete Tate–Huber pair, G finite, acting continuously and preserving A⁺; no sheafiness is assumed.

**Proof outline.**

1. Cont(A)/G → Cont(A^G) is a continuous bijection by the fibre lemma; φ: Cont(A) → Cont(A^G) is a spectral map of spectral spaces (Cont of a Huber ring is spectral and comap along a continuous ring map is spectral).
2. φ is generalizing: the generalizations of a point of Cont of a Tate ring are its vertical generizations (coarsenings by convex subgroups); since Γ_w/Γ_v is torsion for w over v, convex subgroups of Γ_v and Γ_w correspond, so every generalization of v lifts to one of w. (The source asserts this without proof.)
3. A surjective generalizing spectral map of spectral spaces is a quotient map (Hansen, Lemma 3.2 = ECD Lemma 2.5); hence both Cont(A) → Cont(A^G) and the orbit map are quotient maps and Cont(A)/G ≅ Cont(A^G).
4. A valuation is ≤ 1 on A⁺ if and only if it is ≤ 1 on A^{+G}, since A⁺ is the integral closure of A^{+G} (invariant Huber pair (v)) and a valuation bounded by 1 on a ring is bounded by 1 on its integral closure; so Spa(A, A⁺) = φ^{-1}(Spa(A^G, A^{+G})). φ is open (the orbit map, open for a finite group, followed by a homeomorphism), so its restriction to the saturated subset Spa(A, A⁺) is an open surjection onto Spa(A^G, A^{+G}), hence a quotient map, and the homeomorphism restricts.
5. Rational subsets: the preimage of U(f/s) under the comap of A^G → A is U(f/s) ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺); the ideal generated by the f_i and s in A contains the image of an open ideal of A^G, hence a power of the invariant pseudouniformizer, so it is open. It is G-stable because f_i, s are invariant.

**Acceptance.**

- For G acting trivially, q is the identity.
- For Z/2 swapping K × K, |Spa(K × K)|/G is one copy of |Spa(K)|.

**Prerequisites.** [`PerfectoidSpaces:P8/continuous-valuations-over-invariants`](#p8-continuous-valuations-over-invariants), [`PerfectoidSpaces:P8/invariant-huber-pair`](#p8-invariant-huber-pair), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`, `mathlib:GeneralizingMap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`.

**Sources.**
